Cardinals' Injury Report is Downright Ugly
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals revealed their Thursday injury report for Week 7's clash against the Denver Broncos — and it's not pretty.
Darius Robinson and Jon Gaines were added to an already lengthy list of Cardinals that featured Walter Nolen, Budda Baker and Jeremiyah Love among others.
Practice report for Thursday:
Wydett Williams (concussion)
The Cardinals, hoping to again play the role of spoiler against Denver, could be massively shorthanded in making that happen as numerous stars are staring down a legitimate possibility of missing time.
Baker, Love, Wingard and Nolen have all missed consecutive days of practice now for Arizona. With the Cardinals hoping to take advantage of a disfunctional Broncos offense, Arizona's defense needs all hands on deck.
Shifting towards the other side of the ball, the Cardinals' offense will have their work cut out against one of the league's best defenses in Denver.
“Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of the Broncos' defense.
"I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it.
"They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.”

title: Walter Nolen, Jeremiyah Love and More Cardinals Stars Miss Practice
full_text:
TEMPE — Things are not looking good for the Arizona Cardinals in the health department.
The likes of Walter Nolen III, Jeremiyah Love and Budda Baker were the biggest names absent from the Cardinals' Thursday practice. Arizona plays host to the Denver Broncos in Week 7.
Nolen (ankle), Love (ankle) and Baker (groin/illness) all have not practiced for two consecutive days now in the build-up to Sunday. Also not spotted at practice today was Andrew Wingard (knee) and Max Melton (knee) — Wingard was a DNP yesterday while Melton was limited on Wednesday.
Earlier today, CBS Sports reported that Love is not expected to play, which would mark a second consecutive game missed for the third overall pick. His current ankle injury has been managed the last few weeks and is different from the one that saw him miss the end of preseason play.
It's looking as if the Cardinals will again rely on Bam Knight, Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull against a stout Broncos defense.
Nolen's absence would be massive in the trenches, as the second-year defensive lineman was starting to come into his own, playing a big part in helping Arizona control the line of scrimmage and get after the quarterback.
In terms of ceiling and potential, Nolen's is by far the highest out of anybody along the Cardinals' defensive line. Missing him against a struggling Broncos offense would be huge.
Baker's absence would leave an obvious hole in the team's secondary in terms of both talent and game-planning. After a rough start, Baker's quickly turned the corner and has pieced together a strong overall 2026 campaign.
"There's just certain things where if you can try to get him to the point of attack on each play, like you got to do it, just because he makes those plays," Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis told reporters on Baker.
"He puts people in negatives. He creates negative plays, that's a thing week to week is like where can we get Budda around the ball without being obvious?"
The Cardinals, sitting at 2-4, are hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all season when Denver comes to State Farm Stadium.
The official practice report will drop later today, but from a health perspective, things do not look good for Arizona.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur will meet with reporters on Friday morning, where he'll likely verify who is in and out for the weekend.

title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update for Cardinals-Broncos is Disappointing
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals aren't expected to have running back Jeremiyah Love available for their Week 7 tilt against the Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
Love is dealing with an ankle injury and missed last week's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. He didn't practice on Wednesday and now isn't probable to play against Denver:
The current expectation is that the #Cardinals will be without standout rookie running back Jeremiyah Love this week against the #Broncos , sources tell @CBSSports . Love (ankle) missed last week’s game vs. the Rams. Now expected to be out this week too. pic.twitter.com/2rmINyQrKC
“Yes, he’s feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying. (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%," LaFleur said of Love this week.
The Cardinals are likely to lean on Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier once again. The duo helped revamp Arizona's rushing attack last week. It was particularly Knight who tallied 80 yards on the ground with a 31-yard splash play to ignite the Cardinals' offense.
“Not shocking. He’s a stud. He’s a tough dude. He’s a tough tackle. I’ve seen it in a green jersey over in New York and then got to see it obviously yesterday. He ran hard," LaFleur said of Knight when speaking with reporters on Monday.
"I thought the guys did great job. I thought everyone was connected. We have a lot to clean up in the run game. Obviously, we hit some of those ‘G series’ like you’re talking about right there, but we have a lot to clean up with our downhill direct runs, but they still were getting dirty two (and) three-yard runs when it wasn’t necessarily executed.”
Love, the third overall pick in this past draft, has been incredibly exciting when healthy and on the field. However, he's been dealing with multiple ankle injuries since the preseason, which has limited his role in Arizona's offense and impact to begin his rookie campaign.

title: Cardinals Linked to 3 Different QBs in Latest NFL Mock Drafts
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 to begin the first six weeks of the season — which is on the lower end of a top ten pick and not quite bad enough for a top five spot.
The Cardinals are heavily believed to be eying a quarterback if they will indeed pick that high, even with third-round pick Carson Beck currently on the roster. Arizona is expected to play Beck this season before exploring options in 2027.
As it stands, three recent mock drafts all had the Cardinals plucking quarterbacks from the draft order:
Gilberto Manzano : "I think Carr might be the fourth-best quarterback in this year’s class because he doesn’t stand out physically with average size (6'2", 215 pounds) and arm strength. But scouts consider him the safest QB option because of how well he reads defenses. Coach Mike LaFleur just spent three seasons working with Rams coach Sean McVay, who values accuracy and high-level decision making before and after the snap.
"Carr, who has completed 66.8% of his passes for 1,639 yards, 16 touchdowns and only one interception, could hit the ground running and run LaFleur’s scheme efficiently."
Field Yates : "The Cardinals made enough of an investment in Carson Beck this April (65th overall) to suggest he could be the long-term starter, but I'm not sold on that being the case. Enter the dynamic Chambliss, who makes up for below-average size (6-foot, 205 pounds) with playmaking, clutch production, experience and craftiness.
"No quarterback in this class has played better in big games than Chambliss, who averaged 307 passing yards and accounted for six touchdowns in three College Football Playoff games last season. He has led Ole Miss to three wins over AP Top 25 teams in 2026."
Josh Edwards: "Saturday was hardly Austin Simmons' best day of the season, but he is a big quarterback with a strong arm. He operates in the pocket well and has thrown with great touch and anticipation. Thinking back to last season, it was a tale of two seasons for Ty Simpson , who was taken No. 13 overall by the Rams. The first half of the year was excellent, but the second half of the season was very much impacted by injury. All it takes is one team to believe in the talent, but Simpson's stock was on the ropes."

title: Cardinals Claim Panthers OL Off Waivers
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have claimed former Carolina Panthers offensive tackle Albert Reese IV, the team officially announced.
More on Reese from the team's official press release:
"Reese (6-7, 325) entered the NFL with Carolina in May as an undrafted rookie free agent from Mississippi State and was inactive for each of the Panthers first five games this season. A native of Edmonton, Alberta, Reese played 49 games (22 starts) at tackle over five seasons (2021-25) at Mississippi State. He started all nine games played in 2025 and started all 12 games in 2024 and won the Kent Hull Trophy as the best offensive lineman in Mississippi."
Reese was just waived earlier this week. Panthers OL Taylor Morton returned from injury, which prompted the move.
The Cardinals are currently down two starting offensive linemen due to injury while illness is spreading through the team, which has impacted new backup tackle Jedrick Wills according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
Arizona plays the Denver Broncos this week.
The Cardinals believe they got their rushing attack sorted last week after Bam Knight rushed for 80 yards, a much needed sign of life after Arizona's unit upfront struggled. To pair, the Cardinals' line didn't allow a single sack on Jacoby Brissett in Week 6.
"I do think in some aspects our run game has grown from a variation standpoint in terms of what we’re doing schematically and then how those guys are executing, but there are still aspects of our run game we need to improve," LaFleur told reporters today.
"I think the operation’s the one that is the biggest. There's no yards that go with operation in terms of what you guys can see, but we know that when we’re operating at the level that we’re capable of it does lead to yards, which leads to points, which leads to obviously the result that we’re all hunting up, so I'd say those two aspects."

title: Cardinals Battling Injuries, Illness and Weather as Broncos Prep Begins
full_text:
ARIZONA — The weather is changing, and while your coworkers are fighting off the sickness around the office, so too are the Arizona Cardinals.
Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills would miss practice due to illness today while Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen and Andrew Wingard won't practice due to their respective injuries.
"Just get this out of the way for you guys. So Jeremiyah [Love], Walt [Nolen] and Dewey [Wingard] will all be not practicing today, and then [we] got a little bit of an illness going around from a player, coaches [perspective] too, but from a player perspective, Budda and Jedrick Wills will be out. We'll know more a little bit as we go throughout the week. So, going to take it day by day with those guys," said LaFleur.
The Cardinals are beginning Week 7 prep for the Denver Broncos.
Arizona also had to move up their practice time just to account for the weather. Storms and flood warnings are prevalent throughout the Valley, which forced the Cardinals to move their practice time up by an hour.
"They're good. I mean, it wasn't a huge adjustment. We got through all of our meetings. Nothing was rushed," LaFleur said of adjusting the practice schedule.
"The biggest thing is what I like about our schedule, not only from a meeting perspective, a lifting perspective, do all those things, is guys don't mind eating before walkthroughs. And then because obviously it's still just a walk-through, jog-through type deal, and then you give them that extra hour to let it digest a little bit more, if you will, and then you go practice. Well, we're going straight from walk-through to practice, so the biggest adjustment really was just making sure they got a little grub in them before their normal time I guess."
Arizona, sitting at 2-4, is hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all season with Denver making the trek to State Farm Stadium.
What does LaFleur have to combat the traveling illness? Not much.
"I guess I could cancel everything. I don't know. I'm not a doctor. I drink some electrolytes and get some sleep," LaFleur joked. "So I don't know. Yeah, but it's a good question. I don't know."
The Cardinals will reveal their first injury reports of Week 7 later today, so we'll see who exactly is impacted by the array of issues currently impacting the team.
Fans and players alike may be indulging in some chicken noodle soup tonight.

title: Cardinals Kicker Wins NFL Player of the Week Award
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland has won the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after his performance in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Rams.
Ryland scored all 18 points in Arizona's upset victory at SoFi Stadium, booting home six field goals for the Cardinals' second win of the season. This is his first time winning the award and became the ninth kicker in Arizona history to take home such honors.
“I think our special teams has been really good all year," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said after the win. "I think they're an edge for us for sure in all units. I told the guys last night I didn't plan on using our punt team. We obviously had a few punts, but for the most part, did a pretty good job of controlling the ball.
"I never want to see six kicks again unless they're extra points. But if you're going to kick it, you might as well make it. I’m very happy for those guys.”
Ryland was brought back in free agency this past offseason and won an offseason battle with Josh Karty to be Arizona's kicker. After a handful of big kicks for the organization in 2024, Ryland saw some struggles in 2025.
However, Ryland's mostly come up big for the Cardinals this season, which included makes from 34, 30, 22, 38, 27 and 43 yards on the afternoon.
"He is the second Cardinals player to earn 'NFC Special Teams Player of the Week' honors this season after Simi Fehoko was selected following the Cardinals Week 1 win at the Chargers. It is the first time since 2015 that the Cardinals have had two different players each named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week (David Johnson, Chandler Catanzaro).
"Ryland accounted for all 18 points in Arizona’s 18-16 victory, connecting on all six field goal attempts. His final field goal of the day was a 43-yard game-winner as time expired in regulation. Ryland’s six field goals and 18 total points are both career highs.
"Only once in franchise history did a player make more field goals in a game than Ryland did on Sunday (7 by Jim Bakken on 9/24/67 at Pittsburgh). His six field goals in Los Angeles are the most in a single game in the NFL this season and the 43-yarder was his fifth career game-winner.
"He became the first NFL player to have 6+ field goals in a game since Houston’s Ka’imi Fairbairn on 1/4/2026 (6 FG) vs. Indianapolis. Ryland is tied for 3rd in the NFL in made FGs (14) and 4th in the NFL in total points (54) in 2026."

title: Buy or Sell: 5 Biggest Cardinals Storylines Entering Week 7
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 heading into Week 7 with plenty of chatter around the organization.
It's the middle of October and there are rumors galore — what's real, and what's not after six weeks of football?
Playing buy or sell with some major talking points around the desert:
Why we're buying it: Brissett continues to be heralded in the eyes of Mike LaFleur, and orchestrating a game-winning drive against the Rams only did Brissett more favors despite another very average performance. After another upset win, the Cardinals now have less pressure to make changes, which will start at quarterback whenever that time comes. It just won't be next week.
Why we're selling it: Rallis' defense looked renewed on Sunday after dialing up the pressure, which ultimately saw Arizona play their best defensive ball of the season. However, last Sunday shouldn't completely get Rallis off the hook. If the clock strikes midnight this weekend and Arizona's defense reverts back to a pumpkin against Denver, conversations will again arise on bigger-picture problems.
Why we're selling it: The Cardinals don't have the depth or luxury of time to do this. Yes, Bam Knight looked strong on Sunday, though a backfield of only Knight, Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull isn't inspiring. Love's ankle by no means appears serious, and if that were the case, he would have been placed on injured reserve last week. Love could miss multiple games, but completely ruling him out for four weeks during his rookie season when the Cardinals need him most isn't wise.
Why we're buying it : The Cardinals were justified to not trade Sweat at the beginning of the season. Now, times have changed. The more Sweat reverts back to his old self, the more teams are going to pony up for his services near the trade deadline, when his value will be highest. It's clear Sweat wants a pay raise and fresh start elsewhere, and if the Cardinals can see their top pass rusher continue getting to the quarterback, they might just have their price met.
Why we're buying it: It's a week-to-week league, as the Cardinals have now shown numerous times. Next up for Arizona is Denver, Dallas, Seattle and Los Angeles in the next four weeks. All four of these opponents are extremely beatable at this moment in time. Expected? Very much not, though it's conceivable the Cardinals, after downing the Rams, could walk away winners from multiple matchups within the next month.

title: 3 Cardinals Quietly Having a Strong 2026 Season
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 to start the 2026 season — which isn't something to write home about, though it's on par with what many were realistically expecting out of Mike LaFleur's first season in charge.
Stars are beginning to shine in the desert, though there's three Cardinals who are quietly building strong campaigns for Arizona:
So many were disappointed by Robinson's first two seasons in the league, and criticisms surrounding the former first-round pick were fair entering 2026. Robinson had lived nowhere near the level of hype that came with his arrival in 2024, and time was running out for his development to show on the field.
Robinson's steadily improved, and has gotten after the quarterback at much better rates — which might not be saying much compared to his prior outputs  — but we demanded improvement, and Robinson has done just that.
Robinson is tied with Josh Sweat with the team lead in pressures (7) with four quarterback knockdowns. He has 14 tackles and one sack through six games.
He may never live up to the billing of a first-round pick, though Robinson is building himself into a piece Arizona wants to stick around beyond his rookie deal.
Lopez made his return to the desert after a short stint with the Detroit Lions last season, though the Cardinals re-signed him in free agency hoping to revamp their defensive line alongside fellow free agent addition Andrew Billings.
Billings has mostly been inactive, though Lopez has managed to make a legitimate impact for Arizona in the trenches, totaling 20 tackles (3 for loss) with one sack and one pass batted down as well.
The Cardinals have struggled to stop the run in recent years. Lopez has been an energetic and effective presence for Arizona, one that's fair to call underrated.
Trey McBride commands most of the respect in Arizona's tight end room and overall offense. Rightfully so.
However, Elijah Higgins plays a massive role as the Cardinals' TE2. In an offense that uses plenty of multi-TE sets, especially 13 personnel, Higgins has carved out a strong role for himself to help his team far more than a typical backup tight end.
Higgins has caught all 11 targets thrown at him for 124 yards and one touchdown on the season. Perhaps equally as important, he's molded himself into a viable run-blocking tight end for Mike LaFleur to deploy as well.

title: Former Falcons Defender Could Join 49ers Ahead of Week 7 Matchup
full_text:
Former Atlanta Falcons linebacker Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster.
The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following some injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta.
San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. He spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons.
Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie.
Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of the regular season during his first two years with the organization.
The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026, but failed to make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September.
Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure.
The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later.
Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay.
For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender.
Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two.
Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen.

title: Falcons Release DB as A.J. Terrell's Return Gets Closer
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have released cornerback Malcolm DeWalt IV, potentially creating an opportunity for the team to adjust its secondary ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.
DeWalt entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft. Although he did not arrive with the same recognition as some of his fellow rookies, the 24-year-old quickly caught Atlanta’s attention with his athleticism, length and potential to develop into a dependable defensive back.
Standing 6’2 and weighing 190 pounds, DeWalt possesses the physical tools teams look for in an outside cornerback. His collegiate career included stops at Snow College, Butte College and Akron, where he continued developing his coverage skills before getting his opportunity at the professional level.
DeWalt made the most of that opportunity during the offseason. He impressed during rookie minicamp and carried that momentum into training camp and the preseason, earning a spot on Atlanta’s initial 53-man roster.
However, DeWalt did not record any defensive statistics during the 2026 regular season. His release could mean another roster change for a Falcons team
The timing of DeWalt’s release is particularly noteworthy because Atlanta is working toward getting its top cornerback back on the field.
The Falcons designated A.J. Terrell to return from injured reserve on Wednesday, opening a 21-day window for the veteran to practice and potentially return to game action. Terrell has missed the previous four games with a groin injury suffered against the Carolina Panthers in Week 2.
His potential return against San Francisco would provide a significant boost to a secondary that has dealt with injuries at cornerback. C.J. Henderson has also been sidelined, forcing Atlanta to rely on younger options, including Avieon Terrell.
Although the Falcons have not confirmed that DeWalt’s release is directly connected to A.J. Terrell’s possible return, the timing makes it a reasonable possibility as the team evaluates its roster needs.
Atlanta could also bring DeWalt back to its practice squad if he clears waivers. That would allow the organization to continue developing a young cornerback who showed promise throughout the offseason without immediately occupying a spot on the active roster.
For DeWalt, the release does not necessarily mean his time with Atlanta is over. For the Falcons, the move could provide additional flexibility as they prepare for San Francisco and work to strengthen their secondary for the remainder of the season.

title: Brock Purdy Has a Skill That Could Give Falcons Fits
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – One week after struggling against Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears' passing attack, the Atlanta Falcons face another difficult test Sunday against Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers.
Kyle Shanahan is widely regarded as one of the NFL's great offensive minds, and he deserves a lot of praise, but his quarterback does, too. Brock Purdy has been outstanding this season, throwing for 1,460 yards and 14 touchdowns to just two interceptions. Of the quarterbacks who have played six games this season, none have a better completion percentage (69.6%), passer rating (118.1), or EPA per dropback (+0.30).
Purdy thrives on quick processing, accuracy, and consistently making the right decision within Shanahan's offense.
That might not generate the same national buzz as the highlight-reel plays of some of the league's other star quarterbacks, but the results are hard to argue with. The Falcons know where San Francisco's offense starts: with its quarterback.
"He's a very, very special quarterback," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. "I haven't studied the rest of the league – and I'm watching a lot of his tape right now, but it's hard to imagine someone who is playing the position better than he is right now."
Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson can overwhelm defenses with their physical gifts, while Patrick Mahomes can turn broken plays into something extraordinary. Purdy has the traits that a Shanahan offense values most.
"He's an elite processor. You see how quickly he gets through his progressions," Stefanski explained. "He has elite accuracy. And I think he's an elite scrambler. I think he's the best or one of the best off-schedule quarterbacks playing right now.
"You watch him – he's a smart scrambler. He's looking to pass. And then when he runs, he can score from 50 yards out, as he's done. So just very, very smart. Hard to get on the ground. This is a great player."
After being picked apart by Caleb Williams and the Bears , Atlanta's secondary faces another major test against Purdy.
The potential return of veteran cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson would provide a welcome boost. Still, the Falcons will need more than healthier personnel to slow an offense built on quick decisions, accurate throws, and the ability to punish defenses when coverage breaks down.
If the Falcons’ secondary returns to health and the front seven can consistently pressure Purdy’s quick release, they can slow this potent offense. If Sunday looks anything like last week against Chicago, with coverage breakdowns and a clean pocket, Shanahan will make them pay for every mistake. Purdy doesn’t need many.

title: Jahan Dotson Making His Case for Bigger Role in Falcons Offense
full_text:
Jahan Dotson is quietly emerging as a reliable weapon in the Atlanta Falcons ' passing game, and his recent production suggests he could be in line for a bigger role as the season progresses.
Dotson delivered one of his most productive performances of the season Sunday, catching three passes for a team-high 87 yards and a touchdown. The 87-yard performance marked the fourth-highest receiving total of his five-year career, highlighting the big-play ability he has brought to Atlanta's offense.
More importantly, Sunday's performance was not an isolated showing. Dotson has recorded at least 50 receiving yards in each of the last three weeks, making him one of just seven NFL players to reach that mark in every game during that stretch through the early afternoon slate of Week 6.
His recent consistency is particularly encouraging considering his relatively modest target volume. According to Next Gen Stats , Dotson owns a 14.2% target share, the third-highest mark among Falcons receivers, while his 34.6% air yards share ranks second on the team and among the top 20 players in the NFL.
Those numbers show Dotson is making the most of his opportunities while serving as an important downfield option for Atlanta. Although he has not received the same volume of targets as some of the team's other playmakers, his ability to generate yardage has helped him establish a place in the passing game.
Following the Falcons' game against Pittsburgh, Dotson said he spoke with former Atlanta quarterback Matt Ryan. Dotson also explained that his approach remains centered on doing his job.
"For me, it's about getting open and being available to the quarterback. Whether I'm getting the ball or not," Dotson said.
That mentality has allowed Dotson to remain productive without needing a high volume of targets. His recent performances have also showcased the confidence he has in his ability to make difficult catches.
His back shoulder touchdown reception on Sunday was a prime example.
Jahan Dotson WHAT A CATCH CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bl2VvmwJmQ
"I have always had this in his bag," Dotson said, referring to the back shoulder catch. He also recalled the challenge of proving that ability on the field. "He had to go out and show them," Dotson said.
While the touchdown added to his recent scoring production, Dotson made it clear that he values consistent yardage just as much as finding the end zone.
"I'm a big yards guy. Touchdowns are cool. But I like yards," Dotson said.
For Atlanta, that approach could be particularly valuable as the offense looks for more consistent production from its supporting receivers.
Dotson still has to sustain his production to earn a more prominent role, but his recent numbers make a strong case for continued involvement. If he maintains his current trajectory, the Falcons could have another dependable receiving option capable of taking pressure off their top targets.

title: Kevin Stefanski Gives Simple Answer on Atlanta Falcons OL Play
full_text:
Like much of the Atlanta Falcons ' season, the offensive line play for the team has been inconsistent. They looked like world-beaters against the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints, and then they were bullied by the Baltimore Ravens and overwhelmed by the Chicago Bears.
So much of what Atlanta wants to do starts up front, and they've invested heavily in the unit with both draft picks and contracts. The Falcons have the eighth-highest cap hit on the offensive line in the NFL, according to Spotrac .
So, if they're struggling, there are big concerns with the team. Head coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about the overall play of the offensive line on Wednesday, and his answer was clear.
“They’re playing 2-4. I’m coaching 2-4," Stefanski said. "It’s hard to give grand observations on any position right now because I just think you have to just focus on where you are. So, I can tell you how they're working. They're working very hard. I like those guys, but there's plenty of improvement to be made.”
In short, yes, they can play better, but he's not going to single out a unit when time are tough. At 2-4, times are tough. Bedrock offensive tackle Jake Matthews is having his worst season. He had a groin injury and missed most of the New Orleans game, but he hasn't missed any time since. Stefanski assured us Matthews is healthy.
The Falcons face former head coach Raheem Morris as the San Francisco 49ers this week. Morris is going to see how successful the Bears were with their blitz packages, and quarterback Michael Penix Jr. can expect to see plenty of heat again, until the offense figures out how to make defenses pay for being so aggressive.
"When it comes to protection, it very simply can be technique," Stefanski said about dealing with the blitz. "It very simply can be the protections that we're calling. It can be, it goes without saying, staying out of those down and distances. It's a simple thing to say, ‘Hey, we want to be better,’ but it's complicated in how you want to achieve that. But our players, our coaches understand in these given games, teams, when they pressure you, there can be an advantage to the offense as well.”
A blitz is typically a high-risk, high-reward type of play, and the Falcons need to make teams feel the risk side of that equation more frequently than the reward.
The offensive line controlling a good 49ers front will be important in this game. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has his team playing well offensively. The Falcons get a break that long-time nemesis Mike Evans is unavailable. However, the Falcons are beat up at linebacker , and the 49ers have a litany of weapons who attack the second level: running back Christian McCaffrey, tight end George Kittle, and wide receiver Deebo Samuel.
The Bears played keepaway with the Falcons last week. They held a 2-1 time-of-possession advantage. The Falcons' offensive line will need to turn the tables this week if the Falcons are to pull off the upset on the 6-0 49ers.

title: Falcons LB Kendal Daniels Opens Up About Scary Injury
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels returned to full participation in practice Wednesday after suffering a frightening neck injury against the Chicago Bears , providing an encouraging update as the team prepares for Sunday’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.
Daniels was carted off the field during Atlanta’s 31-23 loss to Chicago after a collision left him experiencing neck pain. Now back on the practice field, the rookie is hopeful he can play Sunday, although his final status will depend on the team’s medical evaluation.
“Yeah, it was a scary play. I’m blessed to come out how I did, and it was a bad play, but I’m happy I’m here,” Daniels said.
The injury was a concerning moment for Atlanta, but Daniels’ return to practice represents a significant step forward just days after he required emergency medical attention.
Daniels was injured while attempting to tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland on a screen pass. During the play, Daniels’ facemask collided with Loveland’s knee, causing the linebacker to experience pain in his neck.
“The screen came down. It was the top of my head. It was a pain in my neck, and I just took a knee,” Daniels said.
The rookie initially attempted to get back up but decided against it when the pain persisted.
“Yeah, I tried to get up, but my neck was hurting, so I just went back down and decided to wait till the trainers got over there,” Daniels said.
Medical personnel immobilized his neck and transported him off the field on a stretcher. Daniels was subsequently taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation.
Despite the frightening scene, Daniels said he never lost consciousness and could feel his hands and feet. Medical personnel evaluated his condition at the hospital before he returned to the stadium later that evening.
Daniels also explained that he focused on following instructions from teammate Chris Lindstrom, who told him to remain still while medical personnel assessed him.
“I was just trying to figure out what was going on,” Daniels said.
After reviewing the play, Daniels identified what he needs to correct moving forward.
“I just got to get my head across. Can’t hit with the top of my head,” Daniels said.
The linebacker acknowledged the importance of improving his technique while expressing gratitude that the injury did not result in a more serious outcome.
Daniels’ full participation in Wednesday’s practice is an encouraging sign for the Falcons, but it does not guarantee he will be available against San Francisco.
When asked about the possibility of playing Sunday, Daniels remained optimistic while emphasizing that he would follow the guidance of the medical staff.
“Yeah, for sure. It could be. Just listening to Jake and all those guys and just waiting on what they say,” Daniels said.
Daniels entered Sunday’s game with 22 tackles and one sack after starting Atlanta’s first six games. His potential availability would provide a boost to a defense preparing for an undefeated 49ers team. Fellow starting linebacker Divine Deablo didn't practice on Wednesday. He suffered an arm injury against the Bears.
The Falcons signed TJ Quinn this week to the practice squad as insurance.
For now, Daniels has made meaningful progress since the frightening incident against Chicago. His full participation on Wednesday gives Atlanta reason for optimism, but his final status will depend on the team’s evaluation of his neck injury throughout the week.

title: Falcons Bijan Robinson Shares What He Learned From 49ers Christian McCaffrey
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has embraced his role as the centerpiece of Atlanta's offense, and his respect for San Francisco 49ers star Christian McCaffrey stems partly from their similar responsibilities.
The Falcons face the undefeated 49ers on Sunday, giving Robinson an opportunity to compete against a running back he spent a month working out with during the summer of 2025. Both players are trusted to carry the football, contribute as receivers and handle significant responsibilities within their respective offenses.
Robinson recently offered insight into his willingness to shoulder a heavy workload when discussing how he plays Madden.
"I play Madden how I would run the football in real life," Robinson said. "And people don't like playing Madden against me just because I'm gonna run it like 50 times. But it's just, you just can't stop it in the game."
While Robinson's actual workload depends on Atlanta's offensive game plan, this shows his confidence in carrying the ball repeatedly. Through six games in the 2026 season, Robinson has recorded 111 carries for 641 rushing yards, averaging 5.8 yards per attempt. He has also caught 20 passes for 144 yards and a touchdown.
His ability to contribute in multiple phases gives Atlanta flexibility in how it uses him. Whether running between the tackles, creating explosive plays outside or catching passes, Robinson remains a central component of the Falcons' offensive identity.
McCaffrey fills a comparable role in San Francisco, where his versatility allows the 49ers to keep him involved throughout games.
Through six games in 2026, McCaffrey has recorded 77 carries for 350 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns. He has also caught 28 passes for 190 yards, demonstrating his importance as both a runner and a receiving option.
Robinson has generated more rushing yards, while McCaffrey has scored more frequently. Both players give their teams versatile weapons capable of challenging defenses in different ways.
Robinson's willingness to embrace a heavy workload mirrors the importance McCaffrey holds within San Francisco's offense. Their ability to handle repeated touches while remaining dangerous in the passing game makes them difficult players to account for over four quarters.
Robinson spent a month working out with McCaffrey in California during the summer of 2025, allowing the two running backs to exchange knowledge and observe each other's preparation.
"He's very detailed in his work ethic and probably how he goes about his business," Robinson said to Terrin Waack.
"He's the ultimate competitor. You see he likes to be in the game as much as possible to make an impact as much as possible," Robinson added.
Robinson also praised McCaffrey's recovery routine, highlighting the importance of taking care of his body while preparing for the demands of an NFL season.
That lesson becomes especially relevant when considering the responsibilities both players carry for their teams. Maintaining effectiveness while handling substantial workloads requires preparation and consistency throughout the season.
Atlanta will need Robinson to be productive against a San Francisco team that has won every game entering the matchup. Establishing the run and finding ways to involve Robinson as a receiver could help the Falcons control the tempo.
Robinson understands the challenge ahead and emphasized the importance of execution.
"We have to match the urgency and we have to, for one play at a time, play at the highest level," Robinson said.
Against McCaffrey and the 49ers, Robinson will have an opportunity to demonstrate why he is such an important part of Atlanta's plans while facing a player whose preparation and competitive mentality he admires.

The Atlanta Falcons ’ 2026 season has seen drastic ups and downs. The highs include two lopsided wins, but the lows have left fans scratching their heads.
The last two weeks have been particularly frustrating, with inconsistent performances holding this team back. Against the Ravens, the Falcons went flat in the fourth quarter and overtime after controlling the first three quarters. The opposite happened against the Bears, but both games ended in losses.
Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and the secondary struggled through most of the game, but they turned it around late to keep it close. Ultimately, the 31-7 fourth-quarter deficit proved too much to overcome.
Sunday brings a new challenge as the undefeated San Francisco 49ers head to Atlanta. If the Falcons want to get back on track, they will need a lot of things to get back on track, and quickly.
Elsewhere in the division, the Panthers topped a beat-up Eagles squad, the Buccaneers lost to the Steelers, and the Saints snapped a three-game losing streak with a win over the Giants. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. See below where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
Upcoming Opponent ( 49ers )
A common theme in these power rankings is criticism of quarterback play when pressure gets to Michael Penix Jr. Conor Orr joined them in highlighting the Falcons’ inability to handle the Bears’ pressure, saying they'll see a lot of this until they find a way to respond.
Elsewhere in the South, SI ranks the Panthers No. 13 (up seven spots), the Saints No. 25 (no change), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down three spots). Orr has the 49ers at No. 1.

Marc Raimondi noted how much this offense has struggled when Michael Penix Jr. faces pressure, citing his seventh-worst EPA/dropback and the second-worst completion percentage in those situations. The Bears sacked Penix five times on Sunday, and this will remain an issue until the quarterback finds his footing with defenses coming after him.

title: A.J. Terrell Jr. Takes Major Step Toward Return to Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are potentially getting a major boost to their secondary, as cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. will practice Wednesday after spending the previous four games on injured reserve with a groin injury.
Terrell suffered the injury early in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Carolina Panthers, forcing him to miss several games during a critical stretch of the season. His return to practice gives the Falcons hope that one of their top defensive players could be available for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.
Terrell's return to practice also opens a 21-day window for Atlanta to activate him to its 53-man roster. The Falcons must make that move before the window expires. Otherwise, Terrell will revert to injured reserve and miss the remainder of the season.
Getting Terrell back would be a significant development for an Atlanta defense that has dealt with multiple injuries in its secondary over the past several weeks.
In Terrell's absence, C.J. Henderson stepped into the starting lineup at outside cornerback opposite Mike Hughes. Henderson provided Atlanta with another option on the outside before suffering his own groin injury in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens.
With Henderson unavailable for the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Chicago Bears, rookie Avieon Terrell, A.J.'s brother, stepped into a starting role at outside cornerback. Billy Bowman Jr. handled slot cornerback responsibilities.
However, Bowman exited the loss to Chicago early with an injury, leaving his availability for Week 7 uncertain. His status will be worth monitoring throughout the week as Atlanta prepares for a difficult matchup against San Francisco.
The injuries have forced the Falcons to adjust their secondary and rely on younger players to handle expanded responsibilities. Terrell's return would provide valuable experience and stability to a defensive backfield that has been forced to navigate several personnel changes.
The timing of Terrell's return to practice could not be much better for Atlanta. The Falcons are preparing to face an undefeated San Francisco team that presents a significant challenge on both sides of the ball.
Terrell has established himself as one of Atlanta's most important defensive players, and his presence would give the coaching staff another experienced option to deploy against the 49ers' passing attack.
Still, Wednesday's practice is only the first step toward a potential return. The Falcons will need to evaluate how Terrell responds as he works his way back from the groin injury before determining whether he is ready to play.
For now, the Falcons will continue monitoring the health of their defensive backs while hoping Terrell's return marks the beginning of a healthier stretch for the unit.

title: Falcons' Mike Hughes Struggles as Secondary Needs Reinforcements
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons were on the back foot from the opening kick on Sunday, quickly falling behind the Bears 14-0. The deficit quickly ballooned to 31-7 by the fourth and ultimately proved too much for the Falcons to overcome, despite their improbable late surge.
Plenty of blame goes around for Sunday’s woeful performance, but the secondary must find its footing, and fast.
Caleb Williams’ hamstring looked fine after missing the last several weeks, and the Bears’ quarterback made the Falcons look like the one that needed to shake off the rust.
Williams completed his first 12 passes and went 24-of-24 for 248 yards when he didn’t face pressure (the most attempts without an incompletion from a clean pocket since at least 2018, according to Next Gen Stats ). He finished his day 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown on his return.
The Falcons' secondary had a tough day, particularly Mike Hughes.
The veteran corner stepped in as the primary boundary corner due to injuries in the secondary and allowed 103 yards and a touchdown (QB rating of 158.3) on six catches (seven targets). Sunday’s performance isn't an isolated incident: Hughes has allowed a league-high 394 yards in coverage this season and is third-worst in the NFL in coverage EPA (+21.4).
He's in a difficult situation, playing out of his usual field position, and Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski reiterated his support for Hughes on Monday.
“We'll work through all those things this week. Obviously, Mike's a vet that we're counting on,” Stefanski said Monday. “These are tough matchups. We can always look at things that we can do better. Certainly, as we design the defense and those types of things, we'll always look at what we can do better. But the bottom line is we expect a lot from our corner position.”
Lately, those performances haven't been good enough, and that is on more than just Hughes.
Over six games, the Falcons have allowed 270 yards or more four times. Even in Week 5, when Atlanta held Baltimore below 270 passing yards, backup Tyler Huntley completed all 11 passes for 80 yards and accounted for two scores on the Ravens' final two drives, fueling a late comeback.
Atlanta has dropped to No. 20 in EPA/pass (-0.02) and No. 28 in passing yards per game allowed (252.0), but reinforcements could be coming soon.
Stefanski confirmed Monday that top cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. is “trending” toward an opened window to return from injured reserve, while his backup, C.J. Henderson, could also return this week after not participating in practices last week.
Both corners suffered groin injuries, with Terrell having missed the last four weeks. Henderson stepped in and played well in Terrell’s absence, earning praise from defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich , but the secondary’s already thin depth was tested when he couldn't play on Sunday.
Terrell's return could provide a much-needed boost, while Henderson would give Atlanta valuable depth at cornerback. With the undefeated 49ers coming to town, however, the Falcons need answers in the secondary quickly.

title: Grading Ravens Defensive Position Groups Through Six Weeks
full_text:
With Week 6 in the rearview and Week 7 on the horizon, the 2026 NFL regular season is a third of the way in the books. The Baltimore Ravens currently find themselves in a three-way tie for the best record in the AFC North at 4-2, and the defense has been a work in progress while still contributing to the team's overall success.
Under new head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter, they came into the season expected to be one of the best units in the league, and while they've dominated entire halves and sometimes three quarters of games, they've yet to put together a full four quarters of excellence.
The talent that general manager Eric DeCosta amassed on the defensive side of the ball has shown flashes of dominance and could round into a strength for this year's team as the offense continues to get healthy and keep being explosive . Here's how each position group has graded out thus far.
Gradual ramp-ups in training camp and delayed regular-season debuts prevented this talented bunch from hitting the ground running. However, over the past two games, they've begun to play up to their immense potential collectively instead of as individuals in spurts. The trio of multi-time Pro Bowlers Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell and budding star Travis Jones gives the Ravens one of the best interiors in the league.
In the four games since Madubuike returned from a serious neck injury that cut his 2025 season short, he looks more and more like his game-wrecking pre-injury form. Campbell remains the ageless wonder and has looked great the past two weeks and Jones as been a stud from the start of the season when it comes to making plays against the run at and behind the line of scrimmage. Behind them, veterans John Jenkins, Broderick Washington and third-year pro Aeneas Peebles have provided solid depth but haven't really stood out in a noticeable or consistent way.
This group has been the most pleasant surprise of the entire defense thus far this season, with how consistently disruptive they've been down in and down out each week, especially at the top of the depth chart. After a down year in 2025 that still saw him get voted to his fourth straight Pro Bowl, veteran Roquan Smith is back to playing at an All Pro level, leading the team with 47 total tackles, tying for the second-most sacks with two and making plays on the ball with an interception, forced fumble and two pass breakups.
At the WILL spot, fourth-year pro Trenton Simpson, is finally putting it all together in a contract year and has been enjoying quite the breakout campaign. He's recorded the third-most total tackles on the team with 41, including tying for the most tackles for loss with six, and he also has an interception to go along with a fumble recovery and a pass breakup. Second-year pros Teddye Buchanan and Jay Higgins have predominantly played special teams, with Buchanan seeing some limited snaps on defense in base personnel packages.
This is another group that has been hindered by health to a degree, with four-time Pro Bowl veteran and prized free agent acquisition Trey Hendrickson sustaining a finger injury that required surgery and caused him to miss two games. Yet in four games, he has still managed to record a pair of sacks, four quarterback hits and a 22.7% pressure rate, the highest rate among defenders with at least 25 pressures this season, according to NextGenStats .
Leading the Ravens with 3.5 sacks through six games is Tavius Robinson, another fourth-year pro making the most of his extended playing time in the final season of his rookie deal. He also leads the team with eight quarterback hits, batted down two passes and forced a fumble. Second-year pro Mike Green is tied with Hendrickson for the second-most sacks on the team with a pair and stepped up in a big way during the two games he was out. He ranks second on the team with six quarterback hits and has been playing the run well with four tackles for loss.
The Ravens also have a pair of rookies who have been playing regularly , with second-rounder Zion Young's snaps coming on defense during early downs while undrafted free agent Ethan Burke has primarily played on special teams but was the first of the two to record a sack.
The Ravens have gotten a mixed bag of results from this position group, with some impressive plays and missed opportunities to make more impactful ones despite constantly being in good position in coverage. They've been playing third-year pro Nate Wiggins and four-time Pro Bowl veteran Marlon Humphrey on the perimeter and deploying both second-year pro Keyon Martin and fifth-round rookie Chandler Rivers at nickel for stretches.
As a group, they've struggled to contain No. 1 wide receivers from both inconsistent and highly efficient passing offenses and haven't been making enough plays on the ball, with no interceptions and just nine pass breakups between them. Wiggins has been the best of the bunch, allowing just a 51.7 % completion rate and an opposing passer rating of 65.7. Neither he nor Humphrey has given up a touchdown this year yet and will need to raise their game even more during the next third of the season with tougher opponents yet to come.
The saving grace keeping this grade from being flat-out 'D' or 'C-' at best is the fact that three-time All Pro Kyle Hamilton is playing like a well-deserving Defensive Player of the Year candidate right now, and second-year pro Malaki Starks has shown signs of improvement over the past couple of weeks. What was being billed as potentially the best trio in the league all summer has fallen well short of expectations to start the season.
Collectively, they have not only failed to consistently come up with big plays in key moments but have also been the main culprits in some very detrimental breakdowns in coverage late in games and on third downs, especially.
Starks appears to be turning a corner, making plays both in coverage and as a forceful player against the run. However, the same can not be said about veteran free agent acquisition Jaylinn Hawkins, who has disappointed thus far. He has no pass breakups, interceptions, tackles for loss or plays on the ball of any kind. He'll need to start turning it around before the Ravens' coaches are forced to find a configuration that works better without him, possibly one that utilizes second-year undrafted gem and special teams ace Keondre Jackson.
Coming into the regular season after a disastrous end to his rookie year and a discouraging performance in the preseason, a lot of eyes were on and remain on second-year placekicker Tyler Loop. He's drilled some impressive kicks in high-leverage situations, including the walk-off winner in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3 to beat the Dallas Cowboys in a thriller and setting a new home-field record for the longest successful attempt. However, he's still struggled with consistency when it comes to making clutch kicks in the second half of games. Both of the Ravens' losses have featured missed kicks by Loop from under 50 yards, and this year, he's 10-of-13 on field goals, with one blocked attempt and two bad misses. The Ravens signed veteran kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad at the onset of the season to give Loop some competition and recently brought him back earlier this week in the wake of his recent struggles.
Rookie punter Ryan Eckley has been the field-flipping weapon that the Ravens envisioned they were getting when they selected him in the sixth round of this year's draft. Half of his punts have pinned the opposing team's offense inside its own 20-yard line; he's averaging 46.9 yards per punt and his longest has been 62 yards. As far as the return game goes, the Ravens haven't gotten much juice from second-year pro LaJohntay Wester, who's returned 10 punts for 91 yards with a long of 24. He's one of three players who have returned kicks, and none have broken one longer than 42 yards (Chris Moore in the season opener.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI…

title: Ravens Injury Report Reveals Major Development For Lamar Jackson
full_text:
Baltimore Ravens two-time MVP Lamar Jackson continues to make tangible signs of progress in his return from a two-week absence.
On Thursday, for the first time since suffering an ankle injury late in the first half in Week 4, Jackson was with the team for the start of practice, and he was moving quite well . Even better than on the video that emerged of him Wednesday taking part in what head coach Jesse Minter refereed to as a “little” bit of limited work in that session. Jackson was interacting with teammates in an overt manner Thursday that certainly gave the appearance of the starting quarterback preparing to be back at the helm. Seemed to be a spring in his step.
Minter, like all NFL coaches, does not meet with the media on Thursday and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle spoke prior to the practice session. The Ravens listed Jackson as limited at practice on Wednesday and gave him a limited designation on Thursday. The final injury report will be revealed on Friday, but this is clearly multiple days of progress after none for weeks.
This much is obvious – Minter is virtually certain not to come out tomorrow and rule Jackson out as he did the previous two Fridays. Jackson has finally made significant progress from the injury after Minter referred to it as “day-to-day” for over two weeks and Jackson will continue to get treatment and test the ankle out through the weekend. Barring a setback, based on over 20 years of covering this stuff, it certainly looks to me like the Ravens are preparing for Jackson to return for a vital AFC North game against the Bengals to open what is a difficult middle stretch of the schedule.
It also would not be surprising in the least to see Jackson, and not Huntley, meeting with the media on Friday, which would be another obvious indication of where this is going. We originally circled Week 7 as the first team return date as we gathered information on Jackson’s original injury, and were a little alarmed when Minter spoke so cryptically about the star’s potential return on Monday.
If indeed this is Jackson’s return, it comes at the ideal time. Back-up Snoop Huntley is very limited in how he can attack a defense and Jackson’s absence was also becoming a drain on the run game as opponents did not have to concern themselves with defending Huntley’s legs much. A suspect offensive line was also an issue and new center Cam Jurgens is practicing fully and on track to make his Ravens debut Sunday. (The possibility for other trades does still exist ).
Jackson is 11-2 vs the Bengals in his career and 7-2 against them when Joe Burrow starts. The Ravens average 29 points per game against Cincy with Jackson at the helm – the Bengals defensive line is markedly improved this season  – and he averages over 220 rushing yards and 64 rushing yards.
Jackson has 837 rushing yards in his career against the Bengals, the most any QB has against any team in NFL history. A lot of that was when coordinator Lou Anarumo was at the helm (Jackson carved him up in Indianapolis in Week 1 – but the Bengals still have major issues defending outside runs and their linebackers tend to struggle with tackling; areas Jackson can exploit.

title: One Ravens Player Who Could Surprisingly Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens have already made their trade deadline splash.
Giving up a ransom for an offensive lineman with a deep injury, while still in concussion protocol, and taking on $17M a year in salary a few weeks back drew criticism around the NFL for Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta. And as we have explained, for a team already running a franchise-record payroll and with the least cap space in the NFL, the options for further moves are limited.
Unless, of course they shed significant salary and cap in a transaction that then allows them to add elsewhere in a more meaningful way. It’s complicated for sure, and, most likely, DeCosta maybe tries to pick up a veteran kicker on the cheap (as always we know who they would be looking at ), but the Cam Jurgens trade was certainly a shocker, so maybe team president Sashi Brown and DeCosta have more tricks up their sleeve.
And, assuming they are getting a little heathier at a certain position, and if things don’t improve with certain highly-paid players soon, maybe they could manage to sell and buy something else significant in what could be two-time MVP Lamar Jackson’s final season here and before an inevitable purge of longtime starters that will be coming in 2027.
So, who do we have in mind?
DeCosta is cornerback Marlon Humphrey’s No. 1 fan. He gushed about him before the season started, justifying his $19.3M in total compensation in the final year of his deal (10th among all NFL corners) and how he would bounce back in a big way. Yeah, well, he’s a decent enough player but the Ravens corners still don’t make plays on the ball and their corners and safeties don’t have a pick all season despite being thrown all as much as anyone.
Humphrey, a man-coverage guy for the most part, spoke about how he was “garbage” at times in the preseason and the Ravens are always talking up TJ Tampa, and that oft-injured corner is working his way back from Injured Reserve. Maybe Humphrey moves to the slot and they get better there – the slot has been the abyss and Ja’Marr Chase might be able to go off there Sunday – but if not, even with the corner play being suspect, moving this contract could open up significant wiggle room.
When Humphrey has wanted the other team's best receiver this season, it has not gone well.
With Baltimore less than $3M under the cap, not having many ideal restructure candidates and still needing space to cover additions along the way due to injury and otherwise, including Humphrey in a package would make sense.
Humphrey has been a Pro Bowl performer in the past, going through a walk year doesn’t always bring out the best (especially when you have spent your entire career in one place), and there is always an acute need around the league and people willing to take risks (like DeCosta with Jaire Alexander not that long ago!).
By the deadline, Humphrey will basically be owed $7.7M for the second half of the season, and would save that much in cap if dealt. It’s a lot of money to be sure, but the Ravens already paid him $4M in the offseason in a bonus and if they believe as much in rookie head coach Jesse Minter’s scheme as they should, and believe in their youth at this position (and maybe if they ate a few million of Humphrey’s deal to save $5M) they could have the ability to maneuver in a more meaningful way at the deadline.
If they want to win a Super Bowl, they need to be creative and keep an open mind. There are plenty of Ravens not playing to their contract, but most are untradable; Minter didn’t need a $19M corner to have a top three pass defense with his zone schemes with the Chargers, and this could be addition by subtraction in numerous ways.
Minter knows the Chargers corners incredibly well, and knows how they fit the scheme, and LA is 0-6 and will make trades and shed salary. They wouldn't want Humphrey but the Ravens clearing his salary and opening up a starting spot at corner would seem to make a lot of sense (and personnel guys have expressed as much to me), moving Marlon as a precursor to bringing another corner in.
I seem to recall the Ravens and Chargers making a trade a year ago at this time that worked out damn well for Minter when he got Odafe Oweh (and didn't do much of anything for the Ravens at all).
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Grading Ravens Offensive Position Groups Through Six Weeks
full_text:
With Week 6 in the rearview and Week 7 on the horizon, the 2026 NFL regular season is a third of the way in the books. The Baltimore Ravens currently find themselves in a three-way tie for the best record in the AFC North at 4-2, and the offense has been a major catalyst for the team's overall success.
Under new offensive coordinator and first-time play-caller Declan Doyle, they've fielded one of the most explosive and innovative units in the league, although the overall health of the roster has been an issue and kept them from performing at a high level in all four quarters in most of their games.
The talent that general manager Eric DeCosta amassed on the offensive side of the ball has shown flashes of brilliance and dominance and could be the driving force for this year's team as the defense continues to round into shape. Here's how each position group has graded out thus far.
As with several other position groups on this team, health is the only obstacle keeping the Ravens' most gifted signal-caller from helping the offense reach its full potential. The differences in explosiveness, efficiency, and overall production with and without Lamar Jackson are beyond stark.
In the 14 quarters with the two-time league MVP under center, the Ravens have scored 116 points, 14 touchdowns, 967 passing yards and 1,464 total yards. He suffered an ankle sprain midway through the Ravens' Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans and in the 10 quarters without him, they've only mustered a third of those figures with 40 points, four touchdowns, 429 passing yards and 742 total yards. Jackson was playing at an MVP level before he went down and has more than enough time to catch up with Brock Purdy and Josh Allen and emerge as a frontrunner down the stretch.
While the Ravens rank second in the league in rushing yards and they've eclipsed 100 yards on the ground in all but one game, this position group has been more than solid but not spectacular. Five-time Pro Bowler Derrick Henry leads the team in rushing by a mile with 534 yards, which ranks fourth in the league. He's only had two 100-plus-rushing-yard performances and is coming off his least productive game, where he was held to a season-low 58 yards and committed a costly fumble in the fourth quarter.
Fellow veteran Justice Hill has been a nice change-of-pace option, averaging 7.4 yards per rush and is still excelling in his primary pass-catching-and-blocking role. Third-year pro Rasheen Ali has yet to play a single snap on offense but has been a staple on special teams, covering and returning kicks.
Given Doyle's background as a former tight ends coach, there were heightened expectations for this remodeled bunch coming into the season. Injuries have impacted this group as well, with veteran blocking specialist Durham Smythe suffering a season-ending torn Achilles and both three-time Pro Bowler Mark Andrews and fourth-round rookie Matt Hibner sustaining minor hand injuries. Andrews has struggled with drops and had a slow start to the season with 23 catches on 33 targets for 181 receiving yards and one touchdown, while Hibner and fellow rookie Josh Cuevas have shown some promising flashes and have combined to record 12 catches on 13 targets for 154 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
This is yet another group that's been hit hard by the injury bug, with two-time Pro Bowler Zay Flowers missing a game and a half and being hampered in another with a hamstring strain. Standout third-round rookie Ja'Kobi Lane had his debut cut short in Week 1 with a fractured wrist that kept him out until this past Sunday, but he's looked good when healthy with five catches on eight targets for 51 receiving yards and four first downs.
Veteran Rashod Bateman has been a reliable chain-mover and stepped up when Flowers was hobbled and out of commission, but he is dealing with a nagging shoulder injury. Third-year pro Devontez Walker leads the team with 18.8 receiving yards per catch and has recorded four catches for 75 receiving yards and a touchdown. Fourth-round rookie Elijah Sarratt has been a regular healthy scratch and has recorded one catch on two targets for 13 yards and a first down.
No position group has been hit harder by injury than this group, dating back to the summer when they lost projected starting center Danny Pinter for the year in a joint training camp practice. They lost their next two top centers in the same game in Week 3 and were forced to slide stud rookie right guard over the past three weeks and have had to play third-stringer Emory Jones in his spot the past two weeks. All that shuffling prompted DeCosta to make the bold move to trade for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles. Two-time Pro Bowl left tackle Ronnie Stanley missed a game with a toe injury, and this Sunday will mark their fifth different starting configuration this season.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Ravens-Bengals Matchups: Any Reason To Think Ja'Marr Chase Won't Feast Again?
full_text:
The Ravens have a number one problem with No. 1 wide receivers.
Even by the lowest of standards in terms of what a “No. 1 WR” really is they have it bad. Rookie Carnell Tate (Titans) was at his best against them and true proven go-to guys like Drake London (Falcons) and George Pickens (Cowboys) and CeeDee Lamb (Cowboys) and Chris Olave (Saints) ate them up. And many of them were relying on a suspect quarterback to get the ball and not Joe Burrow, who leads the NFL in completion percentage and can operate at the highest levels.
And Burrow is never more at his best than when he is feeding his top target, Ja’Marr Chase, and Chase has never been better throughout his career than when he faces the Ravens. And this edition of Baltimore’s secondary is having all kinds of issues in the second half of games and on third down and especially making any sort of dynamic plays on the football. And they can’t slow down the main cogs in any functional passing attack.
So, yeah, Sunday is going to be a quite a challenge for rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who has done a fine enough job overall but has been getting worked as a defensive coordinator in the second half of games, and who might just need his cornerback-obsessed general manager to go try to find him one before the trade deadline because his corners and safeties are getting picked apart in coverage on third-and-long when the opposition is desperate to make a play downfield (just happened again in Cleveland Sunday).
They best come correct this weekend hosting the Bengals who are coming off a bye with a QB who usually doesn’t really heat up until mid October.
“It is a work in progress,” Minter said of his defense after Wednesday’s practice. “I do see improvement, and I do appreciate the way the guys are chasing improvement. I think there's just a level that we can get to from a pure confidence and conviction standpoint in what we're doing that you can play things aggressively, that you can anticipate things that are about to happen, that when things happen on the fly, the adjustments and things like that happen in real time.
“We're getting closer and closer to that. So, to the guys' credit, they're working at it. Again, it's six games in. Let's try to keep climbing and keep getting better and better, so that we're at our best as we keep going."
They better a lot closer to their best on Sunday. Chase is uniquely equipped to exploit their weaknesses and the soft spots in this zone defense and he’s been torching these defensive backs his entire career.
In case you haven’t been paying attention to what Chase does to these guys, I’ll refresh your memory. He has 1204 yards in 10 career games, that is the most by any player against any opponent in NFL history over at least 10 games. Let that sink in.
Chase is already fourth all-time in receiving yards against the Ravens, a franchise prided on its defense for a generation, behind only Jimmy Smith, Hines Ward and Chad Ochocinco. Chase already has three games of 190 yards or more against Baltimore, that is the most such games any person has against any team in the history of this league.
“It starts with Burrow,” defensive lineman Calais Campbell said, “he's a general out there. He knows how to check all the right plays and check into the right runs based off how people play them. And you have to give the attention to the receivers. They are the best in the game. Chase is probably No. 1, or arguably the best receiver in the game, and then you have Tee Higgins who's Top 10 at the worst; he's a really elite receiver as well.”
Chase is being used a little differently this season, as even more of a deep ball guy and little less moving the chains in the slot.
But that could change Sunday given how atrocious the Ravens have been defending the slot (more on that in a minute). His YAC per reception is at just 2.7 this season (5.7/catch in his career), but Chase has his second-best Expected Points Added/Target of his career (0.47) and is over 9 air yards per target (second-best) with elite route depth, too.
The EPA is still up there even though he is getting just seven targets per game thus far because his explosive play rate is soaring (over 18%) and Burrow is going to tight end Mike Gesicki more to keep things moving in the slot.
Ravens corners and safeties do not have an interception on the season (Kyle Hamilton’s came as a linebacker) they only have about a half-dozen pass breakups combined and none of them has had much success against this receiver. Chase is a size speed monster, he can run through defenders like a running back, and with how shaky the Ravens deep safeties have been, just putting a top over him likely won’t be enough.
Chase has been in the slot less than a quarter of the time this season, but given Baltimore’s film I bet that changes Sunday. As we have been chronicling in depth , young slot corners Keyon Martin and Chandler Rivers, who couldn’t handle Chase’s size and power, both have an opposing passer rating of 119 when thrown on in the slot. Overall, here’s where Baltimore’s slot defense ranks:
Passer Rating: 117.7 (27th) Comp %: 74.1% (26th)    Y ards: 510 (27th) Yds/Att: 8.8 (23rd)
Gesicki will need attention in the slot, too. Baltimore has faced the fewest passing attempts to TEs in the NFL per game, but is allowing a 121.5 rating when they are targeted (26th). Gesicki in the slot this season has 11 catches on 14 targets at 14.3 yards/catch(!) with three touchdowns.
Baltimore really needs starting QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) back for this game to likely keep pace with the Bengals, but that is anything but a sure thing. Minter better be ready to mix and catch corners and he needs a huge revenge game out of former Bengal pass rusher Trey Hendrickson, because it’s hard to fancy his defensive backs against this group.
And if nothing else, probably see what Nate Wiggins can do. In four games against the Bengals Wiggins has allowed just 13 completions on 28 attempts for a 62.5 passer rating, no TDs and just two plays over 20 yards.
