title: What The Ravens Can Realistically Afford At The NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens are pretty much all-in on 2026 as it stands.
Expecting much at this trade deadline, after general manager Eric DeCosta already overpaid for an expensive center w ho hasn’t even suited up for them yet, is fool’s gold. There are numerous indicators and market forces that are signaling this is about as good as it’s going to get from a roster standpoint, though there is potential to add a low-money item.
With a fungible salary cap and a motivated owner, there is always a way. The question, of course, is, with nearly $370M invested in this payroll already (top five in the NFL and way higher than Steve Bisciotti ever goes), and having just picked up a center making $17M a year who is a substantial injury risk, how much further he’s willing to go?
And the Ravens are already in a far more extreme cap bind than most teams. And DeCosta has already started mortgaging future drafts and he covets nothing more than draft lottery tickets and he’s going to have massive holes to fill on this roster in 2027, so the odds of him dealing any more substantial draft capital are slim.
But they also don’t have to sit on their hands entirely.
So the payroll is basically near it’s limit. As for the cap, well, per spotrac.com. they have the least cap space in the NFL , at under $3M. Again, you can create more, but Baltimore’s options are limited.
Most players are already running threadbare base salaries (like the $50M restructure they ran on Lamar Jackson to drop him to the vet minimum because they can never sign him to extension proactively like top front offices do all the time). Or they have big salaries but they aren’t very good anymore – like Roquan Smith and Marlon Humphrey – so you aren’t going to try to extend them or get cute to create additional space.
Nnamdi Madubuike has a salary of over $1M per game, but he also only has one additional year remaining on his contract which cuts down on your ability to prorate when you convert base salary to a bonus and spread over future years. They could play around with Trey Hendickson’s deal (three years remaining) to create a few more million in cap space.
So could they take on half a season of salary/cap for a player making $4M or so without having to do anything too dramatic? Yeah. But not much else unless they are shipping out salary in return in trade and that’s highly unlikely.
The Ravens want you to believe that kicker Tyler Loop is at the root of their issues , after backing him through the entire offseason. And maybe he is. But it also stands to reason that if Jake Moody, currently on the practice squad, gets the gig he is erratic and he is not a proven NFL starter, either.
So could they trade for All-Pro caliber Cameron Dicker from the failing Chargers? Yeah, they could, for the reasons explained here. If that’s too rich for their blood, Joey Slye is having a heck of a year for the Titans, who are tanking, and he is a pending free agent and only makes $2M. Or even Tampa’s Chase McLaughlin, who is making $3.8M this season and is also a pending free agent.
Outside of that, if the cornerback need becomes acute despite all the "talent" there, picking up a young veteran still on his rookie contract – someone they liked out of college who hasn’t broken through with his current team – is about the best they could try to swing. Teams are loathe to give up on such players who are young and cheap and play a premium position and had a quality college pedigree … but we have seen recent first-round pick QBs and WRs dealt, so trust me, DeCosta will be looking at those types of price points.

title: Ravens Head Coach Updates Lamar Jackson's Week 7 Status
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter, just six games into his career, continues to navigate complex injuries across his roster and particularly at quarterback.
To this point in his regime, there have been telltale signs about how this new staff would handle numerous key injuries – especially Lamar Jackson’s, which we told you would be at least two weeks despite rampant speculation to the contrary. And many of those indicators are flashing again this week as Minter tiptoes around Jackson's status once more. Minter has stuck to a “day-to-day” refrain about the two-time MVP, but the ankle situation has obviously been more serious than that.
Jackson did manage to practice Wednesday in a very limited basis, the coach said, ahead of a meeting with the Bengals ( and their new dominant defensive line ), and everything Minter has said and done to this point regarding every medical situation has been very cautious and judicious. The Ravens are also juggling trying to get new center Cam Jurgens – for whom general manager Eric DeCosta paid a prohibitive price – fully vested in a new offense with a new offensive line as he was fully cleared for practice Wednesday after missing two games in concussion protocol.
"Lamar was actually able to ge a little bit of limited work in, in preparation," Minter said Wednesday afternoon. "That's where that’s at … it's a day by day thing … and he was able to get a little bit of work in."
As one who parses words and writes words for a living, that's a lot of "little" in one response, and an "actually" that seems quite telling. Regardless, this was the first time Jackson got back on a field since the injury, although it does not sound like he tested much. Minter indicated it will take a consensus among player and medical team before Jackson starts a game.
"When it's ready for him to be able to play, from both sides," Minter said, "and we feel like that's the best thing to do, then that's what we'll do."
Minter has been very judicious with early-season injuries and while he has claimed for three weeks now that Jackson is day-to-day and gone out of his way indicate each of those weeks that the superstar could play in a game without practicing much that week … only to then rule him out on Friday. Such an outcome again this week would not come as a surprise.
To expect Jackson to return from an injury clearly this impactful, and one that has now wiped out this much practice time, without a full and vigorous practice tomorrow seems like a stretch. Despite calling it "day-to-day" they have been wary of aggravation. Either way, Thursday will be quite telling.
Jackson was performing at an MVP level prior to getting taken down by his lower leg from behind for a sack at the end of the first half of Week 4’s win over the Titans. He left that game, returned to the sidelines, began getting treatment on the sidelines and got an MRI the next day. The situation is complicated by the fact that Jackson is the rarest of elite QB who is playing out what amounts to the final year of his contract, as his 2027 deal has no guarantees and a ridiculous $85M cap charge that the Ravens cannot withstand.
Jackson has more leverage than any player in perhaps NFL history (NFL analyst Domonique Foxworth explained as such on “The Daily Flock Show” ) and top agent Mike McCartney, who negotiated multiple fully-guaranteed deals for Kirk Cousins (Jackson serves as his own agent) suggested Jackson can dictate at least $70M/year in 2027 from essentially any suitor he wants having achieved “virtual free agency,” due to a no-trade provision and a no-franchise tag provision.
Of course, situations like this are precisely while teams like the Chiefs (Patrick Mahomes) and Bills (Josh Allen) never allow those QBs to get within two years of free agency let alone the cusp of it. Then again, those QBs also never had to endure a collusion case ruling , or sit on the market on a non-exclusive franchise tag, either.

title: Ravens Film Room: The Matchup That Will Mean Everything vs. Bengals Sunday
full_text:
Alas, this is finally the week Cam Jurgens will make his Ravens debut after general manager gave up a second-round pick while the struggling offensive lineman was still in concussion protocol.
But careful what you wish for.
Jurgens was getting whipped at guard for the Eagles – there is just no other way to put it - and his health is a major concern and people close to that team believe Jurgens was about to get benched in Philadelphia before Ravens GM Eric DeCosta panicked and gave up a bounty for him . And now Jurgens is on a path to fully practice and get cleared to play for Baltimore for the first time … just in time to face the most daunting group of defensive tackles in the NFL through the first third of the season led by signature offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence, whom Cincy traded the 10th-overall pick for and who is living up to that price tag.
Oh, and Lamar Jackson is still very much a candidate to miss this game and he hasn’t had a full practice since injuring his ankle Week 4 and backup Snoop Huntley refuses to really lean into using his legs. And Baltimore lost its best blocking tight end for the season.
Jurgens has not been the same player since undergoing back and nerve surgery after helping the Eagles win the Super Bowl in 2024, and time will tell if he is indeed an upgrade over rookie guard Vega Ioane, who was curtailing the spate of A-gap pressure that was occurring before he was forced to move to center, while the run game remains hit-or-miss. Ioane held up quite well against dominating individuals like Jeffery Simmons, and while his snaps were sometimes erratic he showed significant promise and earned high praise in Owings Mills and around the NFL.
Jurgens allows him to shift back to his natural guard spot, but Eagles general manager Howie Roseman doesn’t lose a lot of trades. It’s hard not to look at a chart like this and express concern how Jurgens is going to hold up Sunday playing with a new line and a new quarterback for the first time, with the Bengals coming off a bye and sporting the only trio of defensive tackles in the NFL who each have at least two sacks (Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr.):
How often OGs are on an Island in Pass Blocking and their Successful Block rate on those plays pic.twitter.com/8wzdPIG8kf
Bengals owner Mike Brown went completely out of character with the Lawrence trade and he has devoted big resources to rebuilding his defense at the point of attack after years of failure on that side of the ball. They have a deep rotation up front with four tackles averaging at least 16 snaps per game and that does not include run-stuffer BJ Hill who was injured most of the year but played 33 snaps in his return in Week 5 and got to recover during the bye.
Lawrence is already fifth in NFL history in terms of career sacks among all players 350 pounds or heavier; the Bengals lead the NFL with eight sacks from defensive tackle already (in just five games). But let’s highlight Lawrence for a moment and where he ranks among DTs (again, having already had a bye):
Sacks : 3 (tied for 6th with Allen) Pressure Rate: 14% (3rd) Hurries: 13 (T-10th)
On the season the Bengals are allowing a passer rating of just 87.0 – identical to the vaunted Ravens secondary (that actually hasn’t been very good, especially in the second half ) – in large part due to the tackles. When Lawrence and Allen are on the field together they are collapsing the pocket and picking apart the space between the centers and the guards and producing these results for the Bengals defense:
Pressure Rate: 40.5% Sack Rate: 10% (11 on 111 dropbacks)
Passer Rating: 84.5 TD/INT: 3-2
Total D EPA w/Lawrence + Allen : 24.75 Total D EPA w/o both on field: 6.75
For an AFC North game this critical, knowing exactly how compromised the Ravens are in the interior offensive line (guard John Simpson looks highly overpaid at $10M and Ioane is switching positions, again), I would expect heavy volume from these two tackles but, again, they have maybe the deepest rotation here in the NFL.
Baltimore cannot really run the ball up the middle, and the Bengals have big issues against the run on the perimeter and their linebackers do not tackle well, so Derrick Henry is likely to attack there. Ravens rookie coordinator Declan Doyle needs to get Zay Flowers more involved from the backfield and more Justice Hill on sprint plays in pistol looks and more designed RPOs for Huntley and exploiting the horizontal plane, because vertical ain’t happening with the back-up QB.
If you were wondering where Ioane would look on a scatter chart at center, by the way, when he gets isolated, um, it looks a whole lot more inviting than the one for Jurgens:
How often Centers are on Islands in run blocking and their success blocking on those plays pic.twitter.com/6oVLS9mGgQ
Yeah, I have a hard time thinking Sunday is going to be a whole lot of fun for Jurgens and this offensive line, but we’ll see.

title: Ravens Report Card: Rookie Head Coach Jesse Minter After First 6 Games
full_text:
Jesse Minter couldn’t have asked for a much better schedule for his first six games as an NFL head coach.
The Ravens got a soft launch to his first season in the role, and they mostly took advantage with a 4-2 start. They have dealt with their fair share of injuries, for sure, and two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson might still have to miss another week with his ankle injury. Minter had to navigate a trip to Brazil and his offensive line has been in disrepair and he doesn’t seem very confident in his kicker anymore, either ( maybe they’ll consider a trade ?).
Oh, and he’s already blown three 10-point leads and ended up losing two of them. Nothing is every easy and boring around here, is it?
So what do we make of Minter through his first 1/3 of a season in charge? You’ll have to read the column to find out.
The Ravens showed a flawless execution in Brazil to win a game despite having only seven seconds to pull off that game-winning sequence. They rallied on the road with a back-up QB, after a rough first half, to win in Atlanta in the only game Minter wasn’t the favorite .
They won a game in which they had to cycle through three centers, landing on a rookie guard who then held down snapping duties. They dealt with the usual spate of penalties that come with start-up operations and largely overcame it. Minter made a ballsy call to take the ball in overtime of that game in Atlanta and it led to a seven-minute TD drive.
So at a macro level, given how new this is to him, and some of what’s been thrown at him, his feels appropriate to us.
These players like him and they respond to him. They start games well, and seem generally prepared. He knows how handle the media and convey what needs to be conveyed and he’s generally protective of his players.
He hasn’t tried to BS the fans about injuries and they have taken the long-view with a serious of injuries that should pay off down the road. I don’t have many real issues here. He hasn’t put his foot in his mouth, we haven’t seen any player have major discipline issues or fly off the handle in-game. I don’t have a lot of issues here.
Maybe I am holding him to too high of a standard. But he was a stud with the Chargers without having a top roster and his adjustments and in-game tactics were remarkably on point. So I expected as much here, with these players used to his concepts from their time in Mike Macdonald’s similar defense here.
This side of the ball got loaded with resources in the offseason. It was supposed to be plug-and-play and supposed to start winning on third down and with the pass rush and in coverage and, especially in the fourth quarter. Not so much . They have fallen apart after the half despite having games in hand time and time again, and the secondary has actually been the biggest underperformers on the team. It's gotten bad enough that corner might be the biggest need on the team.
Minter has to wear that. The corners and safeties don’t have an interception yet. These choke gene is alive and well and now it’s 16 times being DeCosta-ed (blowing a 10-point lead and losing) since 2019.
Expected the defensive coordinator thing to be his carrying trait and strength. Wearing all these hats all the time isn’t for everyone and it can take a while to figure it out and that’s an ongoing process for this coach who happens to be the rare first-timer who is replacing a potential Hall of Famer and has a team with Super Bowl expectations.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Week 6 Rookie Report: Pass Catchers Shine Despite Offensive Struggles
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's drag of a 13-10 road loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and after falling to 4-2, they are now tied with the Pittsburgh Steelers for second place in the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. Fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner was out with a hand injury, while the only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his second week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his third straight and final start at center since sliding over from right guard. While the offensive line as a whole struggled to hold up in pass protection and gain much traction in the ground game, Ioane was far from the problem and still managed to put some nice reps on tape of him clearing rushing lanes for star running back Derrick Henry.
The #Ravens successfully executing trap, trying to take advantage of the Browns playing downhill. Works well becuase Ioane clears out the 1T pic.twitter.com/QtUlimNkkv
The second-rounder continues to be a steady rotational presence for the Ravens on early downs, playing 25 defensive snaps against the Browns. He recorded a trio of total tackles for the third time this season, including an assisted takedown for a loss, two solos and his first career quarterback hit.
This is on the Zion young tape every week Putting his hand in the dirt and doing the dirty work in the muck. Fundamentally sound player. pic.twitter.com/RE0UiwIsjo
In his first game back from a four-week stint on injured reserve after suffering a fractured wrist in the season opener, the third-rounder made quite a strong impression and was on the field for over 50% of the offense's total snaps, with 31. Lane made the most of his opportunities by catching four of his five targets for 40 receiving yards and was the highest-graded offensive player on the team according to Pro Football Focus with an overall of 79.7. Each of his snags resulted in a first down, as he presented himself as a quarterback-friendly target for Huntley in the passing game in some key situations, three of which came on third down. Lane also showcased his skills as a downfield blocker in the run game as well.
Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane | 4 catches | 40 yards | 1.82 YPRR Lane made some tough catches into traffic this week, unphased by nearby defenders. Also showed great physicality through his routes, using his large frame to create separation by pushing off on one. pic.twitter.com/cQebyURg1L
"I thought Ja'Kobi did some really nice things," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I think there's parts of the game where [you can see] it's his second game, and it shows that it's his second game. Then you see what also created a lot of the energy and excitement around Ja'Kobi for how he did in training camp with his ability to pluck the ball out of the air and make tough catches and be a really physical receiver and use his body really well. I thought he had some really nice plays and some nice catches. He had a couple really nice blocks as well."
The fifth-rounder didn't see any playing time on defense for the first time since making his regular-season debut in Week 2, after the Ravens decided to deploy second-year pro Keyon Martin at the nickel spot over him. He did play 15 snaps on special teams for the second week in a row, tying his career high, which also ranked second-most among rookies.
The fifth-rounder saw an uptick in his playing time for the fourth week in a row, with 30 combined snaps between offense and special teams, including a season-high 23 on offense and seven on special teams. He was on the field early and often, playing 40.4 % of the team's total offensive snaps and recording career highs with four catches for five targets, 44 receiving yards and his first touchdown.
Rookie Josh Cuevas scores his first career TD! BALvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s38V1mHPG9
Cuevas was the beneficiary of one of offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's most innovative play designs of the season thus far, where he essentially lined up at left guard before going on to record his longest career reception on a 29-yard catch-and-run.
This is sick: #Ravens OC Declan Doyle lined up TE Josh Cuevas at LG, then released him into a route for a 29-yard gain. Because Cuevas was off the line of scrimmage, he was eligible to go downfield. This is brilliant. pic.twitter.com/jN4icyVvEG
The sixth-round specialist impressed as a field-flipping weapon for the third week in a row, setting new career highs for punts in a game and punt yardage with seven for 346 yards. He pinned the Browns' offense inside their 20-yard line three times, including an excellent play where he joined forces with special teams ace Keondre Jackson to stop the ball at the Cleveland one-yard line. Eckley averaged 49.4 yards per punt with a new career-long of 62.
9 iron inside the 5 for @RyanEckley1 . ⛳️ Tune in on FOX. pic.twitter.com/V8ibXW474E
Even with the return of four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher Trey Hendrickson from finger surgery, the undrafted free agent still got to see some playing time on defense, although it wasn't in the double digits, with seven and logged the fourth-most special teams snaps on the team with 18, which was also the most among rookies. During his limited playing time on defense, Burke came close to notching his second career regular-season sack twice. Both instances came with him rushing against the Browns' right tackle, and he narrowly missed Deshaun Watson before one of his teammates came in and finished the play.
Ravens UDFA Ethan Burke almost had 2 sacks Sunday pic.twitter.com/nvFNPoY1oQ

He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Bills' Potential Safety Solution Former Ravens' INT Leader Ready on Practice Squad
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills will be down one safety when they come off their bye week to host the Baltimore Ravens on November 1.
Starter Chauncey Gardner-Johnson must serve a one-game NFL-imposed suspension for violating the conduct policy by spitting on an opponent during the October 18 road game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
As a result, veteran Damar Hamlin will presumably start alongside Cole Bishop at safety in Week 7 with fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore providing insurance off the bench. Kilgore saw his first career defensive snaps as a dime safety in the wake of  Gardner-Johnson's ejection last Sunday.
Although they could likely get away without making the move, especially if versatile defensive back Jordan Hancock, the Bills may opt to call up veteran safety Geno Stone from the practice squad for game day against the Ravens.
Rather than placing Stone in a standby role, Buffalo should give him enough snaps for an in-game evaluation. There's certainly a chance he can provide more of what the Bills need from that position group, especially against the pass.
Putting aside the extracurricular nonsense, Gardner-Johnson's performance has been subpar at best. He owns a 21.6 percent missed tackle rate while opposing passers are averaging 13.8 yards per completion when targeting him in coverage. In fact, the Bills should consider cutting Gardner-Johnson and giving his roster spot to Stone.
As a whole, the Bills' safeties are part of the reason why the team ranks next to last in pass defense (285.8).
Before thinking about a potential trade to upgrade the secondary, why not turn to someone who is already in the building and has experience producing at the NFL level? It certainly isn't the sexiest option, but it may yield better results than any external addition could at this point in time.
The Bills added Stone in March after two seasons, and 34 consecutive starts, with the Cincinnati Bengals.
Stone, who signed a modest veteran contract reportedly worth $1.4 million, was drawn to Buffalo for a number of reasons, including an endorsement from fellow Iowa Hawkeye Micah Hyde .
Prior to spending back-to-back seasons as a Bengals' starter, Stone, a 2020 seventh-round draft pick, played out his rookie contract with the Baltimore Ravens. In 2023, Stone made a team-high seven interceptions to lead all NFL safeties.
While the 27-year-old Stone, who has 85 career appearances (53 starts) under his belt, struggled with his tackling and coverage last season, he has a versatility that gives him a chance to succeed in defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's scheme.
“I was always a Swiss Army knife that kind of did a lot of different things and that's what I like my safety group to be," said Leonhard, who spent 10 years as a NFL safety. "There's going to be a lot of different roles and a lot of different positions and techniques they're asked to do."
Stone has earned starts as both a free safety and a strong safety since being drafted in 2020.

title: Key Stat That Explains NFL Leader Keon Coleman's Redemption Arc  With Bills
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills had high hopes for Keon Coleman when they drafted him in 2024. It may have taken some time, but he looks to be living up to their expectations.
In fact, Coleman's third year in the NFL looks like it could be his best yet. He was selected as a riser in the Bills On SI Bye Week Stock Report .
After scoring four touchdowns in each of his first two seasons with the Bills, Coleman has needed only six games to get to three on the year this season.
But one metric has shown that Coleman may be playing even better than a casual fan may expect. What it shows is that Coleman's development is fully in effect as he plays through his age-23 season.
𝗪𝗢𝗪: Keon Coleman leads the ENTIRE NFL in EPA per target 🤯 Is the Keon breakout REAL? #Bills | #GoBills | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/eOB2WlTufn
One may be wondering: what exactly is EPA? It's Expected Points Added. The metric represents how much a single play increases or decreases a team's likelihood of scoring. So, in essence, no receiver in the NFL this season is enhancing his team's chances of scoring more than Coleman.
Other metrics back this up and show how well Coleman has played thus far. The Florida State product has the highest success rate (70.8 percent) and catch rate (79.2 percent) of his career. Coleman also has zero drops this year and has garnered a 138.0 passer rating when targeted (another career high).
The play of Coleman really seems to be tied to the fact that head coach Joe Brady has heavily invested in his development.
Brady's backing of Coleman when he was named Bills' head coach seems to be paying dividends. Especially as the Buffalo receiving corps dealt with injuries to D.J. Moore and Josh Palmer.
Brady elaborated on the maturity his third-year  wideout is showing and how that has helped his play on the field.
"His play has never been his issue," said Brady. "And right now, there's not issues off the field. He's where he needs to be, he's handling everything like a pro."
It's encouraging to see just how strong Coleman has played in 2026. But like his head coach alluded to, his best days still look to be ahead.
"There's so much trust we have for him as the player, the development, and he continues to just make plays," said Brady.

title: Bills and Dolphins Identified as Potential Trade Partners Ahead of NFL Deadline
full_text:
If there's one area where the Buffalo Bills could use more help at on the defensive side of the ball, it's at linebacker.
The linebacker position has been a sore spot for Buffalo for years now, and that hasn't changed in 2026 , as Terrel Bernard has been disappointing and Dorian Williams has been even worse. Buffalo was hoping for a big contribution from rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr this season, but that simply hasn't happened in six games.
Another concern with Bernard is his injury history, and if he falls victim to that issue once again, Buffalo will have a precarious situation at the position.
Safe to say, general manager Brandon Beane should be on the phone between now and the trade deadline to add an upgrade.
The Athletic's Daniel Popper listed his top 50 trade candidates before the NFL trade deadline next month and among them was Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks.
Popper also named Buffalo as one of the best fits for him.
"Brooks, a reliable veteran off-ball linebacker, is one of the few (attractive Dolphins trade candidates)," Popper said.
"He signed a three-year extension in July and has close to $13 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so any acquiring team would be making a multiyear commitment. The Dolphins would take on $15.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Brooks. This regime, with coach Jeff Hafley and GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, has not been afraid of dead money thus far," Popper added.
"Best fits: Bills, Steelers, Cowboys," Popper said.
The Dolphins are in the midst of a rebuild and the tank is on with Miami sporting an 0-6 record entering Week 7.
Knowing that, the Dolphins need to be stockpiling picks, but with their lack of talent on both sides of the ball, they don't have many viable options to help accomplish that task.
Brooks is their best option to garner more draft capital given his track record of high-level play. Brooks has been a quality starting linebacker for years now, and he cemented himself as one of the league's best in 2025 after getting his first All-Pro nod.
What makes him more attractive is Brooks won't be a rental thanks to his contract that runs through 2029 , so giving up draft capital for him will be easier to stomach for the acquiring team.
We could see Brooks fetching at least a third-round pick in a hot market.
Absolutely, assuming the Dolphins are willing to do an in-division trade. Normally we'd say that's impossible, but with Miami so far off from contending, it's possible.
Brooks is one of the best inside linebackers in the NFL. According to Pro Football Focus , his overall grade of 71.4 ranks 15th at the position, and his run defense and pass-rush grades are both inside the top 10.
Brooks lacks in coverage, where he has posted the 45th-best PFF coverage grade of 56.4, but that's still better than Bernard's and slightly worse than Williams' (57.4).
Adding Brooks gives the Bills an elite linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed who can be a major asset in the blitz and in run defense.
The veteran would also push Williams to the LB3 spot, which in turn gives Buffalo a much better depth situation.
Beane and the Bills need to be all-in on this season and making a trade for Brooks would show they are.

title: Three Safeties Buffalo Bills Should Target at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Entering their Week 7 bye, the Buffalo Bills are in great shape . They’re in first place in  the AFC East with a record of 5-1 and have one of the most potent offenses in the NFL.
Defensively, however, there are some concerns. Buffalo is 31st in the NFL in yards surrendered through the air, giving up 1,715 yards in six games. First-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard will be looking for answers during the bye week, but the Bills could also use an influx of talent in the secondary.
Looking for cornerback help isn’t out of the question , but they did just bring back Tre’Davious White . At safety, they can still use more depth, with these three players standing out as options to pursue at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
A fourth-round pick out of Iowa in 2019, Amani Hooker has been a fixture in the Tennessee Titans secondary for eight years now. He has 457 tackles, 42 pass deflections, and 14 interceptions in 101 career games. He’s been one of the few bright spots on a struggling Tennessee team this season, recording 41 tackles and two interceptions in five games.
Hooker might not have the same name recognition as the two players who follow on this list, but he’s earned an overall PFF grade of 81.1 (eighth best at the position) and a coverage grade of 71.7 (18th best). He also has two years remaining on his deal, so adding him wouldn’t be a rental, but could solve their safety concerns for a couple of seasons.
Despite signing a three-year extension worth $75.6 million this offseason, Derwin James has been frequently named a potential trade target. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and could be ready to blow things up and start a rebuild.
If so, it would make sense for them to move James, who just turned 30 this summer. He’s missed the past three games with a hamstring injury and is playing with a fractured pinky finger. That might give general manager Brandon Beane pause, but James would bring instant credibility to the secondary.
Arguably the most recognizable name at the position that could be moved is Budda Baker. The Arizona Cardinals veteran is an eight-time Pro Bowler, but with his team continuing to struggle, Baker is widely believed to be on the trade block with the Bills being a popular destination.
Baker would be an intriguing fit next to Cole Bishop since both players are versatile enough to play either safety position. Baker wouldn’t be a rental either, since he’s under contract in 2027. That said, there is a buyout that Buffalo could utilize should the fit prove to be wrong.
It’s hard to see that being the case since Baker has been one of the top safeties in the NFL for nearly a decade. His experience and talent could be exactly what Leonhard’s defense needs to begin slowing down opposing passing attacks.

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson Appeal Decision Handed Down After Bills DB Fights Suspension
full_text:
We weren't sure if Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson would appeal his one-game suspension, but it turns out he did.
Of course, Gardner-Johnson was facing a suspension after he spat at a Las Vegas Raiders player during the Week 6 win on Sunday, which got him ejected .
And, as we expected would be the outcome if Gardner-Johnson did appeal his suspension, the ban has been upheld, the NFL announced on Thursday, so he's out for one game.
"The one-game suspension of Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been upheld upon appeal," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote.
It never made any sense for Gardner-Johnson to even waste his time with an appeal.
Why, you ask? Well, he was literally caught on video spitting at the Raiders player, so there was no denying what he did.
Adding to that, Gardner-Johnson gave not one, but two apologies for his actions, with the second coming after his first was less than adequate , to say the least.
"I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me," Gardner-Johnson said.
"My passing and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," Gardner-Johnson added. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game.
"There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intence the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."
Hey, can't blame a guy for trying, I guess.
While many Bills fans called for Gardner-Johnson to be cut, head coach Joe Brady said the team would not take that step and instead will keep Johnson on the team.
“CJ is a member of the Buffalo Bills. We brought him here for a reason," Brady said . "He knows that he has to play better, he knows he has to be better for this team."
Naturally, we were bearish on Gardner-Johnson in our Bills' Bye Week Stock Report .
Gardner-Johnson isn't the only one facing a spitting accusation this week, as Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. has also been hit with a one-game suspension for spitting at an opponent.
However, unlike Gardner-Johnson, there is no clear evidence on video of Franklin taking part in the despicable act, so he has a better chance to appeal.
Franklin has also denied the allegation through a statement from his agents.
“We adamantly deny Sam spit at anyone. We look forward to the process fully exonerating him tomorrow at the hearing and the apology he deserves," the statement read .
A decision on Franklin's appeal should be coming down soon. If he fails, the Bills will be down two defensive backs when they return from their bye in Week 8 to face the Baltimore Ravens.

title: Do Bills Have Enough Respect for 'Fun Uncle' Joe Brady as Head Coach?
full_text:
It's not everyday a NFL team has two players suspended for spitting at an opponent.
Buffalo Bills ' safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson and special teams ace Sam Franklin have received one-game suspensions for violating the league's conduct policy against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, although the latter strongly denies the allegation.
Even if cleared from any wrongdoing in this particular situation, Franklin still fits the narrative that the Bills lack discipline under rookie head coach Joe Brady. Through six weeks, the veteran is tied for the NFL lead with three special teams penalties that have hurt his team's field position.
Buffalo has totaled 51 penalties (that doesn't include the seven that were declined) through six games. That mark is the fifth highest in the NFL with the Green Bay Packers leading the way with 57 enforced infractions.
Three of the those 51 flags belong to Gardner-Johnson. Prior to his Week 6 personal foul penalty that led to his disqualification, the unstable safety committed an unnecessary roughness foul six days earlier against the Los Angeles Rams.
The Bills' penalty issues, however, extend well beyond Gardner-Johnson and the defense.
Against the Raiders, a fourth-down offensive holding penalty took a Dalton Kincaid touchdown reception off the board.
"We've got to be more disciplined, and it's almost, it's kind of a lot of different position groups, too," said Brady prior to the Week 6 chaos in Las Vegas. "Our fundamentals and technique have to improve. Once you put it on tape, regardless of going into each game, some refs call it more, if we're putting it on tape, we're targets in certain elements, and we have a lot of stuff we have to clean up."
Players who respect their head coach and teammates usually refrain from selfish behavior, even in the heat of the moment.
Unfortunately, there have already been multiple occasions where Bills' players lacked both situational awareness and respect for the team's mission.
With the 36-year-old Brady, who had never been a head coach prior to his promotion with the Bills, currently being the youngest in the NFL to hold his position, it's certainly valid to question whether some players see him as a buddy rather than a boss .
"The vibe with Coach Brady is young and fresh," said left guard Alec Anderson to News 8 back in July. "It’s kind of like having your uncle come over, and he’s a little younger than the older brother, and you just know you’re gonna have a good time. ... You know you’re going to be able to go out and get some ice cream and do stuff that your parents wouldn’t really allow you to do, and I think that’s kinda the fun aspect that we’re gonna have."
Brady dismissed the idea of being a "fun uncle" during an on-site training camp interview with Kay Adams.
"The fun uncle, I have no clue what the hell that means. I'm gonna be honest," said Brady.
Bills head coach Joe Brady with a strong response to the “fun uncle” nonsense 🗣️ @heykayadams | @BuffaloBills pic.twitter.com/5hpDunBHz3
Brady needs to send the message that no player is more important than the team, and he can do it by dismissing Gardner-Johnson.
The over-the-top Gardner-Johnson has shown troubling lapses in judgement on multiple occasions since joining the Bills, beginning with his training camp livestream from the locker room .
It looks as if Brady may have erred when professing his desire for players who aren't afraid to "toe the line." Too often it seems that "playing with an edge" becomes an excuse for selfishness and stupidity on the field.
The Bills must be careful with confusing playing with passion and energy for unhinged punk behavior .
A good place to start is by making an example of those players whose default is using their saliva as a weapon of choice on the field.

title: J.J. Watt Provides Recipe for Bills to Reach Super Bowl LXI
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have an offense that’s capable of going the distance this season.
There are plenty of supporters of the notion around the league from other media members, coaches, and players—both current and former—that Buffalo and quarterback Josh Allen could be on the path to SoFi Stadium later this season for Super Bowl LXI.
Now, following the Bills’ most recent back-to-back road victories over the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, longtime NFL defensive end and current CBS broadcaster J.J. Watt says you can add him to the list of names in that category, as well.
“I think, with the Bills (and) the offense, we’ve kind of been saying it for a while—everybody kind of knows that—that offense is good enough to win a Super Bowl,” J.J. Watt said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday.
“They held on to the ball better in this (last) game, obviously, than they have up to this point in the last three weeks or so. Josh Allen continues to do things that maybe only he can do, and some of those Brett Favre-type plays where he draws up the defense (to him and) flips it over the top (for a touchdown).
“(Josh Allen) didn’t run the ball, you know, scramble-wise, nearly as much as he did Monday night, but it’s very, very good.”
Watt just announced Buffalo’s 33-30 victory over Las Vegas at Allegiant Stadium last Sunday, which is a matchup where Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns while his counterpart in the backfield—reigning 2025 rushing champion James Cook III—piled up 95 yards and one touchdown on 22 carries.
The team’s defense, however, surrendered 30 points and 378 total yards of offense on 61 plays (6.2 yards per play) to a reeling Raiders’ squad that was coming off two straight losses and had only managed to record 17 points and 306 yards on offense for an average of 5.4 yards per play the week prior against the New England Patriots .
The outing came on the heels of another shaky, yet victorious performance against the Rams—at that aforementioned Super Bowl venue in Inglewood, California—where Bills’ first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s unit allowed 454 yards to Los Angeles’ 18th-year quarterback Matthew Stafford and Co. under the lights of Monday Night Football .
It’s a major concern, one of which there’s no hiding from . . . and it might end up costing the Bills in a big way at some point down the line later this season if it’s not fixed in a hurry.
“It’s just (about) if the defense can catch up. . . . It’s all going to come down to their defense,” Watt added during his appearance with Pat McAfee.
“And, I liked some of the stuff that they did in the game in terms of playing a little more man, (and) being a little more aggressive. Jim Leonhard put in Christian Benford directly on Brock Bowers at times, and that worked really well.
“It was a fun battle to watch all day long to just see how they were trying to defend Brock Bowers.”
"The Bills offense is good enough to win a Super Bowl but can the defense catch up.. They're a very good football team" ~ @JJWatt #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/IZSHJFNVJK
So, although there are plenty of reasons to be optimistic about Buffalo’s chances later this season under first-year head coach Joe Brady, there are more than a few areas of concern that give outside observers like Watt pause.
However, with that in mind, hopefully Brady and Leonhard—as well as Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane—have a solid plan of attack coming out of the team’s current bye week in order to get things corrected on that side of the ball.
If they can, then Bills Mafia might be dancing in the sunshine of the West Coast once again later on in February like they were over this past two-week stretch.
But, if Buffalo’s brass can’t manage to figure things out , then it might be another year of wondering, “What if?”
The next several weeks of the regular season, especially before the trade deadline , could get very interesting in Western New York.

title: Bills Should Consider Adding $60 Million Titans' Cornerback Via Trade
full_text:
At the bye week, the Buffalo Bills' defense ranks poorly in just about every defensive category.
First-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has vowed to make changes to his defensive unit moving forward, and Bills ON SI recently suggested a few such switchups that Buffalo should consider during the current bye week .
One of those changes involved trading for another defensive playmaker. The upcoming trade deadline is less than three weeks away on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET.
And, apparently, the idea of defensive difference-makers being shipped around the league is a popular idea as ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler revealed that a player on trade watch is Tennessee Titans’ cornerback Alontae Taylor.
Taylor is a former No. 49 overall pick of the New Orleans Saints out of the University of Tennessee in 2022.
In 69 career games, which includes 58 starts, Taylor has been impactful, amassing:
That performance afforded Taylor the opportunity to test free agency inking a three-year deal with the Titans worth up to $60 million.
The switch from New Orleans to Tennessee, however, hasn’t been a warm “homecoming” for the former University of Tennessee Volunteer standout defender.  In Week 6, he was benched by Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh  due to continued poor play this season.
In fact, Taylor, who stands at 6-foot-1 and weighs 199 pounds, was a healthy scratch last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.
Might that mean he’s on the move in the coming weeks? Well, possibly . . . depending on what team can facilitate his hefty salary.
Could the Bills be one of those teams?
The cap space the team has to pull from isn’t very much, though, currently standing at $4.4 million in available space.
Given the team’s struggles in the secondary—both on the boundary and in the slot—the addition of another capable body to help Leonhard’s ailing defense makes plenty of sense .
Taylor's skill set appears much better suited for the nickel cornerback position, which is where he primarily played for the New Orleans Saints during his first four years in the league.
After signing with the Titans prior to this season, Tennessee suprisingly moved him to an outside corner role.  So it’s not hard to see why there might be a disconnect between the 27-year-old’s past success and his failures with his new AFC South squad.
At his stellar size, Taylor is a physical player who seems more comfortable playing closer to the quarterback and near the line of scrimmage where he can be an asset to a team in both the run and the pass game.
While it’s unclear whether or not the Titans would actually move on from their big free-agent signing after just six games, it’s a possibility seeing that Tennessee already benched him before the calendar has even turned to November.
Coupling that with the fact that Tennessee is now fighting for the No. 1 overall pick next April (battling the hapless Miami Dolphins), it would be smart for the Titans to acquire multiple draft picks to retool for 2027.
It’s never a good thing when a franchise i s thinking about the draft in the middle of October, but that’s exactly where Tennessee’s heads should be at.
Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane needs to pick up the phone and talk with the Titans’ brass.
The Bills' current nickelback Dee Alford Alford signed a 3 year, $15M contract with the Buffalo Bills before this season, but is struggling mightily in Leonard's new system.  The Bills can't wait and hope for things to work themselves out and need defensive help now.
At some point, something’s got to give with Leonhard and Co. on the defensive side of the ball, so nobody should be shocked to see Beane pull out all the stops to make sure that dreadful unit isn’t what holds Buffalo back in the playoffs once again.
Pass defense is the biggest area of concern for the Bills, so some sort of defensive back is the most logical move.
So, why not Taylor, Bills Mafia?

title: Bills' Stock Report: Ray Davis Rising, Maxwell Hairston Falling as Bye Week Arrives
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are in the midst of their bye week following a 5-1 start to Joe Brady's first season as a head coach.
While the Bills are the NFL's highest-scoring team (32.8), they are surrendering the fifth-most points per game (28.5) to opponents.
Although Brady and franchise quarterback Josh Allen have admitted that across-the-board improvement is needed , Buffalo enters Week 7 as the No. 2 seed in the AFC behind only the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0).
As for individual performers, we've singled out five players in our bye week stock report. Here are three players rising and two falling.
Don't look now, but Ray Davis is leading the NFL in kick return average (31.0) through the season's first six weeks.
After a slow start, the 2025 All-Pro has rebounded heading into the bye. In addition to huge opening kickoff returns that created points in back-to-back weeks, Davis has also seen a slight bump in offensive snaps .
"But the running back right now, I got to get Ray playing more," said Brady late last month . "He's too good of a player."
Davis, who averaged six offensive snaps per week over the first four outing, totaled 19 reps on offense over the past two games. He had a key 31-yard catch-and-run down to the 1 against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football.
Between the extracurricular nonsense and his subpar performances, the Bills needed to show safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson the door , yesterday.
Already on the decline, Gardner-Johnson's stock dropped like a rock in Week 6. After missing two tackles on Raiders' tight end Michael Mayer, he was ejected from the game due to spitting on tight end Brock Bowers .
It's just one distraction after another with Gardner-Johnson, who has shown to be a selfish player with little situational awareness. Following the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots, he insulted wide receiver Efton Chism in his childish postgame comments.
During training camp, he violated the sanctity of the locker room by live streaming on social media. Even if he played like Ronnie Lott, he wouldn't be worth the excess baggage, and right now, he's not even playing as well as Damar Hamlin.
Keon Coleman was written off by everyone from the fans to the owner , but as Geno Smith once famously said, the Bills' wide receiver "ain't write back."
Instead Coleman has quietly done his job through the season's first six games, and he's done it well. With DJ Moore unavailable, Coleman has answered the bell .
“He's where he needs to be. He's handling everything like a pro," said Brady. "There's so much trust we have for him as the player, the development, and he continues to just make plays."
The 6-foot-3 wide receiver has touchdown receptions in each of his last three outings. For the season, he's averaging a robust 14.9 yards per reception while accounting for a 79.2 catch percentage.
The Bills' 2025 first-round pick earned the starting nod opposite Christian Benford in Week 1, but his struggles in coverage have resulted in a reduced role in Weeks 5 and 6.
He was not in the starting lineup against the Rams and the Raiders. During the two-game road swing, Hairston saw only 29 percent of defensive snaps.
Hairston has already allowed two touchdowns while opposing quarterbacks post a 96.2 rating when targeting the slightly-undersized defender. He also owns an alarming 21.4 percent missed tackle rate.
While he hasn't approached Kaiir Elam bust territory, Hairston is clearly falling out of favor due to his performance .
With Hairston's fall comes second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun's rise . The Ohio State product has earned back-to-back starts, playing with high effort and infectious energy.
According to PFF, Igbinosun has three pass break-ups playing man coverage to lead all rookies in that category. He has seven total break-ups to go with 27 tackles.
"I think what he's done the last couple weeks, he's definitely earned a high majority of the snaps at the corner position," said defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. "I know what I'm getting, play in and play out. I think he's stepped in and done a great job handling more volume in this defense."
