title: Six Buffalo Bills' Bye-Week Superlatives Include James Cook, Davison Igbinosun
full_text:
As of right now, the Buffalo Bills are sitting pretty during their bye week with a 5-1 overall record and the current lead in the AFC East.
For the most part, it’s exactly the type of start to the season that Bills’ owner Terry Pegula and general manager Brandon Beane had probably hoped for this fall after the unexpected firing of longtime head coach Sean McDermott back in January.
And, the adventure to reach their current mark under the guidance of first-year head man Joe Brady has been nothing short of fascinating .
On one hand, the offense and quarterback Josh Allen are humming along at levels hardly seen before in the history of the league, as Allen and Co. are averaging the most points per game of any team aside from the Detroit Lions through six weeks of the season at a rate of 32.8 points per game.
On the other side of the coin, though, new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s unit has been one of the most disappointing groups in all of professional football midway through the month of October.
In short, describing the situation in Western New York as perplexing might be an understatement.
But, there have still been plenty of bright spots to highlight throughout the first several weeks of the 2026 campaign.
Here are Bill ON SI ’s six superlatives for Buffalo at the bye.
Honestly, is there any other player to consider here? I think not.
If it weren’t for ninth-year veteran quarterback Josh Allen, who currently leads the NFL in touchdowns scored through Week 6 with—fittingly, given his jersey number—a total of 17 trips across the goal line (9 passing, 8 rushing), then the Bills probably wouldn’t even be close to the top of the the AFC and the AFC East division at the current moment.
In fact, it wouldn’t be too hard to imagine Buffalo being 1-5 or even 0-6 if it weren’t for the incredible weekly play of Allen on offense.
The former 2024 MVP is on a roll to start the 2026 campaign, and there’s reason to believe that he could even earn another NFL Most Valuable Player award once the season is all said and done later on this winter.
In addition to his incredible touchdown output, the 6-foot-5, 237-pound gunslinger has also tallied 1,504 passing yards, 240 rushing yards, and just four interceptions.
So far, Allen has put the roster on his back, but it’s unclear if Buffalo’s current model for winning is sustainable.
In spite of his ongoing fumbling issues, outside of quarterback Josh Allen there’s no other player more important to Buffalo’s overall success than running back James Cook III .
The defending 2025 NFL rushing champion has seemingly picked up right where he left off last season as Cook’s (627 yards) currently ranked third in the league in rushing behind only Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson (641 yards) and Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III (665 yards) through six weeks of the season.
Averaging 104.5 yards per contest at the moment, the former Georgia Bulldog is actually on pace to break his mark of 1,621 yards on the ground from one season ago as he’s currently on track to rack up 1,777 yards this season if he were to appear in every game and maintain this steady rate. Cook is also tied for second in the NFL in rushing touchdowns for running backs in 2026 with a total of six.
Simply put, the 5-foot-11, 190-pound tailback has been electric once again this season, and it’s clear he’s almost just as valuable to the offense as Allen is at this point in their careers.
It’s not quite the same, but Cook has continued to be an integral part of Joe Brady’s offensive attack, and rightfully so.
Honorable mention: WR Keon Coleman
Just as Cook III is on schedule to break his previous career-high, third-year wideout Keon Coleman is also currently en route to doing so this season for Buffalo.
The Bills have been without veteran D.J. Moore for the past two matchups, as well as during portions of other games this fall, but the unit still hasn’t missed a beat with the team’s former second-round pick out of Florida State getting the lion’s share of the load with Moore in and out of the lineup.
While it hasn’t been a massive amount of production, it’s certainly been a steady output as Coleman has recorded 19 receptions for 283 yards and three touchdowns, which sets him on pace for a solid stat line of 54 catches for 802 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.
If he can keep it up, then people might change their tune about a second contract being handed out to the 23-year-old Opelousas, Louisiana, native.
For that reason, Coleman needed to be listed as an honorable mention.
Much like with the aforementioned Coleman and Cook III, sixth-year veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau is currently on a trajectory to shatter his previous career-highs in quarterback pressures, sacks, and tackles for loss.
Right now, the player nicknamed “Groot” seems to have gained an extra gear under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard despite almost every other player outside of Deone Walker struggling at this point of the season.
Rousseau has more quarterback pressures (39) than any other pass-rusher in the league according to Pro Football Focus , and he’s also second in the NFL in tackles for loss and sacks with a total of eight tackles for loss and six sacks, respectively, which is just two shy of his previous career-high of eight sacks.
The 6-foot-6, 266-pound former Miami Hurricane is on pace for a 2026 stat line of 60 total tackles, 54 quarterback hits, 22 tackles for loss, and 17 sacks.
And, astonishingly, given that Rousseau has those 39 previously mentioned quarterback pressures through six games, he’s also technically on pace for 111 total pressures this season, which is simply amazing.
Will he reach those lofty statistical levels? Probably not, but he’s still the Bills’ most dominant defender to date.
Veteran Tyler Bass had a rough stretch in 2025 due to a bout with multiple injuries pertaining to his left hip, groin, and pelvic areas, which ultimately required surgery to repair the ailments.
He missed the entirety of the season, and some fans and outside media members questioned if Bass would even be Buffalo’s starting kicker in 2026 after Matt Prater had a successful stint as the team’s placekicker last season.
In the end, however, that wasn’t the case as Buffalo didn’t bring in any competition for Bass this summer for training camp, and so far that bet has paid off.
The 29-year-old is a perfect 13-for-13 on his field-goal attempts through six games, and he’s missed just two extra points all year.
It’s been a nice developing story of redemption given Bass’ struggles with both his injuries and shaky past performances in big moments, so it’ll be interesting to see if his individual success continues moving forward after the bye week.
Although Davison “IGB” Igbinosun was a bit of a surprise pick by the Bills in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft this past April, the former Ohio State defensive back has been the team’s most consistent and promising rookie so far this season.
Now, that could all change moving forward given the possible incoming increased roles for fellow rookies Skyler Bell and Kaleb Elarms-Orr, but as of right now Igbinosun has been the best of the bunch from general manager Brandon Beane’s most recent draft class .
The 6-foot-2, 189-pound New Jersey native has started three games thus far, and he’s held his own for the most part as he’s recorded 27 total tackles and seven pass deflections.
And, given that he’s seemingly unseated fellow cornerback Maxwell Hairston at the starting position opposite Christian Benford, there’s no reason why Igbinosun shouldn’t be listed as the “Most Outstanding Rookie” for the Bills so far this season.
Surprisingly, through six games of Buffalo’s 2026 campaign, it’s been special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers—not the highly-touted up-and-comer Jim Leonhard or longtime NFL assistant Pete Carmichael Jr.—who’s been the best new assistant coach in Western New York so far this fall.
Rodgers has somehow helped revive the confidence…

title: The Panthers Have a Serious Conundrum Up Front
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are just five games into their 2026 season, and this certainly looks like a different team on both sides of the ball than a year ago. The offense is humming and looks balanced with quarterback Bryce Young playing the best football of his young career, and running back Chuba Hubbard regaining his standout form from 2024.
Defensively, the team has overcome a very rough start on opening week against the Bears and has settled in nicely. The club is still missing the cornerback tandem of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson and is getting contributions from its younger players.
Still, one aspect of Dave Canales’s club that has been dealing with adversity dating all the way back to January is the offensive line. You will recall that starting left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon early in last season’s playoff lost to the Rams.
That forced Panthers general manager, Dan Morgan to make some big decisions. He plucked starting left tackle Rasheed Walker from the Green Bay Packers via a one year contract. He then used the 19th overall selection in April’s draft to select University of Georgia standout Monroe Freeling.
Then came June when mainstay right tackle Taylor Moton was diagnosed with blood clots in his lung. That put Walker at left tackle and Freeling on the right side to start the season. Last Sunday, Freeling was dealing with a knee injury suffered against the Lions in Week 4 and was inactive at Philadelphia last Sunday. Enter the 10-year pro, who took the field for the first time in 2026.
Pro Football Focus’ Gordon McGuinness came out with his updated offensive line rankings this week. Despite a 25-14 road win over the Birds, the Panthers’ front slipped from one spot from 25th to 26th. McGuinness took some time to mention the big change for Carolina up front.
“Right tackle Taylor Moton returned to the lineup for the first time this season, securing a 63.5 PFF pass-blocking grade and permitting a pair of pressures from 46 pass-blocking snaps in the win over the Philadelphia Eagles…”
Now comes a Sunday showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A season ago, Canales’s team unseated the Bucs as NFC South champions. It’s been a struggle for Todd Bowles’s club early in 2026 as the team is off to a 1-5 start. However, veteran signal-caller Baker Mayfield could make his return after missinng the last three games with a thumb issue.
Back to the Panthers. Freeling remains on the mend, but spoke this week about what he’s learned from a pro who’s made 130 starts (including playoffs) in 10 seasons.
#Panthers tackle Monroe Freeling is focused on getting better at his craft and getting healthy. But he’s learned a lot from Taylor Moton. A fun story about a rookie learning from a vet here: pic.twitter.com/gsMESjZKZH
If Moton remains healthy, it’s hard to fathom that Freeling will be back at right tackle anytime soon. And that may not be such a bad thing.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Panthers Could Face a Tough Trade Decision With One Surprising Starter
full_text:
The Panthers are 3-2, so most of the talk around the trade deadline has been about who Dan Morgan could bring to Carolina. After the last few years, it's a nice change to actually be talking about adding players instead of wondering who might be headed out.
I recently looked at five realistic trade targets Carolina could pursue before the deadline , but that doesn't mean Morgan won't listen if somebody calls about one of his guys.
Bobby Brown III is a name I wouldn't have thought much about a few weeks ago. He's playing, he's been good up front and Carolina isn't exactly in a position where it needs to start getting rid of defensive linemen. Still, I can see why another team would call.
That's the difference between Brown and some of the more obvious names Carolina could move. If you're trading somebody who barely plays, you're probably not getting much in return.
Brown has generated seven pressures this season and has been a solid part of Carolina's defensive line. He's also under contract through 2027 after signing a three-year, $21 million deal with the Panthers.
An October look at Carolina's possible trade chips even pointed to Brown as the player who might bring back the best return. That doesn't mean Morgan is shopping him, because there's been no indication that's happening. But I could see a team looking for help up front calling Carolina and asking what it would take.
The Panthers have some options around him, too. They used a second-round pick on Lee Hunter, traded a 2028 sixth-round pick for TeRah Edwards before the season and now have Tershawn Wharton back.
That doesn't suddenly make Brown expendable. We've already seen enough injuries this season to know how quickly depth can disappear, and Morgan made it pretty clear before the season that having enough bodies up front mattered to him.
There's also the money. Brown is under contract for next season, but his cap number climbs to around $9.8 million in 2027. Carolina doesn't have to do anything about that now, but it's at least something to think about if another team comes calling with a good offer.
This is where I'd have a hard time actually pulling the trigger. The Panthers aren't 1-4 and looking toward next season. They're 3-2 and have a real chance to play meaningful football over the next couple of months.
We just watched Carolina find a way to win the kind of game it usually loses in Philadelphia. Trading a starting defensive lineman who's helping you win doesn't make much sense unless you're getting something worthwhile back.
Carolina has spent too much time trying to build depth up front to turn around and give some of it away for a late pick. If somebody calls and offers a sixth-rounder, I'm keeping Brown. I'd rather have him for the rest of this season, especially with Carolina right in the middle of the division race.
But if a team trying to make a run gets desperate for defensive-line help and offers Morgan something he wasn't expecting, I'd listen. Maybe that offer never comes, and that's fine. Brown is still a player who can help Carolina right now.
That's really what makes his name interesting around the deadline. He's not somebody Carolina needs to trade, and I don't think the Panthers should be calling around trying to move him. He's good enough, though, that another team might be the one making the call.
If that happens, I'd hear them out.
It just better be a pretty good offer.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Panthers Should Be Willing to Pay Proposed Trade Cost for Eagles Defender
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline just 19 days away and after a 3-2 start to the season, the Carolina Panthers could be buyers. No, a deadline deal won't be some blockbuster move for one of the league's biggest stars, but adding an instant starter who may need a fresh start is always on the table.
Carolina has a decent cushion at the top of the NFC South and already has a road division win against the Atlanta Falcons. There's clear belief in the building that another playoff push is imminent, so theres no reason Carolina can't buy into this season even more than they did in the offseason.
As for what area needs to be addressed, it's certainly not the offense, which currently ranks second in the NFL in yards per game. Bryce Young leads the NFL in passing yards per game , being the only QB to post over 300 per game.
That leaves the defense, which has been solid since the Week 1 disaster against the Chicago Bears, but with one clear area of vulnerability: cornerback . With Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn both out for an extended time, the Panthers could trade for a Super Bowl champion.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox dropped his trade block board entering Week 7 of the NFL season. On that list of potential trade candidates, Eagles CB Riq Woolen appeared as a possible trade piece, given where the Eagles stand right now.
Coming off a home loss to the Panthers, the Eagles are 2-4 and just one game ahead of last place in the NFC East. Philadelphia will be without its starting QB, Jalen Hurts, for the rest of the season as he deals with blood clots.
Along with Hurts' season being cut short, the entire offense has dealt with adversity. The offensive line is a complete shell of what it used to be, riddled with injuries and an in-season retirement from Lane Johnson.
Star RB Saquon Barkley has missed two games due to a hamstring injury, but is trending towards returning. The season just isn't at all what the Eagles planned for, and with long-term questions surrounding the QB, the Eagles could be sellers and load up on as much draft compensation as possible.
Woolen, fresh off the Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl 60 victory, signed a one-year deal with the Eagles in free agency. Being on an expiring contract, and not being outstanding thus far in Philly, won't command too steep of a price.
In Knox's analysis of Woolen's trade value, he landed on a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick. Carolina doesn't own a fifth-round pick in 2027, but they do own two fourth-round picks.
The Panthers can send Philadelphia the Vikings' fourth-round pick, which was acquired in a trade that sent Adam Thielen back to Minnesota.
This gives Philadelphia another draft pick in a season when they might be more focused on the draft than on winning games, and Carolina a bona fide starter at secondary next to Will Lee III.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Carolina Panthers Star Is Finally Earning His Spot Atop the Depth Chart
full_text:
Tommy Tremble has been sitting at the top of the Panthers' tight end depth chart all season. I'm not sure many people have really thought of him as Carolina's TE1, though.
It's easy to understand why. Darren Waller is the name everybody knows, and Mitchell Evans is the young guy people want to see more of. Tremble has mostly been the guy who blocks, moves around and does whatever Carolina asks him to do.
Tremble only caught four passes against Philadelphia, but he made them count. He finished with 46 yards and scored twice in Carolina's 25-14 win.
The first touchdown came from 12 yards out in the second quarter. The second one came when Carolina really needed it.
Philadelphia had cut the lead to 19-14 and had a chance to make things interesting late. After the Panthers got the ball back with good field position, Bryce Young found Tremble for a 19-yard touchdown that pretty much shut the door.
It was the first two-touchdown game of Tremble's career. He now has 13 touchdown catches with Carolina, fourth most by a tight end in franchise history.
Maybe we've overlooked him a little bit.
One of Tremble's biggest plays didn't show up in his receiving numbers.
Carolina faced fourth-and-1 during that 94-yard touchdown drive in the second half. Tremble lined up at fullback in front of Chuba Hubbard, and Hubbard ripped off 19 yards.
The Panthers came back to the same look on another fourth-and-1 later in the game. This time they didn't even have to snap it. Young got Philadelphia to jump with a hard count.
That's a big part of why Tremble keeps finding his way onto the field. Carolina can move him around and ask him to do a little bit of everything.
The Panthers had Tremble, Waller and Evans available Sunday. Tremble still played more than either of them.
He was on the field for 54 offensive snaps. Evans played 43 and Waller played 36.
That doesn't mean Tremble is suddenly going to become a huge part of the passing game every Sunday. Through five games, he has 15 catches for 128 yards and two touchdowns. That's probably never going to be the biggest part of his game.
But look at what Carolina got from him in Philadelphia. He helped the running game, caught everything thrown his way and scored twice. When the Panthers needed a touchdown late, Young found him.
Tremble has been listed as TE1 all season.
Maybe Sunday was the first time it really felt like it.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Here's Why Derrick Brown Would Vote Bryce Young for MVP
full_text:
Through six weeks, Bryce Young has firmly inserted himself into the MVP conversation. If the season were to end today, the Carolina Panthers QB would not win the award, but he'd get some down-ballot support from voters.
He leads the NFL in passing yards per game and has 12 touchdowns to two turnovers. He's doing that while facing the most pressure in the NFL. The Panthers are 3-2 largely because of his MVP-level performance.
While Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker, and Brock Purdy exist, if you ask Panthers star Derrick Brown, Young is the MVP right now.
Derrick Brown can't vote for MVP, but if he could, he told Ratings' DJ Siddiqi that he would vote for Bryce Young. He has been that impressed by his quarterback's play through six weeks of the NFL season.
Brown said, "He’s just continuing to be himself. He never, ever let anybody else dictate what he had going on. This guy — he shows up every single day, works his a** off, and he continues to just prove all those people wrong that doubted him. I’m smiling ear to ear watching him do it."
Young has certainly made Brown's life easier. The defense doesn't have as much pressure on them because the offense is scoring a lot of points. When there is less pressure to get do-or-die stops, a defense can play a lot more freely.
What has helped set Young apart, Brown said, is "just being a person that can find the good out of anything." Whatever it is, Young can find the path forward and motivate his teammates on both sides of the ball.
What Young is doing is practically unprecedented. No one in the last decade has improved their yards per game numbers like Young from 2025-2026. He's added over 100 yards a game, an unfathomable number.
It is incredibly rare for a player to make a leap so late. By year four, players, especially quarterbacks, usually are who they are. Who Young was was a solid but inconsistent quarterback. Now, he's one of the league's best.
And while Brown is definitely biased towards his quarterback, the improving MVP odds aren't. They suggest that Young's place in the MVP race can't really be challenged . They keep going up.
NFL analyst Kevin Patra even said Young has arrived as a top-five MVP candidate this year. It's not just Brown and other players on the team. Everyone's taking notice of the immense leap Young has made, and MVP isn't so far-fetched anymore.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: 5 Realistic Panthers Trade Targets Who Won't Cost a Premium Draft Pick
full_text:
The Panthers are 3-2, and I'm still getting used to saying this, but the trade deadline actually matters in Carolina this year.
I'm not saying Dan Morgan should suddenly start throwing draft picks around because the Panthers have won three games. This team isn't one move away from a Super Bowl, and there are still plenty of areas that need work. But Carolina is right in the NFC South race, and if there's a chance to add somebody who can help without giving up a premium pick, Morgan should be on the phone.
That's what I'm looking for here. Forget the blockbuster trades that sound great until you see the price. Give me players who can help this team right now without giving away something Carolina might regret later.
We've seen Donte Jackson in Carolina before, and normally I'm not big on bringing guys back just because they're familiar. This one is a little different.
Jackson spent six seasons with the Panthers after Carolina drafted him in the second round in 2018, and he played his final year here in Ejiro Evero's defense. More importantly, the Panthers could use another corner. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are both on injured reserve, and Carolina has already had to reach pretty far down the depth chart.
Jackson is also on a Chargers team that has started 0-6. There's no guarantee Los Angeles moves him, but he's exactly the type of veteran I'd ask about if the Chargers decide to start selling.
I'm not giving up anything crazy to make the reunion happen, but a Day 3 pick for a veteran corner who already knows Evero and has starting experience? I can talk myself into that pretty quickly.
This is obviously the name everybody is going to stop on. Mack is 35 years old, so we're not talking about the guy who was terrorizing quarterbacks in Oakland and Chicago, but let's not act like he can't still get after the quarterback.
He has three sacks through six games and is playing on a one-year deal for a Chargers team that couldn't have imagined being 0-6 at this point. Mack has said he's still chasing a ring in Los Angeles, so there's no guarantee the Chargers are even willing to move him.
I'd still make the call because Carolina has had stretches this season where the pass rush has gotten home and others where the quarterback has had way too much time. Mack wouldn't have to come here and save the defense. He'd just have to make the rotation better.
The price decides everything for me. I'm not giving Los Angeles a second-round pick for a 35-year-old rental, and a third would make me nervous, too. If the conversation starts with one of Carolina's Day 3 picks, though, now you've got my attention.
This one isn't nearly as exciting as Mack, but not every deadline move has to be.
Thomas has settled into more of a rotational role at this point in his career, and that's probably what he'd be in Carolina. The Panthers don't need him to suddenly turn back into the player San Francisco thought it was getting with the No. 3 pick in 2017. They just need another experienced body up front.
We've already seen injuries test this roster, and getting Tershawn Wharton back doesn't mean Morgan should stop looking for help. Thomas gives Carolina another defensive lineman it could rotate in without asking him to be something he's not.
If Tennessee is willing to move him for a late pick, I'd be fine with it. Nobody is going to spend all day talking about the trade on ESPN, but you might be glad you made it when you're trying to get through November and December.
I know what some of you are probably thinking after watching Chuba Hubbard run for 120 yards against Philadelphia. Why in the world are we talking about another running back?
We're not talking about replacing Hubbard. I've already written about what Hubbard gives this offense , and Sunday was another example. He got stronger as the game went along, finished with 28 carries and helped Carolina put Philadelphia away in the second half.
This one would also require New York to be willing to listen. The Giants just released Najee Harris, and Tracy scored twice against New Orleans, so they may decide they need him more than they did a few weeks ago.
I'd still ask. Tracy has rushed for more than 1,600 yards over his first three seasons and can help in the passing game and on special teams. That would give Carolina another option behind Hubbard without needing to change what it's doing with its starter.
I'm not giving up much for a running back when Hubbard is already here. If the Giants are willing to talk about a late pick, though, it's worth a phone call.
This is probably the one I'm most torn on because I really like what Carolina already has with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker.
We finally got to see those two together against Philadelphia, and it looked pretty good. Coker came back with 97 yards while McMillan finished with 86 , giving Bryce Young two receivers who can make defenses pay instead of asking McMillan to do everything.
I still wouldn't mind adding Jennings. He's physical, he'll block and he's shown he can be productive when he's given opportunities. Jennings had 975 receiving yards in 2024 and nine touchdowns last season in San Francisco, but he has just two catches through four games with Minnesota this year.
With Xavier Legette on injured reserve, adding another veteran would also give Carolina some insurance instead of assuming everybody is going to stay healthy the rest of the way.
This isn't a move I'm forcing. If Minnesota wants something significant, I'm out. If the price gets low enough that Morgan can add another useful receiver without touching an important pick, then it becomes a much more interesting conversation.
That's really where I land on all of this. Carolina being 3-2 changes the conversation, but it shouldn't change the plan.
The Panthers have spent too long trying to build this thing back up to start giving away premium picks the second they get a little success. They just went into Philadelphia and won 25-14 despite committing 13 penalties for 149 yards , which tells me two things: They're good enough to be in this race, and they're still a long way from being a finished product.
So keep the first- and second-round picks, and I'd rather keep the third, too. But if Morgan can use one of those later picks to add a veteran who makes this team better for the second half of the season, go for it.
The Panthers haven't had many trade deadlines lately where buying actually made sense. This year, it does.
Just don't get crazy, Dan.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: NFL Week 7 Expert Picks Reveal Panthers' Chances to Keep Rolling vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have won two straight games over playoff hopefuls, and now they return home to face off with a team that's been a thorn in their side: the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Bucs may or may not get Baker Mayfield back for this contest, but it will be a heated rivalry game regardless. It will also be crucial for the Buccaneers to cut into Carolina's division lead, so it could be a tough game regardless of how the two teams are perceived right now.
What are the experts saying?
CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance.
Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around."
His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff is picking a Panthers win, 24-16, betting on the Bryce Young-led offense to continue clicking at home.
SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte.
"Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face... I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate," he wrote.
Here's how the rest of the SI staff is predicting this one:
Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer disagrees, predicting a 24-17 win. "Jalon Daniels is doing his best to keep the Bucs' competitive with help from the running game. The defense is also bringing a good pass rush of late. Bryce Young is locked in passing all over the field for the Panthers, however and their running game is red-hot with Chuba Hubbard," he wrote.
The Athletic's Nick Kostos picked the Buccaneers straight up and against the spread. If Jalon Daniels starts, he'll take the Panthers, but if it's Mayfield, he believes the Buccaneers will win this one.
"You just get the sense Mayfield will be better when he returns. It’s possible he was pressing after getting his desired contract extension. Mayfield will never be confused with Joe Montana, but he’s a good quarterback," he wrote.
What does this tell us? As mentioned in our coverage of the odds , Baker Mayfield's status is hugely important. But even so, there's a strange amount of belief in the 1-5 Buccaneers and a strange lack of belief in the Panthers.
They can't waltz in expecting to win, in other words.

title: Panthers' Biggest Need Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
With less than three weeks until the NFL trade deadline, the Carolina Panthers can make a move or moves to further bolster their roster as they pursue a second straight NFC South title.
Off to a 3-2 start to the year, Carolina has been one of the league's biggest surprises so far, maybe not because of the record, but because of how they got here.
The offense has been elite, led by QB Bryce Young, who is leading the NFL in passing yards per game, and is the only QB throwing for 300+ per game in the NFL.
Chuba Hubbard has regained his 2024 form , averaging 4.8 yards per carry and posting 6 total touchdowns in five games.
The offensive success is real, and OC Brad Idzik is on fire calling plays in his first season as the playcaller.
All that said, this roster still has holes, areas to clean up, and rooms heavily affected by injury. What better time to improve the roster than at the trade deadline, when teams are willing to sell on talented players.
Over the next three years, Carolina owns all but two of its draft picks and has the Vikings' fourth-round pick in the upcoming draft.
So the Panthers aren't short on draft compensation to make a deal happen, and there's clearly a belief that, given how good the offense is, they can beat top teams in the league. So where would the Panthers look if they made a move at the trade deadline? The answer is obvious.
Both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn are out for the foreseeable future. The hope is that the Panthers will get them both back in the latter half of the season, but nothing is guaranteed. Carolina currently ranks 19th in the NFL in pass defense.
Will Lee III has been solid since taking an elevated role, but he still has rookie moments where receivers beat him, most recently last Sunday, when Devonta Smith caught a 19-yard touchdown over him to make it a one-score game.
Carolina will continue to play elite receivers. In just a month, Carolina will face guys like Matthew Golden, Chris Olave, Zay Flowers, and more great pass-catchers. The secondary will need reinforcements.
Our staff has mentioned many corners that make sense for Carolina. It could be a reunion with Chargers corner Donte Jackson, a veteran on the worst team in the NFL who still has good football left in him. A name like Keishon Nixon of the Packers, who is versatile, still 29, and in the last year of his contract, also makes sense.
Those are just two examples of corners who would make sense for Carolina. No matter who the target is, the Panthers have 20 days to get a deal done and keep the secondary afloat while Jackson and Horn recover.

title: Panthers' Edge Rushers Aren't Making a Huge Impact, But It Doesn't Matter
full_text:
After the 2025 season, there was one area for the Carolina Panthers that had to be the top priority in the offseason. The Panthers were able to win the NFC South and host a playoff game despite having the worst pass rush in the NFL.
Carolina ranked dead last in sacks and in the bottom three in pressure rate, so, naturally, it was the first thing on GM Dan Morgan's list to fix. This, of course, led to the day-one free-agent signing of Jaelan Phillips, who left the Eagles to become the premier pass rusher.
So far in the 2026 season, Carolina ranks 8th in pass-rush win rate, sitting at 54% after Week 6. Along with the pass-rush success, Carolina has allowed the sixth-fewest passing touchdowns this season.
The edge rushers have had their moments this season; Phillip's hasn't been otherworldly but hasn't been a detriment either. That said, he's not the primary reason that Carolina is generating pressure
While Phillips was Carolina's splash signing in free agency, the two best signings so far have been the inside linebacker duo of Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke.
Lloyd signed with Carolina early in free agency, and Okereke was added to the roster just 48 hours before the league-wide cut date, and he immediately found his way into the starting lineup.
So far, they've been the defense's highlight. Against the Eagles, Lloyd generated an 82% pass-rush win rate, which is absurd, especially for an inside linebacker. That win rate made history, as ESPN has never recorded a higher one.
From @espn Analytics and @NextGenStats : #Panthers LB Devin Lloyd posted an 82% Pass Rush Win Rate against the #Eagles . According to ESPN Research, that’s the highest by any player in a game since ESPN started tracking win rates in 2017.
This season, Lloyd has posted 2 sacks and 4 quarterback hits, wreaking havoc on opposing QBs. After an All-Pro season in 2025, this is exactly what Carolina signed Lloyd for, and he's exceeded expectations. Lloyd has 0.5 fewer sacks than Jaelan Phillips.
The same can be said for Bobby Okereke, who's especially exceeded expectations, having been signed less than a week before cut day after his release by the New York Giants. According to PFF , Okereke ranks 11th in pass rush grade among qualifying linebackers, posting a 77.5.
Both linebackers have also thrived in pass coverage as well, combining for three interceptions this season, which is huge considering Carolina is down both their starting cornerbacks, Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson.
The defense as a whole is far from perfect , but having versatile veterans in the middle of the field who can contribute against both the run and the pass is crucial to Carolina staying in games and giving the high-powered offense good field position.

title: The Panthers Are Becoming a Different Team When the Pressure Is On
full_text:
Panthers fans have seen enough games go sideways late that you almost expect it. That's why Sunday in Philadelphia caught my attention. The Panthers didn't play a clean game, not even close, but when things got tight late, Carolina played pretty damn well.
The Panthers had 13 penalties for 149 yards, wiped out some big returns and did just about everything possible to keep the Eagles hanging around. Somehow, none of it ended up costing them. And the more I think about it, Philadelphia wasn't the first time we've seen Carolina play some of its best football late in a game.
The Panthers were up 13-7 late in the third quarter when they got the ball backed up at their own 6. This wasn't exactly great field position for a team that had spent most of the afternoon fighting penalties. Then Jalen Coker made one of the biggest plays of the game.
Carolina was facing third-and-9 from its own 10 when Bryce Young found Coker for 32 yards. Chuba Hubbard later broke a 19-yard run on fourth-and-1, and the Panthers eventually went 94 yards on 14 plays. Hubbard finished it off with the touchdown to give Carolina a 19-7 lead.
Philadelphia answered and cut it to 19-14 in the fourth quarter, and Carolina followed that by going three-and-out. Here came the Eagles again with a chance to take the lead, and we've all seen that movie before. This time, the defense got them off the field.
Tre Tyus nearly got to the punt, it went only nine yards and Carolina suddenly had the ball in Philadelphia territory. A few plays later, Young found Tommy Tremble for the touchdown. The Eagles had made their push, but Carolina never let the game get away from it.
That's probably what I liked most about those last few minutes. Everything didn't have to go right. Philadelphia scored, Carolina went three-and-out and the Eagles got the ball back with a chance to take the lead, but the Panthers still found a way to make the plays they needed.
Cleveland is the reason I'm not going to say the Panthers have completely figured this out. Carolina took an 18-13 lead with 4:25 left after Young found John Metchie III for a touchdown. They had a chance to finish that game, too.
Akayleb Evans looked like he had the interception that might have done it, only for Bobby Okereke to get called for roughing the passer. Cleveland got another shot, scored and eventually won 21-18. There were four lead changes in the fourth quarter, and Carolina didn't make enough plays at the end.
That's why I keep coming back to what happened in Philadelphia. Three weeks after letting one get away in Cleveland, the Panthers found themselves in another tight game with an opponent making a late push. This time Carolina was the team making the plays at the end.
Maybe five games isn't enough to say this has become who they are. I'm not going that far yet. But I'm starting to think there's something to it.
Detroit wasn't nearly as close going into the fourth quarter. Carolina was up 29-19, but there was still enough time left for the Lions to make things uncomfortable. Instead, the Panthers took the ball and basically made Detroit stand there and watch.
Carolina went 72 yards on 13 plays, took 5:44 off the clock and got a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal out of it. Nothing spectacular happened, but I loved that drive. You're up 10 in the fourth quarter, so keep the ball, burn almost six minutes and come away with points.
Detroit eventually scored to make it 32-26, but by then there wasn't enough time left for the Lions to get another possession. Carolina had already taken care of that with the drive to start the quarter. Sometimes that's all you need when you're trying to finish a game.
Dave Canales talked Monday about learning how to play with a lead. I don't know if I'm ready to say the Panthers have learned it yet, especially after what happened in Cleveland. But I do think they're getting better at it.
Sunday wasn't just Young making a play or Hubbard taking over. Coker made the third-down catch when Carolina was backed up, Hubbard got the fourth-and-1 and the defense got Philadelphia off the field when the Eagles had a chance to take the lead. Tyus nearly got to the punt, helping Carolina get the short field, and Young finished it with the touchdown to Tremble.
That's a lot of different guys showing up when Carolina needed somebody to make a play. For a long time, it felt like the Panthers needed almost everything to go right to win. One bad penalty, one bad possession or one big play by the other team could change everything.
Sunday definitely wasn't perfect. You don't get 13 penalties for 149 yards and call that a clean afternoon, but Carolina still walked out of Philadelphia with a 25-14 win. Maybe that's another sign this team is starting to figure out how to handle these games.
I'm not trying to turn a 3-2 start into something bigger than it is. Cleveland happened, there are 12 games left and I'm sure there are going to be a few more Sundays that drive all of us crazy. But I'm starting to feel a little different when these games get tight.
Instead of sitting there waiting for something to go wrong, I'm starting to wonder who's going to make the play.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Ben Johnson Lets It Ride with Cairo Santos as Bears Come Away Winners
full_text:
Cairo Santos was still irritated with himself after the Bears won 30-24 over the New England Patriots.
The team record 58-yard field goal he made, the longest in his career, let the Bears escape with a win and was nice but he could have made it much easier for everyone simply by making a 53-yarder that doinked off the right upright in the south end zone earlier in the fourth quarter.
By giving the Bears a 30-21 lead inside the final two minutes, Santos actually tied Robbie Gould's team record for distance at 58 yards, a mark set in the 2013 season opener. The field goal came after Caleb Wiliams took a sack, when he could have simply thrown away the ball and let Santos try from a much easier 48 yards instead of 58.
The sack left coach Ben Johnson with a big decision. Leading by six, did he punt from the Patriots 40. Right. Ben Johnson punt from the 40? Fat chance. He also could have gone for it but Williams' sack left them in fourth-and-15.
A career-long 58-yard FG from Bears kicker Cairo Santos — and a gutsy decision from HC Ben Johnson. pic.twitter.com/wDNqEVwzxV
So Johnson just did what coaches do. He asked the kicker what he wanted to do. After all, Santos was near the end of his range .
"It's close," Johnson said. "But, it's one of those things. A lot of time and effort goes into it. Our process pregame tells us a lot about how he's feeling and what we feel like those maximum distance lines are.
"One, we felt good about being inside that line, and two, we asked him, he said, ‘Absolutely, I need redemption because I missed one earlier.’ He came through for us in a big way.”
No doubt the missed 53-yarder will aggravate a faction of Bears fans who think they need a kicker like Jacksonville or Dallas have, who can 65-yard kicks. The answer always had been Santos has better accuracy, but he has slipped this year.
Still, there's much to be said for hitting it when it really counts, and besides, those 65-yard kickers don't grow on trees.
It might be time to end the Cairo Santos era in Chicago. In a time where so many NFL teams are easily nailing kicks from 50+ yards, you can’t haven’t someone who’s consistently a liability like this from long distance. #Bears
The 53-yarder was eating at Santos afterward, and no doubt still does, because when everyone else was still celebrating in the locker room the Bears kicker wasn't.
"I'm having a hard time just celebrating these moments and I shouldn't act this way but I just feel like I'm hitting the ball way too good to have these misses happen," Santos said.
Santos missed from 56 in Atlanta on a kick that had plenty of distance. He missed a 43-yarder against Green Bay and had a 23-yard chip shot blocked due to poor blocking.
"Even though they're from 50-plus, I've been making them all the time so I'm just annoyed and have to get back to work and keep pushing through," he said.
4th and 11 · Chicago Bears Cairo Santos ( @cairosantos19 ) 53 yard field goal is No Good, Hit Right Upright, Center-Scott Daly, Holder-Tory Taylor https://t.co/knlJSHswuR pic.twitter.com/ZxvSNuwuBX
Santos said he felt strong in pregame and his range was 62 yards going north and 60 going the direction of his miss and his 58-yarder.
He did admit the miss from 53 was, "...  as close of a miss as you can have," after it seemed to strike the inner part of the upright.
"I'm just thankful they gave me the chance to bounce back," Santos added.
The Bears didn't need a 65-yard guy then. A 58-yard guy was just fine.
Cairo Santos breaks down his mindset on making his career-high 58-yard field goal tonight 🐻⬇️ pic.twitter.com/hhxGTuhxIq

title: Caleb Williams Has All the Answers in Showdown with Drake Maye
full_text:
Caleb Williams was in his element and a few dropped passes or a long missed field goal wouldn't spoil his night.
The Bears quarterback won out in a big-play dual against Drake Maye and the Bears won 30-24 after Cairo Santos clinched it with a personal long 58-yard field goal.
"These nights are awesome," said Williams, who was 22 of 33 for 308 yards and two TDs. "You play against another good team  on a prime time game in a short week. These games are awesome because you get to see who you are as a team.
"That's who we are. We're a smash-mouth football team, an innovative team. And when things happen and things don't go our way and the water is rocky, we stay steady. We're going to keep going, we're going to keep fighting."
So much for that depth-of-target chatter or whatever that was  ... https://t.co/Epmx4CKXHp
Williams kept throwing even when it seemed the game was slipping away. His third-and-9 rocket over the middle for 21 yards to Rome Odunze got the Bears out of a hole at their 10-yard line and sent them on the march to Santos' 58-yard field goal and a 30-21 lead in the final two minutes. On the prior drive, the Bears ate clock but got no points when Santos missed a 58-yarder off the right upright but Williams bailed them out with a third-and-11 strike for 21 yards to Odunze on a similar pass.
Odunze finished with four catches for 69 yards, Colston Loveland seven for 69 yards and Luther Burden lit it up in the first half with all four of his catches for 130 yards and Williams just kept matching Maye, who finished 24 of 31 for 321 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.
CALEB WILLIAMS TO LUTHER BURDEN ON THE SCREEN PASS pic.twitter.com/kSBWH8cEqJ
Williams  admitted to feeling that personal rivalry with Maye, who was drafted third in 2024 after Williams was first. The two are 1-1 in games with each other, while Williams is 1-1 against the second overall pick, Jayden Daniels.
"I think any competitor, it doesn't matter the sport, is when something happens and the other guy that great quarterback, he's been a great quarterback for years, and so when that happens you want to go out there: 'Let's go get one, let's put the score back up, let's match that score from there.' And I think we did just that," Williams said.
Luther Burden in space is a problem for defenses. pic.twitter.com/49Uv7cE4PF
"That's a great team over there. Defensive wise they do a great job. Offensively they obviously do a great job. They're well coached. We just made a few more plays today."
One was a 57-yarder he threw to Burden early to set up a touchdown. Just before halftime he threw a wide receiver screen to Burden, who bolted through a crowd for a 24-yard TD. Loveland caught a 12-yard TD pass on the first drive of the second half to put the Bears up 27-14 and get back momentum after a disastrous end to the first half.
"I thought all of our pass catchers stepped up and had some big nights," coach Ben Johnson said. "Luther started us off with the big spark there early, Colston kind of took it in the middle and then Rome came through with some big ones at the end that were huge for us."
If anyone had doubts about Williams for throwing so short last week but playing effectively, he took this one the opposite way on Thursday and averaged 9.3 yards per pass attempt with a 116.7 passer rating. The
Caleb Williams passing chart vs. Patriots Just elite stuff once again pic.twitter.com/1COBkfpsvJ
"I think he did a pretty good job throughout the night," Johnson said. "I know he had a number of explosive plays. He found some of those guys at the second level that were huge for us. It took us a little bit to get the running game, feeling the running game and so he was able to extend those drives by being fairly accurate in the passing game."
Williams kept going back to his targets after poor plays. Loveland dropped a couple but got targeted for a big conversion on fourth-and-2 and a 9-yard catch over the middle. Odunze had an offensive pass interference but Williams came back to him late as they were able to protect the lead.
"I told Rome, we looked at each other right after we had that pass interference, OPI, down there in the red zone, that I'll come back to you," Williams said. "We didn't know when, and it ended up being a big part of the game.”
Good luck falling asleep after this one pic.twitter.com/YWvaOMGQIr
Williams avoided any more problems with his hamstring and set the Bears  up well at 5-2 for their next big showdown type of game against the other 2025 Super Bowl combatant, the Seahawks.
"We're in a good spot," Williams said. "Obviously a long season and we've got guys that go down we've got guys that come back off injuries, all that."
It looks like one will be Cole Kmet, with a knee injury. Even that rough play near game's end couldn't dampen the feeling the Bears had after seeing Willliams go toe-to-toe with a Super Bowl qualifier and win out.
"So like I said I feel good going into this extended period before this next game," Williams said. "I'll be able to get an ample amount of time to rest, an ample amount of time to get ready for these next guys."
Caleb Williams Rome Odunze pic.twitter.com/kmta0MiQqq

title: 4 Winners and 3 Losers From Chicago Bears Impressive Week 7 Win Against Patriots
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came away with a win over the New England Patriots in a 30-24 thriller on Thursday night. They moved to 5-3 and cemented their status as a legit contender (to those who were still unconvinced) by knocking off the defending AFC champions.
The Bears got off to a quick start, but the Patriots promptly answered back (immediately) before halftime. There was a notion that the matchup could be a potential Super Bowl preview , and it lived up to that billing from a competitive standpoint.
The defense struggled mightily against Drake Maye and Co., and they had a few rough performances on that side of the ball. Meanwhile, the offense (and special teams unit) featured a handful of promising ones .
Who were the most significant instances of each?
Luther Burden III is becoming a feature on these weekly installments . Is there a receiver in the NFL who is better with the ball in his hands than Burden right now? If there is, then there certainly aren't many of them. He followed last week's eight-catch, 95-yard performance with a four-catch, 130-yard showing tonight.
While he didn't make a dent in the stat sheets in the second half, his first-half performance was more than enough to warrant a spot on this list. Even with Rome Odunze catching fire late, it's quickly become clear who the top receiver in the Bears offense is. On that note...
No block, no rock. Unfortunately, rookie receiver Zavion Thomas' blocking issues are not due to a lack of effort. We'll soon see whether the saying "no legal block, no rock" applies to him. Two holding penalties nullified big plays on the ground tonight.
Now, it's also worth noting that one of those holding calls (the second one that took away a  D'Andre Swift first-down run) was highly questionable. Still, with a ref crew that had an eagle eye for anything that looked close to holding, he should've been a bit more careful in that spot. To Thomas' credit (because I do like what he's shown overall, sue me), he did have a huge 47-yard kick return in the second quarter.
D'Marco Jackson easily had the best performance we've seen from a Bears linebacker this season. He was all over the field from the first snap. The end zone interception is obviously the biggest highlight, but he was equally strong against the run. He shot running lanes left and right and is much more a force near the line of scrimmage than Devin Bush.
Jackson finished second on the team with six tackles and he also had a pass deflection. The 28-year-old might not be their biggest name at linebacker, but he's clearly the most well-rounded of the group. He should have a huge role every week, regardless of T.J. Edwards' status.
Cam Lewis played awful tonight. He took poor angles in run support all night, and should lose his blitz privileges if defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can stomach such a thought. Drake Maye shook him out of his cleats a few times, and he lost contain when pinning his ears back more often than not.
It also seemed like Rhamondre Stevenson was his assignment on the unacceptable screen pass that went for a touchdown before halftime (although he might've been on a blitz). He was a step slow in pursuit the whole way, and is at least partially to blame (and fully to blame if that was his assignment) for that play.
Caleb Williams was dealing tonight. Williams notably made a few key plays on third down to keep drives extended. He still doesn't look like he has the same breakaway speed that he had prior to suffering a hamstring injury, but he's been able to get it done with his arm .
Williams completed 22 of 33 attempts for 308 yards and 2 passing TDs tonight. He also added 18 yards on the ground. Unfortunately, Williams almost lost his spot on this list (not really, but it was bad) late in the contest after taking an unacceptable sack that nearly knocked them out of field goal range. However, Cairo Santos bailed him out with a career-long 58-yard kick to make it a two-score game.
Simply put, Drake Maye was on the money tonight. Aside from his rough interception, he was consistently finding the open man whenever the Bears sent extra rushers. He also showed an innate ability to evade the rush and make plays outside the pocket.
Dennis Allen had the Patriots offense on their heels early on, but their counter-punch was far more potent. While Maye deserves a ton of credit for their success through the air, Chicago's defense also deserves some blame for a flat showing. I've already highlighted the TD before halftime that I'm going to try very hard to forget, but that was only one of many plays where they were caught out of position.
Cairo Santos is the hero of tonight's matchup. He absolutely nailed a 58-yard attempt to make it a nine-point game with 1:28 left in the game, and he didn't even make fans sweat it (much) by sending it right down the middle. Not only was it Santos' career long by three yards , but it was the third-longest field goal in Soldier Field history. The fact that Ben Johnson had enough confidence in him to send him out in that spot is also huge.
He more than made up for a miss from 53 yards earlier in the contest (a doink off the upright, naturally). All concerns surrounding Santos leg strength are effectively null-and-void. The most accurate kicker in franchise history came through clutch once again, and he'll stick around for the remainder of his career.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Caleb Williams Calls Out Richard Sherman After Bears Beat Patriots in Week 7
full_text:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams let ex-NFL player and current Prime Video analyst Richard Sherman know he wasn't too pleased with the former cornerback's power rankings going into Week 7.
Williams joined the Prime Video crew after the win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night and discussed how the time he missed due to his hamstring injury added more fire to him.
And while talking about that, Williams called out Sherman and said he hopes Sherman will now put the Bears in the top five of his power rankings after the victory over the Pats.
"That time off just added a little bit more to me," Williams said. "And I'm going to keep using it, keep bringing that energy, that fire in my eyes, I'm going to release it to my teammates, and hopefully to the fans, they feel my energy."
"And hopefully we can get in your top five," Williams added while looking right at Sherman.
Sherman absolutely loved it.
"Yeah!" Sherman said while laughing and banging on the desk. "I like that Caleb! He watches the podcast."
"I see it all," Williams responded.
Sherman went on to note that not only did he pick the Bears to win, but he is also going to put the Bears in his top five.
"I had them winning this game. They make it in my top five," Sherman said.
Going into the weekend of Week 7, the Bears are one of five teams in the NFL to have five wins, so they are definitely worthy of being in the top five in power rankings.
Chicago looks like a true contender through seven games with an elite head coach and offense, and a defense that is perfectly complementing the other side of the ball.
To further bolster their case, the Bears just knocked off one of the hottest teams in the NFL in the Patriots, who are also the reigning AFC champions.
Get excited, Bears fans, this team looks like it can do big things in 2026.
Outside of that sloppy mess of a game in Week 2 that was played in terrible weather conditions, Williams has looked like a signal-caller who is well on his way to elite status.
He has now posted three sensational peformances in four games and has thrown for over 300 yards in each of the last two contests.
There is no doubt he is much-improved from where he was last season, whether you want to talk about his accuracy, decision-making or his pocket presence. The game has very obviously slowed down for Chicago's QB1.
If there's one thing we're confident in saying after seeing what he has put on tape this season, it's that the Bears can beat anyone as long as No. 18 is on the field.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Ben Johnson's 'Stanky Leg' Alive and Well in Postgame Speech After Bears Top Patriots
full_text:
Ben Johnson's "stanky leg" celebration is alive and well.
The Chicago Bears head coach enjoyed yet another electric postgame speech after his team knocked off the reigning AFC champions , the New England Patriots, on Thursday night, 30-24.
And, after giving his speech and handing out some game balls, Johnson made sure to do what has now become his signature move in the aftermath of Bears wins.
Check out Johnson's full postgame speech and his latest interation of the "stanky leg" in the video below.
Good luck falling asleep after this one pic.twitter.com/YWvaOMGQIr
Johnson's four game balls went to Rome Odunze, D'Marco Jackson, Luther Burden and Cairo Santos, all of whom had massive contributions to the victory over the Pats.
As Johnson noted in his postgame speech, the win over the Pats was far from easy.
It looked like Chicago might cruise early, but a defensive lapse at the end of the first half allowed New England to gain some much-needed momentum going into the break.
Things slowed down for the Bears' offense in the second half, but as good teams do, they found a way to hold strong and pull out the win to improve to 5-2 going into the weekend.
Now the Bears will see how the rest of the week unfolds for their divisional foes. The best Chicago can land in is second place, as the first-place Minnesota Vikings are up multiple games on the Bears with a 5-0 record and a win over Chicago from Week 2.
The Vikings have a matchup with the flailing Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, and the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, who sit in third and fourth place, respectively, will square off in their first showdown of the season.
If the Packers lose, the Bears will own second place in the division, but they'll fall to third if Green Bay beats Detroit thanks to the former's win over Chicago in Week 5.
Looking ahead, the Bears will have 11 days worth of rest before they meet the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8 at Lumen Field in what will be yet another tough test against the reigning Super Bowl champions.
While it's way too early to talk about the playoff picture, we'll go over that anyway.
The highest the Bears can be going into Week 8 is the No. 5 spot, and they can't go any lower than No. 6. The spot the Bears land in will again depend on what the Packers do against the Lions.
Beyond that, the Bears would have to lose two straight games and the Seahawks would have to win two straight for the Bears to even have a chance to fall out of a playoff spot, so Chicago has a fairly comfortable cushion after seven games.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Game Balls in Bears' Sensational Primetime Win over Patriots
full_text:
Whatever doubt that lingered around the Chicago Bears before the 2026 NFL season has now fully evaporated. By defeating the New England Patriots, the AFC champions from a year ago, in front of the entire country, the Bears have proven that their 2025 season was no fluke, and that those fans and analysts who picked them to be a legit Super Bowl contender were right to believe in them.
This matchup was always going to be one of the hardest games on the Bears' 2026 schedule , one that would serve as a true litmus test for where the team stands in Year 2 of the Ben Johnson era, and they passed with flying colors. It was touch-and-go for a while, and it came down to the game's final minute, but the Bears pulled it off and deserve all the credit in the world for this win.
We'll have plenty of time to analyze this win in-depth over the weekend and even throughout next week as the Bears now enter their mini-bye with a 5-2 record. For now, let's hand out some game balls, starting with the man of the hour.
Similar to the Bears as a team, Caleb Williams himself entered this season with plenty of doubt around him. People wanted to know if last year a fluke or a sign of even greater things to come. Without a doubt, the answer is the latter. Williams was brilliant again this week against a tough New England defense, completing 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and a pair of touchdowns, which was almost exactly what I put in my stat predictions for this Bears-Patriots game .
Both Williams and New England's Drake Maye put on a show for the NFL world, but Williams walked out with the win. The Bears can now rest easy this weekend, and Williams has the added satisfaction of getting vengeance against Maye and the Patriots , as well as this game ball.
The Bears entered 2026 with a question as to who would be their WR1 on the depth chart in 2026 , and Burden has seized that title and won't let it go. He caught all four of his targets for 130 yards, including turning a screen pass on third-and-17 into a touchdown. Even better, he was just two yards short of a two-touchdown day.
Again and again, Burden showed up when the Bears needed him most, making big plays and putting points on the board and helping put the Patriots away. For that, he gets a game ball.
I struggled with who deserved this last game ball the most, and I decided to go with the guy who potentially saved the game while it was still in the first half: linebacker D'Marco Jackson. On New England's penultimate first half drive, Drake Maye was driving New England down the field and a touchdown seemed inevitable. Instead, Jackson stepped in front of a pass intended for tight end Eli Raridon in the endzone and snagged just his second career interception.
This ended up being a 14-point swing in Chicago's favor, and for that reason this last game ball goes to Jackson.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Chicago Bears' Week 7  Victory Over New England Patriots
full_text:
The Chicago Bears improved to 5-2 on the 2026 season after beating the New England Patriots on Thursday night, 30-24.
The Bears were absolutely rolling on offense in the first half and looked like they might run away with the game before the Pats managed to pull off an improbable touchdown in the closing seconds that flipped the momentum.
However, the Bears didn't let that wreck the game and Chicago was able to do enough over the final two quarters to eventually come away with the win over the reigning AFC champs.
Now, a look at the biggest takeaways from the Bears' Week 7 win over the Patriots.
Caleb Williams continues to ascend toward elite status after yet another impressive showing on Thursday night.
It's clear the game has slowed down for Williams considerably and there is no doubt his accuracy has improved by leaps and bounds.
Williams finished 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns to zero picks. The third-year signal-caller also added four carries for 19 yards. He should have had at least two more completions and more yards, but Colston Loveland dropped two passes.
Chicago's offense sputtered a bit in the second half, but it still was moving the ball throughout the final two quarters and the first half performance was enough to put the Bears over the top.
Burden went quiet in the second half, but he was dominant over the first two quarters.
Burden finished with 130 yards on four catches and notched catches of 58 and 24 yards, with the latter going for a score. The 58-yarder set up the Bears' first touchdown of the game.
The yardage output was the most for Burden in a game this year, and it was the second-highest amount of his career. He continues cementing himself as Chicago's true No. 1 wideout.
The Bears gave up two long touchdowns, one on a 48-yard catch and run to running back Rhamondre Stevenson, and the other came on a 30-yard catch by tight end Eli Raridon.
The one to Stevenson was especially egregious, as it came with no time left on the clock at the end of the first half and saw awful effort from Jaylon Johnson, and Malik Muhammad simply ran in the wrong direction of the play.
According to CBS Sports' Doug Clawson , there have been 1,006 attempts in the last 20 years that have seen a situation in which a team was in the final 10 seconds of a half, was 40-plus yards away from the end zone and threw a pass that traveled 10 or fewer air yards and the Patriots are the only team to score.
If you take out those two plays, it would have been a solid night for the defense, which continues to play good football overall.
D'Marco Jackson was one of the best players on the field for the Bears and notched a pick, and Kyler Gordon had another sack and Austin Booker and Daniel Hardy split one.
Despite being short-handed, we've been impressed with the effort from the defense. Now, Chicago will get Montez Sweat back in Week 8, as he's eligible to come back from suspension.
Nobody can ever say Ben Johnson doesn't have guts.
Despite Cairo Santos having struggles from 50-plus yards this season and missing a field goal from that distance in the fourth quarter, Johnson decided to roll with Santos again on a 58-yard try in the final two minutes of the game.
There was a ton riding on the kick, as a miss would have set the Pats up near midfield with a chance to take the lead. Making the decision even riskier was the fact that Santos had never made a field goal from that distance during his career.
However, Santos repaid Johnson's faith in him by drilling the kick, which put the Bears up nine and sealed the victory for Chicago.
Had Santos missed, Johnson would have faced heavy criticism, as not only would the decision to go for the field goal be ripped, but Johnson's decision to throw on third down before that would've been ripped to shreds, also.
Muhammad came down with a toe injury in the third quarter of the game and did not return. It appears to have happened on his pass break-up on a deep ball to A.J. Brown.
This is obviously a situation to monitor over the next week-plus, as Muhammad has been the Bears' best cornerback this season and Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson have been total liabilities.
The good news is, the Bears have extra rest before their Week 8 game, which takes place on Monday night.
Kmet suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and did not return. Unfortunately, he needed the cart to take him off the field, so it looks like a significant injury for him.
If that ends up being the case, rookie tight end Sam Roush is going to see a massive role moving forward. Hopefully, Kmet's injury isn't as bad as it looked.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Cole Kmet Injury Update: Ben Johnson Fearing the Worst For Bears Tight End
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an injury concern with tight end Cole Kmet after the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots.
Kmet suffered his injury in the fourth quarter after making a catch. He immediately grabbed at his knee after the play and stayed down on the field before being carted off.
Prior to his exit, Kmet had tallied three catches for 28 yards.
Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Kmet's status following the Week 7 contest.
UPDATE: After the game, head coach Ben Johnson did not sound optimistic about Kmet's injury.
"We'll know more tomorrow, but I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said .
It looks like our worst fears will be realized, but we'll have to wait for an update for confirmation. That could come down on Friday.
UPDATE: The Bears announced that Kmet has suffered a knee injury and is out for the game .
The fact that Kmet was immediately ruled out is a sign he suffered a significant injury, but we'll have to wait for more information from the team after the game.
It's possible that update could come from head coach Ben Johnson and hopefully it's not as bad as it looks.
END OF UPDATE (in-game updates are listed below)
UPDATE: Kmet has been carted off the field and players were showing clear concern for him, which is terrible news.
Making matters worse, Kmet wasn't able to put weight on his right leg. For now, it looks like a knee injury, but we can't say for certain.
"They have the cart for Cole Kmet and looked like he wasn't putting weight on his right leg," Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune wrote.
Here's the play in which Kmet got hurt.
Cole Kmet knee injury #dabears pic.twitter.com/FCSM5LUBUU
Still waiting for an update from the team.
There is obvious concern for Kmet immediately after the play. As we said, he was clutching at his knee and was in obvious pain, which has us fearing the worst initially.
However, we don't have an official update on his situation yet, so we're holding out hope it's nothing serious.
With Kmet obviously out for at least the rest of the game, the Bears will need more out of rookie tight end Sam Roush.
Losing Kmet is a blow for a few reasons, as not only is he a plus pass-catcher, he's also a very good blocker. The Bears also love to run multiple tight-end sets and Roush amounts to a downgrade from the veteran.

title: Malik Muhammad Injury Update: Latest News on Bears CB's Status in Week 7 Game
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an injury concern with cornerback Malik Muhammad in the second half of the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots.
Muhammad got hurt in the third quarter. It isn't clear if he was injured on the deep ball he successfully defended against A.J. Brown or if he got hurt on the next play.
Nevertheless, Muhammad is now out of the game for now. Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Muhammad's status for the rest of the game against New England.
UPDATE: Muhammad is dealing with a toe injury and is doubtful to return, the Bears announced.
The doubtful tag means it is highly unlikely Muhammad will return. It'll be Tyrique Stevenson in his place the rest of the night.
UPDATE: Adam Jahns of CHGO Bears is now reporting that Muhammad is headed to the locker room, which is bad news for his chances of returning to the game.
"Bears rookie CB Malik Muhammad II is headed to the locker room. He got hurt on the play after his nice PBU vs. AJ Brown," Jahns wrote.
UPDATE: Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune reports that the rookie cornerback has emerged from the tent for a second time and is now running on the sideline.
"Bears CB Malik Muhammad doing some running on the sideline. He just came out of the medical tent for the 2nd time," Biggs reported.
That seems to be a good sign for his chances of returning. We're still waiting for an update from the team.
Muhammad stayed down on the field after the play and was being tended to by trainers.
He was, however, able to walk off the field under his own power and is now getting checked out in the medical tent .
It looks like Muhammad is dealing with either an ankle or foot injury, but we can't say for sure until the team offers an update.
We'll update this page once more information is known.
Muhammad started on the boundary for the Bears on Thursday night. As long as he's out, the Bears will be deploying Tyrique Stevenson opposite Jaylon Johnson.
That's not good news, as Stevenson has struggled all season long. Muhammad has easily been the Bears' best cornerback overall, even over Johnson, who has also been bad.
Entering Week 7, Muhammad, who was drafted in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, allowed a completion rate of 57.1% and a passer rating of 82.6 when targeted.
Muhammad started off the year in the slot while Kyler Gordon was working his way back from a calf injury that had him sidelined from the offseason through the first handful of games in the regular season.
Muhammad did see some snaps on the outside in that span, but he has since moved to full-time boundary snaps since Gordon's return and re-insertion into the slot.
Along with Johnson, Stevenson and Gordon, the Bears also have Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips active at cornerback. Cam Lewis is capable of playing slot cornerback if needed.
