title: Jaylon Johnson Called Out For Dismal Effort on End of Half TD in Bears vs. Patriots
full_text:
Jaylon Johnson's disastrous 2026 season just got worse at the end of the first half of the Week 7 game between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears.
The Bears looked like they were going to cruise into halftime with a two-score lead after a Luther Burden score in the closing seconds of the first half on a pass from Caleb Williams.
However, after the Patriots got up to midfield on a big play to A.J. Brown, Drake Maye hit his running back, Rhamondre Stevenson, with a dump-off and Stevenson ended up taking it to the house, cutting the Bears lead to 20-13.
It was a total defensive breakdown, but Johnson's lack of effort was especially glaring, as he had a chance to tackle Stevenson before completly whiffing with his putrid attempt.
Jaylon Johnson not good. #DaBears #Besrs pic.twitter.com/hScojUHwT2
"He needs to be benched. He didn’t want to tackle Drake Maye, and now this. It looks like business decisions," one fan said .
"He doesn’t want to compete. It’s obvious," another fan said.
"Just cut him," said another Bears fan.
The frustration is understandable, as tackling hasn't been Johnson's only issue this season.
The veteran cornerback has not been good in coverage, either, as evidenced by his 78.6% completion rate and 130.7 passer rating when targeted going into Week 7.
Johnson's struggles are a continuation of his issues from last year, when he didn't play at the level we expect, either. That was chalked up to Johnson not being at 100%, but that excuse is no longer valid because Johnson has been healthy all season.
At this rate, Johnson may not be on the team next season. In fact, Johnson even admitted this is basically a contract year for him before the season started.
"This is definitely a contract year. We all know with the cap hit and all that stuff. It's definitely a contract year for me so at the end of the day, whether that's here or somewhere else, I gotta put it on tape that I am still a top guy," Johnson said.
According to Over The Cap , the Bears have an out in Johnson's contract in 2027. They would incur a $9 million dead-cap hit by cutting him, but also a cap savings of $16 million.
After what we've seen over seven weeks this season, it's safe to say Johnson is in serious danger of getting cut in the offseason. He needs a major turnaorund to avoid that fate.

title: Dexter Lawrence Reveals Bengals' Key to Stopping Derrick Henry and Ravens
full_text:
Dexter Lawrence and the Bengals defense sport a double dose of tough running matchups to handle this weekend.
Lawrence and that unit are preparing for how Lamar Jackson (ankle) is going to play, and they know they'll have to deal with Derrick Henry. The beast of a running back has ripped Cincinnati apart in his career.
Across eight matchups, Henry's posted 5.4 yards per carry and five touchdowns, including four touchdowns in the past five battles and 11 carries for 100 yards in the final meeting last year.
The whole group has to tackle as one. Cincinnati ranks 24th in rushing yards per game allowed this season largely due to big plays (28th in rushing EPA allowed, 14th in success rate).
“It's going to be a good challenge. My emphasis today at practice was just that we gotta tackle this week," Lawrence told Bengals radio voice Dan Hoard and CLNS Media's Mike Petraglia on Wednesday. "We got to wrap him up, and we got to bring him down. So just watching how he runs the ball, he's a big dude running the ball. If I can say so, like when I was running the ball back in the day, but I think with a guy like him, just the big guys up front just can't let him climb to the second level. We got to build a wall and keep him behind it.”
Lawrence has transformed this run defense in a very positive way.
The veteran has an 82.5 Pro Football Focus grade on 226 snaps and has helped Cincinnati lead the league in run-stuff rate so far (23.93%). Something's gotta give between these two monsters on opposite sides of the ball.
He's searching for the first "complete game" of the Bengals season defensively.
"Just play a complete game, as complete as we can play," Lawrence said about the goal on Sunday. "We know it's not gonna be perfect, but some of the mistakes that we've had that can be there. They can be eliminated."

title: 'Just Gonna Dead It' - Ja'Marr Chase Reveals Future of  'People's Elbow' Celebration After Fine Flip
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase spoke to the media for the first time in a few weeks on Thursday. The superstar receiver has a massive game on deck this weekend against Baltimore, and even though he won his celebration fine appeal against the NFL, don't expect the "people's elbow" to make a return near the Chesapeake Bay.
Chase is letting a sleeping dog rest and not touching those celebration moves anymore despite the league siding with his reasoning for bringing it out in the first place.
"If we could do the celly, we would bring it back, but I don't think they're gonna let us," Chase said. "You know what I'm saying? So it's too many opinions on the celebration, so they're probably just gonna dead it. But I'm just happy that I got a chance to get the opportunity to win my money back."
The NFL fined Tee Higgins four times and Chase twice from doing the celebration in September's game against Houston. The two players were fined $89,556 total for the arm signage.
That's behind Chase; now he's focused on igniting what's been a pretty light season in terms of receiving yards so far (289 yards through five games).
"Started off pretty slow, first game. Haven't had a 100-yard game yet. I think that's a really big key on why I'm so low," Chase noted. "But I'm getting good opportunities. Defense is changing looks, and there hasn't been too many downfield passes for me to make the 100 yards, but they're still using me a good way."
Chase hasn't played under the Baltimore sun since 2021, when he was late for a team activity that week, but still balled out with eight catches for 201 yards and a touchdown.
"I got fined for damn near missing a whole meeting that week that year," Chase said. "So I actually had to play good. I came late to a morning practice, and yeah, I think it was a Friday or Saturday I came late and then after the game, after we won, they (the coaches) was like, 'If you doing stuff like that, you come late every time.' So that's a good little part."
Chase has tightened up the time allocation much better in the ensuing half decade. He takes on the Baltimore secondary Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Solid Cincinnati Health Continues as Attention Focuses on Lamar Jackson
full_text:
The Bengals injury report stayed pretty clean on Thursday.
Cincinnati is battling Baltimore on the road at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday and even had their lone player upgrade on the injury status line. Kyle Dugger (quad) went full in Thursday's practice.
No other Bengals popped up on the injury report .
Meanwhile, Baltimore star Lamar Jackson (ankle) went limited again on Thursday after practicing Wednesday for the first time  since suffering the injury in Week 4.
His status is a bit murky, but he did a lot more at practice today and now seems like near-lock to play in the contest. The Ravens should definitely have newly added center Cam Jurgens on the field after he recovered from a concussion. He practiced fully on Wednesday and Thursday.
Ravens fans are hoping he's snapping to Jackson and not Tyler Huntley on Sunday.
“Lamar [Jackson] was actually able to get a little bit of limited work in today in preparation. So, that’s where that’s at. Again, it’s a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said about Jackson on Wednesday before commenting on the specific workload. "[I am] not really [going] to get into the specifics of anything with that. I know this, when it’s ready for [Lamar Jackson] to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that’s the best thing to do; that’s what we’ll do.”
Minter sounded very confident Jurgens will play. Most of the other notable injured names like Mark Andrews (hand) and Calais Campbell (rest) are dealing with minor problems or just rested on Wednesday. A lot of Ravens upgraded to full showings in practice.
“Yes, Cam [Jurgens]’s doing great," Minter noted. "I think the weekend was really good for him to get past the protocol, and also allow him a lot of time to really, really pick up on things and study. So, again, he’s done a really good job. He’s a veteran. He’s played in a couple of different offensive systems now, which I think I mentioned a while back. [The Eagles] had a system there. Then they learned a new one this year. So, I think he’ll really be in tune and ready to be able to help us this week.”

title: 'In Here Reading Books' - Ja'Marr Chase Details Quick Concussion Recovery
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase is back behind the podcast microphone this week after a break due to his concussion and the Bengals bye week.
Cincinnati's best player broke down how the whole concussion process played out in the most detailed comments yet about the injury .
Chase suffered more of a "whiplash" concussion because of how he got twisted on the play against Jacksonville.
Although he's not holding any ill will towards the Jaguars.
"I thought I was really fine. But after seeing the video, I felt like it was more like a whiplash concussion from just my neck being hit side to side," Chase noted. "I don't think it was anything too crazy from a player. No dirty play. I just think it was maybe a reaction of him trying to grab me or something like that. I can't say he was trying to play dirty at the end of the day; after I really got up and stuff, that's when I found out.
"When you get a concussion, you don't know until they tell you, 'Let's go talk to you.' Then they pull you in a tent, and they ask you a couple questions. Depends on how many questions you get right."
It was Chase's first concussion of his NFL (and possibly) playing career, so he had a chance to return the next week against Miami, and did just that.
He had to be off his phone all week and stay away from screens to let his brain recover in time for the Miami bout.
Chase stuck to paper books for entertainment the old-fashioned way. He did a lot of reading in the past few weeks, including books like The Superior Man, and The 48 Laws of Power.
"I didn't really sit in the dark room. I tried to stay in like a routine to make sure I was okay at the end of the day," Chase said. "But I didn't really wear shades that much. I wore shades on the regular when we had walk-throughs ... I wasn't on my phone. I couldn't play video games. I was in here reading books just to keep my mind off stuff."
Ja'Marr Chase Book Club could be a fun segment on the podcast moving forward.

title: Bengals Top Fit For Potential Secondary Trade Option Ahead of 2026 Deadline
full_text:
Trade deadline season is upon us, and Cincinnati could push in some assets to the middle of the table to improve their 2026 roster. One way to really round out the defensive secondary depth could be to go after Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.
The 30-year-old has one more full season left on his current contract extension. He's struggled with a 52.4 Pro Football Focus grade last season and a 55.1 mark this season, but he graded out at 64 or higher in every season before that dating to 2017.
Cincinnati's already dealt with multiple injuries in the safety room, and more options couldn't hurt.
CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani sees Baker as a strong trade fit for the Bengals . The safety has 42 tackles, a career-high 3.5 sacks, one interception, and four pass breakups this season.
"Budda Baker has been a star for the Arizona Cardinals ever since he was selected No. 36 overall in the 2017 NFL Draft out of Washington," Dajani wrote . "He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie — the first of what have turned into eight Pro Bowl appearances. Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30. Just Bobby Wagner, Roquan Smith, Luke Kuechly, Lavonte David, Ray Lewis, Fred Warner, and ... Budda Baker.
"Baker is still a stud, as evidenced by the Cardinals' upset win over the Rams on Sunday. He recorded six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defensed. He stopped at least one touchdown from being scored, and he was effective in blitzing the quarterback and stopping the running backs. Someone come get him."
Given his age (30) and expensive contract, Baker might be had for a Day 3 draft pick in 2027.
There are no firm reports that Baker is on the trade block, but Arizona hasn't even gotten the quarterback of the future in place yet to start contending at some point this decade. Baker may be long past his prime by the time they do, but the Bengals have a superstar quarterback he can help win right now.
The money may make this really hard in reality. According to Spotrac, Baker has a $9.79 million cap hit the rest of this season and a $20.9 million cap hit in 2027. Paying big money to him and Bryan Cook may not be palatable for Cincinnati . They'd likely have to release someone in the process of this trade just to stay under the 2026 salary cap.

title: Zac Taylor Delivers High Praise to Ravens HC Jesse Minter Prior to Week 7 Clash
full_text:
There are a lot of storylines to follow as the Cincinnati Bengals prepare for their first game against the Baltimore Ravens this Sunday.
This is the first time the Bengals will face off against Trey Hendrickson. Hendrickson called Cincinnati home for five years before turning in his orange and black for purple. Another major headline is that this will be the first time in a long time the Bengals will be playing a Ravens team not led by John Harbaugh.
The Ravens have handed over the head coaching reins to Jesse Minter. Minter was the defensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Chargers before taking the head coaching position with the Ravens. On Monday, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor gave a lot of praise to the first-year head coach.
"Really smart. He's got a lot of confidence. I think the players respect him and have confidence in him," Taylor said when asked about what Minter has brought with him to Baltimore. "Did a great job when he was with the Chargers. You can just tell he's somebody in the industry that has always been well thought of and players have always had respect for him.
Last season with the Chargers, Minter's defense was one of the top in the league. The Chargers allowed just 285.2 yards per game a season ago, which was fourth-best in the NFL. This season, Minter's Ravens are allowing 310 yards per game.
It's going to be a clash of styles when these two teams take the field on Sunday.
The Bengals offense is averaging 342.8 yards per game, and there's a chance that number can get even higher.
The pass game is obviously Cincinnati's strength. Joe Burrow is averaging 260 yards per game through the air, but it's the run game that can elevate this unit to another level.
If the Bengals are going to take the AFC North crown this season, the run game has to be better than what it has been at this stage in the season. The Bengals are bottom 10 in rushing yards per game this season, averaging 82 yards.
There are a lot of variables to play out before these teams take the field on Sunday. Including if Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson will be available . One thing is for certain: Taylor isn't overlooking a first-year head coach who could be without his top offensive talent.

title: Ravens Linebacker Predicts Multi-Sack Game for Trey Hendrickson Against Bengals
full_text:
The Bengals and Ravens meet for the first time this season on Sunday, and it will be the first time the Bengals face their former star pass rusher, Trey Hendrickson. His desire to have a big game against his former team is already on full display, as starting Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson has called for Hendrickson to get multiple sacks on Sunday.
"I believe that this game for him is about to be one of those one's, like multiple sack games, I'm calling it," Simpson said.
Hendrickson returned from a finger injury that forced him to miss two games and recorded his second sack of the season against the Browns last week.
Orlando Brown Jr. knows the task ahead of him against the Ravens on Sunday. In a recent interview with Geoff Hobson , he recalled his first encounter with Hendrickson at Bengals practice in 2023, when he signed in Cincinnati.
Immediately, a scuffle broke out between the two on Brown's first snap of training camp with the Bengals. He acknowledged his respect for Hendrickson and how his past practices with him should help him this Sunday.
"That's who he is, That's why I respect him, He's a fighter," Brown said. "I think it helps him, I think it helps me, Just in terms of the feel, The feel of his rushes, his counter, How much? I can't put my finger on that, But at the end of the day, I've got to play Sunday."
Hendrickson consistently dominated opposing linemen with the Bengals, and he has continued to do so with the Ravens. Over six weeks, he ranks third in the NFL in pressure rate per Next Gen Stats, with a 30% pass-rush win rate across 73 plays.
Brown pointed to Hendrickson's passion to remain a dominant force on the defensive line as the reason the Bengals signed him in 2021 and the Ravens signed him this offseason. He also said Hendrickson will remain one of his good friends whenever he retires.
"A lot of passion, that's why they paid him there, that's why we paid him here," Brown said. "That's why he's been so successful. I have no friends with D-linemen not on my team. When I retire, one day, Trey will be one of my good friends."
The Bengals square off against the Ravens on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Baltimore for a crucial game that could ultimately decide the winner of the AFC North. The tensions between Hendrickson and the Bengals should only add another layer to what should be as competitive a contest as any this season.

title: Joe Burrow Reacts to Vice President JD Vance Attending Bengals Practice
full_text:
The Bengals hosted Vice President JD Vance during their practice session on Wednesday. A few members of the team got to meet the politician as Vance toured the Paycor Stadium facilities following Wednesday's outing.
Burrow discussed the visit during his weekly press conference just minutes after the fellow southern-Ohio native exited.
The Bengals' top leader did not get a chance to meet Vice President Vance . The latter was in town for a rally ahead of next month's midterm elections.
"We did not," Burrow said about having an interaction. "He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn't get to."
Vance grew up in Middletown, Ohio just north of Cincinnati. His large security detail was hard to miss around the practice field on Wednesday.
"Yeah, a lot of people around," Burrow joked. "That's what I love about what I do is it brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I've put in to come and watch greatness. And that's everybody in the locker room. That's why we do what we do, whether it's on the TV, whether it's in person, whether it's on the practice field, that's what we do."
Burrow and the whole team are focused on a massive divisional game in Baltimore.
Cincinnati's playoff chances swing roughly 30% based on Sunday's result, depending on which playoff model you look at. Every AFC North game is one of the most important of the season, especially when the Ravens are on deck.
"It's a big game," Burrow said about the matchup to start his press conference. "There's a lot of football to be played after this, but anytime we play the Ravens with a place in the division on the line, it's going to be a big game. So we're treating it that way."

title: JD Vance Attends Bengals Practice After Cincinnati Visit
full_text:
Vice President JD Vance attended Bengals practice on Wednesday afternoon. Vance spent more than a half hour on the practice field.
The Bengals are preparing for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
After the practice visit, Vance's team walked through the locker room and the facilities. He grew up roughly 37 miles from Paycor Stadium in Middletown.
Vance was elected as Vice President in 2024 and was in town for a visit ahead of next month's midterm election.
Joe Burrow talked with Bengals owner Mike Brown ahead of Wednesday's session. It's easy to think that Brown was talking with Burrow about Vance's visit. Maybe not, but it's rare for Brown to talk to Burrow during practice—even while the star quarterback is warming up.
Vice President JD Vance arriving at Bengals practice today. @WLWT pic.twitter.com/fTCpZcsZM0
Vance hasn't been shy about weighing in on the Bengals in the past. Last year he discussed his fandom on the This Past Weekend Podcast With Theo Von.
Ironically, he made the case for signing Trey Hendrickson. The Bengals let Hendrickson walk in free agency and they'll face off on Sunday in Baltimore.
"Hendrickson is worth it, dude. He's a generational talent," Vance said . "It's very hard to get a guy like that. It's kind of crazy how, like, I'm a big football fan, but edge rushers have become ... It's almost like where left tackles were 10 or 15 years ago, where everybody just realized there's this really underpaid position that you gotta have. And so, yeah, I think we're [the Bengals] gonna have to pay Hendrickson.
"Here's what I'll say to Trey, if you're watching this show. If you're a Republican, I will show up to a Bengals game and take a photo with you if you sign on with the Bengals. And if you're a Democrat, I'll stay the hell away. Just sign with the Bengals because we got a chance, man. I say this every year, but with Burrow, with Ja'Marr Chase, if we get our defense and our offensive line, we could have a true championship run."

title: Where the Cleveland Browns Need Help the Most Ahead of the  NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline inches closer and closer, all 32 teams are getting ready to make one final push in improving their rosters in order to successfully navigate the second half of the season.
The AFC North-leading Cleveland Browns are no exception and as a matter of fact, they could become one of the teams to watch closely as they might end up investing in the same position group that was at the forefront of their free agency acquisitions over the spring.
As it turns out, the Cleveland Browns offensive line, while showing some improvement in regards to last years’ unmitigated disaster, is still struggling to gel after replacing all five starters for the 2026 season.
While the Browns’ two rookies on the O-Line -- left tackle Spencer Fano and Austin Barber at the right guard -- have been playing decently and Elgton Jekins is among the best pass blocking centers in the league when healthy , the unit has been struggling mightily in the ground game.
Pro Football Reference has the Browns tied for the fourth worst average yards per rushing attempt before the first contact at just 2.0, and having no ground game has really handicapped Cleveland’s offense, including the play-action phase.
Back in early March, the Browns finalized a trade for Tytus Howard with the Texans, giving up a fifth round pick, and subsequently extending his deal for three years and $63 million to play right tackle. So far, Howard leads the league in false start penalties (5) and is just one flag away from co-leading the league in that department, regardless of position or infraction.
A few days after the Howard deal, the Browns agreed to sign free agent Zion Johnson from the Chargers for three years and $49.5 million to plug in at left guard, which is future Hall of Famer Joel Bitonio’s former spot. While he has shown some improvement over the weeks in pass protection, he’s still struggling to get some push on running plays through the middle.
Likewise, Jenkins was signed as a free agent through a two-year $24 million deal. And Teven Jenkins was re-signed to the tune of one year and $5 million, hoping he could retain the right guard job before a back injury in the summer opened the door for Barber to take the spot, one he will not relinquish in the near future -- unless he changes position. More on that, below.
As a unit, ESPN Analytics has the Browns ranked 27th in pass block win rate and 24th in run block win rate after six games . And according to PFF’s grades, every single one of these three veterans is ranked much higher in pass protection than run blocking, with Elgton Jenkins’ discrepancy being truly noteworthy.
Something needs to change in the trenches for the Browns offense.
The most intriguing name could be Quenton Nelson, a future Hall of Famer who’s on the last year of his current deal. At 30 years-old, he’s not quite what he used to be, but he’s plenty good enough to anchor an offensive line.
With the Colts recently dismissing general manager Chris Ballard, this team is likely looking at a rebuild, and accumulating draft capital should be a priority. Nelson likely won’t fetch much due to his age and a 10 million cap hit for 2026, but Cleveland could fit that number under its cap if interested. Nelson could then take the left side, move Johnson to the right, and have Barber kick out to right tackle, which should be his position for the future anyway.
A much more affordable option would be the Eagles’ Landon Dickerson, after Philly saw Superstar right tackle Lane Johnson retire and then sent starting center Cam Jurgens away via trade. Dickerson has been hurt, but he’s still a better left guard than Johnson, and like Elgton Jenkins, has plenty of experience at center. Perhaps he could take over in the middle and send Jenkins to left guard, or take left guard and move the rest of the pieces as described above.
Finally, the Bucs’ Ben Bredeson is another interior lineman who could be available before the deadline. Like in Dickerson’s case, he’s a left guard with some flexibility to play center. And, he has no more guaranteed money left on his current deal, so that could help grease the skids towards a projected deal.
Of course, Cleveland has some internal options too. Dawand Jones could be tried at right tackle or right guard, kicking Barber out to tackle. KT Leveston showed some promise at guard, too, during the preseason after a very rough 2025 playing tackle.
The point is that this unit needs to get better, quickly. They need to overcome a lack of explosiveness from the backfield in the ground game, and a quarterback who loves to hold on to the ball really long, leading to sacks. This unit is better than last years’ patchwork line, but by no means should the Browns consider themselves done in the trenches.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Why the Browns Should Be Active at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Before the 2026 NFL Season began, nobody thought the Cleveland Browns would be 4-2 after the first six weeks.
However, given the start they have had, the Browns should definitely be interested in becoming buyers at the trade deadline to fill some holes in the roster.
Here's why the Browns should make some calls and what they should be looking out for.
If there is a year to take advantage of the road map to the playoffs, it is this season.
Not only do the Browns have the easiest strength of schedule , but they also get an entire month without having to travel.
For the rest of the season, the Browns will face opponents such as the 1-5 Tennessee Titans, 2-4 New Orleans Saints, 2-4 Houston Texans, and 2-4 Atlanta Falcons.
From weeks 10-14, Cleveland gets to play one home game, go on a bye week, and come out of it playing the next three at home as well.
If there's a year where the schedule is in your favor, it is this one. That said, a couple of trades in order to help secure more wins would be a good move for the organization.
Since trading for him back in 2022, Deshaun Watson has either not been healthy, not played well, or at times both.
This season, it feels like the stars are aligning and the Browns are actually getting the play they want out of the guy they traded for.
Once again, a couple of trades for some offensive pieces may set the Browns and Deshaun Watson up for further success going down the stretch of the year.
So we know the Browns should try to call up some other teams to talk about trades, but who should they go after, and what should they give up?
At the moment, Cleveland desperately needs help with their offensive line. Additionally, some secondary depth could be useful with the recent injury to Grant Delpit.
In the 2027 NFL Draft, the Browns currently have 11 picks available to use. Out of those, they have two first-rounders, 3 fourth rounds, and numerous late-round picks that may get used if the right trade is there.
Historically, Browns General Manager Andrew Berry has done a fantastic job of buying low on players with high upside. We saw him do it twice in the wide receiver room with Amari Cooper and Jerry Jeudy.
Maybe there is a couple of offensive lineman who aren't playing well with their current team and simply need a change of scenery? One of those late-round picks could get sent in return for a guy like that.
Now, if the Browns really want to make a splash, they could go after a guy like Sam LaPorta from Detroit, who has had some poor contract negotiations with the Lions in the past few weeks.
If there's going to be a year to make some moves, it's 2026.
With the wins the Browns have managed to pull off so far, combined with the favorable schedule, the road to the playoffs is much easier than in years past.
Don't be surprised if you see the Browns sending picks away for some players here in a few weeks, before the trade deadline.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Why the Browns Will Not Trade for Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
It has been no secret that despite the Cleveland Browns’ 4-2 record, they have struggled to run the football. The Browns rank 24th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, and  are only that high due to Deshaun Watson’s 32 yard average. Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor could be available via trade before the November 10 deadline.
Taylor is averaging four yards per carry this season and he is sixth in the NFL with 492 yards. He would be a major upgrade to the running back room as Quinshon Judkins and Reheim Sanders are injured. The running backs that got carries last week for the Browns were not even on the team at the start of the season.
With the Browns making a playoff push, trading for Taylor should be a no brainer. However, the Browns may want to back off and shift their focus elsewhere. The Colts will be asking for a first or second-round pick plus a late pick swap for Taylor. The Browns have two first-round picks in the draft, and they should hold on to both of them.
The talent is in place on the roster around the quarterback. They should keep their picks and hope to package them to move up and pick a quarterback that they like. At the moment, they are winning too much to be able to use their own pick on a quarterback and the Los Angeles Rams will probably turn their season around, so that pick may be too low.
Valuable running backs can be had anywhere in the draft. The Browns have plenty of middle round-picks to find one and that guy would then be on a rookie contract. Watson’s contract is finally starting to dwindle, but it will still get in the way of adding good players. They have put themselves in a position where they have to draft players on rookie contracts to contribute.
Quinshon Judkins showed promise in his rookie season, but he has not looked the same this season. He is adjusting to rushing from the shotgun position and with experience, he will get better. The backup at the beginning season was Dylan Sampson, but he got injured early in the first game of the season. He is expected to be back and the Browns should wait and find out what they have in a fully healthy position group.
Taylor cannot bring his offensive line with him to Cleveland , which would help as the Browns’ unit has failed to make any lanes for the running backs. Cleveland’s offensive line has only played six games together with a new head coach, offensive coordinator, and line coach. The rushing attack is not a finished product and there is still plenty of time for improvement without having to drain the resources by trading for Taylor.
If the Browns wish to add to the room then they have other options. Saquon Barkley may be on the trading block from the Philadelphia Eagles, and the price tag would be less for him. The compensation would still be a valuable pick and he has struggled with injuries as he only has 36 carries this season.
While the 4-2 start has been surprising, the roster is still very young and Watson has not been good for any length of time in a game. A deep playoff run is unlikely for this season and running backs’ health is iffy from year to year. The Browns are better off staying put or adding a running back that will split carries. The potential for Cleveland’s running backs has not been touched, and the offense will benefit when the group is full and healthy.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury Update Raises Concerns Ahead of Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice:
#Browns players not expected to practice today due to injury: Kalia Davis (quad) Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) Elgton Jenkins (knee) Teven Jenkins (back) Carson Schwesinger (ankle)
Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion.
Grant Delpit Took A Hard Hit To The Head As He Was Going In For The Tackle. This Definitely Does Not Look Good. Hope He’s All Good. Scary Moment. 😬 pic.twitter.com/u3VMCaBu40
Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday.
Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return.
Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice.
With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans.
Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6.
While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday.
The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans.
#Browns DT Mason Graham continued practicing today as he aims to return this week from the MCL sprain and ankle sprain he sustained in Week 4. pic.twitter.com/fSpap4sJZ2
While Delpit's status is concerning, the team has some depth at safety to help offset a potential absence. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup.

title: How Many More Wins Can We Expect from the Browns after Week 6?
full_text:
So far in 2026, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people. Quite frankly, even Browns fans themselves thought they were in for another 3-4-win season that sets them up for yet another high draft pick in 2027.
However, head coach Todd Monken has turned the team around in just his first season. Through six weeks, they have been winners four times already.
At this pace, the Browns can make the playoffs. But how far can the Browns really go? Let's take a look at the remainder of the season for Cleveland by breaking it down into three segments.
Starting with the Titans matchup, the Browns are set for three straight road games.
Realistically, the Browns need to try and win two out of three games here. Of course, it would be nice to win all three, winning in Pittsburgh has not been historically easy for the Browns.
As for the Titans and Saints matchups, these are two games the Browns need to make sure they win. Credit to New Orleans and Tennessee, but going into each matchup, the Browns are the better team.
Let's say the Browns hypothetically win two out of three. That would put their record at 6-3 before heading into the best part of their schedule.
After New Orleans, the Browns are set up for success being at home for five straight weeks.
Starting off against the Texans, this is a tough game. CJ Stroud is playing some of his best football and their defense is a top unit in the league. However, this is still weeks away, and you never know what will change by then.
After Week 10, the Browns got lucky with a later bye week this season. Coming out of it, you get the Raiders, Bengals, and Falcons.
Against Las Vegas, the Browns should be able to shut down the Raider offense and put some points on the board against their defense. While it may be close, this is one the Browns need to win.
Your first place 4-2 #Browns ' upcoming schedule: Week 7 @ Titans (1-5) Week 8 @ Steelers (4-2) Week 9 @ Saints (2-4) Week 10 vs. Texans (2-4) Week 11 BYE Week 12 vs. Raiders (3-3) #DawgPound
Following that game, the Bengals come to town for the first battle of Ohio in 2026. If they beat the Raiders, maybe some momentum can carry over to what will be a crucial divisional matchup.
Then, the game with the biggest storyline. The Atlanta Falcons, led by former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, come to play in Week 14. Simply put, the Browns MUST win this one.
Going back to our hypotheticals, let's say the Browns go 2-2 in this stretch. 8-5 would most likely put them somewhere in contention for a wildcard spot, making the final four weeks the biggest yet.
Hopefully, the Browns learned what needs to change to win in MetLife Stadium. That's where they will play for the second time this season when they travel to take on the New York Giants.
Let's say the Browns can get a huge win in Week 15 against the Giants. That leads them straight into their second Ravens matchup the following week.
Something that is pretty clear with the AFC North is that home games give each team an incredible boost. The Browns will most likely struggle in both late divisional games against the Ravens and Bengals.
If the Browns drop one in Baltimore, they then play their final home game against the Colts. Who knows what the season will look like by then, but there could be a serious chance that with a win against Indianapolis, Week 18 in Cincinatti is a potential game for the division title.
Regardless of division, let's say the Browns once again go 2-2 dropping both AFC North matchups. Our hypothetical record is now 10-7, which may be enough to sneak into the playoffs.
Overall, the road to making the postseason for the first time since 2023 is not horrible on paper.
The important thing for Cleveland is to keep their focus on one game at a time, and keep stacking up wins.
For the NFL's second-youngest team, learning how to win going forward is what matters the most.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Browns Reveal Promising Update on Mason Graham Following Lower-Body Injury
full_text:
Even without Mason Graham, the Cleveland Browns' defense is elite.
And whenever he does ultimately return, there's a chance that the Browns get even better.
Fortunately, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, the Browns announced that Graham is getting healthier by the day. He is currently recovering from an ankle and knee injury he suffered in the Browns' Thursday Night Football clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
According to head coach Todd Monken, Graham wanted to play last weekend in the Browns' Week 6 clash with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, he ultimately wasn't able to suit up.
He did share, though, that in the Browns' Sunday meeting with the Tennessee Titans , he should be ready to go.
"I think so. He wanted to go [vs. Baltimore]. He played for Jesse [Minter] at Michigan," Monken said. "He loves football. I think he's thankful and I am thankful it wasn't worse. Pretty good chance we will have him this week."
Browns coach Todd Monken said DT Mason Graham wanted to play last Sunday against the Ravens and his former coach at Michigan, Jesse Minter. "I think there's a pretty good chance we'll have him this week."
And it is obvious that the 23-year-old loves the game.
He made an incredible jump from his rookie campaign, becoming a much more impactful defender.
In his rookie season, he was named to the All-Rookie team by the Pro Football Writers of America , even though he only recorded 0.5 sacks, 49 tackles, seven for a loss and four quarterback hits.
This year, across the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, he was one of the most dominant rushers in the league before injury. He totaled 15 combined tackles, seven of which were solo, and four sacks . His presence in the backfield led to 33 yards lost for opposing quarterbacks when he was credited with the sack.
That type of pressure and ability to back an offense up is incredibly important.
But even when he has been kept off the field, the Browns have had players step up to fill his void.
Maliek Collins is up to 3.5 sacks and five tackles for a loss this season, while Isaiah McGuire sits not far behind at 3.0 sacks and five tackles for a loss. Alongside Collins and McGuire, Adin Huntington, Sam Kamara and Mike Hall Jr. have put in the work, each totaling a sack or more as well.
In Sunday's win, the Browns' run defense had a 97th percentile EPA/rush allowed performance and a 98th percentile designed rushing success rate allowed performance. Their total Defense Impact Metric, according to Pro Football Focus, has them ranked within the Top 5 in the league.
They also rank first in tackles for a loss, fewest rushing touchdowns allowed and second in total sacks.
When Graham returns, that unit will be even better, with those who have filled his spot being warmed up now.
There are just a few more days for Graham to get cleared for this weekend, and even if he just plays on limited snaps, it will be a nice bump for the defense to try and lead the Browns to a 5-2 record.
The Browns and Titans will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville this Sunday.

title: What I'm Buying and Selling About the Cleveland Browns After Week 6
full_text:
It’s hard not to feel good about the Cleveland Browns’ 4-2 start to the season, including wins over divisional rivals Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens so far in 2026.
After all, this is the team with the lowest winning percentage in all the NFL (.346) since it grew to 32 teams divided in eight divisions back in 2002, and the longest active drought without a division title league-wide (36 years and counting). Winning just isn’t a common occurrence here.
But even as the Browns face a very accessible schedule with just one remaining out of division foe with a winning mark, not everything has been smooth sailing for the franchise. Here are three things I’m buying and three things I’m selling from the Browns after Week 6 of the 2026 regular season.
The Browns began their regular season getting their teeth kicked in by the Jaguars on Opening Weekend. Since then, this unit has been one of the best in all the NFL. Cleveland is currently ranked second in the league in sacks in their first year without Myles Garrett and zero sacks by his nominal successor Jared Verse, and fourth in total quarterback pressures. Cleveland has also surrendered just one rushing touchdown all year long.
Granted, there are still some issues that need to be resolved, mainly in the secondary, but this unit is going places. Denzel Ward is enjoying one of his finest seasons as a pro, Carson Schwesinger is proving to be the real deal in his second season, and free agent addition Quincy Williams has been playing a very high level of football, too. The D-Line has been the team’s best group, nonetheless. Isaiah McGuire and Maliek Collins have been phenomenal, while Mason Graham has been living up to his billing when healthy. Sam Williams has also flashed on the edge, and Verse is getting the pressures, if not the sacks.
The Browns went all-in on Watson and, so far, there are reasons to be skeptical about his performance so far. His 4.0 percent touchdown percentage is his second worst as a pro, and his numbers across a few other metrics line up exactly to what he’s done before in Cleveland, very distant to what he did before in Houston, including QBR, success rate, yards per attempt, and sack percentage, while his 70.3 on target rate is his personal worst.
So no, Watson isn’t playing better under head coach Todd Monken than what he did under Kevin Stefanski, in any sense. He’s just being backed by a much better defense and has some top notch weapons at his disposal in the ground game, along with a trust-worthy placekicker in Andre Szmyt.
The Browns are winning despite Watson , and that means they can’t change quarterbacks now, but things are likely to get rocky at some point ahead.
Playing on an island on the left side is inherently more difficult than playing guard but make no mistake, Austin Barber has been as good if not better than Spencer Fano for the Browns. Either way, both are outplaying their respective counterparts in veteran left guard Zion Johnson and especially veteran right tackle Tytus Howard, so far.
There’s still a ton of improvement to be made here, and blocking for a quarterback that’s been responsible for a number of sacks is suboptimal, but expect these two to become cornerstones in Cleveland for the long run.
The team as a whole has been struggling mightily in the ground game , no doubt. But Judkins’ woes should come as no surprise when you take a good look at his rookie season.
He’s averaging 3.0 yards-per-rush this year, which is actually worse than his 3.5 yards-per-rush average from a year ago, and hasn’t been able to reach a 4.0 yard-per-carry average since Week 13 of last year, one of only four games all year long he was able to reach or surpass that number. And this year, he’s scored just once despite receiving the lion’s share in snaps on offense (60 percent, compared to 50 percent last year).
Run blocking has been a problem for the Browns, especially in terms of first contact for the backs, but Judkins’ numbers are worse off than last year’s underwhelming stats, neatly disguised by his seven rushing scores as a rookie.
If the rookie offensive linemen have been a hit for the Browns, the rookie wideouts have been even better.
KC Concepcion recovered from a concussion in time to play this past Sunday for the Browns, and he’s still leading the team with 22 catches for 186 yards. Meanwhile, Denzel Boston has 17 catches for 345 yards and a league-leading 20.3 yard per reception average to go along with his three scores.
Yes, the numbers for both could be better by this point, but they truly don’t have much to work with at the quarterback position. Even so, Boston should be seriously considered among the league favorites to take home the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.
Currently, Cleveland is using play-action at a 18.5 percent rate -- 29th in the NFL -- down from 21.9 percent last year. The team’s EPA per pass attempt is at -0.04, meaning the Browns are faking handoffs at a very low rate, and are not a successful team at passing the ball when they do fake the handoff.
Again, the offensive line has had some protection issues and Watson is not playing good football right now, but a solid ground game would probably earn more respect from the defenses than what’s currently going on. Plus, play-action is known as a good countermeasure to pressure, which would be a good development for a team leading the league in sacks allowed .
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Could Browns’ Carson Schwesinger Enter the Defensive Player of the Year Race?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year , Carson Schwesinger, continues to impress.
In the Browns' Week 6 matchup against division rival Baltimore, Carson Schwesinger was the X factor in the team's win. Despite entering the game listed as questionable with an ankle sprain, Schwesinger recorded 13 tackles. Most importantly, Schwesinger forced running back Derrick Henry to fumble , setting up Cleveland’s game-tying touchdown.
DROY Carson Schwesinger forces the fumble on Derrick Henry! BALvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TY9niNw746
The performance against the Ravens is not a one-off, either. Schwesinger has 56 total tackles through six games.  That averages 9.3 tackles per game, approximately matching Luke Kuechly’s career average. Maintaining that pace over a full 17-game season would put Schwesinger at roughly 159 tackles. Schwesinger has also added quarterback pressure, recording a strip-sack in the Browns’ Week 5 matchup against the Jets.
Carson FLYING in to knock it loose! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/9HFah8X33w
While Schwesinger has been impressive throughout the 2026 season and has largely picked up where he left off in 2025 , his recent two-week stretch of 21 tackles, two forced fumbles, and a sack may strengthen his case for another individual honor.
Schwesinger already emerged in 2025 as one of the league's best defenders , but his recent production, despite injury, may put him in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation. Schwesinger has been nothing short of elite in the middle of the Browns’ defense over the last few weeks. If Schwesinger can keep playing at this level, even with a bad ankle, the illustrious Defensive Player of the Year award could be within reach.
History isn't exactly on Schwesinger's side, as pass rushers dominate the award.  Luke Kuechly was the last off-ball linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year, earning the honor in 2013, when he played in all 16 games and recorded two sacks, four interceptions, and 156 combined tackles. Notably, Kuechly won the award in his second NFL season, the same stage of his career that Schwesinger has reached.
Jared Verse on Carson Schwesinger: “He has an old school linebacker mindset … He’s a hooper … He’s the most reliable person I know.” #browns pic.twitter.com/KoXZaGwh8H
Patrick Surtain II is the most recent non-edge defender to win the award, winning it in 2024 with 45 combined tackles, four interceptions, and 11 passes defended. Recent voting trends favor pass rushers like current betting favorite Will Anderson Jr., making it a tougher path for Schwesinger as an off-ball linebacker.
However, if Carson Schwesinger stays healthy and sustains his recent elite play, he could give the Luke Kuechly comparisons even more weight. Like Kuechly, Schwesinger could follow a Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign by claiming the NFL’s top defensive honor in his second season.

title: Could Audric Estime Be the Answer? Browns Face RB Questions Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 NFL regular season, there weren't many concerns about the running back position.
After all, the front office spent all season focused on building up the offensive line, picking a starting quarterback and developing a young wide receiver room. Of all the positions, the running back room seemed to be the last thing on anyone's mind.
However, after the first six weeks of the campaign, it has jumped to the top of the priorities list.
Both starting running back Quinshon Judkins and backup Dylan Sampson ended up injured at the same time. Judkins missed a Week 6 win against the Baltimore Ravens due to an ankle injury, while Sampson was ruled out in Week 1. He unfortunately ended up on the injured list.
At this time, neither has been cleared for Week 7 when the Browns take on the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
In order to replace some of the lost depth, the Browns' front office went out and signed running back Audric Estime from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad early last week.
Finding at least one body to pair with Jaleel McLaughlin, who was also thrust into a bigger role with Rahiem Sanders ending up on the injured list, was a big-time need for the Browns.
While Estime was somewhat of an unknown, having only rushed for 234 yards and three scores across his first two seasons in the NFL, he impressed in his debut with the Browns.
On nine carries, Estime recorded 19 yards and one touchdown, picking up two first downs as well. When the ball was in his hands, he had a 55.6% success rate . While his average yards per game was certainly down, his usage, especially in power-needed positions, led to this difference compared to his averages in 2024 and 2025.
But even then, the former Notre Dame standout was still able to find the end zone after just joining the franchise days before his debut.
“I just followed the blocker,” Estime said postgame when asked about what led to him finding six. “And the coaches trusted me. They said when we got down there that I was going to get in the end zone. I had confidence in myself. I didn’t know how it was going to look, but I really had confidence that I was going to get in the paint.”
With more time to get acclimated to the team both on the field and off, and more time for the coaches to get him more intertwined into the system, Estime could carve out a nice role for himself heading into Week 7.
At this point, the Browns are just trying to keep the run game afloat while they await the return of Sampson, Judkins and Sanders, and as long as McLaughlin can affect the game outside the hashes and Estime can get to work in the trenches, the Browns don't need to make a move at the deadline.
Instead, they can lean into the two they have on the roster now, with the hope that by the time Judkins and Sampson are fully good to go, the team is still playing competitive football.
Neither Sampson nor Judkins are supposed to be out for too long of a time period; however, any sort of leg injuries are going to slow running backs down. The Browns will want to play it safe, especially up the gut, so keeping Estime around is going to be important.
And at the end of the day, there is very little downside to letting a 23-year-old get another chance at establishing himself in the league.
“(Estime) shows up (at practice) on Wednesday and, heck, he’s taking meaningful snaps and scores a touchdown (a few days later),” Monken said about him in an article in The Athletic . “So that says a lot about the depth of our team and the expectations of the position, which you should have.
"You should have expectations of any player on your roster playing at a high level."
The Browns and Estime return to the gridiron Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium.

title: One Crucial Schedule Twist the Browns Need to Capitalize On Moving Forward
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are already one of teams making most waves through the first six weeks of the regular season thanks to a 4-2 record and the fact that they have already beaten the 4-2 Steelers and the 4-2 Ravens to claim the top spot in the AFC North, for now.
However, one glance at the remaining schedule for the Browns reveals an interesting quirk that head coach Todd Monken’s team will be looking to parlay into the team’s first postseason run since 2023.
Besides the four remaining AFC North games on Cleveland’s schedule -- a rematch against Pittsburgh, a rematch against Baltimore, and two contests against the 3-2 Bengals -- there is only one team currently holding a winning record among the games yet to be played.
The 3-2-1 New York Giants are the only team currently holding a winning record left on the Browns’ schedule. Besides the Giants, the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-3 are the only other team not holding a losing record. All other opponents left currently carry losing records: Titans, Saints, Texans, Falcons and Colts.
While the Browns would need at least two more wins to cover their win total odds of 5.5 from before the season started, winning all five games left against teams with losing records would ensure a winning season for the first time since 2023, and even then, playoffs might not be guaranteed. That’s why the way the Browns’ remaining schedule is lining up is so important for this team.
Life is hard within the league’s most competitive division. It’s not just the fact that back in 2023, it became the only division in league history with all four teams sporting winning records. It has to do with how hard it is to exert dominance over the other clubs.
Since 2002, the league’s probability at sweeping a divisional opponent sits at 42 percent, but in the AFC North, that number is roughly 34 percent. Likewise, the NFL has a league-wide probability of 3.8 percent of sweeping all three divisional opponents in any given year, but that number shrinks to 1.04 percent in the AFC North, where it’s happened just five times in its history -- the Steelers have done it three times, while the Bengals and Ravens just once, each. Cleveland has never swept the entire division since its inception.
Furthermore, since 2002, the Browns have only managed to sweep a single divisional rival three times in one season, all three against Cincinnati (2002, 2018 and 2020). Cleveland has never swept the Steelers while playing in the AFC North, and hasn’t done so generally speaking since 1988. The Browns have yet to sweep the Ravens in any instance.
With the Browns already handing losses to Pittsburgh and Baltimore, nobody says Cleveland can’t get a sweep over any one of those teams. It just hasn’t happened yet in the AFC North. And even thinking about sweeping Cincy is a complicated proposition, too. Moreover, we haven’t even begun to discuss how and why the team is winning despite Deshaun Watson’s poor performances , and without any sign of life from the ground game .
Yes, Cleveland is off to a phenomenal start to the season , but closing in on a postseason berth won’t be easy. That’s why the Browns need to take advantage of every single opportunity they get, including winning all their remaining matchups against non-winning teams.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Cowboys' George Pickens Publicly Criticized by Brian Schottenheimer Before Week 7
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have gotten off to an ugly start this season and are 2-4 as a result headed into Week 7's matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles
However, in a historically poor NFC East division this season, the Cowboys still have a ton to play for. Remarkably, making the playoffs is still realistic for Dallas.
But if Dallas wants to make it to the postseason, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is making it clear he wants to see some improvement from wide receiver George Pickens in a key area.
While speaking with the media on Thursday, Schottenheimer spoke at length about the improvement he wants to see from Pickens as a blocker in the running game.
There's no questioning Pickens' ability as a pass catcher. Even since he was with the Pittsburgh Steelers, he's proven to be one of the league's best contested-catch receivers.
But Schottenheimer didn't hesitate to admit that when the Cowboys run the ball, the opposing defense often gets an easier chance at taking down running back Javonte Williams. Being a productive blocker has never been what Pickens is known for, but that might have to change.
"He needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well," Schottenheimer said of Pickens, per ESPN's Ed Werder. "You know, he's got to do the same thing in the run game — picking up safeties and blocking corners — just like Javonte does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. That's part of the team-first mindset, and GP does understand that. And you know when he's going, they're going to play soft inside. When he's not going, the safety gets pretty good runs at our backs, and that's going to improve.”
That said, Schottenheimer credited Pickens for not getting emotional if he doesn't get the ball. That's been a topic of discussion so far this season, as Pickens has 52 targets compared to 69 for CeeDee Lamb.
“GP is one of those guys where I don't ever see him really affected in terms of you know the emotion. Does he get the ball? Does he not get the ball? If these guys play a lot of snaps, I think part of it is us rotating those guys through.
Pickens had tallied 33 catches for 428 yards and one touchdown so far this season.
He will have a chance to respond to Schottenheimer's challenge when the Cowboys visit the Eagles on Monday Night Football.

title: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer Discusses Criticism He's Receiving, Admits 'Some' is Deserved
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is fully of the criticism he's getting this season.
And that criticism is warranted. The Cowboys are off to a 2-4 start , and he's 9-13-1 overall in his season-plus on the job.
To make the target on his back bigger, Schottenheimer's play-calling on offense has negatively impacted the team's offense , which was supposed to be its strength but simply hasn't been good enough, especially of late.
On Thursday, Schottenheimer was asked about the criticism he has been receiving this season amid the team's putrid six-game start and admitted that while he does try to block some out, there's still instances where he hears it.
He also said "some" of the criticism is deserved and admitted he needs to do a better job coaching. Even still, Schotty believes he's a "great coach" and believes the Cowboys can turn things around.
“I think it comes with the territory," he said of the criticism. "I think some of it is deserved. We got to play better. I got to coach better. When you grow up in a family that your dad is a head coach for over 20 years, you understand that this is part of the job description.
“No one likes it. I block out most of it. Some of it gets to me. Doing this job and having to speak to you guys is part of that. But at the same time, I’ve got strong shoulders. I know what a great coach I am. I know what this team is capable of. That’s what I focus on.”
There's a few things Schottenheimer said that are going to make Cowboys fans face palm, with the first being Schotty saying that "some" of the criticism is deserved. All of it is very deserved.
The part about him believing he's "a great coach" is also going to bother Cowboys fans because they have yet to see evidence of that being the case.
Can that be construed as delusion? Sure, but it's not like he's going to say he's not a great coach because that would open Schottenheimer up to even more scrutiny.
The problem Schottenheimer has is we keep hearing the same things every single week about there being plenty of football left and the belief that the Cowboys can still turn this around, yet we keep seeing the same issues over and over again.
Schottenheimer isn't the only one who is guilty of being a broken record because we hear it from Jerry and Stephen Jones, also .
The bottom line is Cowboys fans don't want words, they want results, and Dallas has given plenty of the former and nowhere near enough of the latter.
And until that flips, calls for Schottenheimer and the rest of the coaching staff to be fired will continue.

title: Cowboys Injury Updates Put Dallas on Track to Get 2 Defensive Starters Back in Week 7
full_text:
As if their deficiencies on defense weren't enough to overcome, the Dallas Cowboys have also dealt with several injuries on that side of the ball this season.
Two players who have missed games this season are linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant.
Durant hasn't played since Week 2 because of a hamstring injury , and Overshown has been out even longer, with his hamstring issue keeping him out since he injured it in Week 1.
However, it appears there's a chance both players are going to make it back this week, as head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed both will practice on Thursday.
"Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said DeMarvion Overshown and Cobie Durant are expected to practice today," Jon Machota of The Athletic reported.
The bigger update there is Durant, who has not practiced at all since his injury. Overshown, on the other hand, showed he was close last week after he logged two limited practices before receiving a questionable tag and ultimately being ruled out.
On the flip side, fellow linebacker Dee Winters is not going to practice with an Achilles injury. Schottenheimer has previously noted that Winters is expected to miss time .
Durant and Overshown could provide a significant boost for the Cowboys' defense, and that's especially true for Durant.
While Joey Porter Jr. has been everything the Cowboys could have hoped for thus far, the other boundary spot is still a huge problem because DaRon Bland has been a total liability .
Durant was easily Dallas' best cornerback during the offseason and whatever snaps he can give this week will be huge. It's conceivable he'll be limited if he plays, though.
That said, we're not sure exactly how much the Cowboys are going to deploy him, even when he's fully ramped up. Durant did not play all of the snaps in Week 1 and instead gave some up to Shavon Revel.
The no-brainer move would be to cut Bland's playing time significantly or all together and give Durant those snaps.
But the Cowboys seem hellbent on keeping Bland on the field no matter how badly he plays and we know Porter is not going to be leaving the field much, assuming he's capable of playing a full amount of snaps this time around.
Cowboys fans can only hope Dallas will no longer be married to the idea that Bland has to play as much as he does and Durant becomes the full-time starting corner across from Porter, but we're not holding our breath for that to happen.

title: Cowboys Could Soon Get Defensive Help With Marist Liufau Update
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys could be getting some defensive reinforcements soon. On Thursday, Nick Harris reported that Dallas opened the 21-day practice window for outside linebacker Marist Liufau.
A former third-round pick out of Notre Dame, Liufau had moved from a traditional linebacker role to an outside linebacker in Christian Parker's defense . Parker believed Liufau could win on the edge with his speed and while it was a steep learning curve, he was starting to come on strong during training camp and the preseason.
Liufau was still on the roster bubble, but ended up beginning the season on the IR after suffering a fractured forearm in the preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints. The Dallas defense has been struggling this season and while we don't know exactly what Liufau will bring as an EDGE, there's no denying that they can't use his energy and aggressive style of play.
With the 21-day window open, the Cowboys can allow Liufau to practice with the team. By the end of the 21 days, they must decide if they want to move him to the active 53-man roster, or send him back to the IR for the remainder of the season.
Cowboys On SI's Josh Sanchez wrote during the preseason that Liufau had one huge advantage when it came to fighting for his spot: special teams. Throughout the first six games of the year, there have been concerns on that unit as well, and Liufau is someone who can contribute on coverage units and make a huge impact.
That said, it would be nice to see if he can take his speed and burst off the line of scrimmage and develop into a pass-rushing specialist. He is undersized at 6-foot-2 and 238 pounds, but Liufau has never been afraid to deliver a hit and should be able to hold his own in the ground game.
Liufau played two seasons in the NFL, recording 80 tackles, 2.5 sacks, three pass deflections, and two forced fumbles.
Getting Liufau back will be intriguing, but a more encouraging return will take place on Monday Night Football against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys will have linebacker DeMarvion Overshown back on the field for the first time since he suffered a hamstring injury during their Week 1 loss to the New York Giants.
Overshown has dealt with multiple injuries throughout his career and the Cowboys were very patient with his latest. If he can return to full strength, that will be a major boost to a defense desperate for playmakers.

title: Former NFL Player Rips Cowboys Jerry Jones' Aggressive Trade Deadline Comment
full_text:
Jerry Jones is at it again. The Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager is letting fans know that he plans to leave no stone unturned ahead of the NFL trade deadline as he looks to get things right on the field.
Following a 2-4 start, Jones made it clear that he's going to be exploring every possible trade as he attempts to stockpile his team with talent as they look to catch up in a winnable NFC East .
While his words might excite fans, former All-Pro Gerald McCoy doesn't want to hear it. McCoy was on First Take discussing the comments from Jones and he said that he doesn't care what Jones has to say on the matter, claiming it should be the job of every general manager to build the best roster possible.
"We don't care. Jerry, listen, you've been doing this way longer than me. You have three Super Bowls. I have none. You got way more money than I have. You are in a position that I am not in. But you are the owner, controller, CEO, all those titles you have," McCoy said. "It is at minimum your job to do whatever to make your team better. We don't care that you saying this because that's your job. I believe that 31 other teams are believing and doing the exact same thing you just said."
“We don’t care, Jerry!” @Geraldini93 with some strong words towards the Cowboys’ owner and GM 😳 pic.twitter.com/LyZkHq76co
McCoy also said throwing money at the problem doesn't work, especially when Jones is addressing the wrong problem. As McCoy points out, the Cowboys have multiple All-Pro and Pro Bowl players, so there's not a shortage of talent. Instead, the problem is with the coaching.
"You don't have a personnel problem. You currently on your roster have 10 All-Pro or Pro Bowl players, 10. And there's five teams that are at the top of the league since 2020 with all pro and pro bowl players," McCoy said.
"The Cowboys are one of them and you have nothing to show for it. So it is not the talent or the players. You keep saying, I'm going to go add these people. I'm going to go add these people. But Louis just told you, You can have all of those players if it's not being coached right or you're allowing these bad things to happen on the field, it does not matter."
These words are a clear indictement of the work done by current head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who has come under fire as of late. Recently, I wrote on Cowboys On SI how the front office needs to truly evaluate his fit as the head coach . His proponents will say Schottenheimer has done a good job since his offense has been good overall, but at some point, the struggling defense needs to fall on his shoulders. And as we have seen with the addition of Quinnen Williams, Joey Porter Jr., and other, adding talent is not making up for the shortcomings on the coaching staff.
Jones' inability to accurately pinpoint where the issues are has been a problem for this team for decades. McCoy praised Jones for having Super Bowls, but it's been 30 years since Dallas has won one. And let's be honest, that dynasty had a lot to do with the fact that legendary coach Jimmy Johnson set the tone and made sure the right players were on the field.
Since Johnson left, Jones is on a mission to prove he's the guy that can build a winner. While he's done a good job getting talented players, his team is still falling short. That's why McCoy doesn't care about their deadline moves, and unless Schottenheimer drastically improves in a hurry, it's impossible to argue against McCoy.

title: Cowboys Viewed as Possible Trade Landing Spot For Pro Bowler Amid Edge Rusher Woes
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have a major problem at edge rusher.
Through six games, the Cowboys have gotten just 2.5 sacks from their overhauled group that includes Rashan Gary (one sack), Von Miller (zero sacks), Malachi Lawrence (one sack) and Donovan Ezeiruaku (0.5 sacks).
The Cowboys' inability to get after the quarterback has been especially glaring because of how poorly the secondary has played. Dallas can't hope to turn things around on defense if production from the edge rushers doesn't improve.
That's why if there's one trade the Cowboys do make before the trade deadline, it should come at that position.
CBS Sports' Carter Bahns put together 10 trades he wants to see before the deadline on Nov. 10 and one of them included a deal between the Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals for veteran edge rusher Josh Sweat.
"He is an expensive veteran for a franchise attempting to build a young core and boasts the kind of perennial sack production and team contract control that a competitive team would pay a premium for," Bahns said of Sweat. "If the Cowboys moved a couple of draft picks to land Sweat, this would be a win-win."
Cardinals insider Kyle Odegard reported back in May that Sweat was not happy in Arizona , and while he didn't provide the reason why that was the case, there are a few logical explanations.
The first is Sweat's contract , which doesn't have any guaranteed money left on it after this season. Sweat would surely like to have that adjusted.
Another potential reason is the Cardinals are in the midst of a rebuild and Sweat probably isn't keen on sticking around for that, especially given his experience winning a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024.
While the Cardinals have stated publicy they don't wish to trade Sweat, it makes sense for them to do so.
He'll be 30 next year and might be on the decline before the Cardinals are good again, so it doesn't make much sense to continue the relationship.
The Cardinals can get max value for Sweat off a 12-sack season and with him having two more years left on his current deal.
He is having a down season so far in 2026, but that isn't going to stop teams from trying to acquire him given the former Pro Bowler's history of stellar production.
Without a doubt, yes, the Cowboys should trade for Josh Sweat .
The Cowboys just cannot continue with the lackluster production the edge rushers room has provided this season. They need more juice than Gary, Miller, Lawrence and Ezeiruaku have offered.
We touched on Sweat having just two sacks this season, but we also know he's capable of much more. Sweat had double-digit sacks in two of the last four seasons, including 12 in 2024.
Since 2021, Sweat has averaged nine sacks per season and hasn't posted less than 6.5 in that span. Even if we just take his two sacks this season at face value, that's still almost more than Dallas' edge rushers room has combined, so he'd still be an upgrade.
The numbers speak for themselves. Dallas has to pounce all over Sweat if he's available at the trade deadline.

title: Saquon Barkley Injury Update Means Cowboys Are Unlikely to Catch Break in Week 7
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' run defense has been the worst in the NFL this season, so the unit could use all the help it can get.
Going into this week, it appeared the Cowboys might catch a break for their game against the Philadelphia Eagles , as running back Saquon Barkley was uncertain to play after missing each of the last two games because of a hamstring injury.
However, it's starting to look like that break isn't coming, as NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported on Thursday that not only is Barkley expected to return to practice, he is expected to play Monday night.
"Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is expected to return to practice today and is in line to play Monday against the Cowboys, sources say. A lift for the team’s offense with a banged-up backfield and Jalen Hurts on the mend," Garafolo said.
This amounts to a huge lift for the Eagles, who, as Garafolo noted, won't have quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season as he treats multiple blood clots in his lungs .
The first sign Barkley would be back came on Tuesday, when the Eagles released former Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue and signed Elijah Mitchell to the practice squad, which left Philly with three backs, the same amount the team carries into gamedays.
The Eagles have been uncharacteristically bad at running the ball in 2026, as evidenced by their ranking 29th in rushing yards per game.
Some of that has to do with Barkley missing games and exiting a few others early over the first six, but the Eagles' offensive line play has not been as good as what we're used to, either, with Philadelphia's group upfront ranked 23rd in run block win rate .
Even still, Barkley is averaging 5.1 yards per carry, so it's not like he hasn't been effective when on the field.
Dallas has actually had success keeping Barkley in check in three of the last four games it has faced him, but that one time saw Barkley rip off 167 yards in Week 17 of the 2024 season.
With how bad the Cowboys are against the run, you can throw out the past rushing numbers for any team they face. All bets are off with how Dallas has played the run this season.
Over six games, Dallas is giving up a robust 149.8 rushing yards per game, which ranks dead-last. Even quarterbacks have had success on the ground against Dallas, which is why Hurts' absence is hugely helpful for the Cowboys.
But, rest assured, the Cowboys are going to see a heavy dose of Barkley as the Eagles look to lean on him with an inferior signal-caller in Tanner McKee under center.
Barkley is going to get plenty of carries, and we expect McKee to be dumping it off to the Eagles running back to make his life a bit easier through the air.
