title: Everything Dallas Cowboys Have to Fear About Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles will take part in their first of two contests against one another this season as their NFC East rivalry continues.
It has been very tough sledding for both teams so far this season, with Dallas and Philly both off to 2-4 starts that can be summed up with one word: dysfunctional.
Entering this contest, the Eagles and Cowboys are looking up at the New York Giants, who are in first place in the division with a 3-2-1 record through six games.
That's not exactly the way anyone drew it up, and especially not the Eagles and Cowboys.
Ahead of this NFC East showdown, here's the biggest concerns the Eagles present for the Cowboys on Monday night.
Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury, but the Eagles cutting Jaydon Blue off the 53-man roster and only having three running backs in total when you include Dameon Pierce on the active roster and Elijah Mitchell on the practice squad suggests the Eagles expect Barkley back this week.
The Eagles' rushing attack has struggled overall this season, but Barkley is averaging 5.5 yards per carry and still has the juice to make game-changing plays on the ground. The Eagles will need every bit of Barkley's game-breaking ability with Jalen Hurts out for the season due to his scary blood clot situation .
The Cowboys are the very definition of a get-right spot for the Eagles' rushing attack, with Dallas allowing a whopping 149.8 rushing yards per game, the most in the NFL.
Dallas simply cannot let Barkley beat them. They have got to shut the star running back down and force Tanner McKee to win this game with his arm. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, we're very skeptical they can pull that off.
The Eagles have one of the better cornerback trios in the NFL with Cooper DeJean in the slot and Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen on the outside.
Each of those players has a Pro Bowl selection to their name, and all three have a completion rate allowed south of 60% and passer ratings permitted of 100 or less in 2026.
We know the Cowboys have been awful at moving the ball on the ground this season, so that puts more on Dak Prescott and the passing attack to carry the offense, but even Dallas' air attack hasn't been playing up to snuff .
There's no guarantee the Cowboys' passing offense gets going in this game with the tough matchups CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens will face.
As we just noted, it has been a difficult season for the Cowboys' rushing attack, which ranks 31st through six weeks.
While the Eagles only rank 19th against the run, a deeper dive shows that's a bit misleading. Philadelphia is giving up a respectable four yards per carry and ranks fifth in run stop win rate , per ESPN.
Adding to that, Jalen Carter ranks seventh in run stop win rate, which shows he's capable of blowing things up at the line of scrimmage and making Javonte Williams' life more difficult.

title: 3 Cowboys With Most to Prove Entering Week 7 vs. Eagles
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are looking to end a two-game losing streak as they visit the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. The Cowboys’ struggles have been well-documented, but Philadelphia has been dealing with just as much frustration.
Following a 2-0 start, the Eagles have lost four consecutive games and are tied with Dallas at 2-4 . Their outlook is arguably worse than the Cowboys, since starting quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season with blood clots in his lungs.
Dallas enters this one with plenty to prove as a team. There are also several individuals who need to step up as well, and here’s a look at the three Cowboys who have the most to prove against the Eagles on Monday Night Football.
Javonte Williams was a surprise star in 2025 , rushing for a career-high 1,201 yards and 11 touchdowns. Through six games in 2026, his numbers have dropped drastically. While he still has been excellent near the goal line with seven touchdowns, Williams has just 317 yards and is averaging 3.7 yards per attempt.
Dallas is being criticized for abandoning the run last week, but Williams wasn’t exactly dominant. Against the Eagles, the Cowboys need him to resemble the player who moved the chains with ease a year ago. If he can’t do that, everything on offense will continue to feel like a chore.
After missing the past five games with a hamstring injury, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is ready to return in Week 7 . Overshown’s return comes at a great time since Dee Winters is likely to miss some time with an Achilles strain .
Overshown has the talent to make a difference, but he must prove to the Cowboys that he can be counted on. He’s missed significant time in each season of his career. Dallas has been dealt one blow after another with injuries and Overshown enters the one feeling the pressure to not only play well, but to stay on the field.
Christian Parker is feeling pressure as a rookie defensive coordinator but after two subpar performances on offense , no one has more to prove than head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
He seemed to get a pass for the team’s struggles in 2025 since his offense was explosive, but now the spotlight is on him. Stephen and Jerry Jones are still singing his praises, but that tune can change in a hurrry, especially if Schottenheimer fails to defeat a wounded Eagles’ team. That’s why the pressure is mounting around the second-year head coach who needs to stop talking about coaching better , and actually begin to coach better.

title: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Who’s Trending For the Field—or IR
full_text:
The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup.
On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday.
Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals.
Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up.
Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year.
“He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday.
Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go.
Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report .
Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited.
Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side.
“They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback.
"I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.”

title: Broncos' Biggest Trade Deadline Need Has Become Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' running back room has failed to perform through six weeks of the 2026 season.
The Broncos are 4-2, but they've gotten little help from their run game. There have been flashes, like Jonah Coleman's rookie debut in Week 2 and the first half of Week 6's win over the Seattle Seahawks, but as a consistent foundation, the Broncos don't have much to build on.
Meanwhile, Bo Nix has been mired in a slump , especially over the past three games. He's won 28 games as a pro, but you could easily count on one hand the number of times he's had a 100-yard rusher.
As Sean Payton has said, quarterback is the hardest position to play in the NFL sans a run game. With the NFL trade deadline approaching on November 10, the Broncos' biggest need is staring them in the face.
Now, there's a chance the worm could turn for this running back ahead of November 10. The Broncos have three games between now and then, and aside from the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8, the defensive competition on the docket pales in comparison to what this offense has faced in the first six weeks.
That's worth remembering: the caliber of defenses the Broncos have gone against to start this season. Not as an excuse, but it's a fact that Denver played the second-toughest schedule through six games based on opposing defenses. It was one slugfest after another.
This is one reason the buzz among the players and coaches at Dove Valley centers on Nix and the offense being poised to finally break out and maybe even go on a run. It's possible, but if the Broncos don't get the answers they're looking for within the next three games, they've got to look hard at possible trades.
Without a viable rushing attack, the Broncos may be able to survive the regular season and make the playoffs, but if they don't win the No. 1 seed and they have to play on the road, the lack of a ground game will catch up with them.
J.K. Dobbins is on pace for a career-low season, averaging 3.3 yards per carry. RJ Harvey has burst and is tough to tackle, but the Broncos seem reluctant to lean on him as a down-to-down rusher.
Coleman is set to return from injured reserve this week, and he's the Broncos' best hope at their run game finally breaking out — beyond a sudden Dobbins resurgence. The rookie runs with good vision and has a blend of power, burst, and contact balance that makes him effective. But Coleman is young and inexperienced.
Dobbins has pointed to the Broncos' schedule as the biggest explanation for the run game's failure to launch, and there's some truth to that. But he doesn't look like the same runner we saw for 10 games last season; he's indecisive and lacking burst.
With only three games between now and the trade deadline, the Broncos need to find out quickly how much Coleman's return can actually help them. Dobbins has been trending toward 20 carries per game of late, but the Broncos would be wise to split a good chunk of those off for Coleman.
There are some potentially great options out there for the Broncos. The Indianapolis Colts are open to parting with Jonathan Taylor , and it's possible the Philadelphia Eagles could listen to offers for Saquon Barkley, given the buzz that they could be poised to kick off a roster reboot.
I'm not sure a back like Tennessee's Tony Pollard would offer a true upgrade over Dobbins worth trading for. And while it would be awesome to see Kyren Williams in the Orange and Blue, the Los Angeles Rams aren't likely to be sellers ahead of the deadline, unless they're unable to snap their two-game losing streak and things only get worse before November 10.
Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving could be interesting, too, as the Bucs seem destined for a losing season and a new coaching regime. The Broncos have options and future draft capital to play with.
Some people would argue that offensive line is a bigger weakness, and I don't disagree that the unit has been disappointing thus far, but if the Broncos went out and acquired left guard Quenton Nelson, as great as he is, he's not going to suddenly spark the offense in the same way that true top-tier running back would.
So, if the Broncos are of a buyer's mindset ahead of the deadline, it's all about the running back market. However, and this is a big caveat, the Broncos have three games left to see whether guys like Dobbins and Harvey can be more productive and how Coleman can help elevate things with his return from IR.

title: Broncos vs. Cardinals: 3 Keys to Avoiding an Arizona Letdown
full_text:
On one hand, Denver Broncos fans can feel good about the team's 4-2 overall record and the defense's performance over the past couple of weeks, particularly with the injuries that have impacted the secondary.
On the other hand, Broncos fans can't be blamed for being worried about the offense, which has yet to put together four quarters of quality play. While it's true the Broncos have faced some good opponents to start the season, they've only surpassed 300 yards of total offense in one game thus far.
One might think facing a 2-4 team is a way to get things right. However, the Arizona Cardinals are not a team to take lightly , as evidenced by their Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
How do the Broncos come out on top in the desert? Let's examine three keys to the Broncos improving to 5-2 rather than winding up in the same position the Rams were in last week.
The Cardinals deserve a lot of credit for finding a way to beat the Rams, despite not scoring a touchdown. But six drives that end in field goals (18 points) are enough when your opponent scores on just three of 10 drives for 16 total points.
"Three of 10 drives for 16 points" could easily describe the Broncos' offense in more than one game this season. But that brings us to a big reason the Cardinals didn't need a touchdown to beat the Rams: they controlled the ball for most of the game.
Against the Rams, the Cardinals won the time of possession, controlling the ball for 34:52 of the game, while L.A. controlled the ball for 25:08. The Cardinals might not have been great on offense, but they did enough to move the chains, keep the Rams' offense on the sideline, and find ways to score.
Time of possession was also key to the Cardinals' season-opening win against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Cardinals controlled the ball for 37:31 while the Chargers controlled it for 22:29.
And time of possession was a key reason the Cardinals stayed in the game when they played the San Francisco 49ers, despite a 36-30 loss. The Cardinals had the ball for 38:44 while the 49ers had it for 21:16. The Cardinals trailed by 11 at halftime (17-6), then outscored the 49ers 24-19 in the second half.
But against the Seattle Seahawks and New York Giants, the Cardinals lost the time-of-possession battle. The Cardinals won that battle against the Detroit Lions, but the difference was less than 30 seconds.
That Rams game is a good example of why a team must be able to move the chains to have success against the Cardinals. And while the 49ers' offense can be explosive, the Broncos have yet to show that trait this season.
Thus, it will be important for the Broncos to show they can control the time of possession and get more points off drives. Doing so will take pressure off the defense.
It will be particularly important for the Broncos to have a good day on offense for two reasons. First, the Cardinals don't have a lot of defensive standouts, with safety Budda Baker as their best player — and he happens to lead the team in sacks with 3.5. The Broncos have to capitalize against a defense that lacks playmakers.
Second, there's no guarantee that the Broncos' offense will always have great field position, even with the defense playing better. That brings us to this point.
This might seem like an obvious point, but against the Cardinals, it carries a lot of importance. That is because the Cardinals have done a good job of taking care of the football over six games.
The Cardinals have just six turnovers in their first six games. The only game in which they had multiple turnovers was against the Giants — the Cardinals had three, but so did New York.
Additionally, the Cardinals have lost the turnover battle just once, that coming against the Lions — and it was Arizona with one while Detroit had none.
Otherwise, the Cardinals have tied with their opponent in turnovers, one to one, against the Rams, 49ers, and Seahawks, while winning the turnover battle against the Chargers, who had two while the Arizona had none.
Because the Cardinals have done a good job limiting turnovers, the Broncos can't depend on the defense to create takeaways, even though that defense has forced six turnovers in the past two weeks. The Broncos' offense has more reason to play well, and taking care of the football is a big step toward having a good day.
The Broncos' offense, to its credit, did not have a single turnover against the Seahawks and has just six in the first six games. But expecting the Broncos' defense to force three turnovers as it did in each of the last two games may be asking a bit much. Bo Nix and the offense need to do their part and do it well.
As for the Cardinals' offense, they don't have a lot of true standouts. Jacoby Brissett is the bridge quarterback to whoever the Cardinals ultimately decide will be the young signal-caller to build around, whether that's Carson Beck or somebody they draft in 2027.
Running back Jeremiyah Love hasn't lived up to expectations thus far, as he's averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, while free-agent signing Tyler Allgeier is averaging 3.0 yards per carry. The Cardinals traded  wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans, leaving them with Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne as their top pass catchers.
But the Cardinals do have one elite playmaker: McBride.
McBride not only leads the Cardinals in receptions with 49, but that number ties him with Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba for the most catches in the NFL through six games. The Cardinals tight end has averaged 7.4 yards per reception and has scored three touchdowns.
Trey McBride somehow makes the grab for the TD 😳 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/GwP9zr7VDe
Broncos fans are all too familiar with the defense's struggles to take opposing tight ends out of the game, particularly those who rank among the best in the NFL. But the Broncos likely won't be able to shut McBride down, even if they have everyone on defense healthy.
That being said, the Broncos do need to find a way to limit McBride's impact. It's possible that linebacker Justin Strnad could get a lot of work here, but who knows what wrinkle Vance Joseph might add to the defense, even if Talanoa Hufanga misses this game and the Broncos might limit Patrick Surtain II's snaps as he returns from an ankle injury, if he plays.
If the Broncos can limit McBride's impact — and if the offense can play well early and build a lead — the pass rush should be able to capitalize.
Brissett has taken 12 sacks in six games, so the Broncos stand a good chance of notching another multi-sack game. But while the Broncos' pass rush is likely to have a good day, the defensive backfield must limit McBride's impact and gains.
On paper, the Broncos are the better team, but what's on paper doesn't always translate to the field. The Cardinals are a well-coached team and have shown they can challenge top-tier opponents in the NFL, especially when they win the time-of-possession battle and limit turnovers.
But because the Cardinals don't have a top defense, the Broncos' offense needs to show it can sustain more drives. If Nix is going to find the game that gets him out of his slump, this is the one.
This game will also require veterans like wide receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle and running back J.K. Dobbins to prove they can make an impact. Getting a healthy Jonah Coleman back should help with the running game.
The defense should do its part, though it may come more in the sack department than in turnovers, which the Cardinals have avoided in most of their games. The main concern is limiting McBride's impact.
If the Broncos' offense can control the time of possession, finish drives, and take care of the football, they should win this one. But if the Broncos have another outing where they score on just three drives for 17 or fewer points, it could come back to haunt them.

title: Courtland Sutton's Bold Prediction Puts Bo Nix Critics on Notice
full_text:
Since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks, the noise surrounding Bo Nix has reached a fever pitch.
Whether it's at the local or national level, the Nix pile-on has reached epic proportions . Since returning from his ankle injury, he hasn't looked the same, but his last three games, in particular, have people around the NFL genuinely concerned. That includes many Broncos fans.
Outside the building, the noise has been deafening. Inside, it's a different story, according to Pro Bowl wide receiver Courtland Sutton, who took to the podium on Wednesday ahead of the Broncos' Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
"Man, there's a sign that's in the building, and I may word it wrong, but I think it's like 'one of the things that can keep a team from being successful is outside noise,'" Sutton said on Wednesday. "For us, the most important thing is this team—everyone that's inside this building. We all know because we're here every day."
Sutton believes that people are entitled to their opinions. And folks are certainly exercising their freedom of speech when it comes to Nix and the Broncos' offense.
Even the nature of the questions Sutton fielded on Wednesday belied the reality of the Broncos sitting at 4-2. You could see that he was a little mystified by the lack of focus on that fact and how the Broncos weathered their initial six-game gauntlet.
"I mean, I'm sure y'all have heard it, and it's not to be taken lightly from the questions you're asking me, but we are 4-2 in this situation," Sutton said.
So, yes. Let's keep things in perspective. The Broncos are 4-2. Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 regular-season starts.
Denver's record has done little to assuage the growing concern over Nix's play, mainly because it contrasts so sharply with the caliber of quarterbacking he showed in his first two years in the league. That's the outside perspective, though; inside the building, Sutton and his teammates see the same all-in preparation and work that Nix has always put in.
"There's not one person, if you ask anybody that's in that building that comes and watches us practice, there's not one person that can say that Bo Nix doesn't come out to practice and give us everything that he has to help us be successful, whether it's in the film room preparing, understanding the game plan, and coming out to practice," Sutton said. "People can say what they want to say. We know that he's putting his all into being the best version of himself so that we can have success."
And that success has been there. That's one of the reasons Sean Payton immediately shot down a question on Monday about whether he's considered benching Nix.
"To answer your question, no," Payton said .
Like Payton and the Broncos' shot-callers, Sutton remains fully of the belief that the worm is going to turn for Nix, and he'll be off and running like the player we saw last year who led this team to a 14-3 finish and the AFC West crown.
"Like I said earlier, at some point the tide's going to turn," Sutton said. "Everyone's entitled to their opinion, and good for them. But we know that he's working his butt off for us to be able to have success, and at some point the tide's going to turn, and everyone's going to be, 'Oh man, Bo Nix is the best. Bo Nix this, Bo Nix that.' And it's like, 'No, keep that same energy.'"
Sutton and his teammates look forward to that moment with relish. He's not panicking, despite being on pace for a career-low season, and we know Nix isn't either.
Nix has maintained his cool throughout this process, even as questions about his health have intensified over the past three weeks. On Wednesday, he may have seemed a bit exasperated to answer the same question about his ankle for the 100th time, but that's the closest I've seen him come to showing any kind of frustration.
"I've told y'all several times I'm all the way back," Nix said toward the end of his presser.
Nix did acknowledge the mental aspect of recovering from a serious injury, but he was adamant, once again, that his ankle is fully healed. However, that doesn't mean that his psyche has caught up quite yet; that much is clear.
The Broncos genuinely believe in Nix — that includes the coaches and the players. He faced a brutal opening schedule — the toughest in the NFL — but things are about to open up.
The Broncos' remaining schedule is the fourth-easiest in the NFL. There are a few toughies along the way, like the Kansas City Chiefs at home in Week 8 and the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 12.
Week 9's road game against the Carolina Panthers could end up being a tougher matchup than it appeared to be when the schedule first dropped back in May. But compared to the weekly onslaught Denver faced to open the season, it's a piece of cake.
The resistance training Nix and the Broncos underwent over the first six weeks has built up some serious strength, both physical and mental. This team's callus is thick, and that's bad news for the opponents remaining on the schedule.
Nix talked Wednesday about his goal to be peaking at the right time — December, January, and February — which is another reason he and the Broncos aren't freaking out like the media and fans are. The Broncos understand how hard it is to win in this league, and they appreciate each one, regardless of the style points.
Despite his foibles in recovering from his ankle, Nix has led the Broncos to a 4-2 start. That can't get lost amid the Nix pile-on.
He's always been more of a finisher. If what Sutton said is any indication, the best of Nix is yet to come.

title: Broncos Can’t Afford to Lose These 2 Matchups vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The schedule might be opening up a bit, but the 4-2 Denver Broncos can't afford to ease off the gas.
Though the schedule is easier, the Broncos have some feisty teams left on the docket, including the 2-4 Arizona Cardinals this week. This isn't a 'gimme' game by any means.
As always, the key matchups will dictate the outcome of this game. If the Broncos want to walk out with a win, they'll have to come out on top in these two matchups.
Nix has played poorly, especially in the past three weeks, and it goes beyond the tough defenses and the type of coverage he's faced. The physical aspect of his ankle isn't the issue, as both Nix and Sean Payton have stated multiple times.
However, Nix did acknowledge on Wednesday that the mental aspect of his ankle recovery has played some role in his early-season performance. When you watch the tape, there is a clear issue with the mental part of the game, so what he said makes sense.
Nix appears to be extra cautious about taking hits. He hasn't been as tough as a runner as he was in years past, and the mental aspect is also showing up in his tendency to bail on clean pockets early.
Nix leads the NFL in clean-pocket bail rate and ranks in the top five in shortest time before leaving the pocket. He's not standing tall and delivering the ball.
Then there's the lack of confidence when attacking vertically, something Nix has talked about at the podium, too. There's a fear of attacking vertically due, perhaps, to some early interceptions, but the Cardinals game is a prime opportunity to work on getting over it.
The Cardinals' defense ranks 31st in explosive pass play rate allowed this season.
Queen's Under Pressure should be the walk-on song for Jacoby Brissett. He's not the most pressured quarterback — ranking eighth-lowest in dropbacks under pressure — but he is one of the worst when pressure does get there.
Brissett averages 3.7 yards per attempt under pressure (third-lowest), and his three interceptions tie for the most. He's not really inclined to take off and scramble, either.
Johnson is part of why Brissett has faced so little pressure. Johnson ranks in the top 10 among tackles in almost every major pass-protection metric.
He has developed into a franchise left tackle and is having the best season of his career by far. However, Johnson hasn't exactly faced the toughest schedule in terms of opposing pass rushers, and none have presented quite the threat that Bonitto does.
In terms of turning pressures into sacks, Bonitto is off to his fastest start as a pro. He ranks 18th in total pressures by edge rushers, but he's also in the top 10 in pass-rush win rate. But when you filter for true pass sets, he drops to 14th.
Bonitto, however, has built up a head of steam over the last couple of weeks, and with the emergence of Que Robinson and the return of Jonathon Cooper , it could put more pressure on the Cardinals' other blockers. Bonitto could be even tougher to contain moving forward.

title: First Week 7 Injury Report Offers Encouragement to Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are getting healthier ahead of their Week 7 road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals.
The team released its first injury report following Wednesday's practice, on which cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss were listed as limited and full participants, respectively.
Moss returned from his rib injury last week, but Surtain has been sidelined with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 4. The perennial All-Pro avoided short-term injured reserve and figures to have a chance to play against the Cardinals — though Week 8 versus Kansas City remains his likeliest target date.
Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was considered limited due to an apparent chest injury he picked up amid last Thursday's win over the Seahawks, during which he exited to the locker room. Waddle seems in little danger of missing Week 7.
Running back Jonah Coleman, as previously reported , logged a full session after being designated to return from injured reserve. Coleman is expected to be activated to the 53-man roster and play at Arizona.
Coleman's services will be required (alongside J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey) with backup RB Tyler Badie nursing a thumb injury, which held him out of Wednesday's practice. Badie will need at least limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at playing.
Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) also did not practice and are unlikely to go Sunday. Elliss is a candidate for IR, though he's anticipated back at some point this season.
“He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," Payton told reporters on Wednesday.
Although some players, such as Hufanga and wide receiver Pat Bryant (IR), are still unavailable due to injury, the Broncos are beginning to round out into shape at an advantageous time — sitting at 4-2 and having completed the toughest portion of their schedule.
Veteran Taylor Rapp filled in admirably for Hufanga last week and figures to do so again. Coleman's reinsertion into the lineup will more than make up for the loss of Badie. Elliss' injury is offset by the reinstatement of incumbent starting OLB Jonathon Cooper, who missed the first six games while on the Commissioner's Exempt list.
“You never know how it’s going to unfold, but that’s a positive relative to our team. We’ll see how this week goes," Payton said regarding Cooper.
All of this, in preparation for a game the Broncos are favored to win by nearly five points. It's been a rollercoaster in the Mile High City thus far, but there's hope that things will soon stabilize.

title: Bo Nix Gets Real About What's Behind His Early Struggles
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 4-2, and that's something to celebrate , especially given the initial six-game gauntlet this team faced.
Alas, the full sweetness of the 4-2 feat has been soured by Bo Nix's ongoing slump. The third-year quarterback simply hasn't looked like himself, leading many to speculate on whether he's truly recovered from his ankle injury.
Nix suffered a fractured ankle in the Broncos' 33-30 overtime win over the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round of the playoffs, which required two surgeries. Both he and the Broncos have been adamant that his ankle is fine, but that doesn't necessarily mean that his psyche has yet to fully recover.
Amid the speculation about the true status of Nix's overall bill of health, the beleaguered signal-caller acknowledged that his ankle injury has played some role in his overall performance this season.
“I’d be lying if I said no," Nix said on Wednesday. "I think that’s just what happens. I think you come back, and every day is a progression. I’m not necessarily doing physical therapy treatment, but I’m out there on the practice field getting rep after rep, trying to get back in super great shape so my carries can go up, so I’m ready when my number’s called and when I can run."
Recovery from severe injury is a process — that, we know. And whether you're an average Joe or a multi-million-dollar pro athlete, the recovery process not only requires the physical injury itself to heal, but also the psyche to trust that it has. The physical and mental healing timetables don't always align perfectly.
Again, Nix emphasized that his ankle is fine. He's healthy, but he was candid in admitting that his recovery has played a role in his relative failure to launch, though he wouldn't say he's been on a "downslope." Perhaps that's because his No. 1 job as a quarterback is to win games, and he's certainly done that.
There may be some lingering mental side effects of his ankle recovery, but Nix was adamant in declaring that he's not afraid. He's not scared to play on his ankle and do his job.
"I’m not scared. I’m not physically worried," Nix said. "I just think there’s something to the sport. I think all guys, when they come back from an injury, just doing it one day at a time. I think that’s just part of the game. That’s part of the process. I had surgery probably six months ago. It takes a while for things to fully reengage."
Recovery is a process, and the time it takes to fully happen is contingent on many variables. According to NFL insider James Palmer , the Broncos have been "concerned" about Nix's performance, but they're standing behind him, fully confident that he's going to turn a corner and get back to the quarterback fans came to know and love over his first two years in the league.
Nix is confident that'll happen, too. And all it could take is one big game for the floodgates to open.
"I feel good physically. I think it’s going to be there," Nix said. "It’s just in football, you have to get that one (game) that just gets you going. I think we’ve been playing some really good teams thus far and haven’t gotten that one, but we’re searching for that one game that sort of just puts us right back where we were.”
Nix has always been a bit of a slow starter. That applies to individual games and seasons as a whole.
It seems to be baked into his DNA as a quarterback. At the same time, though, Nix is a bona fide gamer. And he's one of the NFL's best clutch-time quarterbacks. If we're talking football DNA, he definitely has the clutch gene.
Nix likened his recovery to a mountain. You climb, you climb, and then you finally peak. He wants to be peaking in December and January, rather than, say, September, as we've seen several quarterbacks do throughout NFL history, including this season.
"I don't want to be peaking until the playoffs. I don't want to be peaking at my best because you can't hold it the whole entire season," Nix said. "If you look at a training block, if you look at physical preparation, the guys that can build and grow and get to the peak, which is the playoffs, December, January, February, if you can get to that point and you can hold it, you'll feel really good."
We certainly saw that from Nix last year. He peaked at the best possible time, only to suffer a heartbreaking injury when he'd put the Broncos on the doorstep of the Super Bowl.
Hearkening back to the Peyton Manning days, some Broncos fans may say to themselves, "Well, gee. Can't we have good quarterback play in September, October, November, December, January, and February?"
Touche. But remember, Broncos Country wasn't around for Manning's early-career trial-and-error learning curve. He was an Indianapolis Colt for 14 years first.
Manning is a Hall-of-Famer, as is John Elway. The two have much in common, including multiple World Championships and records, but they also had to bump their heads a bit as young quarterbacks. Neither was a quarterback of legend out of the box, despite both being the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft.
Nix is still in the early developmental years of his NFL career. And yet, he's already accomplished so much. He's got a .700 career winning percentage and is 18-3 in his last 21 starts.
This is why the Broncos' confidence in Nix hasn't been shaken. And despite the funk and the incessant questions about his health, he's still confident he'll get back to playing the brand of football we saw before his ankle injury.
"I'm confident in myself," Nix said. "I know I'm going to get back and be exactly what I was, if not better, because as I get older, that's how it's been. But I do think it's just one game at a time. My training is going like this, and at the end of the day, it's all about getting better."
Getting the run game going would help Nix in his endeavors to improve. Sean Payton is very focused on doing just that entering Week 7's tilt against the Arizona Cardinals.
With rookie running back Jonah Coleman designated to return from injured reserve , the Broncos' ground attack is getting some reinforcements. It can only help Nix get back on his feet and return to playing championship-caliber football.
Nix is looking for that one big game. It could be the Cardinals this week on the road — a place where the Broncos have excelled in recent years.

title: Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman
full_text:
As expected , the Denver Broncos have officially designated rookie running back Jonah Coleman to return from short-term injured reserve—potentially as early as Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
Coleman, placed on IR with an ankle injury following Week 2, was listed as a full practice participant on the team's initial Week 7 status report, along with cornerback Riley Moss (ribs).
The Broncos now have 21 days to activate Coleman to the 53-man roster, for which they'll need to make a corresponding transaction.
The 108th overall pick of this year's draft, Coleman impressed during his limited appearances earlier this season, converting 10 carries into 39 yards and a touchdown. He also caught three passes for 19 yards prior to going down amid Denver's Sept. 20 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
“He played well," head coach Sean Payton said after the Jaguars game. "Then the very end, that last carry was… We work on four-minute [situations], but that certainly didn’t feel like a rookie series, if you will. He came up big, and we needed it. You carry three [running backs] on gameday like everyone else. We were down to two and the fullback. Those guys did a good job, and then we found a couple schemes that we liked and stayed with it. His play right at the end, staying in bounds, that was something you cover, but maybe he doesn’t get those same reps in practice. He did a good job.”
To say there's concern about the Broncos' barely-there rushing attack would be a massive understatement.
Veteran starter J.K. Dobbins has been utterly ineffective , posting a career-worst 3.3 yards per carry across the first six games of the year. RJ Harvey is a dependable pass-catcher out of the backfield, but hardly a workhorse runner. Tyler Badie did not practice Wednesday due to a thumb issue.
As a collective, the Broncos rank 26th in rushing offense, averaging a meager 84.2 yards per game.
Enter Coleman, who should suit up in Arizona and immediately contribute to what could be a ground-oriented game plan versus a susceptible defense, mixing in with (and potentially usurping) Dobbins on early downs before giving way to Harvey in passing situations.
"We think it's a deep room, a talented room," Payton said Wednesday regarding Coleman's return. "So all those things are a positive."

title: Broncos Trade Deadline: 5 Veterans Most Likely to Be Dealt
full_text:
At 4-2, the Denver Broncos are far more likely to be buyers than sellers ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
The Broncos weathered their initial six-game gauntlet as well as anyone could have expected, and now the schedule really opens up, though it's not without its challenges. All of the Broncos' goals are still on the table, which, again, points to the front office being in more of a buyer's mindset.
However, the Broncos do have a handful of potential trade pieces who could draw interest around the NFL. Most of these players are in a contract year, and the Broncos have viable replacement options behind them, in the event of a trade.
Today, we're ranking the players the Broncos would be most likely to trade away. Again, though, the odds of an outbound trade seem pretty slim, as the Broncos are looking to compete for a shot at the Super Bowl.
That being said, you never know. If a team made the Broncos an offer they couldn't refuse, all bets are off. These players will be ranked in order of most to least likely to be traded. Let's dive in.
Moss is in a contract year, and he's poised to command upwards of $20 million per year on his next deal. The Broncos opted not to extend him in the summer, which suggests that the front office is unconvinced on the subject, but it's still possible he could garner an in-season extension at the Week 10 bye.
Moss's rib injury has complicated a potential extension. He originally suffered it in the Broncos' second preseason game , falling on a fumble, but against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 4, he reaggravated it, and missed much of that game, all of Week 5, and only saw 10 snaps in Week 6's win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Meanwhile, Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Daine have played well in the absence of Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Both young cornerbacks have looked starting-caliber , which could clarify the Moss issue for the Broncos.
Barron was a 2025 first-round pick with three more years of cost control on his contract, while Abrams-Draine still has two more years left on his fifth-rounder deal. The Broncos have invested heavily at cornerback for a reason, and in each of the past two seasons, they've had to rely on that depth, which is why I doubt the team looks to trade Moss.
But if the phone rang, GM George Paton will always listen. It would take the right offer to get Moss of Denver's hands, though, especially given that, if they let him depart in free agency in 2027, they could receive a compensatory draft pick as high as a third-rounder.
Moss was a 2023 third-round pick, so if a team wanted him — remember, he's one of the best No. 2 cornerbacks in the NFL — the conversation would likely have to start with a Round 3 pick. Otherwise, there's no upside in Denver losing Moss during the season, although getting a third-round comp pick for him would be the best-case scenario.
Stidham has an $8 million cap number this year , and he just turned 30. He believes he's a starting-caliber quarterback, and despite Nix's slump this season, Stidham is never going to get that opportunity in Denver, especially given how poorly he played in the AFC championship game.
Stidham is also in the final year of his contract. In his training camp battle with Sam Ehlinger , Stidham wasn't the obvious winner, though the Broncos opted to retain him as Bo Nix's primary backup.
I believe the Broncos expect Stidham to leave in 2027 , in hopes of finding a starting opportunity somewhere. The best-case scenario for a comp pick would be a seventh-rounder, so the Broncos could likely be persuaded to part with Stidham with the right offer.
The Broncos have kept Ehlinger around for a reason, and while he's also playing on an expiring contract, I think the team plans on rolling with him as Nix's backup in 2027, while drafting a developmental option in the later rounds.
Mims hasn't looked like himself in his contract year. He changed agents during the offseason in hopes of perhaps getting the Broncos to offer him an extension, and he may have been trending in that direction before a leg injury sidelined him a week into training camp.
Mims missed most of camp and August, but he was able to recover in time to play in the preseason finale. Alas, early in that game, he went up high for a pass near the sideline and came down awkwardly on foot.
In Week 1, Mims didn't look quite right or comfortable, then he missed Week 2 and Week 3. Since his return in Week 4, though, he's been ineffective as a punt returner — his speciality — and a relative non-factor in the passing game.
While Mims was injured, the Broncos elevated undrafted rookie Kolbe Katsis from the practice squad against the Los Angeles Rams, and he turned in a record debut as a returner . The Broncos believe they have something potentially special in Katsis, which is another factor in the cooling of their heels on Mims.
If the Broncos let the chips fall, and Mims departs in free agency next year, depending on the contract he gets from his next team, he could yield a fourth- or fifth-round comp pick. Maybe higher, if some team overpays for him.
Mims was the first draft pick of the Sean Payton era, drafted in Round 2 back in 2023, and he's a two-time Pro Bowl and All-Pro returner. Because Katsis is waiting in the wings, if the right offer came in, I could see the Broncos moving Mims, but given the comp pick the team will receive if it doesn't extend or trade Mims, such an offer would have to be irresistible.
Uwazurike is in a contract year and has not played up to expectations. He's been a key cog in the Broncos' defensive line rotation, but he has failed to build on the progress he showed last year.
Were it not for the emergence of Malcolm Roach , the Broncos' defense wouldn't be weathering the loss of John Franklin-Myers nearly as well as it has. Uwazurike was one of the reasons the Broncos didn't even make an offer to JFM.
Uwazurike was a 2022 fourth-round pick, but he spent the 2023 season suspended for violating the NFL's gambling policy. Otherwise, he would have been a free agent this past spring.
Uwazurike hasn't looked nearly as good against the run and the pass-rush component has been inconsistent. Meanwhile, the Broncos have depth behind him, with a pair of former third-rounders waiting in the wings.
Sai'vion Jones has been getting more playing time this season, and he's looked good as a pass rusher. Meanwhile, rookie Tyler Onyedim has been a healthy scratch all year, while Jones and veteran Jordan Jackson have been getting the game-day nods.
At this stage, I geniunely don't believe the Broncos plan on re-signing Uwazurike. Now, he could turn things around, and change that conversation, but with Roach, Zach Allen, and D.J. Jones balling out, the Broncos have a top-tier starting D-line.
That implies Denver doesn't think Onyedim is ready. But if an interesting offer came in for Uwazurike, you know what they say: necessity is the mother of invention. If Uwazurike walked out the door, the Broncos would have no hesitation in dressing Onyedim.
Losing Uwazurike would weaken them, but at the right price, I could see a deal getting done. However, he's listed second-to-last for a reason: of all the names on this list, his would likely draw the least interest around the league ahead of the deadline.
Sutton is on pace for a career-low season . Much of that is due to Nix's slump and the insane caliber of opponents the Broncos have faced on a weekly basis this season, but Sutton shoulders his share of the blame , too.
Sutton isn't getting off the line of scrimmage well and creating separation consistently. Throw in the absence of his typical intensity at the catch point — turning 50/50 balls into 70/30s — and he's another veteran who simply hasn't looked like himself this season.
At 31, Sutton's best days are behind him, but he's coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons and he made the Pro Bowl last year. His $23.5 million cap number is pretty fair for an aging No. 1 receiver, even if his…

title: Broncos' First Six Games Raise Contract Questions for 5 Veterans
full_text:
Along with decisions on unrestricted and restricted free agents , the Denver Broncos may re-evaluate the contract status of certain players under contract for 2027. There's plenty of time left, but the first six games of the 2026 season may have raised questions about a handful of veterans.
In some cases, these players have little or no guaranteed money left in their deals after this season, while in others, they have option bonuses that the Broncos may exercise to treat as a signing bonus. If they're not exercised, they'd count as base salary.
The Broncos will make these decisions as they figure out their salary cap position. As things currently stand, the Broncos are projected to have about $30.5 million in cap space in 2027, but that's with 38 players under contract and only if the team exercises all of its option bonuses.
Let's examine the Broncos at the top of the list.
The Broncos chose not to exercise Sutton's 2026 option bonus , meaning the $17.5 million he's due will be paid as base salary. In 2027, $10 million of his $19.325 million base salary is injury-only guaranteed, becoming fully guaranteed if he's on the roster on March 17, 2027.
Sutton hasn't had his best start to the 2026 season, with just 9.5 yards per reception. He might be asked to renegotiate his base salary to convert some of it into incentives in exchange for more fully guaranteed money.
If push comes to shove, the Broncos could get out of the deal by cutting Sutton with a post-June 1 designation, which would save $20 million in space with a $6 million dead-money charge. However, it wouldn't be a surprise if the Broncos first try the renegotiation tactic.
Hufanga will be entering the final year of the three-year deal he signed back in 2024. The final year of his contract includes an option bonus of $14.74 million. He also has multiple void years for cap purposes.
Hufanga has played well this season, even though he'll miss a few games with an ankle injury. But if he returns and keeps playing at a high level, the Broncos may want to keep him for the long term.
Thus, the Broncos might choose to extend Hufanga for multiple seasons, which means the option bonus likely becomes an actual signing bonus, and the new years in the contract cover the void years.
If necessary, the Broncos could choose not to exercise the option to reduce dead-money charges when his contract voids. But an extension is in play here.
Jones will enter the final year of the three-year deal he signed in 2024. He's due a $12.235 million base salary and a $765K per-game roster bonus, and none of the money is guaranteed.
Jones has done some good things this season, but he'll be 32 years old. The Broncos could approach him about converting some base salary into incentives in exchange for making the remainder of his salary fully guaranteed.
The Broncos do have the option of cutting Jones, which would free $9.8 million in cap space with a $4.8 million dead-money charge. But the Broncos would likely attempt a contract renegotiation before they'd ever consider cutting him.
Wattenberg had a slow start to the 2025 season, but played better down the stretch, which prompted the Broncos to extend him. This season, he's not off to a good start.
It's possible Wattenberg's play will improve, but if it doesn't, the Broncos will have to decide whether it's worth exercising the option bonus in his contract. He has two such options, one for $3.5 million and another for $7.24 million, that would lower his cap number but come at the cost of pushing his biggest cap hits into future seasons.
Wattenberg's 2027 salary is fully guaranteed, so if he continues to struggle, he can't be cut without significant cap ramifications, and a trade would be unlikely. However, the Broncos could choose not to exercise his option bonuses, which would give them greater flexibility to cut him in 2028 when he'll have no more fully guaranteed money.
Dobbins is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry through six games . He can still break out for a long gain, but he's been slower to hit the hole.
If Dobbins's play doesn't improve in the weeks to come, the Broncos may be prepared to move on next season. That's particularly true if Jonah Coleman impresses once he returns from injured reserve .
Dobbins is due $7 million in base salary and a $1 million per-game roster bonus that aren't guaranteed in 2027. Cutting him would free $8 million in cap space with $2 million in dead money.
If Dobbins doesn't get back on track and the Broncos are content with Coleman and RJ Harvey as the top backs, they may decide to cut Dobbins and not bother with a renegotiated salary.

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games.
Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points.
And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game).
Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game).
Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL.
Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.
Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago.
Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign.
Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit.
In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident.
Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games.
Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday.
However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Thursday Injury Report
full_text:

"And obviously it's good to go into the bye coming off of the performance like we did in the Arizona game. title: Lions Sign Returner to 53-Man Roster, Add Safety to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made two roster moves on Thursday ahead of their Week 7 game against the Green Bay Packers.
Detroit signed wide receiver DeAndre Carter to the active roster from the practice squad, and filled his vacancy on the practice squad by signing veteran defensive back Myles Bryant.
Carter is expected to be the team's primary punt returner and work with Jacob Saylors on kick returns as well after Tom Kennedy suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 5 against Arizona.
Bryant is an intriguing addition and the latest veteran to join Detroit's secondary, albeit on the practice squad. Detroit could elect to elevate him from the practice squad up to three times before they would need to add him to the active roster to continue utilizing him.
The veteran is in his seventh NFL season, having spent four years with the New England Patriots to begin his career before playing for the Houston Texans each of the last two seasons. He had been with the Cleveland Browns' practice squad most recently, and was released by them on Oct. 13.
Bryant has played 77 career games, notching 254 combined tackles, 10 tackles for loss and four interceptions. He has yet to appear in a game in 2026, but played 11 each of the last two years for Houston and appeared in all 17 games for the Patriots in two consecutive seasons from 2022-23.
His most productive season came in 2023, his final year with the Patriots. That year, he started nine games and notched 77 combined tackles, seven tackles for loss and an interception.
Detroit's secondary could get a boost this week , as Brian Branch is on track to play for the first time this season after rehabbing a torn Achilles suffered in December of last season. As a result, Bryant could provide depth on the practice squad or potentially be elevated to contribute on special teams.
The Washington product has logged 515 career snaps on special teams, and even has some experience returning punts for the Patriots where he had 25 returns over the 2022-23 seasons.
Prior to signing Bryant, the Lions had utilized veteran Jalen Mills as a practice squad elevation to provide depth at the safety position. Mills was released from the practice squad after playing the maximum three games.

title: Detroit Lions Make New Punt Returner Decision Crystal Clear
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have made their decision on who will return punts, following the season-ending MCL injury to wide receiver Tom Kennedy.
Special teams coach Dave Fipp, speaking to local reporters prior to practice on Thursday, expressed a new addition on the practice squad will assume the punt return duties.
As MLive explained, "Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp says DeAndre Carter will take over punt return duties for the team and step in as the other kick returner. The Lions signed the veteran WR shortly after Tom Kennedy's season-ending injury."
Carter is currently signed to the practice squad and is a likely candidate to be elevated this week. He could also land a spot on the active roster at some point, if he excels in the role he was brought to Motown to accomplish.
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: One Trade Deadline Move GM Brad Holmes Must Prioritize ASAP
Earlier this week, wide receivers coach Scottie Montgomery explained it would not be that simple to replace Kennedy, whether it was at practice or on Sundays.
“It's more difficult than you think, because for certain instances, he is a security blanket that can actually do more than secure you,” Montgomery expressed. “He can play the F, he can play the X, he can play the Z. I can give him exactly what I want, man, and I get that information even quicker than I can from the box sometimes, because he's right there with me on the sideline.
"So, that part is difficult," Montgomery added further. "The other part is just the competitive nature that he has inside of the room, making our guys compete in the classroom, making sure everybody, the details when it's asked, is answered the right way.”
Carter signed with the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2015. The veteran has also had stints with the Houston Texans and Chicago Bears before finding success with the Washington Commanders in 2021.
He was able that season to secure an NFC Special Teams Player of the Week nod, after a 101-yard kickoff return for a touchdown and a receiving touchdown that was the first of his career.

title: Lions Week 7 Game Officiated by One of NFL's Most Flag-Happy Crews
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions ’ Week 7 game against the Green Bay Packers has been revealed.
For Sunday’s game, the Lions have drawn Alex Moore’s crew to preside over the game. Moore is in his second season as an official, and will be working a Lions game for the first time in his career in the role.
Moore’s first five games have carried an interesting trend, as the road team has won in each of the five games.
Moore had worked the previous three years as an umpire before being promoted to a referee in 2025. In a corresponding move at the time, Tra Blake returned to being an umpire.
While he has never served as a head referee for a Lions game, he did serve as an umpire for the Lions’ Divisional Round playoff game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023.
He has reffed the Bills’ win over the Texans in Week 1, the Panthers win over Atlanta in Week 2, Kansas City over Miami in Week 3, Jacksonville over Cincinnati in Week 4 and Tampa Bay’s win over Dallas on Thursday Night Football in Week 5. Moore’s crew did not work a game in Week 6.
Moore has worked one Packers game in his career as a head referee, that being their win over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 19, 2025.
In terms of penalties called, there has been a slight skew toward the visiting team through Moore’s first five games of the season. There have been 54 penalties called on away teams, while home teams have been flagged 39 times according to NFL Penalties .
In the last two games, Moore’s crew has thrown a total of 45 penalty flags as there have been over 20 in each of those games. His crew has called 30 offensive holding penalties up to this point, according to NFL Penalties, which ranks second behind Scott Novak’s crew.
In total, Moore’s crew ranks second behind Novak for the most penalties enforced. His average of 20.2 total flags called per game is tied-for-second with Craig Wrolstad’s crew behind Novak.

title: Detroit Lions TE Sam LaPorta Is Biggest Loser In Tone-Deaf Interview
full_text:
That is all Detroit sports fans are asking these local athletes to do. Nobody is burying their heads in the sand, oblivious to the fact these athletes are playing a kids game for a significant amount of money.
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta quickly learned that fans in Detroit are not going to sit back and watch him proclaim that he can get paid elsewhere.
Lately, each professional team in Detroit has had one player make their contract situation very awkward and uncomfortable.
LaPorta, a former second-round who is playing on the last year of his rookie contract, went on the "Pardon My Take" podcast and was likely a little too comfortable when he answered the question about playing in 2026 without having a new contract extension.
The Red Wings are dealing with Dylan Larkin, whose demand to be traded went public. The Tigers eventually dealt pitcher Tarik Skubal, but not before he spent a couple of years proclaiming his love for the City and wanting to be a member of the Tigers, yet hired a powerful agent to get him to a team that could possibly pay him a lucrative contract. Jalen Duren of the Pistons caught the wrath of fans for how his saga played out over the course of an entire summer.
How did that trip to Sacramento go Jalen? Nobody believed seriously that he was interested in joining an irrelevant NBA franchise. It was all a negotiation ploy.
LaPorta failed to realize his comments came across to regular fans as tone-deaf and selfish. Everybody understands he wants to be paid a contract that is similar to or exceeds what the top players at his position earn.
He may have even been low-balled by general manager Brad Holmes.
What turned many people off is the flippant answer that came across that he did not care much if his playing days were in Detroit or somewhere else.
Fans have been asked to weather raising ticket prices, a team that has regressed and witnessing one of the worst defenses in NFL history.
The last thing they were interested in hearing was a star player talking about taking his ball and going somewhere else.
Yes, we like players to join podcasts and be honest. But the 25-year-old could have answered the question much, much differently.
Do the Lions even have a P.R. staff? It appeared the staffer assigned to LaPorta might have just taken the week off or didn't care he was going to appear on one of the biggest sports podcast of all-time.
Maybe the Lions public relations department were updating their files that week? Who knows.
He could have mentioned his frustrations and why. The part of the answer that frustrated people the most was, 'If I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever.'
Really showing that appreciation for the fans that pay high ticket prices to watch the Lions each and every week.
In an economy where many are struggling financially, those type of comments should have been reserved for his agent of his friends. Maybe the backlash will wake up more players to the idea that many fans care more about the logo on the front than the name on the back.
If LaPorta leaves, Detroit will simply draft another solid tight end and it will still be all good. So, whatever.
LaPorta should have read the room better and maybe taken a page out of the playbook of Jack Campbell, who masterfully handled his contract talks and eventual extension.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the Lions Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
It's no secret that the Detroit Lions have a glaring need on their roster ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With one of the league's worst pass defenses and little in the way of reinforcements, Detroit would benefit greatly from being active on the trade market and adding a cornerback to the mix.
Fortunately for Detroit, there are some teams with intriguing options who have struggled out of. the gate and as a result could be enticed to make a deal. One team worth watching at the deadline is the winless Los Angeles Chargers, who have fallen to 0-6 with a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6.
Los Angeles has a trio of intriguing cornerbacks who could draw some trade interest, with the top option being third-year option Tarheeb Still. The former fifth-round pick is on his rookie contract through the end of next season, and as a result fits Detroit's current financial situation in addition to having plenty of upside.
Still has been fairly productive through the first six games of the season. While he hasn't logged an interception this season, the Maryland product has notched an overall defensive grade of 71.6 and a coverage grade of 76.6 via Pro Football Focus.
He has allowed an opposing passer rating of 93.6 according to PFF, which is lower than Detroit's three highest-utilized cornerbacks in D.J. Reed (124.2), Roger McCreary (111.6) and Rock Ya-Sin (96.7).
Reed, in particular, has been underwhelming . The veteran was signed last offseason with the expectation of being the top cornerback, but hasn't lived up to that billing early in his tenure.
Ennis Rakestraw, the team's second-round pick in 2024, has been intriguing but hasn't had the level of consistent reps that would cement him as a top option.
The Lions need to find a consistent option to provide them with a boost for the second half of the season, as the assembly they've had early in the year hasn't been satisfactory. Detroit has been fortunate to get enough offensive production throughout the 3-2 start, but these secondary issues could haunt them in pivotal games.
Still has the ability to help right the ship, and may not carry a hefty asking price. As a former fifth-round pick, perhaps the Lions could swing a deal providing the Chargers with a fourth-round pick to give the Chargers more draft value than what they used on him.
With four career interceptions, Still has some proven ball production. He could be a difference-making addition, and as a young player could have plenty of room to grow in Detroit's scheme. Ultimately, making this move would be a win for general manager Brad Holmes, and would give the team another intriguing young option along with Rakestraw.

title: 3 Lions Impacted Most by Brian Branch's Return from Injury
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are getting a big playmaker back for their defense in safety Brian Branch.
Assuming all goes to plan for the remainder of this week, Branch is expected to suit up for the first time this season when the Lions take on the Green Bay Packers Sunday at Ford Field. He could be one of two big returns the Lions get from injury, as center Cade Mays is also trending toward playing.
If Branch is able to go, it adds a significant level of production to Detroit's defense heading into a pivotal stretch that starts with back-to-back division games at home. There will be a ripple effect felt throughout Detroit's defense, as his return will cause some shuffling in the secondary.
Here are three players who will feel the impact of Branch's return from injury.
Clark is a veteran who inked a one-year deal with Detroit heading into the season. He was expected to fill in for depth purposes until Branch returns, but based on how things have shaken out he could still find himself in the starting lineup next to Branch moving forward.
Avonte Maddox, who was the team's other starter at safety to open the year, is out for the season after an injury against Buffalo in Week 2. Christian Izien is another option , but his role has diminished after a decent start to the season. Meanwhile, Thomas Harper is also on injured reserve.
With Branch likely returning in a significant role, Clark appears to be the best option to play alongside him at this stage of the season. He could fill the void left by Kerby Joseph for the time being, as Joseph remains sidelined with a knee injury.
Izien was signed with the thought of playing multiple positions in Detroit's secondary. However, that hasn't quite materialized due to a number of factors throughout the early part of the season. He missed the season opener with an injury, and has shuffled between nickel and safety.
In their win over the Arizona Cardinals, Izien did not play one defensive snap as Detroit turned to Keith Abney to play the safety spot alongside Clark. Injuries could always open up an opportunity down the line, but for the time being it appears Izien may be limited to special teams.
One avenue the Lions could explore with him is playing the nickel spot, though that wasn't an option for him in Arizona. If he's going to get snaps defensively with Branch back in the mix, nickel may be the best spot for him to do
Week 5 was a big one for the rookie out of Arizona State. Abney recorded his first-career interception , and had a huge role playing the safety spot in Detroit's defense for the first time. While it wasn't a perfect debut, Abney showed that he is capable of contributing and earned a longer look.
It's tough to say when that look may come if Branch returns to full health and is able to play a big role right away. He could still spell his veteran counterpart so as not to rush him back too quickly, but the Lions will want Branch on the field whenever possible.
As a result, the Lions could experiment with playing Abney more on the boundary in place of one of their struggling cornerbacks, or align him in the nickel spot more often. He's proven to be deserving of another opportunity, but Branch's return complicates exactly when and how he'll line up moving forward for the Lions' defense.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Estimated Wednesday Injury Report
full_text:
The Detroit Lions released their first Week 7 injury report, ahead of the teams first divisional contest at Ford Field against the Green Bay Packers.
Last week, the team had a bye, so the scheduled players day off was Wednesday this week, resulting in an estimated injury report.
Veteran defensive back Rock Ya-Sin was listed as a limited participant , while Cade Mays and Brian Branch, who are both expected to suit up against Green Bay, were listed as full participants.
Head coach Dan Campbell has expressed respect for the Packers and their ability to force takeaways.
"I know I mentioned some of this yesterday, but they're playing really good football right now," said Campbell. "Two of their best games have been these back-to-back games. Plus-six in the turnover ratio the last two weeks, it was seven takeaways on defense, man. It's an opportunistic defense. They fly around the football. They disguise well and create issues. (Packers Head Coach) Matt (LaFleur)’s doing a hell of a job. They have, they've gotten better every week, man. They've settled some things in in that O-line. (Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan) Gannon's doing a hell of a job with that defense too."
Campbell added further, "They've just steadily gotten better and better and they're playing at a very high level right now. Offensively (Jordan) Love, man, he makes it go. He is the secret sauce. And (Christian) Watson and (Matthew) Golden, man, they're dangerous threats down the field and he's going to give them opportunities that shows up every week. (Tucker) Kraft has come off the injury nicely. He's gotten better every week. He's playing good football right now."
The Packers arrive with a record of 4-2, having defeated the Dallas Cowboys last week.
"This team's playing at a high level," said Campbell. "They're big, physical and special teams, man, they play hard. So, this will be an outstanding test for us. Hell of an opponent, first division game of the season at home. We're looking forward to it, but this is a real good team right now playing good football.”

title: Sam LaPorta Reveals Extreme Frustrations: I Break My F'''ing Back For Lions
full_text:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta sounded off about his contract frustrations during a recent episode of the "Pardon My Take" NFL podcast.
Recently, reports surfaced that indicated LaPorta's camp and the Lions have tabled contract negotiations during the regular season.
The former second-round pick understands part of the reason the Lions' running game has been so successful has been his efforts blocking. He has made previous references to the challenges of blocking defensive ends who are much larger than he is.
“I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport we play, it sucks. It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta explained on the popular sports podcast. "Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f***ing back for this team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m ballin. And maybe they’re just not showing the love.”
Detroit has the option of using the franchise tag on LaPorta for the upcoming 2027 NFL season. General manager Brad Holmes has not chosen to use this salary-cap leverage, but may be forced to.
If LaPorta continues to play at a high level, he could command north of $20 million annually.
Detroit does have the salary-cap space, but may be forced to ink a cornerback to a hefty contract and there is still the matter of what to allocate for safety Brian Branch.
LaPorta indicated he still plans to play at a high level, and if that means he is wearing a new uniform next season, that will just have to be how it is.
As LaPorta explained, “So I’m going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good . I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever."
The highest-paid tight ends in the NFL are George Kittle (19.1 million), Trey McBride (19 million) and Tucker Kraft (18.75 million).
Kraft visits Ford Field this weekend for the matchup against the Lions in Week 7.
