title: 1 Name Keeps Avoiding Blame While Harbaugh, McDaniel Take Heat for Chargers’ Downfall
full_text:
Much has gone wrong for the Los Angeles Chargers this year. It’s quickly becoming one of the most notorious regressions in modern times, which points the finger at Jim Harbaugh and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel .
But one name who keeps avoiding criticism despite being the overarching culprit?
General manager Joe Hortiz.
Hortiz isn’t in Baltimore anymore, but sometimes with the way he operates the Chargers, it makes it feel like he’s confused when looking at maps. The overemphasis on compensatory picks, saving cash for future years and conservative overall approach don’t work in Los Angeles.
That’s not hindsight talking either: The proof has been right there from the beginning.
Hortiz and Harbaugh have cheaped out on the interior offensive line from the jump. The result has been relying on guys like Bradley Bozeman in schemes authored by Greg Roman, essentially asking Justin Herbert to play hero ball and risk himself more than necessary.
Even the overcompensation this offseason has backfired. McDaniel’s scheme is a mess, partially because Hortiz hasn’t built the roster properly. And even going to get Tyler Biadasz was conservative, considering they signed him before the market could open and balloon prices. Bigger, better names weren’t likely realistic because they wanted a "deal."
Again, the Chargers are 31st in cash spend. The Athletic’s Mike Sando re-shared one quote from an anonymous executive.
"Their quarterback is making $24 million (in base salary) this year, and they are going to be the (second-)lowest cash spending team in the league," the exec told Sando. "Take advantage of this and get good players, even if it's just on one-year deals."
Sando followed it up with a haymaker: “In retrospect, think how much better the Chargers might be if they had spent for guard Isaac Seumalo instead of Cole Strange, whom McDaniel knew from Miami, for cheap.”
Thing is, this didn’t need to be in retrospect. The strategy has been off from the beginning. They’re overreliant on struggling draft picks like Quentin Johnston. They don’t want to pay Odafe Oweh despite trading for him, so they burn a first-round pick on an older prospect like Akheem Mesidor. Even burning a first-rounder on a running back is extremely questionable when looking at the whole roster.
All this while the Chargers sit on plenty of cap space while the rest of the NFL outspends them. Spending isn’t everything , but it’s a sign. And for all their faults, Harbaugh and McDaniel are only working with what Hortiz gives them and the organization permits.

title: Jim Harbaugh’s Hot Seat for Chargers Gets Important Detail via NFL Rumors
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers hit the bye week widely expected to, if nothing else, fire offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel .
Yet, to start the brief bye week work, McDaniel was right there alongside head coach Jim Harbaugh for the Chargers. Interviews didn’t hint at much, either.
So, the question is pretty simple: Are the seats hot in Los Angeles at all after an 0-6 start?
It shouldn’t even be a question, of course. But if the Chargers were going to make changes, one would’ve thought they would happen as early in the week as possible in order to use the full bye to get things changed smoothly.
With nothing doing, the gaze for Chargers fans should probably turn toward the end of the season for changes.
And indeed, NFL rumors and buzz have something to say on that topic.
There’s a common idea that Jim Harbaugh’s contract could prevent the Chargers from firing him early. As we broke down on Harbaugh’s contract , he signed a five-year, $80 million deal with a possible $16 million per-year number.
Harbaugh’s contract runs through 2028, making it unlikely that the Chargers just pay him a smooth $16 million or more in 2027 and beyond to not coach the team.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , context around the Chargers is important: They very much care about their image.
“But as a few industry sources pointed out, a bottom-of-the-league finish would force the Chargers to do some soul-searching, in part because the Chargers play home games in a stadium they don't own,” Fowler wrote. “Maintaining excitement is important in that regard.”
Chargers fans would probably like if social media and the “little brother” complex mattered less and that a firing would happen due to justified performance reasons. But hey, something is better than nothing here, right?
The Chargers might be content to call this year a mulligan after Harbaugh’s strong first two years. But flopping this bad with no real end in sight in what was supposed to be a contention year is brutal. And they run the risk of wasting more of Justin Herbert’s prime by rerunning the same thing again in 2027, if not longer.
At the bye, the Chargers are looking at 0-6 and, given the strength of the schedule, potentially 0-9 before things ease up a bit. If they’re 2-15 or 3-14 by the end of the year, there’s no rehabbing the beloved image. The fact folks around the NFL are already talking about this doesn’t paint Harbaugh’s future in the best of lights, at least.

title: Ranking the Chargers Players Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and trying to find answers during their bye week. They entered week six for showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs with a dramatically different group of starters on offense in comparison to week one due to an avalanche of injuries .
The reality of an 0-6 start has started to become publicly evident. Head coach Jim Harbaugh has ditched his typical non-answers at press conferences and has opted to use the "we're looking at everything" response to avoid completely running over some of his coaches with the proverbial bus.
The Chargers front office has yet to publicy acknowledge where the team is currently at but over this bye week and before the  trade deadline of  November 10th general manager Joe Hortiz will undoubtedly be fielding calls from across the NFL inquiring on potential trades for Chargers players.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero wrote about the Chargers potential trade targets on his Substack before their week six loss. Alongside Mack, on defense he named Bud Dupree, Daiyan Henley, Donte Jackson, Denzel Perryman, Dalvin Tomlinson, and Tuli Tuipulotu as all potential trade candidates. On offense, he listed Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and Quentin Johnston as potential players teams may inquire about.
Note that Pelissero did not include franchise quarterback Justin Herbert. That is because trading Justin Hebert for starters would financially be a disaster for the franchise and more importantly, it would be an absolutely insane idea. Justin Herbert is not going anywhere and a Herschel Walker trade offer mid-season would not change that.
Wide receivers, defensive line or edge rushers and cornerbacks are the three position groups most likely to be traded looking back over the past five years with offensive line and running backs being the next most frequently dealt position groups. With that in mind, coupled with contracts, let's go through and rank the Chargers most likely to be traded, why and who would replace their snaps.
52 sacks his 52nd qb pic.twitter.com/M8wEq6sTx9
Khalil Mack is the most obvious and most likely Chargers player to be traded by the trade deadline, if he chooses. Mack is a future Hall of Famer and his loyalty to the organization has earned him the right to make that decision in what could be the final year of his NFL career.
Mack is still playing at a high level and could net the Chargers an early day three pick. He in unlikely to net a Day 2 pick for such a short-term rental despite some current media reports stating otherwise.
The Chargers already have two starting-caliber edge rushers on the roster with Tuli Tuipulotu and rookie Akheem Mesidor. They also have Bud Dupree and Caleb Murphy on the active roster and Andre Carter II on the practice squad. They wouldn't have the deepest edge rusher room without Mack but have the bodies to manage the move.
Cornerbacks are always in high demand around the NFL given the nature of modern NFL offenses and injury rates. Donte Jackson has dealt with a handful of minor injuries this season but is still a well rounded zone cornerback with veteran savvy. The only reason the Chargers would reject offers for him, since he is on an expiring contract, is simply they do not have enough depth to replace him.
Jackson is on the wrong side of 30 but is still playing at a level that contenders would value if they needed a veteran capable of stepping in and starting. He would likely net the Chargers a late day three pick as compensation.
The Chargers cornerback room was thin to start the season and have already dipped into the practice squad for help and have signed several cornerbacks to the practice squad throughout the season for depth.
Keaton Mitchell was one of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's top free agent requests when he came to Los Angeles. The offense has been a mess but Mitchell has been relatively productive when included in the game plan. With the season lost and Mitchell's cap number nearly doubling from just over $3.1 million to just over $6.1 million in 2027, the Chargers may move on from him if a needy team inquires.
The Chargers likely would have to pick between Kimani Vidal and Mitchell. Vidal will be a restricted free agent next offseason and the Chargers could simply choose to prepare to extend or match any offer he receives. Mitchell would likely net the Chargers a mid-late Day 3 pick or could be included in a pick swap.
Los Angeles already has a replacement for Mitchell on the practice squad in Greg Desrosiers Jr. Desrosiers has a very similar skillset and finished off the preseason with a massive performance. Like Mitchell, he can return kicks and is a threat in the passing game.
UDFA Greg Desrosiers Jr. takes off for the TD! He has 73 total yards on just 6 touches 🔥 Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dZ8FKk5DNg
Wide receivers are the most likely position group to be moved at the trade deadline. Quentin Johnston has not done much this season but neither has the entirety of the Chargers offense. Johnston had put together back to back ascending seasons in 2024 and 2025 and the former first round receiver seemed to finally be finding his footing as an NFL receiver.
57 yards from Herbert to Johnston! LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/a6kEFGZWO4
If anyone might benefit from a change in scenery, it would be Johnston. His first-round pedigree will always carry some weight, right or wrong, and he is under contract through 2027. A contender looking for help down the stretch could find the right fit for him and he could net the Chargers an earlier to mid Day 3 pick.
One of the few reasons the Chargers would not entertain offers for Johnston would be that the rest of the wide receiver room have been unable to stay on the field. The Chargers do have a pair of young receivers in Keandre Lambert-Smith and Theo Wease Jr., both of whom could pick up the slack if he were moved as the Chargers may look to the future to see who they will keep around.
The Chargers are likely to move at least one player before the trade deadline. They have massive organizational questions to answer and roster construction issues to reconcile. This is a new situation for the organization. Since the expansion to the seven team playoff, mid-season trades have been occuring at an increased rate. Los Angeles could benefit from extra picks in 2027 and giving young players opportunities to play.
Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs. He graduated from UC Riverside with a degree in Political Science and The University of Redlands with an MBA.

title: Would Chargers Assist Chiefs With Quentin Johnston Trade Before Deadline?
full_text:
The rumors of Quentin Johnston being traded are spreading like wild fire, especially since the Chargers are winless going into the bye week.
Johnston joining the Kansas City Chiefs would be an interesting development , especially considering the rivalry between the two AFC West teams. That is a trade you just wouldn't see coming to be honest.
According to Bleacher Report NFL writer Gary Davenport , the Chiefs were identified as the best landing spot for the wide receiver in a potential trade scenario. Granted, Davenport noted that this could be extremely impossible.
Johnston was selected 21st overall in the 2023 NFL Draft after a standout college career at TCU. While his professional career has included some ups and downs, he has shown flashes of the ability that made him a first-round pick.
Adding another receiver could give Patrick Mahomes another option in the passing game. They are never a team that has true depth at the receiver position. Johnston’s size and ability to stretch the field could make him an intriguing target, particularly if the Chiefs believe a change of scenery could help him reach another level.
However, there is a financial side to consider. Johnston’s fifth-year option reportedly carries a heavy burden. So you would be gambling on his development as a player and his hefty contract.
There is also the obvious rivalry factor. Trading a former first-round pick to a division opponent is not necessarily something a team would want to do, especially if that player could become a bigger threat in a different uniform.
For now, this is simply a proposed landing spot, not a confirmed destination. The Chargers would have to decide whether moving Johnston makes more sense than continuing to develop him, while the Chiefs would need to determine whether the potential reward justifies the cost. Of course, there is so much that would go into this type of situation that everything is theoretical.
Johnston has already demonstrated that he can produce at the NFL level, but his next step will depend on finding consistency and making the most of his opportunities. Sometimes players just need a different scenery to thrive.
A move to Kansas City would certainly add another layer to one of football’s most competitive divisional rivalries. Still, until there is a confirmed report of actual trade discussions or an agreement, this remains a possibility to watch rather than a move that should be expected.
Brennan is sports writer focused on delivering sharp analysis, real-time reactions, and engaging storytelling focused on NFL analysis.  He is passionate about football and breaking down what matters to bring fans closer to the action.  Brennan comes from a family of Chargers fans.

title: Jim Harbaugh Ruining Justin Herbert Rumblings Keep Increasing
full_text:
There’s a concerning, budding idea around the hapless Los Angeles Chargers right now: Jim Harbaugh is doing more harm than good for Justin Herbert.
Most of the attention for the 0-6 Chargers at the bye week falls on offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel . His complexity of the scheme, proper talent for the scheme, all that stuff has come under fire with McDaniel so far.
But that’s overshadowing another uncomfortable topic around the Chargers when it comes to how Harbaugh actually fits Herbert, too.
And no, this doesn’t have anything to do with Harbaugh’s gushy exaggerations about Herbert, such as declaring him on the way to being one of the best ever or that he dreams of getting a Lombardi Trophy with his star quarterback.
In fact, this idea about Harbaugh hurting Herbert goes back to 2024.
While examining the Chargers’ issues, The Athletic’s Mike Sando put Harbaugh himself under the microscope.
Sando’s most crushing point: “Herbert ranked seventh in expected points added per pass play under two other head coaches and three offensive coordinators across his first four seasons. He ranks 23rd under Harbaugh, and the trend is unmistakable (12th in 2024, 21st last season and 32nd this season).”
We can bemoan how the Chargers spend money or how general manager Joe Hortiz builds out a roster. But that roster has input from Harbaugh.
And it’s Harbaugh who went with his friend Greg Roman for multiple years as coordinator, taking Herbert and placing him in a conservative offense that asked him to play hero ball far too much.
And it’s Harbaugh who had an uncanny loyalty to middling players like Bradley Bozeman in the heart of the offensive line.
And now it’s Harbaugh leaving his comfort zone and dramatically over-correcting with the hire of McDaniel, which is currently doing far more harm than good. Credit for trying to right the ship by doing something that was widely accepted as a good move, but it’s a byproduct of the prior mistakes.
Make no mistake, Herbert deserves some blame too. The overarching franchise and Hortiz, especially so.
But it does feel like Harbaugh isn’t getting enough criticism for holding back Herbert because a few years ago, nobody would have expected a regression for the star quarterback compared to the Brandon Staley days.

title: Chargers Could Use Unexpected Veteran Trade Option Before Deadline
full_text:
With the Los Angeles Chargers securing the first overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft order for now, they are expected to be a team looking to "sell" or, in other terms, trade away valuable assets to teams who are looking to "buy" or to improve their roster for a playoff run.
Even with the team being the worst in the NFL, the Chargers still have plenty of players under contract who could be potential trade candidates. The biggest of those names is the veteran, future Hall of Fame EDGE rusher, Khalil Mack.
With Mack swirling in trade rumors, one name has been largely forgotten until a recent CBS Sports article by Carter Bahns named the Chargers veteran CB, Donte Jackson, as a possible candidate to be moved to a different team.
In Bahns' article, he discusses Jackson's possibility of being traded: "Teams with holes on the back end of the defense could call about Jackson and his expiring contract, too. He racked up nine interceptions across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, after all."
Jackson has been a long-time starting-caliber corner since he was drafted in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft by the Carolina Panthers. After six seasons with the Panthers, Jackson spent a year in Pittsburgh, where he began to earn his ballhawking moniker, which he replicated in his first season in Los Angeles under defensive coordinator Jesse Minter.
Now in year two with the Chargers, Jackson has only played in four games, recording two pass deflections and eight tackles. While he has been on the field, he has been a solid contributor for Chris O'Leary's defense, but a hamstring injury has kept him off the field for nearly half the season.
If a team needs a veteran presence who is known for turnovers in their back seven, adding Jackson is a good idea. He would likely only cost a Day 3 selection, with a fifth-round pick being within reason for a player of his caliber.
The Chargers have not exactly found options behind Jackson as starting-caliber cornerbacks in the defense, as Deane Leonard and Rodney Shelley have been either hurt or lackluster, but at 0-6, having strong CBs is somewhat of a luxury, considering the season is just about over.
It should be noted that Bahns' article also mentions Khalil Mack, Quentin Johnston and David Njoku as other trade candidates for the Bolts to "sell."

title: Rams Midweek Report: Sean McVay Faces His Toughest Test, Myles Garrett Uncertainty, Wide Receiver Trade Targets
full_text:
Throughout the Sean McVay era, there have been some difficult seasons and slow starts for the Los Angeles Rams. Despite all of the adversity in past seasons, what the Rams are going through now may be his toughest challenge yet.
In 2020, the Rams started 4-1 and had the No. 1 defense in the NFL. However, the relationship between McVay and quarterback Jared Goff hit a breaking point. After McVay broke out in a “run it back” chant at the Super Bowl parade, the Rams went 5-12 and the head coach almost walked away. The Rams started 3-6 in a “re-tool” year, and McVay clawed that team back to make the playoffs. When the Rams started 1-4 in 2024, McVay got that team out of its funk and won the NFC West.
There have been a lot of trials, tribulations, and moments of adversity for McVay. However, what the Rams have gone through in 2026 through six weeks has been mentally exhausting. This is a team that entered the season as Super Bowl favorites. They traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie to help get them over the top.
However, with each passing week, the Rams seem to hit a new low. The issues that have plagued this roster over the last two years continue to haunt them. Against the Buffalo Bills, they were a blocked field goal away from their most impressive win of the season. This is a roster that should be 4-2 instead of 2-4. But that’s not where this team is.
Over the last two years, this is a team that continues to find new ways to lose. The heartbreaking losses continued to mount following Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals. After the game, running back Kyren Williams seemed to throw shade at his role when asked why the offense lacked energy, saying, “I can't tell you, bro. Probably because I'm not out there.”
This isn’t to say that McVay is on the verge of losing the locker room or anything to that extreme. With that said, he needs to find a way to bring this locker room together. Williams’ comments, for as much as the Rams may want to brush them aside, are a sign of the team imploding from within. How the Rams have lost in combination with the pressure they faced coming into the season would be mentally draining on any team.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have hit the injury bug hard. They lost wide receiver Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks and defensive lineman Kobie Turner also ended up on injured reserve . Puka Nacua hurt his calf and was limited in Thursday’s practice.
Whatever timeline the Rams entered in which it’s as if they walked under a ladder once a day for an entire year, it’s with certainty that they want out. McVay has proven throughout the last decade that he’s one of the best leaders in the NFL. His leadership will be put to the test if he’s going to reel this team back in for another comeback.
Following the game against the Denver Broncos, the Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. The next week on the Coach McVay show, McVay told J.B. Long that Ferguson would be ready to go after the four weeks. “Bummer for Ferg, man. But he’ll be back, he’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” said McVay at the time.
That four-week period would have placed Ferguson’s return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. While McVay didn’t specify an exact timeline, It didn’t sound as if Ferguson would be out past the four-week injured reserve period.
For an offense that has lacked speed and explosiveness out of 13 personnel, Ferguson’s return would certainly be welcomed. McVay answered questions on Ferguson on Monday.
“No updates on Terrance, he's just continuing to rehab,” McVay said. “I don't have any sort of imminent return for him quite yet.”
On Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter noted that Ferguson is not expected to be ready next week. According to Schefter, Ferguson’s recovery will take time. That doesn’t sound as if Ferguson's return is imminent. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams’ tight end was out until the bye week in Week 11.
The Myles Garrett injury saga continues to linger . After Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, he was given a six-week timeline. However, at the time, it was said that Garrett was determined to beat that. Later, it was reported that the Rams were hopeful that Garrett could return last week against the Cardinals, but a return in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders was more realistic. The six-week timeline was a worst-case scenario.
Earlier this week, ESPN’s Dan Graziano slipped in a nugget on Garrett’s potential return in his weekly notebook. While reporting that the Rams would explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver, Graziano also noted that Garrett could likely be out for “another two or three weeks at least.”
If Garrett is out another two or three weeks, that would make the six week timeline a seven or eight week timeline. Much like Ferguson, it would not be surprising if Garrett remained sidelined until after the bye week.
On the final drive against the Cardinals in Week 6, Davante Adams pulled up with a hamstring injury. After the game, it was revealed that Adams had ruptured his hamstring and would be out 6-10 weeks.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Adams is set to undergo a procedure to repair his hamstring by Neal ElAttrache in Los Angeles. Fowler reported that the hope is for Adams to return on the front-end of that 6-10 week timeframe and as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible.
Rams WR Davante Adams will undergo a procedure to repair his ruptured hamstring via renowned Dr Neal ElAttrache, per source. Adams hopes to return on the front end of the 6-10 week timeframe, as close to the post-Week-11 bye as possible, the source said. pic.twitter.com/6V6v0xglhS
McVay said on Wednesday that Adams hadn’t had surgery yet and they were still figuring out details.
“I think they’re going to give it a couple of days and figure out exactly when is the best time. It’s more of a cleanup type of procedure,” said McVay. “There is a surgery, but it's a cleanup. I'm not a doctor so I don't want to speak out of turn, but it will be something that'll get cleaned up.”
Rams Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, according to CBS Sports . Faulk has been dealing with the disease for 18 months. Faulk mentioned in an interview that he’s in a good place.
"The little tremors that I get, you know, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, you know, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is,” said Faulk. “I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just, I think I caught it early. I'm in a good place."
Faulk is third on the Rams’ all-time rushing list and is tied with Todd Gurley for the most rushing touchdowns in franchise history. The Rams traded for Faulk prior to the 1999 season and he played a key role in the Greatest Show on Turf. Faulk retired with the Rams in 2005 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2011.
While the Rams didn’t lose because of the unnecessary roughness call, it almost guaranteed that they would lose. The Rams had already jumped offsides on the play and the 21-yard completion put the Cardinals just outside of field goal range. The following night, Fred Warner was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness for a more egregious hit and it was picked up.

The offense was also stagnant and didn’t start moving the ball until under three minutes to play in the game.

title: Rams Trading for Wide Receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Would Be a Mistake They Can't Afford
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may be 2-4, but that doesn’t mean that general manager Les Snead is simply going to sit back and wave the white flag. On Wednesday, it was reported by ESPN’s Dan Graziano that the Rams will at least e xplore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams being placed on injured reserve.
It shouldn’t be a total surprise that the Rams aren’t just going to call it a season. Back in 2019, with the team at 3-3, the Rams made moves for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey. Both players were key pieces in the team’s Super Bowl run in 2021.
When the Rams were 3-3 in 2022, they were close to trading for Christian McCaffrey and Brian Burns. However, they were outbid for McCaffrey, and the Panthers weren’t ready to part ways with Burns at that time.
Very few would be surprised if the Rams made a move. However, if they do make a trade, it needs to be the right one . A popular name that has surfaced is Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas Jr. would be a perfect replacement for Adams as the team’s “X” receiver and was originally drafted in the first round. He also plays for the Jaguars, whose general manager, James Gladstone, has a relationship with Snead. While an exciting name, trading for Thomas would also only dig the Rams into a deeper hole.
Sometimes, the best moves are the ones that aren’t made. That was likely the case when the Rams didn’t acquire McCaffrey and the Panthers said no on Burns. The Rams went 5-12 in 2022 and the 2023 NFL Draft played a large role in the team’s quick turnaround.
There’s nothing to confirm that the Rams have interest in Thomas. In fact, McVay said on Wednesday that the team isn’t even looking at wide receiver replacements.
“That's not something that we've talked about right now,” said McVay. “We have some depth on our roster. Maybe we talked about the practice squad, but not anything externally.”
Whether McVay was honest in what he told the media can certainly be argued. However, there has been speculation about wide receiver options the Rams could be interested in, with Thomas being near the top of the list.
There’s no doubt that Thomas would fit the type of player the Rams typically target in trades. The moves for Sammy Watkins, Austin Corbett, Dante Fowler Jr., Jalen Ramsey, and Kevin Dotson were all players who had fallen out of favor with their previous teams.
Per Brian Thomas Jr.'s profile via @RecepPerception 🟣 72% success rate on "go" routes 👀 🟡Down on 1st contact on 48% of “in space” attempts 🟡72.7% contested catch rate and 2 dropped passes Would not be shocked if Rams took BTJ at 19 as an Atwell replacement. pic.twitter.com/fLcIbbZb4T
Thomas played just 21.1 percent of the Jaguars’ offensive snaps in Week 6 and doesn’t have a reception on five targets in the last two games. After a promising rookie season in which he had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns on 87 receptions, he has just 57 receptions for 812 yards and three touchdowns since.
Ever since the Jaguars moved on from Doug Pederson and hired Liam Coen, he simply hasn’t been the same player. Given that evidence, it’s worth questioning his fit since Coen and McVay come from the same offensive coaching tree. The schemes are very similar.
Over the last two years, Thomas Jr. has ranked last in adjusted catch percentage via FTN Fantasy. Adjusted catch percentage is the rate of catchable targets converted into a catch. Among players with at least 15 targets this season, his 22.2 percent drop-rate is the highest in the NFL. Last season, he also ranked inside the top-5 in drop-rate at 9.1 percent. Thomas’ targeted success rate of 47.3 percent over the last two years ranks 78th out of 116 qualifying receivers. Much like Konata Mumpfield, Thomas struggles at the catchpoint.
Matt Harmon of Yahoo Sports and founder of Reception Perception, which focuses on charting wide receivers, gave Thomas a pass for 2025 in his offseason profile .
“Brian Thomas Jr.’s second season was a frustrating one. It included both dips in his play across the board in isolation and a role that continued to get scaled back as the season went on until his final profile looked merely that of a low-volume X-receiver,” wrote Harmon. “He’s a good press and man-beater who wins both on the vertical routes and helps clear space for his teammates. If he simply maintains this level of deployment and success as a route runner, while cleaning up his drops and contested-catch rate, he’d be a good and useful starting X.”
However, we’re now one-third of the way into 2026, and it’s been much of the same. It’s possible that Thomas’ rookie year was the exception and what we’ve seen the last 1.5 years is the norm. This isn’t to say that the Rams couldn’t get the most out of Thomas or that a change of scenery couldn’t be beneficial. However, it’s also a massive risk, and arguably too much of a risk that the Rams can’t afford.
After just one 1,000-yard season, the Rams traded for Sammy Watkins in 2017. The Rams traded a second-round pick and EJ Gaines for Watkins and a sixth-round pick. Watkins had 593 yards for the Rams and was not brought back the following year.
Earlier this season, the Houston Texans traded a second and seventh-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick. Harrison Jr. has never had more than 900 receiving yards in a season.
Unlike Watkins and Harrison Jr., Thomas wasn’t taken inside the top five of his draft class. Still, he’s a former first-round pick and has more production than Harrison and Watkins had. His price point likely starts with a second-round pick unless the Jaguars are desperate to get rid of him, which doesn’t appear to be the case.
Looking at the 2027 NFL Draft, the Rams already don’t have a first or third-round pick. If they were to move off of the second-round pick, they wouldn’t draft until the fourth round. Given the state of the roster and pending free agents, the Rams may need their second-round pick to add young, cheap talent to replenish the roster.
While the Baltimore Ravens gave up a 2028 second-round pick for Cam Jurgens, the Rams don’t have a 2028 second-round pick to give up. Considering their current roster situation, they also aren’t in a position to trade away a 2028 first-round pick.
The Rams may believe that adding a wide receiver can help turn their season around. At the same time, it needs to be one that fits their price point. The Rams got Kevin Dotson for a late-round pick swap and Austin Corbett for a fifth-round pick. A fourth-round pick may not get a flashy name like Thomas, but it could still get them what they need.
This is a front office that has already invested significant resources into building this roster, and the results have been disappointing. Doubling down by sacrificing another valuable draft pick for a receiver who has struggled for the better part of two seasons would only compound the problem.

title: Myles Garrett's Uncertain Status Raises Bigger Questions About the Rams' Blockbuster Trade
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams traded for edge rusher Myles Garrett this offseason , it was thought that he would be the missing piece and help lead the team to the Super Bowl. Garrett was coming off a 2025 season in which he won NFL Defensive Player of the Year and broke the single-season sack record.
Over the past few seasons, the Rams have been rebuilding the defense. After moving on from Leonard Floyd, Bobby Wagner, and Jalen Ramsey, along with Aaron Donald's retirement, the Rams essentially tore the kitchen down to the studs and rebuilt it.
They added some pieces that simply allowed them to get by, such as Ahkello Witherspoon and Darious Williams at cornerback, but they also found strong foundational pieces in players like Kobie Turner and Byron Young. Braden Fiske had proven some value on the defensive line as well. While the Rams still cut some corners, going cheap at linebacker, they had their star centerpiece in Jared Verse.
This past offseason, the Rams looked to complete the rebuild project on defense. They traded for cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson to finish the kitchen cupboards. Everything seemed complete until they arguably got greedy.
They had a perfectly good working fridge in Verse. It had plenty of space to work with and had an ice maker. While it may not have been perfect, it was still a high-quality fridge.
In June, Les Snead took a walk through the fridge section at Home Depot when a salesperson on the floor, let's call him Andrew Berry, caught his attention. Snead didn’t need a new fridge, but if he traded in his old one, he could get the Myles Garrett model with all the bells and whistles for a great price. It was a high-end model with commercial-grade engineering and precision climate control. You could control everything from your phone. This was the piece that would bring the entire kitchen together.
While everybody was excited for the new fridge, they were also disappointed to see the old one go. Earlier this offseason, Trent McDuffie went on Bussin’ With The Boys and described the vibe in the locker room after the team acquired Garrett.
“Guys weren't even excited excited, knowing you have Myles Garrett coming,” McDuffie said. “I heard the news, I started smiling. I looked around and I was like, ‘Oh, we’re not like, yeah!’ Everyone was like 'Whoa, hold on. J-Verse? You're going to let him go?'”
Back in August, Byron Young was asked about the trade. “That was unfortunate. It's part of business and it's something that definitely did hit me pretty hard,” said Young. “Building that relationship and friendship with him. That was a brother to me. Still a brother.”
Young wasn’t the only player to voice some disappointment. Braden Fiske also said at the time that his initial reaction was disappointment. That hit pretty hard pretty quick,” said Fiske. “My first instinct isn’t, ‘Oh, s---. We got Myles Garrett.’ My first instinct is like, ‘Oh, s---. We lost Jared. That really sucks.’”
Verse was the heart of the defense. He certainly had his deficiencies, but his presence and impact on the defense and locker room as a whole couldn’t be measured. The NFL isn’t a Madden video game or fantasy football where trading big-time players doesn’t reverberate through a team. There are real human relationships and connections to consider.
This isn’t the first time that general manager Les Snead has traded a player. Back in 2021, the Rams traded Jared Goff for Matthew Stafford. With that said, that trade felt different. Most of the team likely understood that they had reached a ceiling with Goff. That doesn’t mean there wasn’t disappointment, but there was at least some understanding that they had hit a ceiling.
That doesn’t appear to have been the same vibe when the Rams moved on from Verse. Trading away Verse accelerated his development timeline to closer match the Rams' championship window . However, where the argument could be made the Goff was holding the offense back in 2020, that couldn't be said about Verse and the defense.
The core of the defense had been through a lot together.In 2024, they experienced the divisional-round loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Last season, they all came up short together in the NFC Championship game. The Rams built that unit through the draft and it was a tight-knit group.
When the Rams first acquired Garrett, everything appeared to be working great. Everyone seemed pleased with the new fridge in the kitchen. Rams reporter Stu Jackson noted that Garrett looked as fast and explosive as advertised.
“When he's out there, you can just feel his aura,” said McDuffie in training camp.“Everybody likes to say this aura that the guy has. He's gigantic. He's a monster.”
As can be the case with many appliances, that’s when the electronics began to malfunction. Back in early August, Garrett missed consecutive practices with what the team described as lower-body soreness that was expanded to swelling in his knee. While the Rams erred on the side of caution, something still wasn’t right. Garrett didn’t practice for much of August and then was estimated as a full participant in the days leading up to Week 1.
The Rams tested their new fridge for a neighborhood get-together in Week 1with the San Francisco 49ers visiting. Garrett didn’t perform well. For the first time since 2018, he was held without recording a single stat.
When Sean McVay was asked after the game whether Garrett was feeling 100 percent , he responded, “To my knowledge, ya.” Minutes later, Garrett walked in and said, “No. This was the worst version of myself.”
The Rams did what they should have done weeks prior and sent their new fridge back to the factory to get fixed, placing Garrett on injured reserve. Garrett would be out at least four weeks.
While Garrett recovered from arthroscopic knee surgery, reports flooded in on his potential return timeline. To be fair, the Rams never put a timeline on Garrett. However, according to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport on September 27, Garrett was given a six-week timeline . Rapoport reported then that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline.
On October 4, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added more information . Jones noted that the six-week timeline would be a worst-case scenario. The team remained hopeful that Garrett could return in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, but people inside the building believed that Garrett could return against the Las Vegas Raiders.
As we know now, Garrett didn’t play against the Cardinals, and McVay already stated on Monday that he would not return to practice this week ahead of the Raiders. ESPN’s Dan Graziano added in a report on Wednesday that Garrett could be out another two or three weeks at least.
We’ve gone from being hopeful about four weeks and realistic about five, with six weeks being a worst-case scenario and Garrett being determined to beat that timeline, to Garrett potentially missing at least seven or eight games.
The Rams sent their malfunctioning fridge back to the factory, were given a timeline, and that timeline continues to get pushed back. Without Garrett, the Rams have been left with a minifridge that they could have gotten by with for four or five weeks, but half the season has put them in a difficult spot.
Over the last four weeks, Josaiah Stewart has just a 7.8 percent pressure rate. That ranks 72nd out of 81 qualifying edge rushers. That’s not a knock on Stewart. Coming into the season, he was expected to be the minifridge used to keep drinks cold. Now, he’s one of two edge rushers on the Rams with over 100 snaps and a full-time player.
After Garrett’s surgery, McVay was asked how it went. “He's like Wolverine, healing fast,” McVay said. However, Garrett is like Wolverine if Wolverine healed very slowly and nobody knew when he’d be good to go again.

title: Kevin Dotson’s Disappointing Start Raises Questions About His Future With Rams
full_text:
Looking ahead to the 2027 offseason, the Los Angeles Rams are going to have some difficult decisions to make . While they will have around $78.2 million in cap space, they also have several free agents they will likely try to bring back. Given their salary cap constraints, it’s highly unlikely that the Rams will be able to bring back everybody.
One of those decisions is whether the Rams should bring back Steve Avila or Kevin Dotson. Both players are set to hit free agency and will be top guard options if they become available. According to Spotrac, Avila’s market value is set at $13.5 million while Dotson is at $19.4 million.
Coming into the season, it was still up in the air who the Rams might bring back one of those two players. With that said, given Avila’s injury history and inconsistency, combined with Dotson’s importance to the run game, the veteran may have had the upper hand.
While Avila has been a promising young player, he’s dealt with injuries and had some lapses in pass protection over the past few years. Meanwhile, when Dotson was out last year, the Rams’ run game went from averaging 4.8 yards per carry down to 4.0.
However, through the first six weeks of the season, the outlook may have changed significantly. Dotson has taken a significant step back, and with the Rams at 2-4, that may change how they approach the offseason.
Pro Football Focus certainly isn’t the be-all and end-all, but even on tape, Dotson has struggled. Among the Rams’ starting five offensive linemen, Dotson’s overall grade of 55.5 is the lowest. Additionally, Dotson’s pass-blocking grade of 44.5 is almost 20 points worse than the Rams’ next closest offensive lineman. That ranks 48th out of 55 qualifying guards this season as well.
Being able to protect from the interior is very important at this point in Matthew Stafford’s career. At 38 years old, Stafford isn’t able to escape the pocket as easily as he used to. Dotson has allowed a 4.9 percent pressure rate, which is 1.2 percentage points higher than Avila’s this season.
He’s also taken a step back in the run gameIn 2025, Dotson was PFF’s third-highest-graded run-blocking offensive lineman. Dotson was fourth in 2024. This season, Dotson’s 62.8 run-blocking grade ranks 30th among guards.
Overall, Dotson ranks 41st out of 55 guards this season via PFF. It’s very possible that Dotson isn’t 100 percent. Back in Week 3, he missed three snaps with an injury. He hasn’t missed a game, but that’s not to say that he’s been fully healthy.
LDT slaps Dotsons hand down after getting Dotson off balance with a strong fake to the B gap, but takes the A gap ... pic.twitter.com/eH7xXfAqvy
The play above is just one example, but Dotson has been on the losing end in pass protection a lot more than he has in the past. Pass protection hasn’t ever been his strength with the Rams, but it’s never been a liability.
There’s also the aspect that Dotson isn’t playing next to a veteran right tackle like he has in the past. Over the past few seasons, Dotson and Rob Havenstein were dominant on the right side. While Dotson played alongside Warren McClendon last year, McClendon has also taken a step back. As Avila has continued playing alongside Alaric Jackson, Dotson is playing next to McClendon, who is in his first full season as a starter.
With the Rams at 2-4 and it potentially being a lost season, it’s fair to wonder if that also changes how they approach the offseason. This past offseason, the Rams started to look at what life would be like after Stafford retires. They took Ty Simpson to be Stafford’s replacement, displaying that the Rams were at least beginning to prepare for the future.
If the Rams were in a spot where they were still committed to the aging core and that group came up just short again, bringing back a 30-year-old Dotson would make sense. Avila may be cheaper and he’s still just 27. The Rams may be able to get another three or four years from Avila in his prime. Avila also remains a steady top-20 guard.
There is still plenty of time for Dotson to turn it around and prove that the first six weeks aren’t a sign of what’s to come. He’s arguably been the most important player on the Rams’ offensive line over the last two years. However, the Rams can’t make a decision based solely on past performance.
With Avila younger, playing better, and potentially cheaper, the Rams may need to reconsider which guard they build around. What looked like a decision that favored Dotson entering the season may now be trending in the opposite direction.

title: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: More Bad News as Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman Face Uncertainty
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks.
However, the Rams will be monitoring other key starters as well this week. On Wednesday, cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice with a groin injury and remains day-to-day. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has been placed in the concussion protocol.
“Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.”
McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report last week. While McVay said that he felt good about him going into Sunday, McDuffie was inactive for the game. McDuffie will certainly be one to monitor this week.
While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff.
Once he passes that, he’ll be able to perform sport-specific activities.Step four involves returning to non-contact drills. Finally, in the last phase, Landman would have to be a full participant in practice and contact without showing any signs or symptoms of a concussion.
Cornerback Josh Wallace and tight end Colby Parkinson were also on the injury report, but both were full participants.
Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad.
While the Rams only have four players on the injury report to start the week, that’s the same number of players they’ve put on injured reserve over the last few days. It’s almost as if you wake up and expect more injury news from the Rams.
“Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.”
For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday.
The Rams will already be shorthanded against the Raiders, and losing McDuffie or Landman would only make matters worse. With several key starters already sidelined, the Rams can’t afford to lose more players as they look to get back in the win column.

title: 5 Biggest Problems With the Rams and Why There's No Easy Fix
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 and not where anybody expected them to be . They are coming off of a disappointing loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and seem to lack an identity. As much as the Rams could be 4-2, they are what their record says they are. This is a team with glaring issues. Here are the top five things wrong with the Rams to start the season.
Matthew Stafford is part of the problem on offense for the Rams, and specifically his inability to hit the deep ball. It’s as if Stafford doesn’t have confidence attacking that area of the field, and because of that, the offense has felt constricted. On deep passes of 20 yards or more, Stafford has just a 26.7 percent success rate. That ranks 27th in the NFL.
Teams are daring the Rams to win deep, and they can’t do it. Stafford’s 1.2 completed air yards per pass attempt against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 was the lowest of his career. The Rams are facing the second-most heavy boxes, but only throwing it deep at the 19th-highest rate. The offense feels a lot like it did in 2019 when Brandin Cooks got hurt and the Rams couldn’t stretch the field.
Some of that has to do with the receivers, but part of it is Stafford.He has one touchdown to five interceptions on passes of 15 yards or more with a 52.4 quarterback rating. Last season, he had 15 touchdowns with one interception and a 127.7 quarterback rating.
Many of the problems on offense stem from a lack of execution. While some may want to focus on the play-calling , it’s not all on Sean McVay. However, that’s not to say that McVay has been perfect. The Rams have only trailed by double digits in two games.
However, the Rams rank fifth in pass-rate over expected and are first over the last four games. The Rams are currently throwing the ball at a 63.9 percent rate, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. Again, it’s not because the Rams are trailing in games. Their 46.6 percent rushing success rate also ranks fourth in the NFL. If the Rams can get back to committing to running the ball, it should help settle down their quarterback.
Not much needs to be said here when it comes to the Rams’ special teams. Poor coverage and short punts allowed the Broncos to come back from a 16-0 deficit. If the field goal unit does its job against the Bills, the Rams win that game as well. After moving on from Mevis, Blake Grupe ended up on injured reserve because he was forced to make a tackle after the coverage unit let Devin Duvernay through. Now, the Rams signed Brandon McManus .
This season, the Rams have accumulated -29.4 EPA on special teams alone. They have a -13.8 percent special teams DVOA, which also ranks 32nd. Nobody cares about special teams until it matters and the Rams are paying the price for that right now. It’s costing them games.
Special Teams EPA through Week 6 1. MIN +26.5 2. BUF +23.7 3. SEA +23.5 ... 29.SF -18.0 30.HOU -20.5 31. MIA -21.1 32. LAR -29.4 pic.twitter.com/UP5EUHqgYG
The lack of discipline in timely moments this season has been uncharacteristic for a Sean McVay-coached football team. A big reason why the Rams were unable to capitalize in the red zone against the Broncos was because of penalties on offense. Steve Avila and Davante Adams had penalties on plays that would have resulted in a first down.
Against the Cardinals, Warren McClendon had a false start that made a 4th-and-3 a 4th-and-8. Additionally, while the unnecessary roughness penalty was questionable, the defense was still offside, allowing Jacoby Brissett to be more aggressive than he might have otherwise.
For the amount of talent that the Rams have on the defensive line, even without Myles Garrett, it is odd how unproductive they are rushing the quarterback. The Rams get pressure at a respectable rate. Their 40 percent pressure rate ranks 15th in the NFL and is right there with the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks. However, the Rams aren’t getting to the quarterback. They have a four percent sack rate, which ranks 27th in the NFL. The Rams also have just eight sacks, which ranks 28th.
The Rams generated plenty of pressure last year as well, but they also ranked seventh in sacks and ninth in sack rate. Only four players have recorded a sack this season, and not a single one is a defensive lineman. Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, and Aaron Donald have not recorded a sack in 2026. The absence of Garrett certainly plays a role, but that needs to change.

title: Rams Expected to Explore Wide Receiver Trade, and One Target Makes Too Much Sense
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may be 2-4, but don’t expect them to wave the white flag anytime soon. With wide receiver Davante Adams going on injured reserve, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams will at least explore the possibility of trading for a replacement.
“My understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of the Davante Adams injury,” said Graziano. “Even with a 2-4 record, four games out of first place in their division, Adams out at least six weeks and Garrett likely out another two or three weeks at least, this is a Rams team that had the highest of hopes for 2026 and still believes it can play well enough to salvage this season.”
While the Rams may be sitting at 2-4, it’s not surprising that general manager Les Snead is at least expected to make calls . Back in 2019, the Rams were 3-3 when they traded for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey. They finished the season 9-7 and missed the postseason.
When the Rams were 3-3 in 2022, they made calls on Christian McCaffrey and Brian Burns. Had the Rams not traded away a fourth-round pick for Sony Michel the year prior, they may have landed McCaffrey. At that point, the Carolina Panthers weren’t interested in trading Burns.
A few weeks ago, the Philadelphia Eagles and general manager Howie Roseman traded Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens in order to acquire an extra second-round pick in 2028. The Rams are 2-4, but Les Snead has never taken that approach when the season may appear lost. If anything, that’s when he’s tried to improve the roster the most.
The question becomes, which wide receiver would the Rams be targeting in this situation? Graziano brought up the idea of a player swap and whether they could trade Stetson Bennett . Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was Bennett’s former offensive coordinator at Georgia. Trading Bennett would also allow the Rams to make Ty Simpson the backup. Additionally, wide receiver Jerry Jeudy could be on the trade block.
However, the Browns already have a plethora of quarterbacks with Shedeur Sanders and Taylen Green. Dillon Gabriel is also on injured reserve. Additionally, Jeudy’s contract isn’t very attractive.Jeudy would be cheap this year, but his cap hit goes up to $13.5 million next year. If any team were to cut him, they would take on $25.4 million in dead money because Jeudy has four void years at the end of his deal.
It’s possible the Rams could trade for Brian Thomas Jr., but his asking price may be too high. Thomas has more receiving yards in his career than Marvin Harrison Jr. Harrison just went for a second-round pick, and that’s likely where Thomas’ asking price would start.
Given that the Rams are 2-4, it would seem ill-advised to give up their 2027 second-round pick. If they were to do that, the Rams wouldn’t draft until the fourth round. For a team that needs some quality depth and a cheap replacement, that price may be too high.
There is a wide receiver who does make a lot of sense if the Rams are exploring that position. The Indianapolis Colts just fired general manager Chris Ballard. With a new regime set to come in and wide receiver Josh Downs entering the final year of his rookie contract, he makes a lot of sense as a potential fit.
4 clips of the Colts in 12 personnel in 2025 with Josh Downs and Alec Pierce as the 2 WRs on the field. Can see the "slot" formations (two WRs on the same side of the field) that they created on most of these plays. It's a classic play action shot play formation that also gets… pic.twitter.com/UAAUfumgSl
Downs hasn’t been heavily involved in the Colts’ offense in 2026, but he had over 750 yards in each of his first two seasons. He had 800 yards and five touchdowns in 2024. However, his lack of size at 5-foot-9 and 170 pounds, along with poor quarterback play, has contributed to injuries and inconsistent usage.
With that said, the talent is very clearly there, and he fills a void in the Rams’ offense. Without Adams for the next two months , the Rams are missing a wide receiver who can win against man coverage. Adams led Rams receivers with a 50 percent targeted success rate against man coverage this season. While Puka Nacua has improved against man coverage, Adams has been that guy for the Rams. He had a 70.1 percent success rate against man coverage last season.
In 2025, Downs had a 75.3 percent success rate against man, which was in the 82nd percentile among wide receivers. Additionally, his 82.4 percent success rate against press was in the 96th percentile.
Matt Harmon of Yahoo Sports and founder of Reception Perception, specializing in charting wide receivers and understanding their impact beyond the box score, did a profile on Downs this offseason.
“Downs’ route success rate chart shows a player who can win at all three levels but is naturally best at layup routes close to the line of scrimmage. His success rates on slants, curls and flats are outstanding. His work on digs, posts and outs is solid to good,” wrote Harmon. “Beyond route running, Downs is a strong performer in other areas that it takes to be a great receiver. He once again demonstrated that he has firm hands at all levels of the field. He didn’t drop a pass across his entire sample and caught four of five contested targets.”
Harmon also noted that it’s obvious that Downs is a good football player, and even if he can’t make it work in an expanded role, it’s at least worth a try. His profile is similar to that of Travis Hunter and Jaylin Noel as well as Jayden Reed and Tyler Lockett.
What the Rams lack on offense is speed. As much as some may want to say that Tutu Atwell just needs a chance, he’s ‘just needed a chance’ for six years. At some point, the situation simply is what it is. Downs can win deep, but that’s not his specialty. The Rams need a player who can replace Mumpfield, create after the catch and find the soft spot in zones on key downs. This is where Downs excels.
Downs primarily operates out of the slot, which would give the Rams an upgrade over Mumpfield in that role. Downs is everything that the Rams have wanted Atwell to be, but actually has the production. Despite only having 24 receptions, Downs has 13 impact plays via Sumer Sports.
While Downs isn’t primarily a deep threat, he brings 4.4 speed, which is enough to create explosive plays. The Rams don’t have a wide receiver who can do that outside of Nacua. Just as important, he’s a reliable target. Downs had 0.165 first downs per route run on third and fourth down last year. That ranked fourth in the NFL behind only Nacua, Keenan Allen, and Amon-Ra St. Brown. While blocking may not be his specialty, he’s always been a willing blocker in the run game.
Right now, the Rams need a player with Downs’ ability to create explosive plays. Their offense feels constricted because teams are daring them to win over the top, and they can’t do it. The Rams are facing the second-most heavy boxes, but are 19th in deep throw rate. Matthew Stafford has a 26.9 percent success rate on deep throws, which ranks 27th.
Watch Josh Downs slot left here. 3rd down in the red zone, Chiefs rush 7 and man up behind. Solution: run quick hitters and get open fast. Downs COOKS Sneed off the line, and a better ball from Jones makes this a TD. #49ers pic.twitter.com/31xTOk9vJn
Another benefit of Downs is his experience returning punts, a role the Colts used him in situationally during his first three seasons. The Rams don’t have a dynamic threat there and are relying on Alex Bachman. That would be a spot that Downs could slide into as well.
Downs isn’t going to be a WR1 in an offense, but he can slide into a WR2 role and that’s what the Rams need. He also isn’t a direct replacement for Adams. However, unlike Thomas Jr., Downs won’t cost a second-round pick. In all likelihood, the Colts may part ways with Downs for the equivalent of a fourth or fifth-round pick. That’s more affordable given the Rams’ draft capital. He gives the Rams a reliable…

title: Rams Have Tough Choices Ahead as Injured Reserve Decisions Become More Complicated
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have caught a bad case of the injury bug as they enter Week 7. On Monday, head coach Sean McVay announced that the Rams would be placing nose tackle Poona Ford and wide receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve with injuries and that defensive lineman Kobie Turner would be missing time with an injury.
As injuries begin to pile up, how the Rams manage their injured reserve list becomes increasingly important. NFL teams are limited to eight players per season that they can designate to return off of injured reserve during the season. That extends to 10 if a team makes the postseason.
The Rams are in an uncomfortable spot now, especially with the season only in Week 7. Myles Garrett has been on injured reserve since Week 1 and the Rams also placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve after Week 3. The Rams also hope to get Davante Adams back at some point , as his injury has an expected recovery timeline of 6-10 weeks.
The Rams will be in an uncomfortable spot moving forward that will take careful management regarding their injured reserve list. NFL teams are limited to 8 players per year that you can designate to return off IR during the season (extends to 10 for playoff teams). *They used… pic.twitter.com/vM10MFwDJ7
Due to Alaric Jackson’s suspension in Week 6 and the need for tackle depth, the Rams used one of their eight return designations on rookie Keagen Trost. Garrett will take another one as well as Ferguson. If the plan is to also use one on Adams later in the year, the Rams have already used or committed half of their return designations.
This appears to be something the Rams are already keeping in mind. It’s a reason why they didn’t immediately designate Justin Dedich and Trost to return from IR and instead waited until one was needed.
While the injuries to Adams, Ford, and Turner were significant for the Rams in Week 6, not all three players landed on injured reserve. Per the NFL’s transaction wire, the team only placed Adams and Ford on injured reserve, excluding Turner.
Leaving Turner off of injured reserve can mean one of two things. It’s possible that the Rams have some optimism that he could return before the four-week window that he’d be required to miss if placed on injured reserve. Another possibility is that the Rams don’t believe Turner’s injury is long-term and want to preserve a return designation for later in the year if they need it.
If the Rams opted to put Turner on injured reserve and bring him back, that would put them at five players designated to return with the planned returns of Garrett, Ferguson, and Adams in addition to one spot already being used on Trost.
As it stands, the Rams currently have 10 players on injured reserve. Unless needed, it’s unlikely the Rams will use a return designation on depth players such as Dedich, Rivers, and Thomas. At that point, the Rams may simply sign a free agent instead of using a return designation spot.
6-10 Weeks (Likely to Return)
Week-to-Week, Likely to Return
Week-to-Week, Likely to Return
Keeping Turner off injured reserve leaves the Rams with four return designations for the remainder of the season.That’s likely why the Rams didn’t place him on injured reserve, as they want to maintain flexibility moving forward. As much as the Rams hope they remain healthy, they have to anticipate other injuries popping up over the next 10 games.
The last thing the Rams want is a situation where a key player is ready to return, but they don't have a designation available. That’s a big reason why they are being so selective now. With several key players already on injured reserve, every decision matters.

title: 5 Rams Overreactions After Disastrous 2-4 Start: Which Ones Are Actually Justified?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams opened the season as Super Bowl favorites, and through six weeks, they sit at 2-4 with a 41 percent chance to make the playoffs. After losing to the Cardinals, t he Rams hit rock bottom and the season continues to spiral.
Naturally, the overreactions have started pouring in. Sean McVay should give up playcalling duties and needs to be on the hot seat. The Rams blew it with a super team. The list goes on. Let's break down five of the biggest overreactions surrounding the Rams and determine which ones are justified.
Following the loss to the Cardinals, one of the primary talking points is how Sean McVay needs to give up playcalling . McVay certainly hasn’t been perfect, and his call on 4th-and-1 against the Cardinals wasn’t good. However, he’s still one of the NFL’s best offensive minds and playcallers. It simply doesn’t make sense to take that away from him and give it to an offensive coordinator in his first season. McVay may be part of the problem right now, but he’s also a big part of the solution. Overreaction Validity: 2/10
For much of the offseason, the Rams were labeled a super team. To be fair, nobody on the team mentioned that phrase. The Rams understood that they looked good on paper, but still had to prove it on the field. With that said, the super team that the media has referred to hasn’t played a single snap together. Myles Garrett wasn’t 100 percent in Week 1 and Aaron Donald didn’t make the trip.
Garrett was immediately placed on injured reserve and the Rams have been managing injuries ever since. We may not see the “Super Team” at full strength this season, but it’s unfair to call the experiment a failure the vision of the roster never came to fruition in the first place. Overreaction Validity: 1/10
It might not be time to start Ty Simpson, but it’s time to at least make him the backup. Much like McVay, Stafford deserves some blame for the Rams’ early-season troubles, but he’s also a big part of the solution. An argument can be made that the game against the Eagles isn't close with Simpson under center, given that Stafford threw two ill-advised interceptions. The Rams may have beaten the Cardinals with Simpson. A time may come when the Rams do decide to start their rookie quarterback, but the only player capable of digging this team out of the current hole it's in is Stafford. Overreaction Validity: 5/10
We’ve been doing the same exhausting dance with the Rams’ defensive coordinators going back to Raheem Morris. This isn’t to say that the defense is faultless. However, they made a play that should have won the game against the Buffalo Bills. They held the Cardinals to 18 points and 0-for-5 in the red zone. A McVay-led offense should be expected to score 20 points against the worst scoring defense in the NFL.
Through six weeks, the Rams’ defense ranks 10th in defensive DVOA and third in yards allowed per game. That’s without Garrett and other key pieces in several games. Shula has implemented the exact style of defense that fans wanted early in the season. Overreaction Validity: 4/10
It’s going to be interesting to see what the Rams do at the trade deadline. With that said, Les Snead isn’t known to sell assets and call it a season. The Rams could certainly trade Byron Young and get decent draft capital in return. However, it’s hard to see them going that route.
It’s more likely that the Rams stand pat or make a move to improve the roster. While the Rams didn’t make the playoffs in 2019, they traded for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey. In 2022, they made calls on Christian McCaffrey and Brian Burns. The Rams may not make a splashy move, but Les Snead will likely be actively working the phones. Overreaction Validity: 6/10
