title: Where to Assign Blame For the Dolphins' Grounded Passing Attack
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins passing game has been abysmal. Through five weeks, they’re tied for last in terms of EPA per pass, and Malik Willis has the lowest completion rate in the NFL among qualified quarterbacks.
There’s more than enough blame to go around for this fluttering offense, with multiple groups and individuals needing to improve.
Miami’s offensive coordinator, Bobby Slowik, is running very similar concepts to those from the previous regime, which makes sense considering Slowik was the senior passing game coordinator under Mike McDaniel.
That isn’t a pass, however, for a scheme that, to this point, hasn’t matched the skill sets of its players or the philosophy on defense.
Jeff Hafley’s defensive system has been ultra-conservative, playing with deep safeties and linebackers to limit explosives and slow down the pace of the game. Rather than matching this with a ball-control style of offense, however, Slowik has thrown haymakers more than about every other offense in football. Through week five, Miami’s offense ranks fourth in pass attempts of 20+ yards, but is fourth-worst in terms of EPA per dropback on those looks, per NextGenStats.
Miami’s pass plays look far too similar to what they ran for Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, especially considering this receiving corps is among the youngest in football and is bereft of top-end talent. Their two-man concepts are non-threatening when being run by rookies Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr., especially when paired with a first down rushing attack that ranks second-to-last in success rate, meaning defenses don’t bite down as hard on play action.
Miami hasn’t put together an honest effort to get Malik Willis easy completions on early downs, instead playing touchdown-to-checkdown for a quarterback who hasn’t been willing to take the latter. Instead, Slowik has pressed early, Miami has fallen behind the sticks, and he has placed Willis in disadvantageous situations for large portions of each game.
A lack of top-end talent is one thing, but as former Dolphins head coach Brian Flores once harkened on, many of this group’s mistakes take no talent to fix.
Inexperience has shown up early and often for the receiver group. On crucial downs, receivers line up in the wrong spot, with the primary culprit being third-round rookie Chris Bell, who notably missed a vast majority of the offseason while recovering from an ACL tear. Malik Willis is forced to redirect traffic late in the play clock, rather than having the time to survey the defense pre-snap.
There have also been gaffes in route-running that have made life difficult on the young quarterback. On Willis’ first pass against Cincinnati, a deep shot to Malik Washington, both Washington and coach Jeff Hafley said the receiver turned the wrong direction, pushing the route to the sideline, rather than vertically up the numbers.
Later in that same game, three of Miami’s eligibles, lined up in a bunch, comically bumped into each other, throwing off the timing of a route concept.
The Miami Dolphins passing game is BROKEN. Sure, Malik Willis bears some of the blame, but there have been countless errors out of his control that have contributed to poor results. pic.twitter.com/xDFvnHPT8U
Their scramble drill procedures have been off as well. The spacing has become congested late in plays, and it’s clear players aren’t sure where to go. On Willis’ second interception of Week 5, Malik Washington stayed in one spot, bringing his defender into the window where Willis attempted to throw the ball to Kevin Coleman Jr.
Miami’s top four receivers (including the injured Caleb Douglas) are all in their third year or younger, and they need to grow up fast if they want to make the plays needed to start winning games.
Miami’s new quarterback bears plenty of blame for Miami’s failed aerial assault. It’s unfair to ask him to put out all of the fires started by his supporting cast, but he will be judged on whether or not he gets burned.
On the aforementioned interception intended for Kevin Coleman Jr., for instance, Willis can’t control whether Washington operates the scramble drill correctly. However, he had more than enough time to see that Coleman was running into defenders and live to play another down.
Despite the sixth-best time-to-pressure in the NFL, Willis ranks 23rd in pressure-to-sack rate, per PFF. As the film has shown, these sacks often happen in back-breaking situations, such as second down inside the 5-yard line in Week 5, where he had plenty of time to throw the ball away, but made an abysmal decision to hold on to it.
Quicker decision-making will be the biggest key for Willis. His process has yet to speed up the requisite level to avoid major mistakes. He needs to be able to consistently get through his progressions, while also deciphering when to abandon the pocket or give up on a play. Thus far, he looks like a quarterback who has only started eleven career games, when this version of the Dolphins needs a higher level of maturation in order to put together complete performances.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: Quick Thought on Each Dolphins Defensive Starter
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins are into their bye weekend after a disappointing 0-5 start made worse by the fact they have yet to hold a lead, which is a good time to examine what has stood out about all the players who have started at least one game.
There have been 16 of those on defense, so here's a thought on each from Zach Sieler to Julius Wood.
DT ZACH SIELER — Sieler remains a very solid starter at a minimum and he would be a long-term fixture on this team under different circumstances. But he could wind up moved out at some point during this rebuilding project.
DT JORDAN PHILLIPS — Because of the role he plays, Phillips never will be a star, but he's a valuable member of the defense when it comes to stopping the run.
DT ZEEK BIGGERS — There's potential with Biggers, particularly as a big lineman who can move around on the defensive line, but there also hasn't been nearly enough impact just yet.
EDGE CHOP ROBINSON — Some of the analytics suggest Robinson is being very effective as a pass rusher, but the film suggests otherwise (other than the Minnesota game). That said, he still does look better than last season; it's just that the Dolphins need more from him.
EDGE JOSHUA UCHE — There haven't been flashy plays, but it says here that it's Uche who's been the best edge defender for the Dolphins, to the point where maybe the team needs to consider bringing back him next season.
EDGE ROBERT BEAL JR. — There was very little noticeable about Beal in the first two games before he landed on injured reserve, so the hope is he flashes when he comes back from his hamstring injury.
LB JORDYN BROOKS — Brooks hasn't been the dominating force he was in 2025 (especially in the second half of the season), but there obviously are tough circumstances at play, including a training camp injury. That said, while he's been overshadowed by Jacob Rodriguez, he's actually graded out better so far if you go by the Pro Football Focus numbers.
LB JACOB RODRIGUEZ — It's been quite the start for Rodriguez, who has demonstrated the great instincts he showed at Texas Tech, and though we feel at times his performance has been oversold, he's certainly got the look of a long-term fixture at linebacker at worst and a future All-Pro at best.
LB WILLIE GAY JR. — Gay still looks like the most athletic linebacker on the team, but he also looks like he'll get caught out of position from time to time.
CB CHRIS JOHNSON — Johnson has rebounded nicely from a rough start that includes a forgettable Week 1 outing against the Raiders and he's impressed from the start with his tackling ability.
CB JASON MARSHALL JR. — Because the Dolphins have played a lot of soft zones, the defense hasn't gotten beat over the top but there also have been very few pass breakups. All that said, Marshall has been solid and looks like a keeper.
CB JUJU BRENTS — It's the same old story with Brents, who still totally looks the part of an elite cornerback and plays that way at times. But then there's always the feeling it's a matter of time before he gets injured. The Cincinnati game was a great example because he was outstanding before leaving the game not once but twice.
S MICHAEL TAAFFE — Props to Taaffe for earning a starting job as a rookie fifth-round pick and that was thanks in large part to his off-the-chart intangibles. The question with Taaffe continues to concern his NFL ceiling because of his lack of ideal size and athleticis.
S DANTE TRADER JR. — Still not quite sure why Trader wasn't in the starting lineup from the start of the regular season, but he's back in there now and his physical presence is quite welcome in the back end.
S ZAYNE ANDERSON — A special teams specialist in Green Bay, Anderson got his shot as the opening-day starter, but it went south pretty quickly for him and now he's back to mostly being a special-teamer.
S JULIUS WOOD — Wood got one start when he was the nickel against the Kansas City Chiefs to open the game with Johnson and Marshall outside, but he's played 17 snaps on defense the whole year. His role is on special teams.

title: How the Waddle Trade Keeps Looking Better and Better for the Dolphins
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins sacrificed the present for a better future when they moved Jaylen Waddle in the offseason, but their big trade with the Denver Broncos continues to look good in the moment.
While Waddle had yet another uneventful outing in the Broncos' ugly Thursday night overtime victory against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night, the main piece the Dolphins in the trade got some national love Friday morning.
In short, a trade we liked very much from the start has become one we downright love at this point.
To refresh everyone's memory, the Dolphins traded Waddle and a 2026 fourth-round pick (111th overall) to Denver for the 30th overall pick, and picks in the third (94th overall) and fourth rounds (130th overall).
The Dolphins then moved the 30th overall along with the 90th overall selection to the San Francisco 49ers for the 27th overall selection and the 138th overall pick in the fourth round.
With the 27th pick, the Dolphins selected cornerback Chris Johnson, then took wide receiver Chris Bell with the 94th pick, linebacker Trey Moore with the 130th pick and safety Kyle Louis with the 138th pick.
So looking at the complete deal, it comes down to the Dolphins trading Waddle, the 90th pick and the 111th pick for Chris Johnson, Chris Bell, Trey Moore and Kyle Louis.
Oh, and the Dolphins cleared Waddle from their books moving forward, though they did take a $23 million dead cap hit for him in 2026.
It probably will take a couple of years before a final verdict can be rendered on this trade, but the early indications are that it was a big win for Miami.
Regardless of what happened, it helped accomplished the goal of clearing the books beyond this one year of pain, but Waddle's production in Denver through the first six games has eliminated any buyer's remorse.
In Denver's 17-14 victory against Seattle, Waddle had four catches for only 24 yards, the fifth time in six games he failed to top 35 receiving yards.
Since his one big game, a 138-yard performance in Week 2 against Jacksonville, Waddle has recorded 13 catches for 88 yards in the past four games combined.
That four-game stretch is the worst of his career in terms of yardage, not even remotely close to his previous four-game low of 135 yards during the 2024 season.
Waddle was expected to provide the big-play element to a Denver team that reached the AFC Championship Game last year, but instead their offense has faced little but criticism this season even though the team still has a 4-2 record.
Meanwhile in Miami, we also could make the argument that Johnson has performed better, particularly considering he's a rookie.
While the start of his NFL career was bumpy, he has been impressive of late, enough that Sports Illustrated draft analyst Justin Melo mentioned him among his five rookies on the move.
Bell is off to a slow start in his first NFL season, but that's somewhat to be expected considering he's coming back from a serious knee injury and the Dolphins offense as a whole has been dysfunctional.
Moore and Louis are on injured reserve and it's safe to wonder how much they will contribute, if at all, in 2026.
But Moore looked like he was ready in camp to become a major contributor, and Louis will be given a chance at a new position when he returns.
Either way, this trade is looking very good indeed at this time.

title: Demond Claiborne's Vikings Future Could Be Crystal Clear After Week 7
full_text:
There's no sugarcoating it: Vikings rookie running back Demond Claiborne has been a huge letdown early in the 2026 NFL season . The preseason hype built around his excellent training camp, where he showed great speed and athleticism, has not translated into regular-season success.
Claiborne played in four of the Vikings' first five games, but the rookie running back has only six rushing attempts for 13 yards and two catches for eight receiving yards. He has played 18 offensive snaps for the Purple and Gold this season despite Jordan Mason being on injured reserve and Aaron Jones Sr. playing through a knee injury , further hammering home that the Vikings don't trust the first-year runner.
If head coach Kevin O'Connell trusted Minnesota's sixth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft more, he would receive more opportunities. Instead, the 23-year-old rookie is finding himself on the sidelines instead of on the field, and it might not be much longer before his future with the Vikings becomes crystal clear.
After sitting out Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers, Claiborne has struggled to get playing time. He hasn't played double-digit snaps in a game yet, but came close in Week 4 against the Miami Dolphins when he played nine snaps.
Demond Claiborne offensive snaps
That said, Mason—who had 15 carries in Week 1—is expected to return from injured reserve now that his thumb has healed, which means Claiborne could be used even less moving forward. Even then, the rookie will still be splitting RB3 work with DeeJay Dallas, making those opportunities even more scarce.
Dallas's seven years of experience have led to him having a bigger offensive role than Claiborne this season. He also knows general manager Nolan Teasley from their days in Seattle. The veteran running back has played 40 offensive snaps this year, carrying the ball three times for 10 yards and catching four passes for 34 yards.
At this point, it seems unnecessary to keep Claiborne on the 53-man roster for any reason other than the fear of another team claiming him off waivers or signing him off the practice squad. It might be too early for Minnesota to give up on him or risk losing him, so it is understandable not to gamble with his future.
The most logical move for the Vikings moving forward might be to keep Claiborne inactive on game day until there is a role for him on offense. Keeping him dressed and active when he isn't contributing as a running back and has played only four special teams snaps doesn't make sense.
Keep a close eye on Claiborne's role in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts . If he doesn't get involved on the field or blows any limited chances he gets, expect the Vikings to change how they'll handle the rookie's development moving forward.

title: Vikings' Biggest Need Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The undefeated Vikings need to decide how aggressive they will be before the 2026 NFL trade deadline , which takes place on Tuesday, Nov. 10. If the Purple and Gold feel they are truly contenders, general manager Nolan Teasley should do what he can to strengthen the roster and prepare for a potential playoff run.
The Vikings have been fortunate to lean on defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit and the strong leg of kicker Will Reichard through the first five games of the season, but teams will soon start exploiting any weaknesses Minnesota's roster could have.
Much of the trade talk around the Purple and Gold involves offensive players ,  as Vikings fans want to see the team trade for a weapon to help put points on the board. That said, the team's biggest weakness is actually a defensive position that desperately needs more depth.
The strong play of other defenders, particularly close to the line of scrimmage, has hidden the Vikings' struggles at safety fairly well. At one time, the combination of Harrison Smith and Josh Metellus was enough to carry the position, but that duo has struggled to be effective this year .
Smith is 37 years old and in his ninth season as a pro. For the first time in his career, he is playing less than half of Minnesota's defensive snaps. Even in his limited role, he has been the worst safety in the league , earning a 31.5 Pro Football Focus grade—dead last among 98 qualified players.
Metellus isn't much better than Smith when it comes to PFF . The 28-year-old defensive back's 40.2 grade ranks him 93rd while allowing a 145.8 passer rating to opposing quarterbacks.
Even Theo Jackson (63.7 PFF grade) and Jay Ward (59.9 PFF grade) have been just okay. However, Ward has only played two defensive snaps, while Jackson has been attempting to pick up the slack with 191 defensive snaps.
The Vikings have rookies Jacob Thomas and Jakobe Thomas on the roster to insert into the lineup when they are ready, but Minnesota needs to do something to get better play at the safety position this year.
Don't be surprised if the Purple and Gold explore trade options before the Nov. 10 deadline. To keep the defense strong for the rest of the season, adding an experienced safety to Flores's aggressive unit would prove that the Vikings are serious about being contenders this season.

title: Surprise Aaron Jones Injury Update Gives Vikings Even More Reason to Bolster RB Depth
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline was always going to be an interesting time for the Vikings, but things are already changing with some recent running back news.
On Thursday, ESPN 's Kevin Seifert reported that Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. has actually been playing with a sprained MCL . Despite suffering the injury in Week 2 against the Bears, Jones has carried the ball 90% of the time since Jordan Mason went down after the season opener.
I spoke with Aaron Jones about the career-high burden he has carried in 2026, at age 31 and with a sprained MCL. It was a lot. "They can measure your weight. They can't measure your heart." On the Vikings' "warrior" as they return to a backfield rotation: https://t.co/DCn9ZIW1xB
While Jones's toughness was never questioned, the string of various running back signings and cuts over the last few weeks was clearly some attempt at insurance for their RB1.
With Mason now expected to return , Jones should get some much needed rest as the duo once again splits the workload, but his injury does add some fuel to the fire of a potential trade for another rusher.
Clearly, Jones was able to carry the entire burden of the Vikings' rushing attack over the last few weeks, racking up 410 yards on the season, but could Minnesota look to make a splash in their backfield at the deadline ?
Jones is nearing 32 years old and is essentially playing hurt the rest of the way, while Mason is fresh off an injury himself that cost him four weeks. Looking beyond 2026, neither back is under contract for next year, so the Vikings could look to add both a short- and long-term solution with one swing of the bat.
Rookie Demond Claiborne clearly isn't ready for that role , and may never be, so Minnesota may do something drastic to take advantage of their hot start and dirt-cheap quarterback.
Big names like Saquon Barkley or Jonathan Taylor have been thrown around as possible fits, but those aren't perfect options either. Barkley has been banged up himself this year and will turn 30 in February. It's just hard to be a top producer at running back at that age, and even Dalvin Cook was just 27 when the Vikings decided to move on.
Meanwhile, Taylor is two years younger, but also already has over 1,600 carries on his legs, 400 more than Cook did at this age. Obviously both Taylor and Barkley at this point would be upgrades over the current Minnesota stable, but the cost will determine if the Vikings bite.
If Mason returns with some juice and Jones can manage his injury, the Vikings may opt for a deal for a committee-type back or stand pat altogether. Conversely, there's no question that if either Jones or Mason goes down again, this team may struggle in the playoffs.
So do the Vikings get ahead of those issues now with a trade, or let things unfold how they may?
How the backfield performs against the Colts will be the first step in determining a plan. If the run game is effective over the next week or two, it'll be hard to see general manager Nolan Teasley pulling the trigger on a big-name RB using valuable picks. That doesn't rule out some more palatable options like Kenny Gainwell or James Conner.
At the same time, the Vikings can't roll into the playoffs hoping Claiborne or DeeJay Dallas can move the needle if either starter has to miss time. It'll be interesting to see Teasley & Co.'s next RB-related move, to say the least.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Kyle Murray & Co. Host the Colts in Week 7
full_text:
The Vikings will host a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday for just the third time this season as they welcome the 2-4 Colts to the Twin Cities in Week 7 . Minnesota looks to remain undefeated coming off an early Week 6 bye, while Indy will be scratching to salvage a start that has already led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard .
Needless to say, these are two teams currently heading in completely different directions.
With a beast of a November schedule looming, here are my predictions for a Vikings team looking to put together a dominating performance.
While the early bye provided desperately needed injury relief for the Vikings, there are fair concerns that the break may have disrupted the progress Kyler Murray and the passing game were starting to make.
Murray’s performance in New Orleans was especially promising, mainly due to the fact that the offense entered the game without wideout Jordan Addison and left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and then lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion early. With all three looking to return this weekend, I see Murray having his best day yet in purple.
Indy’s 351.2 yards allowed per game rank ninth in the league, and Murray’s abilities through the air and on the ground make him especially hard to stop (h/t: Ian Hartitz).
Next-Gen Stats fastest ball carrier speed in Week 5: Kyler Murray (20.82 MPH) Also the fastest ball carrier speed by a QB this season. pic.twitter.com/GSZ61DBqzc
After totaling 280 total yards against the Saints (229 passing, 51 rushing), I predict Murray will finish with over 300 total yards on Sunday.
The Vikings’ season started with a bang, scoring 39 points in the season opener against the Packers. Since then, they have not scored more than 23 points in a game.
Sunday is the perfect opportunity for that to change.
The Colts have given up 27.3 points per game so far this season, the sixth-highest average in the league. Minnesota, meanwhile, is looking for its first truly dominant offensive showing as it prepares for the hardest stretch of its schedule.
The returns of Hockenson and Addison should open up passing options, and Jordan Mason’s possible return to the backfield could elevate a run game that Aaron Jones has carried almost entirely on his own so far. The Vikings’ offense needs to prove it can score consistently before facing some of the league's toughest opponents, and the Colts’ shaky defense may give them plenty of opportunities.
Franchise legend Harrison Smith has had a relatively quiet start to his 15th NFL season .
Smith announced his return a week before the Vikings kicked off their 2026 campaign and has mostly been a rotational piece in defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s ever-evolving defense. Even though “The Hitman” is clearly past his prime, he’s still one of the smartest defenders in the game, and I expect that to pay off this weekend.
Smith recently confirmed to Richard Sherman that this will be his last season , so there is no better time to snag his 40th interception than now (h/t: "Richard Sherman Podcast").
. @RSherman_25 is joined by #HarrisonSmith and he talks his FUTURE with the @NFL , Minnesota @Vikings and MORE 👀 New ‘NFL Week 7 Predictions’ episode with @MitchEisenstein and Harrison Smith is Now Available on @YouTube HERE: https://t.co/HtJLz9SYDS pic.twitter.com/z14KXIo0Wd
Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown six interceptions this season, tied for the third-most in the league , and anyone who's watched him through his career knows he’ll eventually throw a duck or two (h/t: NFL).
Smith’s football IQ and Jones’s occasional recklessness may just be the perfect combination to get the NFL’s active interception leader his next pick.

title: Perfect Vikings WR Trade Target Couldn't Be Clearer as Jauan Jennings Remains an Issue
full_text:
There is no polite way to say that Jauan Jennings has been a free-agent bust for the Vikings. He has played in four of the team's first five games, catching two passes for nine yards on five targets.
Jennings's lack of production has put even more pressure on Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison to pick up the slack. It's disappointing when both Myles Price (26) and Tai Felton (41) have more receiving yards than the sixth-year pro.
That said, it wouldn't be shocking to see the Vikings make a move for a wide receiver before the trade deadline to spark the offense and give starting quarterback Kyler Murray another potential target to throw the ball to.
Fortunately, one potential target for general manager Nolan Teasley is beginning to emerge.
The Vikings should call the Browns before the trade deadline to ask about the availability of wide receiver Jerry Jeudy. He could do a lot more with the 201 offensive snaps that Jennings has played for Minnesota this year.
Jeudy has played only 19 more snaps than Jennings this year, but has 12 receptions for 150 yards this season. Of those 150 yards, 42 were gained after the catch despite running routes that average more than 10 yards deep.
The Browns would need to take on a large amount of his three-year, $52.5 million contract, which carries approximately a $10.4 million cap hit this season and $13.5 million next season. However, his contract has no guaranteed money left in 2027 , according to OverTheCap , making him a potential rental player should the Vikings want to move on after the 2026 season ends.
Jennings has made it clear that he isn't a good fit for the Vikings' offense. He isn't contributing as a receiver, and he has the lowest run-blocking grade on the team, according to Pro Football Focus . Jeudy would instantly upgrade the Minnesota roster.
Of course, a trade might not happen if the Browns continue winning. They are currently 4-2 and in a three-way tie for the top of the AFC North. If the Browns believe they can make the playoffs, they may not want to deal the seventh-year pro.
Jeudy has had a knack for making big catches lately. His Week 4 heroics saw him catch two big late-game passes to put away the Steelers, and in Week 6 he hauled in a 33-yard pass on third down to finish off the Ravens.
According to Sports News ' Aman Sharma, Jeudy had an opportunity to shoot down any potential trade talks but instead called it a "day-to-day" situation. That response is interesting because it amplified any trade rumors that were already swirling.
The Vikings need to at least inquire about what it would take to acquire Jeudy ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. If the cost isn't too high, adding him to Minnesota's roster as a clutch receiver to take pressure off Jefferson and Addison makes a lot of sense, especially if it means finally addressing the Jennings problem.

title: Vikings Week 7 Mailbag: NFC North Picture, Historical Concerns, Early Grades & More
full_text:
Vikings football is back after a bye week that felt like it lasted a lifetime. As the Vikings prepare to host the Colts this weekend, the fanbase will learn just how good the undefeated Vikings truly are as they prepare to face the most challenging stretch of their schedule.
I took to X to grab your questions, so let’s break down what’s on your minds.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
This one is fun. Even five weeks into the season, you could ask multiple people and get completely different answers. At this time, I’d go:
The Vikings’ undefeated record and two divisional wins automatically put them at the top, but their upcoming November schedule will prove whether they truly deserve it. I have the Bears in the two-spot now that quarterback Caleb Williams is back. Their defense has serious questions, but when Williams and head coach Ben Johnson are at their best, they’re hard to beat.
The Packers appear to be finding a flow, and the return of running back Josh Jacobs and star pass rusher Micah Parsons makes them a scary sight on the Vikings’ upcoming calendar. Detroit comes in at four, even though its offense is fourth in yards per game at 393.8. Their defense, by contrast, gives up the most total yards per game in the league, averaging a whopping 404.4 ypg.
This division is incredibly talented —with every team above .500—but these rankings could flip over the course of just a few games. For now, Vikings fans should enjoy the view (h/t: Pro Football Focus ).
The North is STRONG pic.twitter.com/TTnun1UomG
I’m glad to see someone finally brought this up. We certainly love our PTSD here in Vikings nation, don’t we?
To be honest, a similar outcome is technically possible, but I'm confident this team will make the playoffs at the very least, even if there are still questions about how sustainable their success has been. The biggest reason? The chaos across the rest of the NFC.
If the season ended today, the entire NFC North would be in the playoffs, and I think that’s still a possibility by season’s end. The NFC West looks like a one-horse race unless Seattle finds a way to get its running game working; the NFC South may once again send a team with a losing record to the playoffs; and the NFC East is a total mess right now. The Vikings' early wins against the Packers and Bears add a valuable divisional cushion.
If November proves to be a total disaster for the Vikes, it may be time to panic, but I think defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit will allow them to leave with at least two wins over four challenging matchups.
Defense and special teams each get an A+ from me. There’s simply no denying that Minnesota’s 5-0 start is largely due to those two units , especially as the offense struggled mightily early on.
I’ll give the offense a B- for the progress the passing game showed in Week 5 against the Saints after flashing improvements late in Week 4 against the Dolphins. Context also matters given the injury troubles the offense has faced. Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison have shared the field for just 18 snaps so far this season .
Jordan Addison is “good to go” according to Kevin O’Connell. Reminder that Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson, and Addison have played only 18 snaps together this season. pic.twitter.com/2gcwzsZ4L9
The coaching staff gets an A-, with Flores and special teams coordinator Matt Daniels doing the heavy lifting there. To head coach Kevin O’Connell’s credit, he's adjusted his scheme to account for Murray’s unique skill set. The next step is for the offense to find consistent success.
I’m not sure if there’s an exact statistical output to look for since I don’t think we’ll see the same high-flying offense we saw with Sam Darnold at the helm in 2024. But the Vikings’ next five games are a perfect chance for the offense to prove its doubters wrong, especially with Addison, Jordan Mason, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw returning from injury soon .
Even though Minnesota’s defense has been stellar, teams like Detroit, Buffalo, Green Bay and San Francisco will test Flores’s squad. The offense will eventually have to take control and be the reason they win games. If Murray and company can consistently dominate time of possession and walk away with points, fears around the offense should finally be put to rest.

title: The Best, Worst and Most Likely Outcomes for Vikings vs. Colts
full_text:
The Vikings are getting healthy after their bye week , and the first test after a week away will be against the spiraling Indianapolis Colts. Still, despite the Vikings being favorites, anything can happen in this league, like, say a 33-0 comeback.
Ideally, the Vikings move to 6-0 with a demonstrative win, but it may not be so simple. Here are the best, worst and likliest scenarios for Minnesota's matchup with the Colts in Week 7.
The bye week came at a fortunate time for getting players healthy, but it also might have taken a bit of wind out of the sails of the 5-0 Vikings.
Murray played his best game of the season against the Saints, but will now need to regain a bit of steam against Indianapolis after getting the week off. Fortunately, the 2-4 Colts are fresh off a loss to what were the winless Titans, and will likely be without their top defender in Sauce Gardner. With a healthy receiving corps and the return of Jordan Mason, the excuses will be few and far between for Murray on Sunday.
And while there's little question that the defense will once again show up for Minnesota, they do need keep the injury bug away . Eight defensive starters have played at least 80% of the snaps this season, and their health has been key to driving one of the best defenses in football. Coming out of Week 7 without injury will be the ultimate goal in what should otherwise be a quick dispatch of Daniel Jones and company.
Five games into the season, opposing offenses still haven't figured out how to break Flores' scheme, but at some point there's bound to be some progress. Obviously teams know the pressure is coming, but the difficult part of playing the Vikings is their disguises and pre-snap confusion. Still, no system is without their tells, and eventually you'd think some team latches on to something...anything.
A loss to Indy isn't the end of the world, but if Shane Steichen exposes a crack in the armor, the Vikings defense may be forced to get even more creative the rest of the way (if such a thing is possible).
On offense, things are trending up, but Minnesota is still looking for much better production out of Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings. If neither impress against the Colts, the trade talks for either may see a big spike.
Jennings' name has already been a hot topic after notching just two catches on the season, but Addison may fetch more value, and is already on track for a third-straight year of worse production than his standout rookie year.
The combined record from the Vikings previous three opponents is just 3-14, which isn't exactly a ringing endorsement of their undefeated season. The Colts are 2-4, and just lost to the previously 0-5 Titans, prompting the firing of longtime general manager Chris Ballard. A win is expected here to move to 6-0, but it won't do much to dispel the notions that Minnesota is punching above their weight this season.
National opinions aside, though, the Vikings offense hopefully once again shows some progress, while the defense continues their historic level of dominance. At this point, the playoffs are almost a certainty with a 91% chance according to ESPN, so marginal improvement week-to-week is the most important thing.

title: Another Potential Demond Claiborne Replacement Just Became Available for Vikings
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 heading into Week 7 and sitting at the top of the NFC North. While that is great for now, there are areas of the roster that could be improved to prepare for the remainder of the games on the schedule.
One position where the Vikings could use a boost is running back. While Jordan Mason was out, Aaron Jones Sr. was responsible for getting production on the ground since Demond Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas have struggled to be effective.
Mason is on track to return against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, but Minnesota could still use depth beyond their one-two punch of Jones and Mason. A recently released running back could help to improve that situation.
On Tuesday, the Philadelphia Eagles announced that they waived running back Jaydon Blue. Blue was picked up by the Eagles at the start of September, but didn't see any game action.
The 22-year-old rusher joined the Dallas Cowboys as a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft and played five games as a rookie.
Blue ended his rookie campaign with 38 rushing attempts for 129 yards and a touchdown. He picked up seven first downs for Dallas and averaged 3.4 yards per carry. The Cowboys waived him as part of their final roster cuts, which led him to the Eagles' practice squad.
The Vikings are currently ranked 22nd in rushing yards per attempt at 3.8. However, Claiborne has struggled mightily as a rookie, averaging only 2.2 yards per rushing attempt on six carries this season, making him an unreliable third option for Minnesota.
Claiborne is only 23 years old, so there's plenty of time for him to find his footing in the NFL. But until he can, the Vikings might want to look into a player like the 5-foot-9, 198-pound Blue to hold down the RB3 job until he is ready.
During the 2025 NFL Scouting Combine, Blue ran an impressive 4.38 seconds in the 40-yard dash, which is a great measure of his speed. The only question marks surrounding him at this point in his career are his maturity and fashion sense.
Last year, Blue wore a pair of Louis Vuitton-Nike cleats at practice, and it did not go over well. The footwear gave him blisters. His footwear choice gave him a reputation for choosing style over function, which did not go over well with the team or fans.
Nonetheless, if a tryout and physical go well for the young running back, the Vikings might be smart to add him to the practice squad and potentially elevate him to the 53-man roster if they need a speedy running back with some experience to take pressure off Jones or Mason.

title: Harrison Smith Is Slowly Becoming a Concern for Vikings (Even If It Hurts to Say)
full_text:
If you go to a Minnesota Vikings game at U.S. Bank Stadium, you will probably see quite a few fans wearing a #22 Harrison Smith jersey. Now in his 15th season with the Purple and Gold, the veteran safety is universally loved and respected for his contributions to the team.
It was exciting when it was announced that Smith would return for the 2026 NFL season . A future Vikings Ring of Honor player, giving fans one more season of his hard-hitting, smothering play.
However, that is not what fans are getting this season. Instead, the six-time Pro Bowl, one-time All-Pro First-Team, and one-time All-Pro Second-Team defender has seldom been on the field. And when he is on the field, he looks like a shell of his former self.
This season, Smith is playing less than half of the Vikings' defensive snaps. Of a possible 295 plays, he has been in on 140. He hasn't started a single one of Minnesota's first five games.
Smith's limited role in defensive coordinator Brian Flores' scheme isn't a problem, but there is an issue with his effectiveness on the field. His Pro Football Focus grade of 31.5 says it all. Smith is ranked dead last among 98 qualifying safeties.
The 37-year-old defensive back has been particularly bad in pass coverage. His PFF grade of 33.5 is the second-worst of all qualifying safeties this year. He has recorded seven combined tackles, three pass defenses, and a quarterback hit in the team's first five games.
What makes the situation even more complicated is that the player benefiting from extra playing time by picking up Smith's reps this year is Josh Metellus. In fact, Metellus has played all 295 defensive snaps for Minnesota so far this season.
The problem is that Metellus is struggling almost as badly as Smith. His 40.2 PFF grade ranks him 93rd among 98 safeties, and his 33.4 pass coverage grade, while allowing a 145.8 passer rating, is unacceptable.
The Vikings have done a good job hiding Smith and Metellus' struggles this year, but there will be a time when the team won't be able to pick up the slack, and an opposing offense will exploit their safety weakness.
It hurts to say it, but the Vikings need to figure out a way to get better play from Smith if they want to be contenders this year.

title: Why the NFL Trade Deadline Will Be Nolan Teasley's Biggest Test Yet as Vikings GM
full_text:
The 5-0 Vikings are emerging from their bye with their eyes on their upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium this Sunday. Head coach Kevin O’Connell and his staff have finished their self-evaluation, players are back from spending time with family, and the training staff is hard at work making sure any injuries are left in the dust . But for general manager Nolan Teasley, the next few weeks are anything but business as usual.
In fact, what he does between now and the looming November 10 trade deadline will provide the first real indication of what kind of GM he plans to be.
The Vikings are in a very unique spot. They’re undefeated, with a stellar defense, an offense finally finding an identity, and many starters in the final years of their contracts. Any moves Teasley makes or doesn't make will carry vast implications for 2026 and beyond, significantly impacting his tenure. Needless to say, there are no easy answers.
We’ll be diving into specific possibilities as the deadline approaches, but for now, here are three paths the first-year GM could take with the trade deadline rapidly approaching.
Let’s get the boos out of the way early. As unpopular as it may be, there is a strong argument to be made for why the Vikings should not be buyers at the trade deadline. It’s important to remember that we really have no insight into Teasley’s true thoughts on this roster since he had almost no say in the bulk of its construction. This was always going to be a challenge once the team made it clear they had no intention of naming their next GM until after the draft.
Next offseason also represents a major fork in the road, with multiple key players in the final year of their current deals. Some soon-to-be free agents include:
While a “re-sign everyone” button would certainly come in handy here, OverTheCap projects the Vikings at just $35,023,180 in cap space for next season . Unless the league significantly increases the cap, some tough decisions will have to be made.
The Vikings currently have nine draft selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, and incoming free-agent decisions could leave them needing every one. I believe the Vikings’ success through five games makes it hard to do nothing at the deadline, but I couldn’t blame Teasley if he decided to think long-term.
Consider this the “safe” option: finding a way to add a potential impact maker for a relatively low cost. Think back to the team’s 2024 acquisition of former Jaguars tackle Cam Robinson after Christian Darrisaw was lost for the season to a torn ACL/MCL.
Minnesota traded a conditional 2026 fifth-round pick for Robinson and a 2026 conditional seventh-round pick. Ultimately, the trade worked out well for Minnesota, as Robinson played valiantly in Darrisaw’s place before departing for Houston in free agency. The loss of left guard Donovan Jackson for the season may create a similar opportunity to add a solid offensive lineman in exchange for a day-three pick.
Pass rusher is another area where depth may be needed. After all, you can never have enough ammo for Brian Flores’ aggressive, all-out blitz attack. Chargers outside linebacker Khalil Mack is one name I’ve been watching as LA continues to spiral through a winless season.
It was no secret that the Vikings would be a dream job for any potential GM candidate, but even the most optimistic predictions likely didn’t expect them to start this hot. Teasely entered truly rare air as he took over as GM for a ready-to-compete roster in June, with little input or say on a roster that's off to an undefeated 5-0 start. The question now is how confident he is in the roster he took over. If he believes this roster can win it all this season, we may see the former Seahawks assistant GM go all in on earning his second ring in a row.
One big name making the rounds? Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. While the trade compensation and salary-cap gymnastics required to make this kind of move work need their own deep dive, I don’t think a move like this could be entirely ruled out. There are two main reasons why this kind of aggressive move makes sense, especially after the Colts fired GM Chris Ballard this week:
This move would in no way be a referendum on Jones, who has run admirably this season while Mason recovered from a thumb injury on IR. However, it would solve a long-term need and give the Vikings their first true bell cow back since Dalvin Cook's departure in 2023. Teasley played a key role in building a similar formula in Seattle, and he could make a similar impact in Minnesota. Simply put, this is the move you make if you want to bet it all on this current squad.

title: Patriots Stock Report: Which Position Groups Rose, Fell vs. Bears?
full_text:
The New England Patriots' battle with the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Thursday night had the visiting team flash plenty of inconsistencies.
Many of New England's positions shined, or struggled, as a collective. Here are the stock reports on the groups which had the biggest impacts in either regard.
New England's wide receiver room may have been the biggest contributor to the team's loss on Thursday night. A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams combined for just seven receptions on 12 targets. Those catches went for 87 yards and no touchdowns.
As the primary target at wide receiver, Brown struggled once again. He has caught just three passes in each of his trio of games as a Patriot.
"I think (the Bears' defense) did a really good job," Brown said after the game. "Early on, (offensive coordinator) Josh (McDaniels) tried to do a really good job of getting me involved and Drake just was taking what they were giving. They were trying to take me away early on, and that's just kind of how the game played."
What the Patriots lacked in production from its wide receivers, it made up for with its tight ends. Veteran Hunter Henry tallied seven receptions for 71 yards, including multiple crucial first down conversions. Also, rookie Eli Raridon got on the board for three receptions, 56 yards and a touchdown.
The main highlight from those two? Raridon's 30-yard score late in the third quarter.
Drake Maye DIME to Eli Raridon 🪙 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/ajUvbcD8Oo
"(He's) great, man," Henry said on Thursday about Raridon. "Just continuing to get better and growing that confidence. A lot of fun to play with."
To address the elephant in the room, yes, Drake Maye's interception was borderline unacceptable. After being turnover-free in his last two games, the third-year signal caller reverted back to his early-season struggles by tossing a pick in the red zone.
Other than that, however, Maye was near-perfect on the evening. He finished 24/31 passing for 321 yards and two touchdowns, alongside the interception. On the ground, he added an extra 26 yards and a score.
In a game where he was constantly pressured, and his receivers were struggling to get open, Maye was one of the lone reasons why New England had any chance of beating Chicago.
"He gave us a chance," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said about Maye after the loss. "He competed. And I know he'd like to have that throw back to Eli, but I thought that he really competed. Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football, he gave us a chance."
The Patriots' pass defense was borderline non-existent on Thursday. Their completion percentage allowed (66.7%) was largely aided by a few bad drops by Bears receivers. Plus, Caleb Williams tossed for over 300 yards and two touchdowns.
While the defense as a whole improved in the second half, the secondary struggled immensely in the first 30 minutes against dynamic wide receiver Luther Burden III. The second-year pass catcher hauled in four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown — all coming in the first half of play.
New England's running back room struggled immensely in the ground game, but helped make up for the wide receivers' struggles in the pass game. Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combined for only 13 carries and 44 yards, and played a significant role in the Patriots' slow start to the night.
However, Stevenson also ended the night with five receptions for a team-high 93 yards and a touchdown. The score came on a 48-yard catch-and-run with no time remaining in the first half to cut the Bears' lead to one possession.
Crazy things happening 🤯 @budlight | 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/QdmQ1DOPPX
Between penalties, pressures allowed on Maye and an inability to find momentum in the run game, the Patriots offensive line combined for a perfectly imperfect performance on Thursday.
Offensive tackle Morgan Moses was called for a hold to back New England up from 2nd-and-2 to 2nd-and-12. Plus, he allowed three pressures and a sack on the evening, per PFF. Every other starter on the line allowed one pressure and was called for a penalty, except for center Jared Wilson who had a clean sheet in both regards.

title: Patriots, Bears QB Duel Lived Up To The Hype
full_text:
CHICAGO — It lived up to the hype, that's for sure.
The second-ever meeting between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams was far better than their first one two seasons ago. The young quarterbacks for the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears had excellent days for their respective sides on Thursday Night Football, with Williams' Bears grabbing the 30-24 win in the final moments .
"Shoulda, woulda, coulda," Maye told reporters postgame. "I'm proud of the guys for the effort. I think we did some good things, we've got a lot of stuff to clean up."
But that loss wasn't on Maye's shoulders, at least not entirely. The 24-year-old went 24-for-31 for 347 total yards and three total touchdowns (two passing, one rushing). It was a fantastic effort by Maye, who kept the Patriots offense in the game all night.
And yet, it was Williams' scrambling and elite arm talent that led the Bears. He finished the night going 22-for-33 for 308 yards and two passing touchdowns, and hit Rome Odunze on a pair of first downs that started to break the Patriots' proverbial defensive back.
It was two juggernauts dueling it out.
"Drake's a competitor, man," tight end Hunter Henry said in the locker room. "That's what he does. We always got a chance when 10's back there, that's for sure."
"He did a great job extending plays," A.J. Brown, who caught three passes in the loss, said. "He did great."
Maye's one blip on his radar was a bad interception in the first half. Looking to hit rookie Eli Raridon in the end zone, he didn't put enough air on his pass and Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson picked it off. It was Maye's third INT thrown in the end zone this season, the most in the entire NFL.
On the other side of the field, Williams completed eight passes of 20+ yards, tied for the most by any quarterback in 2026. He didn't turn the ball over and used his legs to buy some time for his receivers, which hurt the Patriots secondary's ability to defend "the second play."
"We talked about it all week," Christian Gonzalez said. "He's very gifted with how he can run and how he can extend plays. ... You gotta defend the second play. There's a play and then there's a second play with a quarterback like Caleb."
"Anytime a quarterback that's as mobile as him gets out of the pocket, they definitely put stress on the DBs," Charles Woods told Patriots On SI. "It's definitely difficult, but that's what we signed up."
Williams ran for just 18 yards, but his legs helped set up some of the game's biggest plays. He rolled out to find Colston Loveland on a 12-yard touchdown in the third quarter. He escaped the pocket to help pick up big conversions late in the fourth. He was the victor in Week 7, and deservingly so.
If this was the type of matchup these two young quarterbacks can provide , watch out NFL. Instead of rookie gunslingers on bad teams in 2024, these were two grown quarterbacks that offer plenty of skills under center. It was a fun one to watch at Soldier Field.
"I just appreciate we have him back there and (to) be able to block for him," Walter Rouse, who started his first game of the season at left guard, told Patriots On SI. "Drake's an awesome, great guy."
The loss wasn't the outcome the Patriots had hoped for, but it was a gutsy effort by their quarterback. It's just the latest in a string of them, and it's proving why he's the face of this franchise.
"He gave us a chance," Mike Vrabel said. "He competed. ... He'll learn from it like he always does. I'm glad he's ours."

title: Patriots Defense Struggles, and 6 More Takeaways From Groggy TNF Loss to Bears
full_text:
CHICAGO — At some point, the New England Patriots ' three game-winning streak was going to end. That happened at Soldier Field Thursday, as they ran into a Chicago Bears-shaped buzzsaw and couldn't get anything cooking.
Struggles upfront on an injury-depleted offensive line, penalties and an inability to stop the chunk play was what caused the Patriots to drop this one 30-24 to the Bears on a national stage. They kept it close in the final frame, but several long first downs from Rome Odunze wiped that dream away.
Drake Maye (23-for-29, 305 passing yards, two total touchdowns) was efficient, but couldn't will his team to the win. Instead, it was Caleb Williams (22-for-33, 308 passing yards, two passing touchdowns) who emerged victorious, handing the Patriots their first loss in the city of Chicago since 2000.
Here's what happened, and what it means moving forward.
The Patriots lost Alijah Vera-Tucker (who was placed on IR pregame) and Ben Brown last week in their win over the New York Jets. So they had to turn to Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse to step into the starting lineup.
it didn't go that well. The Bears continued to dial up pressure — both up the middle and off the edge — to make life difficult for Maye in the pocket. Chicago really got into the backfield consistently, allowing just 70 yards on the ground. They also sacked Maye twice.
The Patriots would get on the board with a seven-yard rushing touchdown from Maye, but for the most part, the ground game was not the way to go. They consistently lost battles in the trenches and it really took the running attack out of the playbook down the line.
For the entire first half, the Patriots struggled to stay on Burden in coverage. The speedy wideout — who came into the game with just 361 receiving yards on the year — tallied 130 receiving yards with a touchdown.
A 58-yard catch-and-run early helped set up a four-yard D'Andre Swift touchdown in the first quarter, and he'd hit paydirt himself on a weaving 24-yard score. The Patriots would soon adapt, and Burden would be shut down in the second half and held without a catch.
After several weeks of playing nearly-flawless football, Maye made his first bad decision in a while. Driving down the field, he tried to hit Eli Raridon in the end zone in the second quarter. He didn't put enough juice on the throw, and it was picked off by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson.
That was the third time in seven games that Maye has been intercepted in the end zone this year, the most by any NFL quarterback. Other than that, the Patriots quarterback was good at getting the ball out to his open receivers.
He could have had A.J. Brown deep down the sideline , but the perfectly thrown ball was deflected by Malik Muhammed in coverage. Brown's night ended with just three catches and he's yet to make that big play the Patriots need him to make .
After Burden ran his way in for a touchdown and a 20-7 lead, it looked like the Patriots were heading into the locker room on life support. But somehow, someway, they made something out of nothing.
Maye connected with A.J. Brown on his first reception of the game, good for 18 yards. The Patriots would call a timeout with three ticks left and line up for appeared to be a Hail Mary attempt.
Instead, they checked it down to Rhamondre Stevenson out of the backfield. He would run and pick up some yardage against a Chicago defense playing pretty soft coverage. Then he'd cut back and pick up some more yardage. And more, until the Patriots running back waltzed into the end zone untouched. That 48-yard pickup was the longest play by New England all night, and got them back into the game.
On the Bears' opening drive of the second half, they'd pick up chunk play after chunk play to drive deep into New England territory. Williams would roll out and hit tight end Colston Loveland — who'd power his way into the end zone and give the Bears the 27-14 lead.
But not so fast. Maye and the Patriots go on an impressive drive of their own in response. They drive 80 yards on nine plays, and it ends with Maye hitting Rairdon down the right seam for a 30-yard touchdown.
After back-to-back drives where both offenses sputtered out, the Bears would try to extend their lead with a Cairo Santos field goal. That 53-yard attempt would hit the right upright, giving the Patriots a chance — a chance they'd squander away after giving up a big sack on second down.
All night, the Patriots defense was just getting gashed . Whether it was a long pass from Williams to Odunze or a crisp off-tackle run for Swift that picked up a first down, it was difficult for the Patriots to make life difficult for the home team. The Bears had more than 400 total yards of offense, and that was even converting just four third downs.
But they were oh so close plenty of times. Kevin Byard nearly broke up a pass, but a dart from Williams to Odunze turned into a 21-yard pickup. Neither Milton Williams nor Christian Barmore — the team's top stars on the interior — could muster up any consistent pressure. Williams' ability to move in the pocket and scramble if needed really limited the impact that the Patriots could have done.
Barmore would sack Williams on a third down with 1:39 left, but Santos would drill a 58-field goal one play later to essentially put the nail in the coffin. Barmore would also get banged up on the play and leave the game.
The Patriots lost to the Bears, but they also kept beating themselves.
They were flagged 10 times for 71 total yards, and consistently put themselves behind the 8-ball. A false start from Pryor turned what would have been a fourth down conversion attempt into a punt, and a Cory Durden encroachment flag gave the Bears a first down after the final two-minute warning.
It wasn't just the Patriots, though. The Bears were also called for eight penalties for 56 yards.
The Patriots, after playing two games in five days and now sitting at 4-3, will now have the next three days off.

title: Patriots Week 7 Inactives vs. Bears: Breaking Down What to Expect at OL Tonight
full_text:
CHICAGO — In under 90 minutes, two teams with Super Bowl aspirations will duke it out in front of a national audience. The New England Patriots and Chicago Bears , both sporting 4-2 records, will do battle on Thursday Night Football — but not at full strength.
The Patriots have taken a beating in recent weeks . They've had to put a number of players on injured reserve this season, including wide receiver Romeo Doubs this week. It hasn't been easy sledding for the defending AFC champions, and a short week certainly won't help that.
Here's a look at the inactives from both sides, including key offensive linemen who won't be able to dress:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
QB Case Keenum (emergency third QB)
RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe)
CB Channing Canada (hamstring)
CB Karon Prunty (hamstring)
For the Patriots, there isn't any surprises. Head coach Mike Vrabel shared all of these names (other than Behren Morton and Joshua Farmer) at his final press conference of the week on Wednesday.
Rookie offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover will return to the lineup after being inactive for the last  five games. Behren Morton, who's been the third quarterback all season, won't be able to play unless Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito leave with injuries.
For the Bears, losing their downhill running back in Kyle Monangai is a break for the Patriots — who have struggled against the run in recent weeks. They'll still have to deal with D'Andre Swift , who had two touchdowns on 44 yards a week ago against Atlanta.
"Their runners or anybody that touches the ball is going to be a physical player, is going to be a tough tackle," Vrabel said. "We'll have to be great tacklers."
After Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown went down a week ago, the Patriots got inspiring outings from their backups. Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor , the last two active linemen on the game day roster, stepped up to fill in at both guard spots. They'll now be in the starting lineup tonight, with Rouse handling the left side and Pryor the right.
It's just another offensive line combination that the Patriots will need to navigate through . They lost Mike Onwenu early in the season, and then lost his backup Greg Van Roten one week later. Just a few games later, and we're seeing two players who didn't spend the summer in New England starting a primetime game. Vera-Tucker was placed on IR prior to kickoff , ruling him out for the next four games.
Vrabel was asked Wednesday about the possibility of rookie tackle Caleb Lomu, who's gotten reps on both sides of the line the last two weeks, potentially kicking inside at guard.
"We have a lot of consideration," he said. "We go through things, different scenarios. We're going to go with where we finished on Sunday and see what that looks like, and then have everybody else ready to go."
The Patriots are also down three cornerbacks, the biggest name being Carlton Davis. He's been dealing with a neck injury for a lot of the season, and this will be his fourth missed game of the year. They're also down rookies Channing Canada and Karon Prunty, who both have hamstring injuries.
Davis is the team's second-best cornerback and easily their top one when it comes to playing the run. But he's struggled to stay healthy in 2026, and while he was spotted at practice for the first time in three weeks leading up to this game, the Patriots still didn't feel comfortable rolling him out there.
The Patriots will have four active cornerbacks for this matchup against a high-flying Bears offense, with Christian Gonzalez, Marcus Jones, Charles Woods and Kindle Vildor ready to go. Second-year safety Elliott Davison has also gotten snaps at cornerback this season in a reserve role.
The Patriots nearly got a scare at cornerback, as Gonzalez was downgraded to questionable pregame with an illness. However, he was warming up on the field and will suit up.
The Bears come into this matchup with one of the league's best defenses — especially against the run. But they rank 14th in the NFL in passing defense through six games, and with a few players banged up in the secondary, the Patriots can try to push the ball through the air.
Chicago will be without cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, who was ruled out with a hip injury. They'll also line up without Nick McCloud (who's played in just two games this year) on the field. They do have Kyler Gordon back, who played last week after opening the year on the PUP list, but he's still trying to knock the rust off.
If the Patriots want to try and air the ball out against a secondary that isn't at full strength, they could end up putting up a bunch of points in a hurry. Avoiding a stout Bears run defense, especially early in drives, could be beneficial.

title: Key Patriots Starter Goes to IR, Pair of Practice Squad Elevations for TNF
full_text:
Ahead of Thursday night's game against the Chicago Bears, the New England Patriots have announced that guard Alijah Vera-Tucker has been placed on the injured reserve . Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in Sunday's win over the New York Jets .
Vera-Tucker is a former first-round NFL Draft selection, who spent his first four years with the Jets. This past offseason, the 6-foot-4, 308 pound linemen signed with New England on a three-year contract worth up to $48 million.
The Patriots starting left guard has had a career riddled with injuries. Since entering the league six years ago, Vera-Tucker has only played 55.1% of offensive snaps. Vera-Tucker becomes the 22nd player to be placed on a reserve list for the Patriots this year, and is the ninth projected starter to miss at least four weeks with an injury.
Vera-Tucker will be eligible to return in Week 13, four games after his IR designation.
The Patriots will rely on players listed deep in the depth chart at the guard position against the Bears. With Ben Brown ruled out, and both Greg Van Roten and Mike Onwenu on injured reserve, the Patriots will start Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse — their fifth and sixth options, at guard .
In addition to Pryor and Rouse, New England will have lineman Xavier Newman-Johnson available Thursday night, as he's been announced as a practice squad elevation.
Newman-Johnson has been with the Patriots since Week 2 of the NFL season, and will be on the Patriots game roster for the first time. It's his first of three elevations for the season
A fifth-year player, Newman-Johnson got his start in Tennessee while Mike Vrabel was the head coach. He then spent three seasons in New York with the Jets, with extended time on the team's 53-man roster. Newman-Johnson will serve as a a back-up to Pryor and Rouse at both guard positions.
The Patriots have placed LG Alijah Vera-Tucker on IR with a hamstring injury. They also elevated OG Xavier Newman-Johnson and LB Benton Whitley to the game day roster from the practice squad.
The Patriots have also elevated linebacker Benton Whitley. Whitley has been with the Patriots for just under a month, and will also be seeing his first game action as a Patriot on Thursday night.
A Holy Cross graduate, Whitley is in his fifth year in the NFL after bouncing around to multiple teams, six of which he was signed to the 53-man roster. He'll be making his seventh appearance in an NFL game on Thursday night, and will supplement a linebacker room consisting of Robert Spillane , Christian Ellis, Namdi Obiazor, Darius Muasa, and Erick Hunter.

title: Patriots Host Veteran OG on Visit, Which Might Tip Their Hand Injury-Wise
full_text:
The New England Patriots have taken body blow after body blow when it comes to the health of their offensive tackles. They've lost four offensive guards to injuries so far ( Mike Onwenu - ankle , Greg Van Roten - knee, Alijah Vera-Tucker - hamstring, Ben Brown - knee), really pushing that unit to the limit.
So it comes as no surprise that the Patriots are trying to cross every t and dot every i when it comes to the offensive line position this week. After signing familiar faces Andrew Rupcich and Jacob Rizy to the practice squad, they're also hosting a veteran guard on a visit to the facility.
According to NFL insider Aaron Wilson , the Patriots hosted Jamaree Salyer on a visit. Salyer, a Los Angeles Chargers' sixth round pick back in 2022, spent the summer with the Miami Dolphins and has remained a free agent since being released in August.
Could the Patriots sign Sayler to help add some much-needed depth to their depleted offensive line? They certainly could. This visit could also tip the Patriots' hands when it comes to the health of some of their banged-up players.
Salyer was a great player at Georgia in college, and was teammates with current Patriots center Jared Wlson. Since being drafted in 2022, Salyer suited up for 67 total games with the Chargers — 43 of those games were starters. He's gotten experience at several spots on the line, starting games at left tackle and right guard during his career.
The 26-year-old then signed with the Dolphins in the offseason, but a knee injury led to him being placed on IR. The Patriots' division rival would go on to release him from IR with an injury settlement.
Salyer was primarily a backup in recent seasons, but his versatility is a nice thing to keep in your back pocket if you're the Patriots. He's 6-foot-4, 325 pounds and could help add some much-needed depth while the statuses of some of your players hangs in the balance.
Last season with Los Angeles, Salyer recorded a 69.0 pass blocking grade and 61.5 run blocking grade (according to Pro Football Focus). He played 449 total snaps, allowing 19 pressures and four sacks.
The Patriots have plenty of offensive linemen in the building right now, but you'd be hard pressed to find some that aren't dealing with an injury of some sort. They've already ruled out Vera-Tucker and Brown for tonight's primetime game against the Chicago Bears , and still haven't activated offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (ankle) from IR.
There are plenty of depth pieces on the practice squad (Rupcich, Rizy, Xavier Newman-Johnson, Jake Kubas, Lorenz Metz), but none of those options are players that feel like an easy plug and play on any given Sunday. Salyer — who played against the Patriots in last year's AFC Wild Card game — has more of an opportunity to do so.
As it stands right now, the Patriots are set to roll with Walter Rouse (left guard) and Matt Pryor (right guard) in the starting lineup, two players who weren't on the roster three months ago. In case one of them goes down, the Patriots will need to find some sort of break glass in case of emergency plan.
Could that plan end up being Salyer?

title: Patriots, Bears in Eerily Similar Situations at QB: Comparing Drake Maye, Caleb Williams
full_text:
Similiar stories have defined the recent history of both franchises that are set to meet on Thursday night. The New England Patriots and Chicago Bears, both with a 4-2 record, are two of the most promising teams of the future of the NFL.
Each team is coming off their first playoff appearance in years, with both playoff runs including at least one win. Additionally, the Bears and Patriots won their respective divisions for the first time in over five years.
The recent success isn't what makes this matchup of two up-and-coming teams so similiar. The personell, the identity, and the revitilization of historic franchises have put both brands on a similar timeline, just in different conferences.
Take, for example, the head coach of each team. Both Mike Vrabel and Ben Johnson are in their second year with their respective clubs, and were NFL Coach of the Year finalists in 2025 (Vrabel won the award).
Johnson, in his first stint as head coach, is known for his aggressive play calling and willingness to take risks — something Vrabel introduced to the league when he was first hired by Tennessee in 2018.
Back in 2025, both coaches interviewed for each other's positions and were considered the top two candidates of that offseason's hiring cycle. Now, each coach will have a chance to prove why they were the better hiring decision.
More significant than the person with the headset, is the player on the field that has defined each franchise over the past two years.
Quarterbacks Caleb Williams and Drake Maye were centerpieces of the 2024 NFL Draft — a weekend that saw three quarterbacks be taken before any other position, and six quarterbacks taken in the first round. Williams went first, and Maye was the third pick to New England, after the Commanders selected Jayden Daniels.
Both 24-year-old quarterbacks play at a quick pace, with the opportunity to extend plays with their legs and their ability to create more time with elite pocket presence instincts.
Williams, a product of Southern California, won a lot of games for Chicago with his eagerness to shorten deficits and take the lead late in the game. He showcased his arm and his legs, often putting together late-game wins in pursuit of Chicago's NFC North division victory.
4th-and-8 with the game on the line and Caleb Williams delivered this throw 😱 @ChicagoBears pic.twitter.com/kmNDl8Y6hy
Maye, on the other hand, found excellence in his consitency and precision as a passer. He was one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the league in 2025. Just barely the Most Valuable Player runner-up, the North Carolina Tar Heel impressed all with his first to second year jump.
What makes this meeting even more freaky, is the similarity in the on-field production from each player. Williams has only played one more game in the NFL than Maye, but their statistics are almost identical.
Williams has thrown just 62 passing yards more than Maye in their careers, with both quarterbacks surpassing 8,100 yards. Additionally, they each have over a 60% completion rating, with Maye completing 68.7% of passes and Williams completing 61.2%.
Each has thrown for 50 or more touchdowns, with Williams at the 50 mark and Maye edging seven more than his Thursday night counterpart. Williams, however, has the edge on Maye in turnovers, as he's thrown only 14 interceptions in comparison to Maye's 25.
Additionally, their rushing statistics give extremely similar outputs. Maye has run for just 69 more yards in his career (1,056 total rush yards) than Williams has, and his 7 touchdowns on the ground are two more than Chicago's dual-threat player.
While the second and third year success of both quarterbacks have built excitement for Thursday night's game, many forget that Maye and Williams met in a rookie year contest where the Patriots bested Chicago 19-3.
Two years ago, an afternoon defined by elite defense overshadowed the rookie duel. The quarterbacks threw for a combined 304 yards and the singular touchdown of the game belonged to Ja'Lynn Polk on a two-yard pass from Maye. Williams was sacked nine times as the Patriot defense carried Maye to his first win in a completed game (the Patriots beat the New York Jets two games prior in a match that saw Maye exit early with an injury).
Thursday's Week 7 primetime bout will feature two teams that are forced to rely on their high-powered offenses. Williams, with his weapons Colston Loveland, Luther Burden, and Rome Odunze; and Maye, who's limited to a wide receiver room of just four, including the newly acquired and activated A.J. Brown.
"I've kind of grown up with Drake," shared the Bears quarterback. "Throughout the years we've grown up in the same class, been to the same camps. [He's] probably one of the guys I'm closer to in my class."
Drake Maye on Caleb Williams: pic.twitter.com/80iHGvMAxS
Maye, who's been statistically the best quarterback in the NFL over the past three weeks , also had positive things to say about his draft classmate: "I don't know if I could do some of the things he could do. He's special in the way he can move and kinda escape and evade pressure."
Maye and Williams will meet Thursday night, in an attempt to hand their opponent a third loss on the season. The Bears are looking to find their groove with Williams back as their quarterback after missing three weeks with a hamstring injury, while the Patriots are riding Maye's hot hand in search of a fourth straight victory.
