title: Potential Quenton Nelson Trade Makes Too Much Sense for Jets on Multiple Fronts
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline looms for the Jets and the other 31 teams , the Colts are emerging as a potential trade partner for all.
Heading into Week 7, the Colts are 2-4 and just fired long-time general manager Chris Ballard earlier this week. Indianapolis looks like a deadline seller, as the Daniel Jones magic hasn't continued into his second year. The Colts don't look like a team that will blow everything up, but they'll likely move a player like left guard Quenton Nelson, who becomes an unrestricted free agent in March.
If Nelson is for sale, the Jets should throw their hat in the ring.
Nelson has been a dominant left guard since he entered the league in 2018. Nelson earned an AP First-Team All-Pro selection as a rookie and has remained one of the league's best. This is his ninth season, and Pro Football Focus still grades him highest at his position . The Jets could bring in Nelson if the Colts are willing to sell the aging superstar.
Nelson is in the twilight of his career. The 30-year-old is in the last year of a four-year, $80 million contract , allowing the Jets to trade for him as a low-risk rental. If he plays well, the Jets— who have over $105 million to spend next offseason —would already have him in the building to talk about an extension or re-signing. If he doesn't, it's no harm, no foul for the team in Florham Park.
The guard's contract should also lower the Colts' asking price in a trade. Instead of paying top dollar, the Jets could trade away some of their less desirable draft capital or players who don't fit their future plans. New York could pull off a team-friendly trade deal if the Colts are truly in fire-sale mode.
The Jets have a chance to bring Nelson home , something 30 other teams in the league can't do. The perennial All-Pro is a New Jersey native. Nelson began his football career an hour away from the Jets' facility, at Red Bank Catholic High School in Red Bank, New Jersey. The guard would have a chance to finish his career where it began, back home.
Getting one of the best to ever do it to bolster the o-line is great, but the storyline could be even better. New York has the ability to act as a homecoming for Nelson, and if things go right, bring a storybook ending to his illustrious career.
If a trade to the Jets happens, Nelson would immediately slot in at left guard. This would allow the rest of the Jets' offensive line to shift to different positions. Both Joe Tippmann and Dylan Parham have been moved along the line throughout their careers. Nelson coming in wouldn't force either of the Jets' guards out, as they have been flexible along the line throughout their careers.
Tippmann was drafted as a center coming out of the University of Wisconsin. Tippmann has played 1,720 snaps at the center position throughout his career. He could slot back in ahead of Josh Myers, who's been graded 60.3 this year , while Tippmann graded 73.4 during his last year as a primary center .
If Nelson becomes a Jet, Tippmann can go back to his natural position, where he grades well.
Dylan Parham has also shown that he can play at either guard position. Parham has been great on the left side, grading as the second-best at the position behind Nelson. If healthy, he could slot back on the right side if the Jets were to acquire Nelson.
Parham has played 992 snaps at right guard, despite spending the majority of his career on the left side. That experience could be utilized if changes come.
Nelson is a once-in-a-generation type of player. The Colts are clearly headed towards a rebuild. Bringing the All-Pro home must be on the table for the Jets, given the aging star's contract and the flexibility of the current Jets' offensive line.

title: Garrett Wilson Could Be Jets' Biggest Winner If Omar Cooper Jr.'s Breakout Continues
full_text:
Following a disappointing 26-19 loss to the Patriots last Sunday, the Jets turn their attention to a Week 7 clash with the Dolphins on Sunday as they look to win their first divisional game in head coach Aaron Glenn’s tenure.
While the game itself could be Glenn’s last chance to keep his job against a winless Dolphins team, a lot of blame for the 2-4 start to the season also rests on the shoulders of offensive coordinator Frank Reich, who continues to be one of the biggest letdowns on the entire team through six games.
Aside from his poor play-calling, particularly in short-yardage situations, Reich has failed to consistently get the ball to his best players. One of those is WR1 Garrett Wilson, who has only received double-digit targets twice in six games and has had five or fewer receptions three times.
The lack of targets and receptions was especially on display when rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. made his return from a high ankle sprain against the Patriots , leading the Jets' WR group with six catches for 103 yards and one touchdown.
While another quiet performance from the veteran playmaker wasn't ideal, it won't be long before Wilson makes some noise again if Cooper can keep his foot on the gas pedal.
With three 1,000-yard seasons to his credit—and likely four if he did not miss the final 10 games of last season with a right knee injury—Wilson was certainly worthy of the four-year, $130 million contract he signed prior to the start of the 2025 season.
His 35 receptions are ninth-most in the league, while his 418 receiving yards are 14th. According to Pro Football Focus , Wilson has the 18th-ranked overall grade (79) out of 80 qualified WRs , but that is still not where it should be for the top receiver on the team and someone who should be the go-to target each week.
But if the targets don't start coming, the Jets are nearing the point of no return with Wilson if they are not careful. This is a player who is already beginning to show his frustration with the lack of targets coming his way, and it is no surprise that New York’s best games have come when he has been the central focus of the aerial attack.
In the Week 6 loss to the Patriots, specifically, Wilson was targeted just two times in the first three quarters, only to receive four targets alone in the fourth. The fact that it took that long before the ball finally started going his way speaks to why it is time to start worrying about his future in Gang Green , unless the door finally starts to open as Cooper garners some additional attention away from him.
More performances like the one from Week 6 will force opposing defenses to pay closer attention to Cooper, which opens the door for more favorable matchups for Wilson. Not every team can defend two wideouts capable of 100-yard performances, and the Jets need to take advantage of that as much as possible.
The Dolphins possess the league's 16th-ranked passing defense (219.2 ypg), but they also give up the 24th-most points per game (26.4 ppg) and should present some opportunities for Wilson to exploit.
JuJu Brents and Jason Marshall Jr. are the two starting corners for the Dolphins, while Chris Johnson handles heavy slot responsibilities as the nickel and Dante Trader Jr. and Zayne Anderson man the strong and free safety positions, respectively. Trader has one of just three interceptions for the Dolphins this season, and Johnson has forced a fumble, but this is a unit the Jets should feel confident going up against.
The Dolphins average less than a turnover per game (0.8), which is tied for 27th, but even if Miami is able to leave an impact and make it challenging on New York's wideouts, Wilson should not have to worry about as much double-team coverage with Cooper back on the field. The rookie WR had an average depth of target of 12.3 yards last week , according to Pro Football Focus , showing how much the Jets trust him to make big plays (h/t NFL) and open up the field.
The rookie Omar Cooper Jr. makes the 48-yard touchdown catch! NYJvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/y88N5gruHa
That could allow Wilson to finally become the red-zone target that he needs to be after receiving just three targets in Gang Green's 14 trips to that area of the field this season. The Jets simply need to feed their WR1 when the end zone is in sight and give him a chance to come down with a TD, which he did the only time that he and quarterback Geno Smith connected in the red zone earlier this season.
The Dolphins allow the sixth-most yards per reception (7.8) this season, so there should be increased opportunities for Wilson to take advantage of that and make them pay—as long as he gets the ball. After all, he has still played well when he has been a focal point of the offense.
Additionally, Wilson has 39 catches for 436 yards and two touchdowns in seven all-time meetings with the AFC East rival.
With Cooper talented enough to draw some of the focus away from Wilson, the Jets need to capitalize on their wealth of talent by throwing the ball to their WR1 any and every chance they get.

title: Jets Can't Rule Out a Dane Belton Trade Despite Being Their Best Offseason Signing
full_text:
It's only taken six games for Dane Belton to be a revelation for a Jets defense that was a sieve last season. New York signed the fifth-year safety to a one-year, $4 million contract during the offseason, and he's been paying that back in dividends.
Pro Football Focus ranks Belton 17th overall among qualified safeties and third at the position in the run game. The 25-year-old has clearly improved the defense, but let's not forget: the Jets are 2-4 and trending towards selling pieces ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
There have been calls for Belton to get a contract extension (and rightfully so), but if New York continues to trend toward being sellers at the deadline , Belton should be shopped around.
New York currently holds nine picks for the upcoming draft, including three first-rounders. The Jets look better than last season, but they're still in the midst of a rebuild. General manager Darren Mougey has shown no fear of trading away supposed cornerstones of the franchise, and Belton isn't that caliber yet.
As such, Mougey could use Belton as an asset at the deadline to bolster the Jets' draft capital.
Trading a player who is performing well for the team may not be the most popular move, but Belton fits the bill. The Jets turned the Sauce Gardner trade into Kenyon Sadiq, who has shown flashes of superstar potential. Trading the former Giant to a Super Bowl contender could bring another potential superstar to Florham Park.
Belton won't fetch the Jets a first-round pick like Sauce Gardner or Quinnen Williams, but could bring day two and three value for Gang Green. Belton could be sold high, as his performance has been among the league's best at the position. There are a plethora of teams that need safety help ; Mougey shouldn't hesitate to make those calls.
Belton has been one of Mougey's best signings during his tenure in New York. He has another chance to make the right decision if the Jets decide to sell. The Jets may have a chance to flip a one-year player into rookie contracts; failing to do so would be malpractice.
Trading away Belton does not mean that he can't come back to the Jets either. The safety's contract will allow him to test free agency if that is what he desires. It may be in the best interest of the Jets to allow Belton to leave if they want him back.
The Jets have been competitive, but they're still pieces away from becoming a true contender. Belton has never had the chance to play for one, with his first four years being on the other cellar-dwelling team in East Rutherford. The Jets could let Belton chase playoff success while boosting their own chances at playoff relevance.
Gang Green has clearly taken a step up from who they have been in the past. The eye test shows more than their record, as New York has been competitive in almost every game this season. The Jets may be a hot destination come free agency. With a competitive roster and the aforementioned draft capital, selling the dream should be easier than in years past.
If the Jets trade Belton in good faith, who is to say he won't want to return to the team after his contract runs out? A trade could allow Belton to see that the grass isn't as Gotham green on the other side.
With 11 games remaining, New York still has a chance to turn the season around.
If head coach Aaron Glenn's squad can win a couple of games in the upcoming weeks, the conversation about selling players may become moot . But the options should still be on the table. Belton has been great on the field, but if the Jets don't improve, he could make his biggest impact as a trade asset.

title: Garrett Wilson's Frustration Could Boil Over Again If Jets Don't Walk Fine Line
full_text:
A quick look at the stat sheet shows Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson is off to another stellar season in 2026 .
Over six weeks, Wilson ranks in the top 15 in key receiving categories, including catches (35), receiving yards (418), touchdowns (three), and targets (48). The Ohio State product is on pace for his second 100-catch, 1,000-yard season. Wilson's stats show he remains New York's top dog in the passing game.
So why did the veteran wide receiver look so frustrated after Week 6's 26-19 loss to the Patriots ?
A despondent Wilson appeared very frustrated after New York's fourth loss of the season. He has remained steadfast in his belief that the Jets are building the right kind of team, but as the losses continue, it isn't rocket science to ask when enough is enough for the veteran.
The good news for Jets fans is, after Wednesday's practice, those concerns seem subsided... for now.
It's not that Wilson seemed to be an issue or was openly furious over the Jets' performance on Sunday. He looked like a player who was frustrated with the loss and his lack of touches (four catches on six targets), as more could've helped alter the outcome.
According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, frustrating after New York's latest defeat wasn't exclusive to Wilson.
"We have a number of players; really all of our players feel that way," Glenn said. "They're highly competitive; they hate losing. Everybody, emotionally, is different on how they handle things, and that's okay."
It wasn't too long ago that Wilson's future in New York was in jeopardy. After a disastrous 2024 season with Aaron Rodgers, Wilson reportedly demanded to be shipped out if Rodgers returned for 2025. New York chose Wilson instead and gave him a nice four-year, $130 million extension to go along with that call.
Since the rescinded trade request, Wilson and Glenn have enjoyed a positive relationship. It's one built on allowing the 26-year-old playmaker to express himself while also playing within the confines of the organization each week.
That's great for Jets fans to hear, but...
It isn't a coincidence that the three best games the Jets have had this season—from an offensive perspective—have come when Wilson is the highest-targeted player. He remains a top receiver in the game and deserves the touches to go along with that.
Garrett Wilson targets (receptions)
Wilson's frustration from Sunday's loss may have subsided, but the roster will need to start winning games in droves. Otherwise, the other part of Wilson's nature is going to return and demand better results.
For his part, Wilson has taken ownership of his frustration during losses, but more so in the concept of the team losing rather than the lack of impact he has on a particular game. The balance he searches to find is one  of "productive vs. destructive."
"We all have plays we want back that are proven disruptive down the road," Wilson said. "All of us have been productive when called upon. It's real. For me, it's getting my feet wet early."
Hopefully, the Jets find a way to get Wilson's feet wet early against a Dolphins defense allowing the sixth-most yards per reception (7.8) this season.

title: Jets' Biggest Need Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's early defensive success this season should be commended ahead of a Week 7 clash with the Dolphins .
There is little true superstar talent among the group, and yet the Jets remain a top-10 unit against the pass and in points allowed. They also rank 11th this season in total yards allowed—the mark of a unit continuing to improve despite seeing quality offenses on their schedule.
But as improved as the unit has been this season, Gang Green's defense still has one glaring hole, and that is the one position the Jets will need to target as we get closer to the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
For all the success the Jets' defense has had this year, one group that has been an unequivocal disappointment has been the interior defensive line.
New York isn't generating enough pressure this season. Some will point to a low sack total from Will McDonald IV , or the hit-and-miss display from second-overall pick David Bailey, but the reality is the defensive interior is just as much to blame.
Consider the Jets' most recent loss . The Patriots chipped Gang Green's edge rushers because they understood the team did not have enough interior linemen who could get after quarterback Drake Maye. New England's strategy paid off, as Maye was hit sparingly throughout the 26-19 win.
The collection of T'Vondre Sweat, Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs just hasn't been good enough.
In fact, Phillips and Briggs have been two of the worst defensive tackles in the league this season. That shows in New York's run defense, allowing 123.0 rushing yards per game (23rd). If the Jets want to be competitive defensively down the stretch, this group will need to improve.
And it's important to add some added help to the unit as well.
As November nears, several defensive tackles are expected to be shopped around the trade market before the deadline. Eagles tackle Moro Ojomo has a much better history of getting after the passer ; Buccaneers All-Pro Vita Vea is an all-around star; and the Commanders' Daron Payne has Pro Bowl pedigree over his career.
These three players may not be options for general manager Darren Mougey and the Jets ahead of this trade deadline, but they do highlight an improved market for the team to potentially dip their toes into if it gets to that point.
Part of that will depend on what the Jets do on the field over the next two weeks. If the Jets beat both the Dolphins and Raiders, it would move Gang Green to 4-4 and put them in the driver's seat to compete for talent as the second half of the year begins.
Going 2-0 in that stretch would put the Jets in a good spot to add a defensive tackle to their weaker group. Anything less, and a solution to the Jets' defensive tackle problem could be punted to the 2027 offseason.

title: Why Jets vs. Dolphins Week 7 Could Be Aaron Glenn's Last Chance to Keep His Job
full_text:
As the Jets try to move past a frustrating 26-19 loss to the Patriots last Sunday, the focus shifts to another divisional clash against the Dolphins in the first of back-to-back home games at MetLife Stadium.
While a matchup against a winless Dolphins team seems like a game the Jets should win on paper, it is not that simple for a team that continues to struggle with situational football and beat itself. Look no further than the Week 6 loss to New England when the Jets went from trailing, 7-3, to falling behind, 17-3, after allowing a field goal and a touchdown and going three-and-out offensively to end the first half.
From an early challenge on a nine-yard catch from Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown and the decision to pass up multiple field-goal attempts in the first half to his defensive alignment and stubbornness offensively with an overreliance on the run game, Glenn was wrong in several areas of the Week 6 loss to the Patriots .
With an 0-7 record against AFC East opponents—the worst divisional start by a full-time Jets coach in franchise history—Glenn has put himself in a vulnerable position to where a loss to Miami could change his job status. He simply cannot afford to drop a lose-lose matchup where a win gives him zero credit and a loss only adds another blemish to an unproven record.
The disappointing loss to the Patriots is one thing , especially when you consider the Jets allowed them to convert eight of their 15 third downs and the offense's continued struggles in two-minute situations, but Glenn has clearly positioned himself on the hot seat despite improving the defense from where it was last season.
The Jets are 20th in average scoring margin this season (-1.7). While that is not ideal, it is well ahead of the last-place Dolphins (-12.4) and speaks to how competitive they have been through six games. If anything, that is another reminder of Glenn's poor game management and the team's inability to finish out drives when momentum is shifting their way.
Collapses late in each half has been a recurring issue, but the Jets were also a combined 0-of-5 on fourth-down and red-zone opportunities. In fact, they have been outscored, 20-0, in the final two minutes of the first half this season and an astounding 100-6 in Glenn's 23 games as the team's HC, all while giving up 11 TDs and eight field goals in that area since the start of last season.
As poor as the end-of-half situations have been, the glaring red-zone struggles are becoming too hard to ignore . The Jets are last in red-zone scoring through six games (37.5%), which is just behind the Dolphins and Browns (46.2%). New York only has six TDs in 14 red-zone trips this season (h/t Sharp Football), primarily due to costly penalties, a lack of usage with WR1 Garrett Wilson and not putting the ball in quarterback Geno Smith's hands enough when the end zone is in sight.
The Jets have a favorable schedule with the Dolphins and Raiders up next before back-to-back games against the 5-0 Chiefs and 5-1 Bills afterward. If the Jets cannot beat a winless Dolphins team on their home field, how can they be expected to be anywhere close to competitive against more formidable competition down the road?
Injuries to key players have certainly played a role this season, but that is no excuse for the lack of situational awareness and poor game management week in and week out from Glenn and this coaching staff. While some teams wait until their bye week to fire their coach, which would be Week 13 for the Jets, a loss to the Dolphins might be the last straw for Glenn to salvage his job in Gang Green.

title: 3 Potential Aaron Glenn Replacements Should Already Be on the Jets' Radar
full_text:
The Jets have had their own coaching carousel during their 16-year playoff drought. Aaron Glenn , New York's latest head coach, has a 5-18 record through 23 games.
He will likely be gone if the Jets' win-loss record doesn't improve this season, sitting at 2-4 in Week 7. If so, Woody Johnson and Co. should have these coaches on their shortlist for next season.
Mike Tomlin has been rumored as an option for the Jets job since he resigned at the end of last season. The former Steelers head coach has made waves for his building in Minecraft, but could do wonders building a new culture for the Jets.
Tomlin is a winner, plain and simple. He boasts a career .628 win percentage, made the playoffs 13 times, and has a Super Bowl ring to boot. The Jets need a winner; since 2010, they've had the NFL's second-worst win percentage. Meanwhile, Tomlin has never had a losing season during his tenure in Pittsburgh.
Tomlin would be a safe hire if the Jets can get him in the building. While his time with the Steelers ended unceremoniously, Jets fans would see Tomlin's shortcomings in the playoffs as champagne problems. Tomlin's career speaks for itself. He should be one of their first calls if the Jets are to fire Aaron Glenn.
The 49ers have been a hotbed of offensive coaching talent since Kyle Shanahan took the job in 2017.   Klay Kubiak may be the next leaf on the Shanahan tree to branch out. The Jets have had six head coaches since their last playoff appearance. Only one has been offensive-minded: Adam Gase.
Kubiak would be a perfect fit, especially if the Jets are to use one of their three first-round draft picks on a QB. The 38-year-old has led the 49ers' offense to a top-10 offense in the NFL during their 6-0 start. Kubiak will be a hot commodity come the offseason as teams change up coaching regimes.
Kubiak has succeeded despite the injuries that his offense has sustained. The Jets have weapons; they just haven't unlocked them consistently. Kubiak could be the answer to those issues. With the draft capital spent on offensive talent , the contracts for Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall, and a possible new rookie QB going into 2027, Kubiak should be someone the Jets keep an eye on.
If the Jets are looking for a new defensive mind, Chris Shula should be on that list. The 40-year-old has led the Rams to a top-three defense through six weeks. Shula comes from football royalty, with his grandfather being the legendary Don Shula. The Rams DC has been around football his whole life and is now under Sean McVay's tutelage, one of the league's best.
The Rams have been one of the best teams since McVay took over, winning one Super Bowl and appearing in two. The Jets could benefit from someone who comes from a sustained winning culture, both personally and professionally.
New York has had a good defense this year, ranking top-12 in total defense in 2026. Shula could raise that number while handling the head coaching job better than Glenn has so far. Woody Johnson clearly likes defensive-minded head coaches; Shula could bring a winning edge to a team that desperately needs it.
Glenn has clearly taken a step up from last season, but issues still remain. The former Lions' DC has been outscored 100-6 in the last two minutes of halves and still is losing games. If he loses his job before the start of the 2027 season, the Jets must take a look at these candidates.

title: Jamie Sherwood's Jets Future Has Become Clear as Contract Questions Loom
full_text:
Two years ago, he was named the team's MVP for a stellar breakout year.
One year ago, there was concern if he had played his final game with the team.
Despite the rollercoaster ride Jamien Sherwood has been on since the 2025 offseason with the New York Jets, the veteran linebacker seems to be back to his old shenanigans with the team this season.
That is, he's back to being one of the more underrated and better players at his position.
With his improved play come bigger questions about Sherwood's future with the team, though. And what his outlook will be beyond this upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins.
Through the first two weeks of the season, Sherwood appeared to be back to his 2025 form. He was slow to read, struggled in pass coverage, and was a net-negative player on the field.
Over the last three weeks, though, things have changed.
Pro Football Focus has graded Sherwood's season as the 31st-best of all linebackers in the league. His pass coverage grade ranks as the 22nd-best among all linebackers. Sherwood is playing the kind of football he did back in 2024: he's reading faster, he's instinctive, and he isn't afraid to use his athleticism to go downfield.
That was clear in New York's latest game, a 26-19 loss to the New England Patriots . Sherwood led the team with 11 tackles and even recovered a fumble early in the third quarter. However, his work in the fourth quarter really set him apart.
New York was down 10 midway through the final quarter. Demario Douglas and Drake Maye had connected on a 39-yard pass-and-catch. Douglas could have kept running for the game-ending score.
Instead, Sherwood ran 77 yards to not only get back into the play, but force a fumble that gave the Jets life. It was a hustle play coaches preach about never giving up on a play.
And highlights the breakout Sherwood is under.
If the veteran linebacker continues to play as he has over the last three weeks, his extension from last offseason will be well worth it, even if it raises some questions going forward.
What makes Sherwood's bounce-back so important is the fact that the Jets have gotten poor play from their other linebacker. Demario Davis was brought in to provide veteran leadership and consistent play at the position.
So far, his leadership has been great, but his play on the field has not been remotely competent . PFF graded Davis as the 13th-worst linebacker in the sport this season. At 37 years old, Davis has taken a step back both in coverage and against the run, which isn't good for a roster that gave him a two-year deal in the offseason.
Sherwood's play can mask some of Davis' struggles, though. Teams can target the veteran in coverage, but Sherwood has improved in that area. Instead, New York could utilize Davis in a way that focuses his efforts at the line of scrimmage.
In that capacity, the team should be thrilled with Sherwood's play. He's covering up a lot of the schematic defensive breakdowns this season.
But how long will that continue?
At 2-4, the Jets are entering a two-week stretch of must-win games. If the team beats the Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders, the Jets will move to 4-4 going into the midway point of the season and the trade deadline.
Getting to .500 would give general manager Darren Mougey a reason to "buy." Any loss in between, though, would drop the Jets to 3-5 or worse. That would not be enough to provide the front office with a reason to buy into this current core. If anything, it may lead the front office to sell some of the assets on expiring contracts.
At first glance, Sherwood is not a player from that perspective. A potential pre-June 1st release that would save the Jets $11 million in cap space despite a $7.5 million cap hit. But those numbers are based on when the season ends. Not now. It would be extremely hard for the Jets to move on from Sherwood until the 2027 offseason.
That said, his improved play does bring up interesting questions moving forward.
If he continues to play well, the Jets will want to move forward with him as their starting lead backer instead of an aging Davis. It will also call his contract into question. Sherwood being the 31st-best linebacker is nice. It's a solid ranking.
But is that an acceptable number for a player currently ranked as the 10th-highest-paid player at the position? No. Sherwood still needs to play better to be worthy of his current contract. If not, the Jets won't be able to justify another year of Sherwood under the current numbers.
So while Sherwood's play is important, there will need to be an even bigger jump going forward.

title: 3 Steps Jets Must Take to Fix Glaring Red-Zone Struggles Before It’s Too Late
full_text:
An inconsistent offensive flow has plagued the Jets this season, especially deep in enemy territory.
Heading into Week 7, the Jets rank last in red-zone scoring rate through games, clicking in at 37.5%. The Dolphins and Browns are tied for the next-worst market at 46.2%, show just how much worse Gang Green is in this department.
The Jets have been visibly better on offense than last season, but these struggles are holding them back from reaching their full potential. New York has 14 red-zone trips but only six touchdowns to show for it.
Head coach Aaron Glenn's team must fix these issues if it wants to be competitive for the rest of the year, and these three steps could help spark a turnaround.
The Jets have had four red-zone drives affected by a penalty this season. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich's offense has struggled with discipline in the red zone, settling for field goals instead of touchdowns. New York has almost as many red-zone penalties as touchdowns. That must change.
The offense gives itself chances to score but keeps stumbling at the last hurdle. Red-zone discipline needs to be a priority for the Jets. They aren't turning the ball over, but losing four points to penalties nearly 30% of the time is unacceptable.
The Jets need to clean up the penalties all over the field , but ones in the red zone have hurt them most. Penalties by the Jets allow bad teams to stay in the game and good teams to pull away. Gang Green has had the fifth most penalties in the league so far. The offense must bring those numbers down if the Jets are to fix the red-zone issues that have plagued them.
New York has one of the league's most talented receivers in Garrett Wilson. Wilson has only three targets in the Jets' 14 red-zone trips this season. New York's lack of usage of Wilson is mind-boggling compared to other top-tier receivers. The former 10th overall pick ranks 67th among the position in red-zone targets.
Compare this to other number-one receivers around the league. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 11 red-zone targets, Amon-Ra St. Brown has 16, CeeDee Lamb has 10, and even AJ Brown—who has played a game and a half—has reached Wilson's target total inside the 20. When a team pays a receiver over $100 million, it usually tries to make sure that receiver is part of the red-zone offense .
This isn't a situation where Wilson can't produce when the field shrinks. Wilson has shown throughout his career that he can make plays in the end zone, whether through a jump ball or his route running. Wilson's limited usage inside the 20 is holding New York back. The one time that Smith and Wilson connected in the red zone this year, it ended in six points.
Looking for the team's number-one receiver may be a good way to cut these red-zone struggles.
Smith has looked serviceable throughout the first six weeks of the season. The veteran quarterback has seven touchdowns, only one interception, and is averaging 7.5 yards per attempt. That has not translated to the red zone.
Geno Smith is 10-for-16 with 49 yards and just two touchdowns inside the 20. His yards per attempt is an abysmal 2.9 . It seems the coaching staff doesn't want Geno Smith to win games; they want him to not lose them. That hasn't worked; the Jets are two games below .500.
The Jets must let Smith make throws. When the defense has less field to cover, underneath routes lose their effect, as the defense can swarm to the ball. Reich must let his quarterback throw, even if it leads to mistakes. Football games are not won by kicking field goals; they are won by getting in the endzone. Smith must be allowed to be a part of the offense if the Jets want to fix their red-zone performance.
The bad news is New York has put up league-worst numbers inside the 20 this season. The good news is there are still 11 more games to be played. The Jets must fix discipline issues and let their best players be a part of the offense if they want to turn this season around.

title: 3 Realistic Riq Woolen Trade Destinations That Would Net Eagles Biggest Return
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is under three weeks away. In recent seasons, this is when general manager Howie Roseman would start searching for veterans to boost Philadelphia's roster in hopes of winning a Super Bowl. However, a disastrous first six weeks means he could be the one dealing talent away .
A four-game losing streak fueled by injuries has the Eagles facing an uphill battle to make the playoffs. Most notably, quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the rest of the season due to blood clots. That said, players across the roster could be floated in trade talks , especially those on expiring contracts.
Cornerback Riq Woolen, one of those expiring deals, was inked to a one-year, $12 million deal in March. The former Seahawk has been solid in coverage, surrendering 15 receptions for 187 yards (two touchdowns) in six games. He has allowed a 51.7% completion rate when targeted and racked up four pass breakups.
Here are three teams that would benefit from acquiring Woolen and have the ammunition to pull it off.
The Jaguars' need for help in the secondary became clear during their Week 6 loss to the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud zeroed in on cornerback Jarrian Jones, who conceded six catches for 100 yards. He has been a liability all year, ranking 100th out of 102 cornerbacks in PFF's coverage grade.
Jones has been on the field for nearly every defensive snap over the last three weeks due to Montaric Brown's hamstring injury. Solely banking on Brown returning to full health and stepping up in pass coverage alongside Travis Hunter would be unwise when an AFC South title is within reach.
Adding Woolen to the mix would give Jacksonville a veteran with the necessary closing speed to eliminate throwing lanes and swat away jump balls. The Jaguars are projected to have three fifth-round picks in 2027, which could be used to sweeten the pot on Woolen's expected trade value of a fourth-round pick.
Carolina's secondary has been bitten by the injury bug. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) have both landed on injured reserve. It's a duo that guided the Panthers' defense in 2025. Horn registered five interceptions, and Jackson led the NFL with a stellar 19 pass breakups.
However, it leaves the Panthers in desperate need of a cornerback. The group of Akayleb Evans, Will Lee III, and Chau-Smith Wade is inexperienced. Carolina defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero runs a similar scheme to that of Philadelphia's Vic Fangio. It utilizes zone coverage to keep the action in front of defenders.
It's a scheme that plays to Woolen's strengths. The former UTSA standout can use his 6'4" frame to disrupt route timing, while also reading the quarterback's eyes. Carolina has intriguing trade chips like wide receiver Xavier Legette and tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders that it can add to a late-round pick.
The Bills enter their bye week looking like a true AFC contender with a 5-1 record. A glaring weakness remains, though. Buffalo is allowing the second-most passing yards per game (285.8) and the eighth-most yards per completion (10.9). Opposing pass-catchers are constantly finding open space.
Cornerback Christian Benford has done his job. He lacks a reliable partner. Second-year pro Maxwell Hairston has posted a dismal 21.4% missed-tackle rate. Rookie Davison Igbinosun has tallied five pass breakups, but two early penalties in Buffalo's Week 6 game show he still has a way to go.
Woolen's covering skills on deep routes would come in handy when the Bills battle elite offenses. Buffalo general manager Brandon Beane has displayed aggressive trade techniques before, most recently trading out of the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft in three separate moves. He could offer a deal to Roseman that would be hard to refuse.

title: McMullen: Eagles' Are Playing Risky Game With Unsustainable Defensive Workload
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ defense was on the field for 79 snaps in Sunday’s 25-14 loss to the Panthers , marking the fifth time in six games this season that the unit has played 70 or more defensive snaps.⁠
That volume is consistently rising into Vic Fangio's third season as Philadelphia's defensive coordinator. In 2025, the Eagles reached 70-plus defensive snaps in six of 17 games. During the 2024 Super Bowl-winning campaign, that number was hit only three times all year.⁠
Through six games in 2026, the defense is averaging 71.7 reps per contest —the highest mark of the Nick Sirianni era and well above the 61.6 average from the Super Bowl season. Over the last four games, the figure has climbed even higher as the offense has struggled to sustain drives.⁠
The disparity was a little better against the Panthers: the Eagles’ offense managed  64 snaps while the defense faced 79. The time of possession was tilted heavily toward Carolina (34:48 to 25:12), consistent with a season-long pattern in which the Eagles’ offense has produced a league-high number of three-and-outs and often failed to manage the clock well.
In a complementary game, those short possessions leave Fangio’s group with little rest between series.⁠
Key defenders absorbed the bulk of the work against the Panthers. Linebacker Zack Baun and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell played all 79 snaps, while safety Drew Mukuba matched them. Cooper DeJean logged 78 snaps and Riq Woolen 77. Up front, Jalen Carter played 74 snaps (94 percent), and edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie played 72—both heavy loads given the rotation and injuries that limited others, including Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith, who exited early with a concussion after just 14 snaps.⁠
On Wednesday, Fangio addressed the cumulative toll of the repeated high snap counts when asked by Eagles On SI whether the volume could wear a defense down week after week. He rejected the idea of letting it become an emotional burden.
“No, you can’t let it emotionally,” Fangio said. “We tell [the players] very early in training camp, we have no control how we get on the field. We control how we get off the field, and that’s where our mindset is.”
The comment reflects a consistent message from Fangio and his staff.
The control what you can control mindset. Players are expected to focus solely on the snaps they can influence—getting stops and forcing the offense back onto the field—rather than dwelling on the circumstances created by the other side of the ball.
Earlier in the season, after a high-snap outing against the Rams that included a late collapse, Fangio acknowledged that extreme volume “has an effect” while still insisting the unit must find ways to finish games.
The current pattern raises practical questions about sustainability moving forward, especially with the unproven Tanner McKee subbing in for Jalen Hurts , who is likely done for the season with blood clots in both lungs.
While Fangio’s group has shown resilience in stretches, the combination of frequent three-and-outs on offense and late-game defensive lapses has contributed to a four-game losing streak . Fourth-quarter points allowed have been a recurring problem, with a sizable share of the season’s total points surrendered coming after intermission.
Complementary football remains the stated ideal. When the offense cannot stay on the field, the defense inherits longer periods of work and fewer opportunities for rest or rotation.
Fangio’s emphasis on mindset and controllable factors is admirable and obviously designed to keep the unit from fracturing under those conditions, but the sheer volume of snaps through the first six weeks is not the formula for winning football.

title: One Thought on Every Eagles Rookie Six Games Into the Season
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are in the midst of a disastrous four-game losing streak. Injuries have been piling up, with star players like quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley missing action. The next-man-up mentality that comes with playing in the NFL is certainly being put to work.
The roster depth general manager Howie Roseman has built through the NFL Draft is being tested on a weekly basis. There are opportunities for young rookies to take over starting roles, much like linebacker Jihaad Campbell and safety Andrew Mukuba did last year. It's all about taking advantage.
With that being said, here's a thought on every Eagles rookie through six weeks of action.
Makai Lemon has tallied 127 yards on 18 receptions through six games. It's a lackluster result that is shaped by Philly's complete lack of offensive rhythm. There have been multiple instances where Lemon has caught the ball behind the line of scrimmage and has been immediately met by an unblocked defender.
Lemon excelled at running sharp routes to create separation and racking up yards after the catch at USC. Those talents are being wasted with vertical routes and bubble screens. The Eagles battle poor pass defenses in the next few weeks. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has to make adjustments .
If Philly can scheme Lemon open in the middle of the field, he can make opposing defenses look silly.
An early first down for the Eagles goes to Makai Lemon! #NFL pic.twitter.com/LkmEYfmGnn
Roseman turned heads when he drafted Eli Stowers in the second round back in April. It was the first time he selected a tight end in the first two rounds since Dallas Goedert in 2018. Unfortunately, Stowers suffered hamstring and quadriceps injuries that landed him on injured reserve before Week 1.
The good news is that Stowers is making strides. The 2025 John Mackey Award winner returned to practice on Oct. 14. Stowers was praised for his pass-catching versatility and pure athleticism coming out of college. Inserting him into a retooled offense would give McKee a tantalizing weapon.
The abrupt retirement of All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson caught everyone off guard. It was news that opened the door for Markel Bell to start . The third-round pick has wasted no time flashing his strength as a run-blocker, pancaking defenders and crushing linebackers at the second level.
There are improvements to be made in Bell's pass protection. Miscommunications with his fellow linemen have led to costly sacks. Of course, that can be fixed with experience. It's not fair to expect Bell to be Johnson 2.0. A steady right tackle would go a long way in Philly's hopes of righting the ship.
Cole Payton served as the No. 4 quarterback on the depth chart throughout training camp. The former North Dakota State standout has now slid into the backup quarterback role , following the departure of veteran signal-caller Andy Dalton and the devastating injury update on Jalen Hurts.
That means Payton is one Tanner McKee injury away from taking command of the offense.
Sirianni has backed up Payton's development, explaining how the 23-year-old gets reps on the scout team and works hard with the coaches after practice. Momentum is not on Philly's side right now. If the playoffs become out of reach during the final few weeks, Peyton could draw a start or two.
You don't have to dig deep to find Micah Morris' stats. The 6'5", 334-pound lineman out of Georgia has played one snap for the Eagles, and it came on special teams against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Despite multiple injuries along the offensive line, Morris remains buried on the depth chart.
Wisniewski spent the first five weeks of the regular season on the Eagles' practice squad. The seventh-round pick out of Texas Tech was elevated before Week 6's game against Carolina, playing  15 snaps on special teams. Wisniewski logged one tackle and showcased that he has the skills to be reliable in kickoff coverage. There are no expectations that he'll earn defensive snaps anytime soon.
Keyshawn James-Newby was another practice squad call-up for the Eagles in Week 6. No one expected him to play 61% of the defensive snaps, though (48). The absence of Jalyx Hunt and a concussion suffered by Nolan Smith Jr. forced defensive coordinator Vic Fangio to rely on the rookie.
James-Newby held his own, posting one tackle and two pressures (19 pass-rush snaps). He led the Mountain West Conference with 9.0 sacks in 2025 and has the potential to improve under defensive line coach Clint Hurtt. Expect James-Newby to see more action in Week 7 as Philly navigates injuries.

title: No Room for a Franchise Legend? Zach Ertz's Future With the Eagles Is Officially Cloudy
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. —  Zach Ertz remains with the Eagles , but his path to game action is now unclear after exhausting his practice squad elevations.
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni addressed the veteran tight end’s status Thursday before practice, offering measured praise without committing to a potential 53-man roster spot.
“Zach’s obviously still here. He’s out of elevations at this particular time,” the head coach said. “I think Zach’s been having really good practices. There’s things that you can’t predict, but I love having Zach on this football team, and we’ll see as the season progresses.”
Ertz, a longtime Eagles staple who returned on a practice squad deal in late September amid injuries and ineffectiveness at the tight end position, quickly used up his three standard elevations. He caught three passes for 22 yards in the three games he was active for the Eagles.
With no more elevations available, the only way Ertz suits up again is if Philadelphia signs him to the 53-man roster.
That decision is complicated by other tight ends getting healthier, injuries elsewhere and Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement (which has kept a roster spot occupied for salary-cap reasons).
Openings on the 53 are scarce and getting cloudier now that the 21-day practice windows have been opened for TEs Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers, who both remain on injured reserve but should be ahead of Ertz in the pecking order, the former being valued as an immediate contributor by the coaching staff and the latter buoyed by his status of being the 54th overall pick in April's draft.
The Eagles’ current trio is Goedert, the one plus-level player at the position, blocker Johnny Mundt and No. 3 E.J. Jenkins, who makes a big contribution on special teams but is expected to be released on Thursday , per NFL insider Mike Garafolo.
The options are straightforward enough: promote Ertz to the active roster, keep the franchise icon on the practice squad without the ability to elevate him for games, or eventually move on.
The calculus could change as well with another tight end injury or a trade involving Goedert, who is on an expiring contract and could add value for a contender if things continue to go south for the Eagles.
Ertz, a three-time Pro Bowl selection and Super Bowl LII hero during his first stint with the Eagles, which ran from 2013 through the midway point of the 2021 season, needs seven more receptions to match the franchise’s record of 589, held by Hall of Famer Harold Carmichael.
“When he’s been in with the ones, he’s had great reps, and when he’s been in with the scout team, he’s given our defense great looks, phenomenal looks,” Sirianni said of Ertz.

title: No Disappearing Act: Jalen Hurts Can Still Help the Eagles' QB Room Even From IR
full_text:
It may have been easy to miss or to gloss over this sentence: “He will remain active around the team.”
‘He’ is Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. That line was deep into the third paragraph of a four- paragraph release earlier in the week by Hurts’ agent , Nicole Lynn. Now, we are more aware of what those seven words mean.
Hurts is going to serve as a resource in the quarterback room, perhaps even for the entire offense, but especially for Tanner McKee, who is expected to serve as the starter while Hurts is on injured reserve, being treated with blood thinners to treat blood clots that have settled in both lungs.
“Obviously, we just want (Jalen) to get healthy and just care for the guy and the work that he puts into our team each and every week,” offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said. “Certainly, want him to continue to be around and be a positive impact for us while he's getting himself healthy. That's the ultimate priority. He was around last week, and I know he's tackling the health stuff he's got going on, but he'll still be a big positive impact anytime he's around the team.”
The Eagles have a string of three straight games against their NFC East rivals , beginning Monday night at home against the Cowboys. That will be followed by a road game at the Commanders on Sunday Night Football and then a visit from the Giants, which is the last game before the Eagles’ bye week and just two days before the NFL’s trade deadline .
Hurts’s knowledge of those opponents should be a big benefit for McKee and the other two quarterbacks in the room—rookie Cole Payton and Joe Milton, a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024, who has played in just five games without any career starts .
Mannion made it clear what kind of impact Hurts could have on McKee moving forward.
“Jalen's been through the fire of the regular season, and Tanner, I think it was his third start last week,” Mannion said. “I think just any veteran quarterback, because that's what Jalen is, there's always going to be insight in terms of, 'Hey, this is how the preparation for a Monday night game week can look. This is how you can use your extra time. Hey, we played Dallas last year. These were the things I felt in my preparation there. These are some of my old notes.'"
There is also the insight Hurts can provide on just about anything because he is a veteran quarterback with 97 career starts, including playoffs.
“There's so much insight to be gained from a quarterback with Jalen's experience," Mannion said. "I know Tanner, Cole, and adding Joe to the mix, these guys all work really, really well with one another in that QB room. That makes it fun to be around on a day-to-day basis. It's just the game experience and the insight of playing specifically these upcoming opponents. I think Jalen will be able to give Tanner some great help there.”
Monday night will be McKee’s fourth start in his three-plus years with the team. He played last week despite not getting starter’s reps in practice until Thursday—just three days before the game against the Panthers.
He attempted 45 passes in a game plan that was way off balance, with only 12 called running plays. McKee was sacked three times.
“I think having the full slate of reps will help (Tanner) grow more and more comfortable going into each week," Mannion said. "He's done everything he can to get as close as he can be, but that will help moving forward. It'll be different this week that way.”

title: Saquon Barkley's Expected Return Could Expedite Eagles QB Change
full_text:
A three-game NFC East gauntlet starts in Week 7 when the Eagles host the Cowboys for a Monday Night Football clash at Lincoln Financial Field. By now, Eagles fans are well aware that star quarterback Jalen Hurts won't be suiting up this week ( or possibly again this season ) due to a blood clot issue, but that doesn't mean all hope is lost—especially with Saquon Barkley's return reportedly on the horizon.
After missing the last two losses due to a hamstring injury, " Barkley is expected to return to practice (Thursday) ," according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo. Even though that doesn't confirm a Week 7 return, the fact that Philadelphia's No. 1 running back is back at practice is good news for his availability on Monday.
#Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is expected to return to practice today and is in line to play Monday against the #Cowboys , sources say. A lift for the team’s offense with a banged-up backfield and Jalen Hurts on the mend. pic.twitter.com/pRpndoEPcQ
Barkley's return alone won't turn the Eagles around, but his presence is important both in terms of remaining in the playoff hunt, as well as what happens next at the QB position.
With Barkley potentially returning to the backfield, all eyes will be on de facto QB1 Tanner McKee to have a better performance than he did against the Panthers last week.
Although he was far from horrible, throwing for 215 yards, one touchdown and a 77.5 passer rating on  26-of-45 (57.8%) passing attempts isn't much to write home about. It also doesn't exactly scream, "McKee can get the Eagles into the playoffs." He also didn't do anything on the ground, and while no one expected him to be as impactful as Hurts, McKee's lack of mobility and how that impacts the offensive flow can't be ignored.
That's why getting Barkley back is important.
The three-time Pro Bowl RB isn't having his best season and hasn't found the end zone yet, but he's averaging 5.1 yards per carry (up from 4.1 in 2025) and already has two 80-yard performances in four appearances. He'll keep the Cowboys' defensive line—which allows 149.8 rushing yards per game (32nd) and 4.7 yards per carry (26th)—honest, which should also open up passing opportunities.
Failure to beat the pitiful Cowboys defense could force the Eagles to end the McKee experiment, as they'd need to feel confident heading into must-win games against the Commanders and Giants. If that's the case, Joe Milton would be the next man up in head coach Nick Sirianni's lineup.
It's been less than a week since the Eagles signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad, and it might not be long before they put their shiny new toy to the test if McKee crumbles under the pressure.
After all, Milton's mobility alone creates intrigue to see what he could do as Hurts's replacement. He wasn't afraid to use his legs back in college, rushing for 661 yards and 12 touchdowns—including seven TDs in his last year—on 174 carries during his time at Tennessee and Michigan. He hasn't made an NFL start yet, but Milton's legs were on display in relief appearances with the Patriots and Cowboys, turning 15 carries into 66 rushing yards and a touchdown.
Like McKee, Milton is an upcoming restricted free agent, so the Eagles will want to see how both QBs can do in high-pressure situations before committing to their future . McKee had a chance last week and will get another against the Cowboys, but if he can't handle the heat, it's a no-brainer decision to see whether Milton can keep the Eagles' playoff hopes alive against the Commanders and Giants before the Week 10 bye.
Whether it's McKee or Milton, one of the young signal-callers will hopefully emerge as a reliable arm to get the Eagles through the rest of the season. Otherwise, the stretch between now and January will be a slog to navigate, adding to the already murky outlook surrounding Philadelphia's quarterback room.

title: Sean Mannion Doubles Down on Offensive Approach Despite Sirianni's 'Everything is on the Table' Comment
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion made clear Wednesday that he remains fully convinced in the process guiding his unit, even as the offense continues searching for the results it desires.
“I feel convicted in the process by which we’ve been doing things,” Mannion said at his weekly press conference. “I feel convicted in the things that we make a point of emphasis with our guys in terms of what we’re doing fundamentally and with our play style, with our schematic, you know, what we’re doing schematically.”
The Eagles have not produced the output they want through the early portion of the season. Mannion acknowledged as much, noting that the staff is attacking the issues daily and claimed that many of the problems sit within the team’s control.
The young coach pointed to fundamentals, execution, and communication as the core areas that must improve so the offense can operate at the level expected.
“A lot of it comes down to fundamentals, execution, communication, and for us as a staff to always look to put our guys in the best position possible,” he said. “We gotta get better there. We’re attacking it each day.”
Mannion described the situation as a double-edged sword. The shortcomings are frustrating because so much of what is holding the group back is fixable, yet that same reality offers a path forward.
“If we just handle our simple, simple stuff, we’re gonna yield a better result,” the OC insisted. “If we just master our own stuff, I think it’ll make compounding improvements across our offense.”
Mannion remains a believer in the under-center elements of the scheme despite poor results to date, albeit while stressing weekly flexibility.
“I do still feel good about it. Obviously, things to clean up, but I think in terms of the schematic, what it is schematically, I’m still a believer in it,” Mannion said. “Every week you may approach things differently based on the opponent, based on your own personnel, based on your own tendencies that you may be trying to break.”
With Tanner McKee now established as the starter going forward in the wake of Jalen Hurts' likely season-ending blood clots, Mannion highlighted the unproven quarterback’s growth and skill set.
Mannion described McKee as sharp mentally, accurate, and able to get the ball out quickly while handling pre-snap operation and line-of-scrimmage adjustments.
“He’s been getting better and better,” Mannion said. “I think he’s really sharp mentally. He’s accurate. He gets the ball out of his hands quickly. … I think he’s strong in a lot of those areas, and I think it opens up some things for us offensively.”
A full week of practice reps, Mannion added, should help McKee continue to settle in, something that was limited the previous week. The coordinator also noted that practice effort and attention to detail have been strong; the challenge is translating that to the game field.
On the broader approach of Nick Sirianni saying “everything is on the table” to help the offense , Mannion said the staff’s mindset of studying opponents, examining league trends, and bringing fresh ideas has been consistent all year.
“That mindset really, it’s not a departure from anything we’ve been doing throughout the year,” said Mannion. “We’re always looking to do everything we can each and every week to give ourselves the best chance to go out there and execute better.”
Asked whether he feels supported by Sirianni and the organization as the offense works through its issues, Mannion was direct.
“Absolutely. Absolutely,” he said. “Nick’s support, Nick’s help, his advice … just the collaborative effort between Nick and [GM] Howie [Roseman] and everybody in the building. Everyone’s pulling in the same direction here. I’ve felt that since day one, and I still feel it today.”

title: Has Jalen Hurts Played His Final Game with Eagles?
full_text:
No quarterback in Philadelphia Eagles history has won quite like Jalen Hurts. The former second-round pick has led the team to the playoffs in each full season as a starter and is the only quarterback in team history to reach two Super Bowls.
But just as the era of Donovan McNabb, Randall Cunningham and Ron Jaworski ended, eventually the team will look to life beyond what Hurts can bring to the table.
Has that process sped up with Hurts done for the year with a blood clot? Philadelphia was 2-3 before Hurts was lost for the season, but now his absence calls into question a much bigger issue.
With the quarterback in need of a new contract, and the team in the midst of a potential retool, questions will begin on whether Hurts has played his final down with the organization. Unlike what many radio hosts and hot-take enthusiasts would push, there is no reason for the team to be at this point.
There's no denying the Eagles are entering a crossroads with Hurts. He hasn't shown the ability to become an elite passer like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, but he doesn't turn the ball over, and he finds ways to win games even when things aren't going his way. There is a reason why he has been well worth the $50 million per year spent on him over his first extension.
The big question regarding Hurts' contract, though, is that his guaranteed money decreases to just $22 million in 2027. He won't have any guaranteed money coming in 2028. That said, he does carry a massive cap hit of $42 million next year.
The issue, though, is what happens if the Eagles try to move on from him before the 2027 season ends. Hurts will be owed $67 million in dead cap should the team move on from him before June 1 this offseason. That is double what the team paid Carson Wentz in dead money back in 2021. The number is $42 million if they wait for after June 1.
The reality of the situation is Hurts' contract does not leave for much of a departure this offseason.
2028 is a different story, though. And that is where the questions start.
If the Eagles were to acquire Justin Herbert or any other veteran quarterback in a trade, would they remain a Super Bowl contender? It's easy to say that would be the case, but strong arms and athletic profiles do not win football games.
There's a reason why the Chargers are 0-6 even with Herbert on the field. Even elite quarterbacks cannot make up when a team is devoid of something important on the field.
Even if the team were to bring in a quarterback from the upcoming rookie class , there would be no guarantee that he found the same success as Hurts. Therein lies the difficult situation befalling the Eagles. They have a quarterback who may not be able to stand toe-to-toe with some of the elite players in the game, and with a new contract could cripple the hopes of the organization getting back to an elite roster, but enjoy the reality of having success no other quarterback has seen.
It's not an easy answer for any Eagles executive. But with a large dead cap charge, and the belief he will be 100% following his blood clot, there's no reason to move on from Hurts just yet.
At the very least, he's earned the right to prove he can keep the ship afloat.

title: 3 Potential Hollywood Brown Trade Destinations as Eagles Debate Deadline Sale
full_text:
When the Philadelphia Eagles first signed Hollywood Brown, there was hope his experience would help a reshapen receiving core with the departure of AJ Brown.
Instead, "Hollywood" has seldom played, and has been a healthy scratch over the last several weeks.
As the Eagles continue to struggle this season , many of their current veterans could end up being shipped off in potential trades. Brown, having not played for several weeks, seems to be one of those veterans.
And three teams seems like fair trade partners.
Admittedly, the Steelers weren't going to be considered much of a fit for Brown before the season began. Then Michael Pittman went down with a foot injury and the Steelers are now back needing help at the receiver position.
Pittsburgh is a half game out of the AFC North lead and any sort of help it can get on the outside would be huge as it tires to get one more title run out of Aaron Rodgers.
It won't be easy, and Brown would have to get quick chemistry with the likes of the former NFL MVP, but if Pittsburgh is desperate enough to add receiver talent, then the Eagles and Brown seem like a fair pairing.
Much has been made about the Chiefs and running back Kenneth Walker's historic season thus far. One issue that the Chiefs are having, though, is in their passing game. They lack a deep threat as Patrick Mahomes gets 100% healthy from the ACL injury he suffered last year.
With the Chiefs, Brown wasn't too overly special. He suffered injuries in 2024 and was not very effective in 2025. That said, Kansas City is undefeated and could use any and all weapons available to them.
That's what makes Brown an intriguing idea. He could provide the team with a necessary veteran needed for the room as they try and get back to the Super Bowl.
The Raiders have played a lot better football than anyone really expected at this point of the season. Their defense is significantly better than last year, and Kirk Cousins has the offense competing against some of the top units in the league. Everything seems to be on schedule for this rebuild.
That said, they could always use some more talent at wide receiver.
Brown may not be the same player he once was, but he is a former 1,000-yard receiver and that could be huge for a Raiders offense whose best receiver this year is Tre Tucker. This seems like a logical fit for a team expecting to compete by the end of the year.

title: Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Eagles' Playoff Outlook After Loss to Panthers
full_text:
With six weeks of action in the books, we are officially a third of the way through the 2026 NFL season. For the Philadelphia Eagles, the season hasn't gone at all as they expected or hoped. The Eagles sit at 2-4 after six games, and even worse than their record is the fact that they will be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the campaign due to blood clots .
Understandably, morale is pretty low among the fan base at this point in time. But there's still a lot of football left this season, and thanks to the NFC East, the Eagles are still technically well inside the playoff picture. So, all hope isn't lost. With two-thirds of the season still ahead, now seems like a good time for a confidence check, so let's give it a go.
Eagles fans won't have a hard time finding reasons for pessimism at this point in the season, starting with the absence of Hurts, who led the team to a Super Bowl victory two seasons ago. Hurts' entire tenure with the Eagles has been defined by success. Over his first five years as a starter for Philly, Hurts led the Eagles to five consecutive playoff berths, two Super Bowl appearances, and one victory in the Big Game.
While people like to downplay Hurts' stats, Philadelphia's recent run of success would have been impossible without Hurts' poise and penchant for making big plays in big moments. Just look at both of his Super Bowl performances, when he was the best player on the field in both games. We don't really know what the Eagles look like without Hurts for an extended period. If Tanner McKee's Week 6 performance against the Carolina Panthers is any indication, it's not great.
Philadelphia's injury issues aren't limited to Hurts, either. It feels like virtually every key contributor on offense for the Eagles is dealing with some sort of injury, and the defense is decently banged up too.
Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert have all missed time this season, and the offensive line looks completely different from what it did at the start of the season due to a combination of injuries, trades, and Lane Johnson's retirement. Hopefully the Eagles can get the bulk of their key cogs back on the field in the coming weeks, but even that might not be enough to overcome an uninspired offensive approach.
Sean Mannion's first six games as the Eagles' offensive coordinator have left a lot to be desired, and there's reason to doubt it will improve, especially without Hurts. We're seeing a lot of the same issues under Mannion that we saw last season, including a lack of creativity and an inability to create easy opportunities for the offense. After six games, the Eagles sit 30th in total yards per game (255.5), 29th in rushing yards per game (82.2), 25th in passing yards per game (173.3), and 28th in points per game (17.7).
Despite the offense's struggles, Nick Sirianni made it clear that the Eagles don't plan to relieve Mannion of his play-calling duties.
“I’ll do everything we can do, our coaches will do everything we can do to help us win football games,” Sirianni said ( h/t Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia ). “. . . But as far as who’s coaching the positions and who’s calling the plays, that will remain the same. We’re looking for answers and we’re looking for solutions.”
It's usually not a great sign when a head coach has to answer questions about his coordinator's job security six weeks into a season.
While they're harder to identify, there are still a few reasons for optimism when it comes to the Eagles' postseason outlook, with the main one being that they play in the NFC East, which might be the worst division in football this year.
No team in the division has won a game since Week 4, and the losses have kept the Eagles' hopes alive, statistically at least. The Eagles still have five games against division opponents this season, starting with a matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7. How they fare in those games could go a long way towards determining who wins the division and gets the guaranteed playoff spot that comes with it.
Plus, you have to hope the injury bug that has plagued the Eagles all season will begin to die down at some point. Smith returned to game action last week, while Barkley could be back sometime in the near future, too. Plus, reinforcements could be coming on the offensive line with the looming returns of Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall.
Having all of those guys back should make things easier for Mannion, McKee, and the rest of the offense. Philadelphia's defense has been largely good enough to keep the team in games. If they could get some help from the other side, perhaps the Eagles could pull out some wins and remain in the postseason conversation. With that said, a sixth consecutive playoff berth for the Birds still feels extremely unlikely.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Wanted a Few Extra Days in Paris
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers arrived in Paris, France, with just 48 hours before kickoff in Week 7 against the New Orleans Saints.
Just like last year against the Minnesota Vikings in Dublin, Ireland, the Steelers traveled overnight on Thursday, landing Friday morning in Paris and planning to go straight to work. This year, they decided to cancel practice due to inclement weather, refocusing their plan as they finalize preparation for the Saints on Sunday.
The plan is one the team came up with months ago and will likely stick with moving forward for international trips as well. Meanwhile, the Saints flew over to Paris on Monday, giving themselves the entire week to prepare and acclimate themselves to the changes.
Something quarterback Aaron Rodgers would've liked to experience just once throughout his career.
Speaking with the media over in France, Rodgers didn't have much to say about the safety concerns due to the protests happening in Paris, but did open up about wanting to come over a little earlier in the week.
"I played in three countries now, and each of them we've left on Thursday early evening. Would have been nice one time to come over on a Monday," Rodgers said.
He had a similar sentiment last year when addressing the travel to Dublin. With the team's 2025 win over the Vikings, though, they were bound to stick to a formula that worked for them.
As for the concerns from fans over the protests and unrest happening in the country, Rodgers is putting his faith in the NFL. Something all of the Steelers' players and staff have reiterated throughout the week.
"I definitely think that the NFL is alert to what's going on. This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I'm sure we wouldn't be here," Rodgers said.
Aaron Rodgers on safety concerns in Paris amid the ongoing demonstrations: “I definitely think that the NFL is alert to what's going on. This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I'm sure we wouldn't be here.” pic.twitter.com/leCjXeE0Xv
As for the Steelers' plans this weekend, they'll likely give the players a chance to explore the city, but in groups. Last year, players were able to utilize most of Friday night and Saturday afternoon to explore the city of Dublin. Some, like star wide receiver DK Metcalf, chose to stay back and view it as a business trip.
DK Metcalf, asked if there was a country he would like to play a next international game at: “No, sir, because I really don’t like traveling outside the U.S. to play football.”
Rodgers has 12 touchdowns to five interceptions this season and has been the focal point of the offense for most of the season . Last week, he threw the ball 49 times for 253 yards and two touchdowns in the team's comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
While exploring Paris might be on his agenda, winning a game will top the list. And the Steelers are going to need him to move to 5-2 on the season before returning to the States and hosting the Cleveland Browns.

title: Steelers Cancel Paris Practice Due to Weather
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers will not practice Friday in Paris, France , before taking on the New Orleans Saints in Week 7. The team has canceled their scheduled practice due to inclement weather, leaving their Saturday walk-through as their only workout in the country prior to kickoff.
The Steelers traveled overnight and landed in Paris with the expectation of going straight from the plane to the hotel, where they would receive bodywork and treatment. Then, they would host a 30-minute practice.
"We had two plans coming in," McCarthy told reporters in Paris. "Just really wanted to acclimate the players after the long flight, just based off the communication with the weather and the reality of the timing too. We had to make the decision before we landed just to put it together. But frankly, driving by, I wish we would've stopped. But this is part of our plan."
Mike McCarthy says he had to cancel today’s practice in advance because of a significant wind storm. But once they landed and passed the stadium he wishes they had gone thru with it. It is not raining at the moment in Paris.  But it is very windy. pic.twitter.com/sCU2BaM15X
While it was not raining in Paris during the time of interviews, there was a wind storm happening.
The team's PR staff sent out a memo upon arrival that the team was canceling their practice at Stade de France and instead headed straight for the hotel, where they would do their media availability.
The Saints have been in town throughout the week, getting acclimated and practicing in the country before the game. The Steelers held practices in Pittsburgh on Wednesday and Thursday, and typically have one more on Saturday before game day.
While the weather may have disrupted the team's plans this time around, the Steelers were successful in traveling in the same fashion last year to Dublin, Ireland. They flew overnight on Thursday and landed Friday morning, going straight to practice.
They defeated the Minnesota Vikings in that game.
"Just like anything, when the schedule comes out we’re on a 7-day week flow here," McCarthy said earlier in the week about the team's travel plans. "Played yesterday in Tampa, had to travel back, so that factors into it... Whether you’re playing in the Super Bowl or you're playing in a Monday night game, you look at all of those things and the reality of it is I've always tried to stick to the basics. The hydration, the sleep, just to give the men the best opportunity to prepare and perform while staying in the normal flow of operation as possible."
Pittsburgh will take on New Orleans on Sunday with a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff time.
