title: Steelers Rule Out Two Players Early Against Saints
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have already ruled out two players for their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints.
Before flying over to Paris, the Steelers released their second injury report of the week and revealed that both cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) will be inactive when the teams hits the field at the Stade de France vs. New Orleans.
Echols and Skowronek have each been non-participants in practice this week, which foreshadowed their eventual absences against the Saints.
Echols suffered his injury on a Steelers punt return with under two minutes left in the first half of the team's Week 6 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and was later ruled out for the remainder of the contest.
The 28-year-old had previously been in the concussion protocol following Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals, though he was cleared in time to suit up on a short week for a Thursday Night Football bout with the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 and had been active from that point forward until suffering his hamstring injury.
Skowronek, meanwhile, sustained his injury in the first half of Pittsburgh's win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 and did not play vs. Tampa Bay.
With Echols out, the Steelers are going to have to count on Sean Murphy-Bunting and/or Terell Smith against the Saints.
Neither Murphy-Bunting or Smith has seen the field since signing to the team's 53-man roster from the practice squads of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Washington Commanders, respectively, ahead of Week 5.
Now, though, at least one of them will likely be active and potentially see the field, albeit in a limited role, this week unless Pittsburgh signs Doneiko Slaughter to its 53-man roster.
At receiver, DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard will handle just about the entire workload with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on IR while Skowronek misses a second-straight game.
Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson could very well be elevated from the practice squad once again, though Marquez Valdes-Scantling may get the nod too despite returning to the Steelers just a matter of days ago .
Then, on the interior of the defensive line, Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) was placed on IR before Pittsburgh left for Paris. With Derrick Harmon (foot) having been on IR after suffering his injury in Week 4, the Steelers are short at that position as well and will need sixth-round Gabriel Rubio to continue stepping up while potentially having undrafted rooke Kevin Jobity Jr. active for the first time this season too.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: T.J. Watt Pops Up on Steelers Injury Report Before Paris Trip
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are one of the most injured teams in the NFL currently, and their bad luck continues.
As the Steelers prepare to board their flight for Paris, France , the team got one final practice in before departing from Pittsburgh. Already down several key players, the Steelers cannot afford to lose another impact player.
Which made superstar edge rusher T.J. Watt’s sudden appearance on the Injury Report quite the concerning update. The top-paid defender missed a previous practice due to rest, but the latest report from the organization classified him as a limited participant due to a calf injury. The team did not include any type of game designation for Watt, although they did rule out wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols for their Week 7 matchup a day early.
Watt was seen in the locker room after practice and did not seem to be in any discomfort, but popping up on the injury report during the week with a limited role usually means whatever did happened happened during practice. That could mean discomfort or something else.
The Steelers also placed defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day on the Reserved/Injured List.
This is now the second star edge rusher to appear on the injury report this week. The team’s other starter , Alex Highsmith , popped up on the Injury Report with a groin injury. The injury reduced him to a limited participant in practice ahead of their international contest.
Now, Watt is working through his own ailment. It’s good news that the organization hasn’t ruled him out, but how healthy he is entering Week 7 is under serious question.
This update could push Nick Herbig into even more snaps against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7. Herbig was already in line for more playing time due to Highsmith’s groin issue, and now that will be compounded by the team managing Watt’s new injury.
Herbig had an excellent Week 6, which came at the perfect time for him and the defense. After posting 2.0 sacks against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Steelers will be counting on him to be an impact player once again in Week 7.
The Steelers are keeping their fingers crossed when it comes to this update. The defense has put up with multiple injuries already and various degrees of underachievement.
At outside linebacker, they’ve had someone playing well each week. Even if Watt was held off the stat sheet, Highsmith had an explosive performance. Last week, Herbig gave them that spark on the edge.
The key to that is options and a rotation. Balancing all three of their premier pass rushers has helped this team reach a 4-2 record, and they need it in place to keep stacking wins.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Christian Kuntz Reveals What NFL is Telling Steelers About Paris
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are ready to take to the sky as the New Orleans Saints await them in Paris, France. The team tries to secure their third consecutive victory in an effort to keep pace with the rest of the AFC North division.
This game comes with just a bit more than bragging rights between the Steelers and Saints. The NFL’s travels to France come at a time when a series of protests have erupted in the country. That’s led to some questioning whether or not the teams should go through with the game at all.
But according to the team’s long snapper, Christian Kuntz, the organization has been reassured by the league that the conditions are being monitored and precautionary measures have been put in place for the players' and their families’ safety. Speaking on his show, The Christian Kuntz Podcast, he shared details about the team’s recent meeting with league officials.
"We had an NFL security meeting. Which, I'm sure every team when you travel overseas, you have a meeting," he said. "Basically, they told us that, 'Yeah, there's riots going on. This is why they're rioting. It's not a threat in our area. We have tripled the security now. Everything's gonna be fine. Your families are gonna be safe.' So, they've advised us that it's gonna be safe."
This topic of safety in Paris has been broached several times, by players and coaching staff alike. In his recent press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy was asked and shared his thoughts on the situation, and Kuntz's response certainly echoes the sentiment.
"I'm obviously very aware," he said when asked about the political unrest in France. "We have a lot of confidence in our plan."
The league has maintained the same messaging. They've added a heightened security presence, as Kuntz noted, and the NFL is committed to making this happen without a hitch.
As all of this continues to swirl around, eventually the game has to be played. The concerns and safety questions will go away and the football contest will commence. What happens then?
The Steelers are hoping that all of the outside noise fades away and both sides can focus on football. It's not totally within their control, as so much happens outside of the stadium they will be playing in, but the NFL is hell-bent on getting this game played on their terms.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Place Another Veteran Defender on IR
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have placed another interior defensive lineman on the reserve/injured list.
Before heading to Paris for their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, the Steelers announced that Sebastian Joseph-Day has landed on IR.
Joseph-Day was listed as a non-participant on the first injury report of the week with a triceps injury, and now he'll be forced to miss at least four games while he's on the mend.
As a result, the earliest Joseph-Day will be eligible to play for Pittsburgh is in Week 12 against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
An eight-year NFL veteran out of Rutgers who won Super Bowl LVI with the Los Angeles Rams in 2021 alongside Jalen Ramsey , Joseph-Day signed a two-year deal worth $11 million with the Steelers this past offseason.
He had appeared in all six of the team's regular season games up to this point. Over that stretch, Joseph-Day recorded 10 tackles and a fumble recovery while playing 111 defensive snaps, which comes out to 29 percent of Pittsburgh's total defensive reps.
With Derrick Harmon already on IR due to a foot injury he suffered in Week 4 , the Steelers are now down two key pieces along their defensive line.
With Harmon out the past two weeks, sixth-round pick Gabriel Rubio has been active and played a total of 27 defensive snaps over that span.
Keeanu Benton has seen a leap in his playing time too, eclipsing the 40-snap mark in each of the past three games after Harmon went down during the first half vs. the Cleveland Browns in Week 4.
The same can be said for Cameron Heyward, who has been on the field for a total of 138 snaps on defense from Weeks 4 through 6 after that number sat at 110 from Weeks 1 through 3.
With Joseph-Day now out for at least the next four games while Harmon will have to miss a minimum of two more, however, there's a bit of a hole along the interior of the defensive line for Pittsburgh for the time being.
Heyward and Benton will continue to bear the brunt of that workload while Yahya Black and Rubio play sizable roles next to them, particularly in run situations.
The Steelers will need another player to step up at the position, though, whether that's undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr., who has been inactive all season up to this point while residing on the 53-man roster, or someone who is brought up from the practice squad, such as Esezi Otomewo or even Kyler Baugh.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers NT Yahya Black Reveals Actual Weight, And It's Shocking
full_text:
You'd be hard-pressed to find an NFL player bigger than Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Yahya Black.
During Week 6, Black's conversation with Tampa Bay Buccaneers All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs, both of whom played at Iowa, was caught since the latter was mic'd up for NFL Films .
Black first asked Wirfs, "What they got you weighing at?" to which he responded 340 pounds. Wirfs turned around and asked the same question to Black, who stated that he is 370 pounds.
Wirfs told him that he looks "like an absolute unit," and was later shown telling a story about Black from when he went back to train at Iowa after his rookie season, which would've been in 2021.
"When I went back to train after my rookie year, he was like a freshman or something," Wirfs said. "He was not that big... He's like, doubled in size."
"You look huge." "Thank you." Linemen banter is the best. 😂 @insidetheNFL Week 6 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/9fTdAHKSxZ
On his 247 Sports player page from when he was a four-star high school recruit in the class of 2020, Black was listed as being 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds by the platform.
Then, Iowa listed him at 6-foot-5 and 317 pounds on their official website during his senior season back in 2024.
Black went on to weigh in at 336 pounds at the NFL Scouting Combine in 2025, and Pittsburgh currently has him listed at 330 pounds on its official roster .
It's clear that number is incorrect, however, and the former fifth-round pick is now among the heaviest players in the NFL while holding down the fort in the middle of the Steelers' defensive line.
During the offseason program in May, defensive line coach Domata Peko stated that he believes Black can grow into one of the best nose tackles across the NFL .
”Black can be one of the best noses in the game if he just keeps on doing what he’s been doing, and us working his butt off,” Peko said. “Really good on his technique and his details. I just want to sharpen him up and get him really going, and try to bring out the best in him.”
After a good summer, Black has played 39 percent of Pittsburgh's defensive snaps thus far, which comes out to a total of 148 reps.
He hasn't made much of an impact as a pass rusher, which hasn't come as much of a surprise, though he did record the first sack of his career in the Steelers ' win over Tampa Bay.
Black's bread-and-butter as a nose tackle is his run defense, and he does a good job of eating up space and clogging running lanes with his ability to anchor given his size.
He still has room for growth, but Black has emerged as a quality piece in the trenches for Pittsburgh as a second-year player.

title: Former Browns HC Slams Steelers' Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The start of Mike McCarthy’s era as the Pittsburgh Steelers’ head coach has been met with mixed reviews. You cannot deny that this team is 4-2 and in the middle of the AFC North divisional race.
But it hasn't been a seamless transition for the Steelers. Two ugly losses early in the year created doubt, and that concern is sticking with some.
One huge example of this just popped up, with former Cleveland Browns head coach Eric Mangini sharing his disappointment with McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers so far. Speaking on a recent television appearance, the former Cleveland Browns and New York Jets boss explained why he is "not as impressed" as others are with the Steelers' start.
"He's worse at this point his year than he was last year," he stated on First Things First . "Here's where I'm disappointed. I do think, with McCarthy, this should be better than it was last year. Because of their familiarity, because of the system. And there's more talent on this team offensively."
One of the big criticisms Mangini levied against the Steelers is their ease of schedule, which is a fair point. The Steelers have played the Indianapolis Colts and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in back-to-back weeks, two franchises that appear destined to miss the postseason this go-around.
The Steelers won both games, but it didn't do anything to prove to Mangini that this team is legitimate.
"I'm not as impressed by this as other people are," he admitted. "Who have the last two weeks been (against)? They're (the Buccaneers) okay, and the week before was another situation where he should have probably been very productive."
Up next, the Steelers face the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. It's probably a fair guess to state that Mangini won't be too impressed with Pittsburgh taking them down in Week 7.
I have been just as critical about the quarterback and head coach as anyone, but Mangini is dead wrong. Rodgers is more productive through the first six games of the 2026 season than last year. He's exceeded 290 passing yards twice already, something he did one single time in 2025.
This offense is far from perfect. They still haven't established and stuck to their identity, that much is true.
But to suggest this group is less productive this year than last year is simply false. This offense has figured out ways to be slightly better than last year's edition. It's not much, but it's a considerable step for the Steelers.
It just doesn't impress Eric Mangini.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Ranking Steelers Top Trade Needs And Their Best Targets
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Your guess is as good as mine when it comes to the Pittsburgh Steelers' plans for the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline. The team hasn't waited long to make improvements, adding cornerbacks Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terrell Smith as well as wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
But all three of those additions were signings for the Steelers. The two cornerbacks were claimed from practice squads, while MVS was added shortly after being released by the Los Angeles Chargers. A trade hasn't happened yet, but that doesn't mean it won't.
Especially when the Steelers have multiple areas of their lineup that could use outside reinforcements. These four positions are the most important to upgrade before the deadline, and there is an ideal player available to fill each void.
Brock Hoffman has been rock-solid at right guard, and left guard Mason McCormick is the model of consistency and dogged determination.
Even with that, this position remains a need to monitor. Hoffman is a reliable veteran, but he's only been a starter for one season in his NFL career. For right now, it's lower on the list, but it could shoot up depending on how the next couple of weeks play out.
If you're going to go for broke, you might as well get the best player possible. Quenton Nelson is one of the most respected interior linemen in the NFL. It gets complicated with his contract situation, but who cares, because Nelson makes this offensive line undeniably Super Bowl-caliber.
Jamel Dean had an otherworldly game in Week 6, and he's made the loss of Joey Porter Jr. much easier to digest. Asante Samuel Jr. is playing well in an elevated role, with rookie third-round pick Daylen Everette playing some important snaps early in the season.
But to become a postseason challenge, they need better play in the secondary. Thankfully, several winning veterans could fill the role of CB2. Immediate veteran options that come to mind are Tennessee Titans newcomer Alontae Taylor, Philadelphia Eagles corner and Super Bowl winner Riq Woolen and Zyon McCollum from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Riq Woolen gives the Steelers exactly what they need: a number two cornerback with experience, a Super Bowl on his resume and he's not a huge commitment. He signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia for the 2026 season, meaning the Steelers could get a productive rental for very cheap.
If they want to add some real intrigue, New York Giants former first-roud pick Deonte Banks is a good option. He's had two terrible seasons in the NFL, but as a rookie he flashed excellence. Once again in 2026, he's finding his form. He's set to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027, so he's also a flyer of an option that wouldn't put the Steelers in a corner contractually.
Patrick Queen is playing elsewhere in 2027, that much feels obvious. And his play this season makes you wonder if the Steelers would be better off finding another option in 2026.
Payton Wilson has played well, but he needs a running mate to complement his skill set. Elandon Roberts might be that player, but the solution might be waiting outside the organization.
Pete Werner, the Ohio State product, has Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker written all over him. He explodes towards the ball. He's agile and nimble enough to hold his own in coverage. And he's a well-respected teammate.
While the team awaits further updates on Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr., I get the sense that the Steelers are entering with a conservative approach to upgrading the wide receiver room. MVS fills out the depth chart when called up from the practice squad, but they need someone who can oscillate between being a top-three option and a bottom-of-the-lineup player.
A quick, outside receiver like Dontayvion Wicks is perfect for their needs. It's a compromise between another expensive veteran and an unproven practice squad member. Wicks is a deep ball threat and can complement what DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard bring to the offense. Plus, he's on the books for slightly more than $4 million in 2027. For a fifth or sixth-round draft pick, he makes too much sense for the Steelers.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Starting OLB Suffers Groin Injury
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are dealing with a rather long list of injuries as they get ready to head over to Paris for a Week 7 matchup with the New Orleans Saints .
Perhaps the most notable development on the Steelers' first injury report of the week is Alex Highsmith (groin) being listed as a limited participant.
Furthermore, running back Rico Dowdle (knee) also registered as a limited participant while defensive tackle Sebastian Joseph-Day (tricep) was a non-participant.
Cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Brandin Echols (hamstring), EDGE rusher T.J. Watt (NIR/rest), defensive tackle Cameron Heyward (NIR/rest) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) were all non-participants too. Safety DeShon Elliott (knee) was a full participant and remains in his 21-day practice window while on the reserve/injured list.
Highsmith was incredibly durable for the first four seasons of his NFL career, appearing in all but one of Pittsburgh's regular season games from 2020 through 2023.
He began running into some issues on the injury front once the 2024 campaign, arrived, however.
That year, Highsmith suffered a groin injury in Week 3 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers that kept him out for three games.
He returned in Week 7, though he later sustained an ankle injury against the Washington Commanders in Week 10 that resulted in a three-game absence.
In 2025, Highsmith suffered another groin injury during training camp. He did not miss any regular season time, though.
He did, however, go down with an ankle injury in Week 2 vs. the Seattle Seahawks that sidelined him for two games.
Highsmith then suffered a pectoral injury before Pittsburgh's Week 11 contest against the Cincinnati Bengals and missed two games from there.
The 29-year-old has been out for a total of 10 regular season games since the start of 2024, and the hope is that he doesn't have to miss any time with his current groin injury.
If he is out vs. New Orleans, Nick Herbig would likely take on a majority of his usual workload opposite T.J. Watt after a two-sack outing in Week 6's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Jack Sawyer would also factor into the Steelers ' defensive game plan more heavily as well after logging 107 snaps on that side of the ball thus far.
Dowdle dislocated his toe twice against the New England Patriots in Week 2 and went on to miss Pittsburgh's next three games.
He returned to the field against Tampa Bay and posted 49 yards on 10 touches, but his knee injury is a new development in what's becoming an injury-ravaged season for the 28-year-old.
The fact that Dowdle was a limited participant is good news rather than him not practicing at all, though his status bears watching over the next few days before the Steelers hit the field vs. New Orleans.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: 3 Positions Seahawks Should Trade For Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are moving closer to the NFL trade deadline next month, and their positions of need are changing day by day.
Injuries are piling up for the Seahawks , and that is making their focus a lot more clear when negotiating with teams over the next couple of weeks. Here's a look at the three positions the Seahawks need the most at the trade deadline.
After losing second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo for the season as he was placed on injured reserve, the Seahawks are in line to add a tight end at the deadline.
Philadelphia Eagles star Dallas Goedert has been linked to the Seahawks in the past, but there could be others scouring around the league that might make sense for Seattle.
The Seahawks have been dealing with a number of injuries at the linebacker position this season. Players like Drake Thomas, Chazz Surratt, Connor O'Toole, and Tyrice Knight have all been out due to injury at some point this year. This could open the door for the Seahawks to make a depth trade for someone looking for a new home.
Players like SirVocea Dennis of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Akeem Davis-Gaither of the Indianapolis Colts could make sense for the Seahawks in a potential trade.
The Seahawks have not been strangers to running back issues throughout the season. Zach Charbonnet has been injured for the first six weeks, but he is returning from the physically unable to perform list and could play as early as Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Even if he's healthy, there still needs to be depth behind him because he is coming off a torn ACL suffered back in the playoffs against the San Francisco 49ers.
Rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price could help, but he is also dealing with a chest injury that has landed him on injured reserve. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have filled in, but not to the standard of a Super Bowl contender.
The Seahawks could look at a veteran like Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans to fill that void, or they could try to swing another small deal for a late-round pick.
The NFL trade deadline is scheduled for Tuesday, November 10, at 1 pm PT.

title: Seahawks Thursday Injury Report a Mixed Bag, Zach Charbonnet, Drake Thomas, More
full_text:
Another day of practice, another injury report outlining what can be expected this weekend when the Seattle Seahawks play the Kansas City Chiefs. Let’s open it up and see where things are trending for both sides, starting with the Seahawks. In terms of the big landmarks the team wanted to hit this week, it all looks pretty favorable .
Starting with the good news, the Seahawks look like they can count on Anthony Bradford (knee) and Zach Charbonnet (knee) , after both checked in with full participation today. Bradford was limited yesterday, so the step forward is encouraging. Tyrice Knight (oblique), Rashid Shaheed (hip), and Beau Stephens (knee) also made the climb to full practice.
The limited pool is a little concerning this week. DeMarcus Lawrence (knee), who was just resting yesterday, now apparently has an actual injury that held him back at practice. Uchenna Nwosu (hip) also added an ailment to the list. I don’t mind either player getting practice time off, but if one or both left practice midway through because of injury that could be trouble.
The ones to at least consider scratching off this weekend are Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt (calf), and Drake Thomas (ankle) , who all went DNP again. Obviously of the three, Thomas is certainly the most significant, but Knight’s progression today indicates he’s ready to take on that starting role, so Thomas has leeway to take his time here.
On the other side, the Chiefs had a pretty easy practice report. Almost everything was the same as yesterday. Cyrus Allen (knee), Chamarri Conner (knee), Patrick Mahomes (knee), and Trey Smith (hip) all practiced in full again despite various injury acknowledgements. Expect all four to be fully available and ready to let it rip.
Travis Kelce (ankle), L’Jarius Sneed (knee), and Cooper McDonald (knee) all held at limited, so they may not be 100% there but are certainly there enough to suit up and play this weekend. One of the new wrinkles with this report is here, with running back Brashard Smith (hamstring) getting held to limited. He rarely plays, so the impact is minor.
The DNPs stayed the same, although they carry much more weight now. Jaylon Moore (concussion) and Rashee Rice (hamstring, knee) can both be considered unlikely to play, and Josh Simmons (back) was placed on IR, as his injury is apparently much worse than initially thought. That’s both starting tackles and the top wide receiver, probably unavailable.

title: Byron Murphy II's Emergence is Huge For Seahawks' Defense
full_text:
The last four games haven’t gone as planned for the Seattle Seahawks , losing three of those contests as a result of their struggling offense . But even at 3-3, there have been some major bright spots for the Seahawks in 2026.
Defensive lineman Byron Murphy II is one of those players who have impressed for Seattle. The former 2024 No. 16 overall pick began breaking out during the Seahawks’ Super Bowl-winning season, and he’s continued his rise this season.
Murphy is emerging as one of the best interior linemen in the NFL, and he’s helping solidify a Seahawks defense that remains one of the best units in the league.
Seattle’s defensive front has all the same major contributors this season as it did in 2025. But Murphy is flashing far more often and becoming much more effective in the pass rush than he has been in the last two years.
In 2025, Murphy totaled seven tackles for loss, 21 pressures, 7.0 sacks and 62 total tackles in 786 defensive snaps (17 games played). He was an effective run stuffer who occasionally made a splashy play rushing the quarterback.
But this season has felt different, as Murphy is consistently getting in the backfield and pressuring opposing quarterbacks.
Murphy, in just six games, has five tackles for loss, six pressures, 3.0 sacks and 21 total tackles in 258 snaps. He’s outpacing basically all of his numbers from last season and is stacking up to the rest of the league production-wise.
The combination of Leonard Williams and Murphy is one of the best in the NFL. Williams was a Second Team All-Pro in 2025 and deserved a similar honor the year before, but was snubbed. If they continue playing the way they are now, there’s a chance both players could earn All-Pro honors in 2026.
Before Murphy, Seahawks general manager John Schneider struggled for multiple years drafting early-round interior defensive linemen.
High-profile selections L.J. Collier (29th overall in 2019) and Malik McDowell (35th overall in 2017) didn’t work out, and Seattle shifted their strategy to drafting the position in later rounds. That was until Murphy became the team’s highest-drafted defensive tackle since Sam Adams (8th overall) in 1994.
With Murphy’s slow rookie season, the pick was immediately criticized. However, now that he’s playing at a high level, it’s clear how impactful the selection was to the Seahawks’ championship-winning season.
The versatility along the defensive line has also given head coach Mike Macdonald more freedom with the scheme, and Murphy is key to that. He doesn’t have to play every snap, and that helps him and Williams stay fresh overall.

title: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo Out for Season
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo was placed on injured reserve on Thursday in a pair of transactions that also activated running back Zach Charbonnet from the physically unable to perform list.
Arroyo will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery, per ESPN's Adam Schefter , and will miss the team's final 11 games. The 2025 second-round pick has been injury-prone throughout his college career and into the NFL, and this is yet another blow to a high-potential talent.
The Seahawks haven't used Arroyo much this season, as he only has one catch for 17 yards in six games. Arroyo was expected to be a hybrid tight end and wide receiver after compiling 35 catches for 590 yards and seven touchdowns in his final college season at Miami.
Arroyo suffered the shoulder injury in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos on Oct. 15.
A season-ending injury for Arroyo is more disappointing to his overall potential than it is an actual detriment to the Seahawks in the short term.
Arroyo has played just 88 offensive snaps this season (22% of total) and has only been targeted twice. He hasn't been a big piece of the offense by any means, as AJ Barner has commanded the majority of the targets at the tight end position.
Eric Saubert, the No. 2 tight end, is a significantly better blocker, and that's been a focus for the Seahawks at the position. Former undrafted free agent Nick Kallerup is also better in that regard.
The primary loss for Seattle is missing a change-of-pace pass-catcher, and that's not a big loss. Expectations were much higher for Arroyo, however, especially in his second season. He was a dynamic receiver in college, but it hasn't fully come together for him in the pros.
Arroyo also missed a chunk of the 2025 regular season after being placed on IR with a knee strain. He suffered a torn ACL in college and and had another minor knee injury during preparation for the NFL Draft. Another significant injury will only slow Arroyo's development into what the Seahawks were hoping he would become.
In the meantime, expect more playtime for Saubert and Kallerup behind Barner. That trio will be the Seahawks' top players at the position moving forward.

title: Zach Charbonnet Heads to Active Roster: What it Means for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are welcoming Zach Charbonnet back to the 53-man roster after spending the last three weeks in his 21-day window to return to practice.
This gives Charbonnet a chance to make his season debut in Week 7 when the Seahawks host Patrick Mahomes , Kenneth Walker III, and the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Here's a look at what it means for the Seahawks.
The Seahawks are hopeful that Charbonnet will be able to play against the Chiefs, but moving him to the active roster doesn't guarantee that . There is a chance he could be inactive for the game as he works his way back from his injury. The move the Seahawks made was procedural: they had to do this, or he would not have been able to play for the rest of the season. Getting him back on the 53-man roster gives him a chance to play this year.
The Seahawks will continue to monitor his status, and they may want to wait until he's perfectly healthy before he takes the field again. Now he has more time to heal, but getting back on the 53-man roster is definitely a step in the right direction and the next stage of a full recovery.
It's been a difficult season for the Seahawks in the running back room. Upon learning about Charbonnet's torn ACL, the team went out and selected Jadarian Price out of Notre Dame with their first-round pick. Price struggled with fumbles in his first three weeks with the team before he suffered a chest injury that put him on injured reserve.
Price was forced to miss four games in a stretch that ends on Sunday against the Chiefs. He will be able to come back in Week 8 when the Seahawks host the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football.
In the meantime, the team is working with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, among others. The group simply is not as strong as it could be, but getting Charbonnet back could help fortify the rushing attack, which could change the entire offense.
Kickoff between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: Seahawks Can Exploit This Weakness vs. Chiefs
full_text:
Week 7 is going to be a big test for many teams, but no team arguably has more pressure than the Seattle Seahawks (3-3). They will host the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) on Sunday Night Football in primetime. Seattle will also face its former Super Bowl LXI MVP in Kenneth Walker III , who is tearing it up for the Chiefs.
​This game has storylines of Walker, his time and departure from Seattle, and the Seahawks’ recent offensive struggles. There is some hope for the Seahawks to bounce back from losing three of their last four games and it starts with Wednesday’s injury report . While most of the attention is on the Seahawks’ returns on offense, it is the injuries on the Chiefs’ offense that could be a deciding factor.
​Kansas City is coming out of Wednesday’s practice having to adjust to the injury concerns. Three offensive starters for the Chiefs didn’t participate and another in tight end Travis Kelce had limited participation with an ankle injury.
Among those who didn’t participate in practice were left tackle Josh Simmons (back), right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring). Finally, quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee), left guard Trey Smith (hip) and wide receiver Cyrus Allen (knee).
​The Chiefs should have some real concerns about some of their offensive starters potentially not being able to face the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense . This is a defense that remains one of the toughest defenses this season despite some new flaws of their own. Oftentimes, they are put into bad situations by the offense.
​Within the last few years, the Chiefs haven’t possessed a reliable deep passing game. This season, they are able to cover up the problem thanks to Walker’s elite performances. The Chiefs rank 19th in the league in passing yards accounted for. If Kelce and/or Rice are going to be injured, that is going to leave the Chiefs’ short-to-mid-range passing game less effective. This is an area where the Seahawks aren’t great at defending.
​Whether it is in the middle of the field or on the outside when a cornerback is sent on a blitz, the opposing offenses can usually quickly get the ball out to a pass-catcher for at least seven yards consistently. Inside linebacker Ernest Jones IV is a reliable player , but isn’t quick enough to respond to an open receiver near his zone coverage.
​The Chiefs might have to utilize the quick passing game if the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense shuts down Walker and the running game. It would be even more difficult for the Chiefs to run to the outside with both of their starting tackles injured. With Rice injured and Kelce older and injured, the Seahawks give the Chiefs’ offense their most frustrating performance of the season.

title: Six Players the Seahawks Should Note from College Football Week 7
full_text:
Throughout the College Football Season, we’ll be monitoring top performers who might be available to the Seattle Seahawks in the 2027 draft . We’ll focus on players that play positions that are likely, or at least possibly, going to be one the team considers going after. This should give us a chance to spotlight players that the team targets well ahead of time.
I’m not the biggest fan in the world of Sam Leavitt, but when the performance is this strong he should be pointed out. Two weeks in a row he’s delivered the goods for LSU, including 300 combined yards and four touchdowns this last week. He lacks the star power of the top quarterbacks this year, but is viable as a day two or early day three pick.
Not a name I’ve heard much buzz around, but stomping a mudhole into the Alabama defense will get people talking. Tennessee’s top running back gave 175 yards from scrimmage on 25 touches and 2 rushing touchdowns, one of the primary reasons why the Vols found their way to an upset. He’s making his move and has a chance to be a mid-level prospect.
I’m not sure if Justin Scott can play one-technique at the next level, but Miami puts him there a decent amount, and he finds ways to be productive. This last week, in a surprisingly close game for the Hurricanes, Scott had eight tackles and a sack. It might be an overreach to spend a pick as high as will be needed to get Scott as a nose, but if he can do both, it’s viable.
It’s something of a low moment for the Oregon Ducks program, but I really like a lot of their defense, especially Tuioti. He’s got the size and run stopping ability coveted by Mike Macdonald. Last week, when the Ducks needed a dominant defense to have a chance to win, he provided 5 tackles, 2 sacks, and another half a tackle for loss with 5 total pressures.
It’s not entirely fair to everyone else since Cole is both an off-ball linebacker and edge rusher, but either way, he’s now the clear top dog. Georgia lost last week, but Cole provided 10 tackles, a sack, and 7 (!) total QB pressures, while allowing only one eight-yard catch in coverage. Anyone looking for the next Micah Parsons should focus in on this one here.
Finally, Amare Ferrell did everything he could to try to get Indiana the win over Ohio State. HIs efforts were in vain, but they did not go unnoticed. 7 tackles, 2 picks, 2 pass breakups, and allowing just one seven-yard completion spells a dominant performance, especially against the great Jeremiah Smith and the vaunted OSU attack. He’s quickly becoming a guy.

title: 4 Trade Partners, Targets for Seahawks Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have aspirations of winning their second consecutive Super Bowl, but they might need a little bit more help than what's currently on the roster.
Last year, the Seahawks made a big swing and traded for New Orleans Saints wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. He ended up playing a large role down the stretch as the team marched on to the playoffs. Shaheed returned the kickoff on the first play of their playoff run, and it led to a Super Bowl title. He then signed a 3-year, $51 million contract , which showed how important the trade deadline can be for certain teams.
Here's a look at four teams that could be sellers at the trade deadline and could call the Seahawks for some help.
Trade Target: RB Tony Pollard
Even after the Titans won their first game in Week 6 against the Indianapolis Colts, they still are on pace to be one of the worst teams in the league. Therefore, their status as a trade deadline seller is all but certain, and the Seahawks benefit.
The Seahawks could be in the market for a running back upgrade, and Tony Pollard would be a solid fit for them. Pollard is entering the final year of his contract, and he can eat up carries and lead a backfield if need be. At worst, he's someone who could split carries with Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet.
Trade Target: TE Dallas Goedert
The Seahawks got some unfortunate news this past week regarding tight end Elijah Arroyo, who is expected to be out for a long period of time. If his absence extends for the rest of the season, the Seahawks would benefit from adding a veteran to the group. Dallas Goedert is someone with Super Bowl experience, and he could fit into this role.
The Eagles are losers of four straight games and have lost their starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season. With their current outlook, they are likely going to try and accrue some more draft picks for the next two years. The Seahawks can oblige and send a Day 3 selection for Goedert.
Trade Target: LB SirVocea Dennis
The Seahawks have gone through a number of injuries at the linebacker position, and the veteran could be of interest to them at the trade deadline. Among those players is Buccaneers linebacker SirVocea Dennis.
Dennis, a fifth-round pick in the 2023 draft out of Pittsburgh, has spent his first four seasons with the Bucks and is approaching free agency this offseason.
Considering the fact that the team signed Alex Anzalone in the offseason and selected Josiah Trotter in the draft, Dennis's time with the Bucs appears to be coming to an end. The Seahawks can offer an escape pod with an early out at the trade deadline.
Dennis started 16 games last season and recorded over 100 tackles, but he is at just six so far this year and could do damage in a different situation.
Trade Target: LB Akeem Davis-Gaither
The Colts find themselves on the verge of blowing things up after firing general manager Chris Ballard earlier this week. With Ballard no longer with the team, the Colts could see more exits down the line.
Another player who could depart the Colts is linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither, who signed a one-year contract with the team this offseason. Davis-Gaither was a starter with the Arizona Cardinals last year, but he finds himself in an interesting position with the Colts.
While Davis-Gaither has started every game for the Colts so far, they also selected Georgia's CJ Allen in the second round of the draft. If the Colts are angling toward the future, they may want to go with Allen rather than Davis-Gaither, and they could probably add an additional draft pick in the process.

title: What Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid Said About Seahawks Confirms Game Plan
full_text:
The stage is set for the No. 1 defense in the NFL to face off against the No. 1 offense in the NFL. The Seattle Seahawks will host the Kansas City Chiefs in the ultimate battle between the best offense and the best defense.
Both teams have a great amount of respect for the other, and it's clear that the Chiefs know what they're getting into.
“They’re the best in the business right now,” Reid told reporters . “Mike [Macdonald] does a nice job with the defense, and they have a good scheme; then they fly around. They believe in it, and they fly around. They aren’t a lot of hiccups on the back end. You see some teams where something goes on, and suddenly someone is popping free. You don’t see that with these guys.”
The key to holding the Chiefs' offense at bay is containing quarterback Patrick Mahomes and making sure he doesn't have the opportunity to make an explosive play.
“They’re good at every single level of the defense,” Mahomes said in a press conference. “Defensive line, linebackers, secondary, everybody, and they have a great scheme. They’re going to make you earn it every single drive, and it’s not always going to be pretty, but you have to be consistent and not push it too far, but push it enough to make plays happen.”
Mahomes recalled his past matchups against the Baltimore Ravens when Macdonald was the defensive coordinator there in 2022 and 2023. Macdonald's final game with the Ravens came in the AFC Championship, where they lost to the Chiefs.
During that game, the Ravens held the Chiefs to just 17 points, but it wasn't enough as Baltimore's offense mustered only 10 points themselves. Mahomes was able to flush the ball out of the pocket quickly to combat the quickness of the pass rushers, and that should be part of Kansas City's strategy against Seattle on Sunday Night Football.
With that previous experience, the Seahawks defense has to match the speed of the Chiefs and lock down the passing routes to ensure Mahomes throws the ball away or keeps it in his hands long enough to draw a sack.

title: Why Seahawks Won't Trade for Colts Star Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are a team to keep an eye on during the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline on November 10, but it is very difficult to pull off a midseason deal.
While the Seahawks could be in the market for an upgrade at the running back position and Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor could be an option, the two sides are unlikely to consummate a trade.
The Colts made a bold move earlier this week by firing general manager Chris Ballard after nine seasons with the team. Ballard's departure is a sign of what could be coming down the line for the Colts as they encounter an organizational reset. They could set the future general manager up nicely by acquiring draft picks for some of their top players, including Taylor.
Their 2-4 start, including a Week 6 loss at home to the winless Tennessee Titans, suggests that Indianapolis is not ready for a deep playoff run. At the very least, they should be listening to calls for Taylor, who has been one of the best backs in the league since he made his debut in 2020.
So far this season, Taylor has 122 carries for 492 yards and seven touchdowns. He ranks sixth in rushing yards behind Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry, James Cook, Bijan Robinson and Kenneth Walker. He ranks first among all running backs in touchdowns.
If the Colts sell high, they could get a premium pick or two for Taylor if they find the right suitor.
Taylor's contract is ultimately the reason why the Seahawks are unlikely to acquire him in a trade. He has a $16.1 million cap hit this season and is under contract for the next two seasons for $44 million. The team could cut him in the offseason and save up to $11 million, but the Seahawks aren't going to trade for someone just to move on from him a few months later.
If the Seahawks weren't willing to pay Walker the three-year, $43 million contract the Chiefs offered him in the offseason, they likely won't do the same for Taylor, especially for just half a season.
For now, the Seahawks need to find a cheaper option on the running back market if they are interested in an upgrade, or they need to count on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to get healthier sooner rather than later.

title: 49ers TE George Kittle's 2026 NFL Season is Flying Under the Radar
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle's 2026 NFL season is flying completely under the radar.
Firstly, let's rewind to January, when Kittle was carted off the field during the 49ers' Wild Card Round matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. He had suffered a devastating Achilles injury, bringing his season to a devastating end after already missing six regular-season games.
Yet, somehow, Kittle made it back for Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams in Australia. He defied expectations, returning to the field in just eight months despite a typical Achilles recovery taking nine to 12 months. He set out to be ready for the season opener, and that's exactly what he did.
And ESPN reported that in June 2026, Michigan State University published in the Physician and Sportsmedicine Journal said only 27.1% of NFL players return to pre-injury performance levels. That recovery rate is already remarkably low, and the odds are arguably even more daunting given Kittle's age and the stage of his career.
Now in Week 6, the newly turned 33-year-old has made an incredible start to the season, which is remarkable given the serious injury he suffered and spent the whole offseason rehabbing.
Yes, there was some rust in Week 1 , which was understandable, but through six games, Kittle is tied for the team lead in receiving touchdowns with five and has racked up 338 receiving yards - more than half of his total from last season.
All things considered, he's on pace to record the fifth 1,000-yard receiving season of his career for the City by the Bay. Don't forget this year is his tenth representing the franchise.
Kittle has also overtaken Vernon Davis to become the 49ers' all-time leader in touchdown receptions among tight ends. With 57 receiving touchdowns, he is closing in on third place on the franchise's all-time list, currently held by Gene Washington with 59. Terrell Owens ranks second with 81, while Jerry Rice leads the way with 176. Obviously, he won't ever beat Rice's tally, though.
Kittle defied the odds and came out the other side looking like his same explosive self. For whatever reason, he isn't getting the attention he deserves, but this is a storyline the 49ers should be shouting from the rooftops.
In my eyes, no other comeback story comes close to his, and if his performances continue at this pace, he'd have a compelling case for Comeback Player of the Year.

title: What the 49ers Can Realistically Afford at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
In most years, trade proposals are pipe dreams or fan desires. The San Francisco 49ers will likely be active at the trade deadline, but, in addition, similar to Keion White. However, this is a team that added Emmanuel Sanders at the trade deadline before, albeit at a reasonable price. Still, they have swung when the time is right. Looking at the 49ers' cap, draft picks, and roster outlook, it feels like this year is the best year for the team to go all-in.
It does not hurt that the team is off to a 6-0 start while the Seattle Seahawks are 3-3 and the Los Angeles Rams are 2-4. Aside from the Minnesota Vikings, every team in the NFC has at least two losses. The conference is not going to be more wide open entering November.
The team also has Trent Williams, who is 38 years old. George Kittle and Mike Evans are 33 years old. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Fred Warner is 39, and while Nick Bosa is 28, he has some of the biggest injury concerns of the group. They need to win a Super Bowl with this corps, and they are running out of seasons.
The addition of Evans showed they are going for it and not worrying about the future. Now they can make a splash to solidify it.
More than that, the team is well equipped to make a run. They currently have the most salary cap space in the NFL. With $43M in cap space , the team can take on a big salary this year, and they will still have money to roll over for next year.
So, they can rid any team of their bad contract players without much issue. More than that, they have all of their noteworthy draft picks for the foreseeable future. Their first- through third-round picks for the next three seasons are all accounted for.
There are not many teams across past seasons that sit with such a lead in the division with the cap space and pick situation that they have. When adding in the win-now nature of their roster, there are few teams that historically are more primed to make a blockbuster trade deadline move than the 49ers.
While the team could put a few band-aids on the roster with smart and savvy moves, they could also be the team that goes all-in this year.

title: Why the 49ers Should Sit Out Mike Evans and Nick Bosa Against the Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers should rest Mike Evans and Nick Bosa against the Atlanta Falcons to avoid risking further injuries.
It's almost Week 7 and San Francisco is 6-0 for the season. A perfect start to the season. But now it's time to think smartly about two key players who could feature against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
Firstly, Evans is now dealing with Achilles tendinitis, with previous reports suggesting the issue will trouble him throughout the season . He's played in every game so far, despite dealing with rib issues and, more recently, Achilles soreness over the past three weeks. Yet he's continued to perform at an incredibly high level, and the 49ers are undoubtedly a stronger team with him on the field.
But now it's time to rest him. The bye week is coming anyways, but general manager John Lynch isn't exactly sure whether he will play.
"I wouldn't say 'not likely.' I think it's still TBD," Lynch said on his usual weekly appearance on Bay Area radio station KNBR. "We've got a couple of more days. We're going to take every bit of those to try to ascertain where Mike's at. He's done a really good job treating this thing, and obviously, we know of Mike's toughness.
"So, we'll let these next couple of days play out and make a decision when we have to. Mike's that type of player that you wait, you let the process play itself out, and we'll see where we're at at the end of the week. Not fun—just kind of nagging," Lynch said of it. "And so, we're doing our best to kind of alleviate that from Mike so he can go play the fantastic football he has."
In addition to Evans, Bosa could make a return for the first time since Week 2 after calf troubles. He didn't practice on Wednesday, but he may practice on Thursday ahead of the game. But even then, he should still miss the game.
"He's kind of in that same Mike Evans bucket where we will kind of evaluate Nick here in the next couple of days, and I'm sure [head coach] Kyle [Shanahan] will have something for you on Friday while we're leaving for Atlanta," shared Lynch.
In short, the bye week comes at a convenient time, so the 49ers should make the most of it by resting both players, even if they're cleared to play. Atlanta aren't the strongest opponents and San Francisco should be capable of winning regardless.
Even if that means accepting a worst-case 6–1 record, having Bosa and Evans as healthy as possible heading into the bye is a bigger victory in the long run than risking further injuries for the sake of one game.

title: Former Falcons Star Doubts 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Will Ever Win a Super Bowl
full_text:
Will the San Francisco 49ers win a Super Bowl under head coach Kyle Shanahan?
It's the age-old question. Shanahan enters his 10th season with the 49ers this year, making him the team's longest-tenured head coach, yet they still haven't won a Super Bowl.
They have come close on two occasions, losing to the Kansas City Chiefs in the Super Bowl following fourth-quarter and overtime heartbreak. They also blew a lead against the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Championship Game and suffered a blowout loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in a separate season.
Roddy White, a former Atlanta Falcons wide receiver who spent all 11 seasons of his NFL career with the franchise, delivered a brutal verdict on Shanahan's Super Bowl-winning credentials. White played his final season in Atlanta under Shanahan, who served as the Falcons' offensive coordinator at the time.
"Yeah, but they start like this every year," White said on the Up & Adams Show . "That team starts very fast every year. The only time they haven't started fast is when they had everybody hurt. And this year, they're still managing to get people hurt, but they're off to a good start."
"I think, me personally, that he's a great offensive mind," White said. "But in tough situations, in pressure situations, the over-aggressive play calls always get him in trouble. And I think that's just his mentality. He doesn't play situational football well. That's the only thing that I think that's really like a knock on his game, and the thing that he does—he doesn't play situational football well.
"And that gets his team in trouble when you play against great quarterbacks. And when you make it to the Super Bowl, you're going to be playing against a great quarterback. So your ability to understand the flow of the game, and the things like that, is going to help you win those games.
"I think that Kyle always thinks about, 'I have to win the game. I have to win the game,' instead of putting his players in the best position to win the game," White added.
"He's a great play-caller, like great play-caller. The play call sheet is deep, I will say that ... So, he's very, very smart. I just think the aggressive play calling was not needed. A pressure situation always gets the best of him."
With this take in mind and the 49ers 6-0 to start the season , will the past repeat itself?

title: 49ers are to Blame for Mike Evans’ Achilles Injury
full_text:
Mike Evans was expectedly held out of the 49ers’ first Week 7 practice against the Falcons.
He left Monday night’s game against the Commanders right before halftime with an Achilles injury and wouldn’t return. Anytime a player leaves a game with an Achilles injury, it causes panic.
Thankfully, Evans didn’t suffer a season-ending Achilles tear. But he is experiencing tendinitis. It would be very surprising if Evans plays this week against the Falcons, especially with the Bye week after.
Evans’ injury is twofold. On one hand, it’s a sigh of relief that Evans didn’t tear his Achilles. On the other hand, he shouldn’t have gotten hurt against the Commanders because he shouldn’t have played.
The 49ers deserve blame for Evans’ Achilles injury. Evans didn’t take part in a single practice in the lead-up to Monday night against the Commanders because of Achilles soreness.
That should’ve been a red flag to the 49ers. They, of all teams, should know how serious Achilles injuries are, even if it’s just soreness. It happened two years ago with Christian McCaffrey.
You’d think they’d learn that it’s best to be extremely cautious with a player who’s dealing with any Achilles-related issue. Instead, they allowed Evans to play because he wanted to. They failed to protect him from himself.
“Mike's got a lot of experience doing this stuff,” Kyle Shanahan said in Monday night’s postgame. “Mike's pretty honest with us too, and my life experiences with him over six games, if he says he's ready to go, I believe him.”
Believing in Evans is foolish. What NFL star doesn’t want to play, no matter how they’re feeling? Evans isn’t thinking about the consequences and risks of playing through Achilles soreness.
All that matters to him is playing and helping his team. That’s how tough he is, but he doesn’t need to prove anything to anyone. What he needs is someone to hold him out from worsening his injury.
The 49ers failed to prevent that because Evans wanted to play. They let him play that game as if it were against the Seahawks in December, with the NFC West on the line.
Now, they have to rely on Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and a newly signed Brandin Cooks. The wide receiver position was already razor-thin.
It's desolate now, and it opens the floodgates for 49ers fans to pound the table for a wide receiver trade. This all could've been avoided if they had sat him against the Commanders.

title: 5 Realistic Trade Targets for the 49ers Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are expected to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline. With defensive tackle being one of their most glaring needs, who are the most likely trade options for the 49ers?
The 49ers just saw Payne up close and personal to decide if he is worth acquiring in a trade. Payne is in the last year of his deal with Washington, and they are sitting at 1-4-1. Getting something back would make sense . The former first-round pick would instantly be the 49ers' best run defender.
Sieler might cost more to acquire than Payne. He is two years older, but he is signed through the 2029 season. Getting that type of team control will require more draft capital. Sieler only had five sacks last year, but had 20 in the two years combined before that.
The 0-5 Dolphins are looking to rebuild, and the current GM and head coach did not draft Sieler. They could try to trade him while his value is still high.
The 49ers were linked to Vita Vea earlier in the offseason when he had contract issues. While Tampa Bay extended Vea, they did not add too much in guarantees to the point that he is now untradable. Tampa Bay is sitting at 1-5, and they might be firing their head coach soon.
Vea is still one of the best run defenders in the NFL and he has won a Super Bowl. That type of impact and experience would be valuable. The 49ers could try to re-open trade talks.
If the 49ers cannot pry Vea away from the Bucs, Robinson is a great consolation prize. Robinson has been as good, if not better than Vea as a run defender this year. He is a leader in the locker room. Robinson has 11 years of NFL experience. However, this veteran being on a one-year deal should make him easier to obtain in a trade.
The Colts trading for DeForest Buckner when they could have taken a quarterback with that first-round pick might end up being the reason Buckner heads back to the 49ers years later. The Colts fired the GM who made the Buckner trade. Now, the All-Pro defensive tackle is not happy with the organization and is a free agent at the end of the year. The Colts could let him leave for nothing, or they could trade him for something now.

title: 49ers Defensive End Mykel Williams Suffers Another Knee Injury
full_text:
Mykel Williams seems to have re-injured his surgically repaired knee during the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Washington Commanders.
Williams seemed fine after the game. But today, head coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned that Williams has a knee injury and listed him among the players who would not participate in Wednesday's practice. When asked if Williams' surgically repaired knee "flared up" on Monday night during the game, Shanahan said, "Just knee," meaning that's all the information he was required to divulge.
It sounds like Williams did indeed re-aggravate his knee during the game on Monday night. If Shanahan could have provided some reassuring nugget of information, he probably would have, but he didn't. He allowed us to use our imaginations, which usually is a bad sign.
Williams tore his ACL on Nov. 2 last year. He missed all of training camp and the first four games of this season as he recovered as quickly as possible. As soon as he was eligible to be activated from the Physically Unable to Perform List, the 49ers activated him. That was two weeks ago.
Since then, Williams has come off the bench as a rotational defensive lineman and played fewer than 50 percent of the time. Clearly, he was not quite ready to play, even though he recorded his second career sack on Monday against the Commanders. The 49ers were trying to manage him prudently.
And Williams still re-injured his knee. That's disconcerting.
In hindsight, the 49ers once again allowed a player to play before he should have. I'm guessing the 49ers asked Williams if he felt ready to go, and he said yes, as almost any professional football player would say. They're programmed to want to play no matter what.
That's why teams have to protect players from themselves. You've heard that cliché a million times because it's true. Teams must prevent players from making shortsighted decisions. Teams have to be the ones who consider the big picture and worry about the long haul.
The 49ers don't do a good enough job of protecting players from themselves. Just last week, the 49ers let Mike Evans play through Achilles tendinitis, and he made it worse. Earlier in the season, they let Nick Bosa return from his third ACL tear before he had completed a full practice, and he wound up injuring his calf.
When players come back too early, they often reinjure themselves. If anyone should understand that by now, it's the 49ers.
When will they realize that they have to be more careful?

title: 9 49ers Miss First Week 7 Practice Against Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers were missing nine players in their first Week 7 practice against the Atlanta Falcons. It wouldn't be a normal practice report without multiple players out for the 49ers.
Many of the players who were held out were the usual suspects. Nick Bosa (calf) is still out, but Kyle Shanahan did leave the door open for him to practice on Thursday.
Although, at this point, it's best for the 49ers to hold him out through the Bye, since it comes after this week. They might as well give Bosa all the rest he can get for the second-half push.
Mike Evans (Achilles) isn't participating, which was to be expected after he exited the game on Monday night. He's dealing with Achilles tendinitis, so the 49ers need to be extra careful with him.
Evans should never have played against the Washington Commanders. He didn't participate in a single practice for that game because of his Achilles.
Yet the 49ers thought it was okay to trot him out there. Achilles injuries should always be treated with extreme caution. It's malpractice by the 49ers, especially since they dealt with this two years ago with Christian McCaffrey.
They should know better. Now, they will most likely play without Evans against the Falcons. I wouldn't expect him to be ready for Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders either.
Without Evans, the 49ers will rely on Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and veteran Brandin Cooks. Brock Purdy is going to need to turn nothing into something with these receivers .
As for the rest of the players who missed practice: Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Luke Gifford (groin), Garrett Wallow (hamstring), Siran Neal (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle), Upton Stout (shoulder), and Mykel Williams (knee).
Samuel, Gifford, Wallow, and Sigle aren't a surprise. Neither is Stout. He left the game on Monday night because of his injury.
Williams, however, is a surprise for missing practice. The 49ers held him out because of a knee issue, but you have to wonder if it's soreness from back-to-back intense weeks.
Remember, Bosa dealt with knee soreness in training camp after intensifying his workload. The same could be happening to Williams
In any case, this is worth monitoring throughout the week, along with Stout's shoulder injury. So long as both players practice on Friday, they'll be good to go against the Falcons.

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey Hits New Rushing TD Milestone After Week 6 Win
full_text:
After six weeks, the San Francisco 49ers' touchdown leader is running back Christian McCaffrey.
Is it a surprise? Not really.
Despite seeing his workload reduced , McCaffrey has recorded seven rushing touchdowns, leading the franchise. Most, if not all, have come from short-range situations, typically between two and five yards out.
Let's be honest, keeping him fresh for those crucial goal-line carries is a smart move, especially given his ability to power through multiple defenders and find the end zone.
Against the Washington Commanders in Week 6 , McCaffrey recorded two as the 49ers won 23-17. It was a closer game than they wanted after an impressive start, but a win is a win.
At the time of writing, this week is especially significant for McCaffrey as he was traded by San Francisco four years ago. In that time, he's secured 55 touchdowns in total, from 54 games, which puts him in ninth on the franchise's all-time list.
But after two rushing touchdowns in Week 6, he's on 37 for the franchise, which places him fifth all time.
5. Christian McCaffrey (37 - Tied with J.D. Smith and Steve Young)
It would come as little surprise if McCaffrey overtakes Roger Craig before he retires, given his continued importance to San Francisco's offense. Despite a slight drop-off in explosiveness, he remains a key figure in the 49ers' running game.
His impact extends far beyond the end zone, though. With 34 games in which he's recorded at least 100 yards from scrimmage as a 49er, he ranks fourth in franchise history, behind Jerry Rice (70), Gore (66) and Craig (50).
His all-around ability was also on display after recording 64 rushing yards and 53 receiving yards, marking the 39th game of his career with at least 50 yards in both categories. That puts him second in NFL history, just two games behind Marshall Faulk’s record of 41. He's also two games behind Craig to equal the franchise record.
It is increasingly difficult to imagine McCaffrey's career ending without a place in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. His versatility as both a runner and receiver sets him apart. But to be so high up in franchise history just four years after joining is even more incredible.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the 49ers Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are expected to be buyers at the trade deadline. While trading for Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle A’Shawn Robinson is not the flashiest move the team can make, it is the smartest.
To start, the 49ers could use a wide receiver and an edge rusher. However, while both positions are thin, they are both expected to get significant starters back. Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling could all be back in the lineup four weeks from now.
On the edge, they already got Mykel Williams back from injury, and Nick Bosa is expected to be back any week. However, they are not going to get Alfred Collins back this year, and run defense was already a weakness.
The 49ers currently rank 29th in success rate allowed on the ground. Because they lead in games and teams have to throw, it has not cost them. However, in tight playoff games, this flaw is big enough to end their season .
They have to make a move, and Robinson makes the most sense. Most fans will want DeForest Buckner or Daron Payne. Those are big names, but they come with big price tags. Both are free agents after the year as well.
So, the 49ers can trade a notable draft pick and pay a decent chunk of their salary for a run at the playoffs. However, Robinson might bring exactly what the 49ers need, and he can do it a fraction of the cost.
Gracen Halton and Osa Odighizuwa are great pass rushers. They both struggle against the run. They do not need Buckner or Payne to replace one of them. They need a complementary run defender to take them off the field when they are not needed.
Buckner or Payne would limit the progress of Halton. Robinson would put Halton in better positions to succeed while maintaining a high snap count.
This season, Payne has eight run stops and a 7.8% stop rate. Buckner has seven run stops and a 6.7% stop rate. Robinson has seven run stops and a 9.7% stop rate. The difference is that Buckner has 19 pressures, Payne has 17, and Robinson has seven.
If San Francisco needed a game-changing starter or impact pass rusher, those options make a lot of sense. Their biggest issue is depth and run defense. When it comes to cost, fit, and need, Robinson checks every box.

title: Could 2 Crucial Buccaneers Starters Miss Week 7 Game vs. Panthers?
full_text:
Every game is a must-win in the NFL, but for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , this Week 7 game really earns the term. The Bucs are playing the NFC South leaders, the Carolina Panthers, in their first NFC South game of the year — a win keeps their meager playoff hopes alive, and a loss could bury them entirely.
Naturally, the team will want everyone healthy to try and pick up the crucial victory, but that's never all that simple in the NFL. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is likely to return for Tampa Bay under center for the first time since Week 3, but he may not have as many offensive players to work with as he'd like.
Based on Thursday's practice, the Buccaneers could go without two important members of their offense.
A few players, like running back Bucky Irving and cornerback Zyon McCollum, were back at practice on Thursday after being absent on Wednesday. But two key Buccaneers did not practice, and that could put them in danger of not playing on Sunday.
Left tackle Luke Goedeke was listed as a non-participant with a calf injury on Wednesday, and he also did not participate on Thursday. Additionally, wideout Emeka Egbuka, listed with a concussion and a foot injury, was working off to the side with a trainer and thus was also not practicing.
With two days off of practice, both players are in danger of missing Tampa Bay's game against Carolina on Sunday.
Goedeke has been a bright spot on Tampa Bay's offensive line along with left tackle Tristan Wirfs. If he cannot go because of his calf injury, one of the team's swing tackles — likely Ben Chukwuma — would step in for him at right tackle.
Egbuka has been healthy this whole year so far, but he'll have to clear concussion protocol to play against the Panthers — and that's assuming that his foot is healthy. If he cannot go, wideouts like Tez Johnson and potentially David Sills, should the latter come off of IR, could help bolster the receiving corps. Rookie wideout Ted Hurst has already been involved in the offense in the absence of receiver Jalen McMillan, who re-injured his knee in Week 3.
The Buccaneers would love to see one or both of Egbuka and Goedeke be able to make it for Sunday. But in the very real possibility that they aren't able to, Tampa Bay's depth will have to step up when the team heads to Charlotte on Oct. 25.

title: Could the Buccaneers Actually Trade Away Vita Vea?
full_text:
As each week passes, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' chances of making the postseason drift further and further away.
That's what happens when you consistently lose football games.
Another thing that happens when you consistently lose football games, as the Bucs have done this year, is that you gradually begin to focus on the future more than the present. If the Buccaneers can't knock off the Carolina Panthers this Sunday in what will be their first divisional matchup of the season, then prioritizing future seasons over this one becomes a necessity rather than just a consideration.
Should Jason Licht and the Buccaneers truly commit to focusing on the future, then they would be well positioned to do so simply because they have plenty of high-quality, established NFL talent at a number of different positions.
That being said, it's not like every player on the roster would all of a sudden become available for a trade. If the Bucs do head down that path, which players might the Bucs be willing to part with in order to improve their roster for the future?
ESPN recently published an article by a collection of NFL insiders exploring the latest intel and buzz traveling around the NFL, and according to Dan Graziano, one player we could see the Bucs look to move on from is veteran defensive tackle Vita Vea.
"The Buccaneers are 1-5. Vea is 31 years old, and he and the team begrudgingly came to a compromise agreement on his contract during training camp," Graziano wrote. "The Bucs didn't act as if he was part of their long-term future, and if teams come looking for a big, run-stuffing defensive tackle, Tampa would be silly not to listen."
Graziano also dug into why a trade for Vea would make sense for plenty of teams in the market for an upgrade along the interior of their defensive line.
"He is on a minimum salary this year and is guaranteed $23 million for 2027, which would rank about 15th in terms of cap numbers for defensive tackles in the league," he wrote. "If you need interior D-line help right now and don't mind paying Vea $23 million next season at age 32, why not call to see what it would take to get him out of Tampa?"
Based on his contract, consistent production and championship experience, the concept of adding a player like Vea would certainly appeal to a variety of teams. The same could be said for Antoine Winfield Jr., Chris Godwin Jr. and other veterans on the roster who still have plenty of gas left in the tank.
What's more of an unknown is, will the Bucs actually commit to that approach?
Whether or not Licht and his staff are seriously considering moving on from homegrown stars to acquire valuable draft capital for the future remains to be seen, but they will need to make that decision soon.
And if the Bucs do lose to the Panthers this week and fall to 1-6? That decision should become that much easier to make.
